tools.title: Export policy trajectory
tools.summary: qpos episode -> named joint groups at a target rate with end-effector poses, object poses, labels and timestamps (npz/json/csv).
tools.description: Resolves each requested group to qpos columns: an explicit list of joint names, 'subtree:<body>' for every scalar joint under a body (a hand), or 'chain:<body>' for the joints above a body (an arm). Resamples the trajectory from the source fps to target_fps by linear interpolation (free-joint quaternions re-normalized), computes end-effector world poses (position + quaternion wxyz + rotation matrix) and object free-joint poses by forward kinematics on the resampled frames, carries the phase label of the nearest source frame, and writes an npz with one array per group plus joint-name lists, a json manifest with the layout, and optionally a wide CSV. Also returns the arrays. Nothing depends on a specific robot.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz.

inputs.name: out_path
inputs.description: Output .npz (a .json manifest is written beside it).

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Joint groups to export, in order.

inputs.name: end_effectors
inputs.description: Bodies whose world pose is exported.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Free bodies whose pose is exported.

inputs.name: target_fps
inputs.description: Resample rate; default the source rate.

inputs.name: csv
inputs.description: Also write a wide CSV. Default False.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: paths, n_frames, fps, per-group dimensionality, total action dimension, arrays (groups, ee poses, object poses, labels, t).

tools.name: extract_frames
tools.title: Extract frames
tools.summary: Decode a video into frame%05d.jpg files, optionally at a stride, with a meta.json recording the mapping.
tools.description: Every perception tool in this library reads frames from a folder rather than from the video, so that detection, tracking, depth and hand recovery all see exactly the same pixels and agree on frame numbers. This writes that folder. A stride keeps every n-th frame (the recorded effective frame rate goes into meta.json), and a frame range cuts the clip. Frames are numbered from 0 in output order.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: The source video.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Folder that receives frame%05d.jpg and meta.json.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Keep every n-th frame. Default 1.

inputs.name: start, stop
inputs.description: Source frame range [start, stop).

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Stop after this many output frames.

inputs.name: quality
inputs.description: JPEG quality. Default 95.

outputs.name: meta
outputs.description: frames_dir, n_frames, source fps, effective fps, stride, start, and the list of source frame indices kept.

tools.name: extract_hand_meshes
tools.title: Extract hand meshes
tools.summary: MANO hand meshes for every frame: ViTPose finds the hands and their handedness, HaMeR recovers vertices, camera translation and MANO parameters.
tools.description: Runs ViTPose whole-body pose on the full frame (egocentric footage rarely shows a person, so a person detector would find nothing), turns the wrist and finger keypoints into hand boxes with correct left/right labels, and passes each box to HaMeR. Per frame it records the MANO vertices, the weak-perspective camera translation lifted to the full image, handedness, boxes and MANO parameters, and renders an overlay video plus per-frame RGBA hand layers for compositing. Detection runs on the raw frame and falls back to a contrast/brightness-boosted copy only when nothing is found: the boost raised recall on dark egocentric clips and lowered it on bright bench footage. The output npz is what hand retargeting and the robot's initial pose are read from.

inputs.name: frames_dir
inputs.description: Folder of frame%05d.jpg.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives hands.npz, overlay.mp4, layers/frame%05d.png, summary.json.

inputs.name: hamer_root
inputs.description: HaMeR checkout holding _DATA/ (MANO, HaMeR and ViTPose checkpoints), vitpose_model.py and third-party/ViTPose; the tool runs with this as the working directory because HaMeR resolves its data relatively.

inputs.name: checkpoint
inputs.description: HaMeR checkpoint; the package default when None.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frame rate of the overlay video. Default 10.

inputs.name: enhance
inputs.description: 'auto' (default): detect on the raw frame and, when no hand is found, retry on a contrast x2 + 50 brightened copy (the setting a sweep picked for dark egocentric clips; measured to HURT on well-lit bench footage). A (contrast, brightness) tuple forces it; None disables.

inputs.name: kp_thresh
inputs.description: Keypoint confidence for a hand box. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: rescale_factor
inputs.description: HaMeR crop padding. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Limit the frames processed.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.description: frames processed, frames_with_hands, detection_rate, hands_left, hands_right, paths. hands.npz holds per-frame object arrays verts (n_hands,778,3), cam_t, is_right, bbox, global_orient, hand_pose, betas and the MANO faces.

requirements: hamer (github.com/geopavlakos/hamer, with its ViTPose third-party checkout)

tools.name: fill_arm_joints
tools.title: Fill arm joints
tools.summary: Fit each arm's joints frame by frame so its flange holds the hand it is bolted to (the hand's pose times the fixed mount), by exact 6-DoF IK with warm starts and branch continuity, and write the episode with the arm columns filled.
tools.description: The hands are driven by their virtual wrist servos during execution and the arm-hand welds are off; the arm columns of the executed trajectory still hold the home joints. This skill discovers each side's arm chain (the gripper body welded to the hand's end-effector body), reads the fixed flange-to-hand rotation and offset from the scene's home keyframe, and fits the chain to every frame with the continuous arm fitter (trust region, limit-aware, a multi-start reset when the warm chain is badly off, blended so the command stays smooth). Reports per side the position and tilt residuals, branch resets and the smallest joint-limit margin; arm_reach_check turns the residuals into a pass/fail.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz (qpos, labels, fps) with the hands' motion.

inputs.name: out_npz
inputs.description: Where to write the filled episode.

inputs.name: sides
inputs.description: Arms to fit (default both).

inputs.name: max_arm_rate_deg_s
inputs.description: method='legacy' only: joint-rate ceiling of the fit (95 deg/s; a hand that leaves home faster leaves the arm behind, which arm_reach_check then reports).

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: 'exact' (default): strict 6-DoF IK of the flange under the hand on every frame, warm-started and branch-continuous, never rate-limited (an arm that cannot keep up shows as a joint-speed failure in arm_reach_check instead of a hidden gap at the wrist); 'legacy': the old trust-region fitter with rate limit and smoothing. For new episodes prefer execute_subgoal_plan with couple_arms (the arm is planned with the hand).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: per side: pos_err_mm {max, mean}, tilt_err_deg, roll_err_deg, branch_resets, worst_frame, limit_margin_deg; out_npz.

tools.name: find_example
tools.title: Find a verified example
tools.summary: Compares a video's perceptual fingerprint (and, when given, its Stage 1 result) with every verified example (examples/default and examples/asset_reuse) and says whether it is the SAME recording (reuse the example's outputs verbatim), the SAME TASK in another take or layout (reuse the example's objects and adapt its trajectory), or neither.
tools.description: Every example stores a fingerprint of its video (24 frames at equal fractions of the clip, grey 32x24, normalised), its Stage 1 result, its scene and its verified trajectory, but no video. A re-encoded or resized copy of the same clip scores a mean normalised cross-correlation above 0.99; two takes of one task on the same bench score 0.8-0.92. `identical` needs mean >= 0.97, every frame >= 0.93 and durations within 5%. `same_task` needs the Stage 1 result to list the same objects (ids and types) with a similar prompt, or a close video with the same object words. Call it first in every stage: an identical match is reused with reuse_example (the stage is then done); a same-task match lets Stage 2 start from the example's objects and Stage 3 adapt the example's trajectory to the new layout (adapt_example_trajectory) instead of solving from scratch.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: The run's video.

inputs.name: scene_semantic
inputs.description: The run's Stage 1 result (for the same-task test). Default none.

inputs.name: examples_dir
inputs.description: Folder with default/ and asset_reuse/. Default the repository's examples/.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: match ('identical' | 'same_task' | 'none'), example (folder), task, best {video similarity, semantic similarity}, candidates (top 5).

tools.name: finger_press_targets
tools.title: Finger press targets for a held object
tools.summary: From a grasp that holds an object with one finger resting on a sprung part (a spray pump head, a trigger, a push button), solve the finger joint targets that drive that finger's pad through the part's stroke along its joint, and write the hold, pressed and released poses the subgoal planner's hold motion executes as finger-only steps.
tools.description: The grasp pose (pose_from_points, generate_rigid_grasps ...) is placed in its hand scene with its closed finger targets. The pressing finger is taken out of the gripping fingers, so the executor's grip clamp (press_targets: the gripping fingers' flexion pushed depth_rad past touch) squeezes the body without driving the pressing finger into the part. The part's joint (slide or hinge) gives the press direction at the pad: along the slide axis, or along the hinge tangent at the pad, toward the joint limit farther from the current value. Damped-least-squares finger IK (only that finger's joints move, the wrist and the other fingers stay) drives the fingertip site to the pad position moved by stroke_m + overdrive_m along that direction. Three poses are written with the same wrist pose: `hold` (the grasp with the pressing finger out of the grip, its own open shape and press_depth_rad = depth_rad so the executor clamps exactly as the press was solved, every finger backed off without folding the pressing finger into the palm), `pressed` (finger_targets = the grip clamp with the pressing finger on its IK targets) and `released` (the grip clamp with the pressing finger back on its resting targets). Pressed and released carry finger_targets_open = the previous step's command and press_depth_rad 0, so a hold motion with approach_m 0 on them moves only the pressing finger. The IK is kinematic: the part does not move during the solve, the servo target simply lies past the part's rest so the finger pushes it; finger_press_in_hand_test proves the stroke in physics.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon dict or its JSON path); the grasped object is the last object.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Grasp pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers, ...} or its JSON path; the pressing finger rests on the part.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: The part's slide or hinge joint (full name, or a unique suffix of it, e.g. 'pump_slide').

inputs.name: finger
inputs.description: Pressing finger: thumb | index | middle | ring | pinky. Default 'index'.

inputs.name: stroke_m
inputs.description: Pad travel along the press direction; default the joint's range span (radians times the pad's lever for a hinge).

inputs.name: rest_offset_m
inputs.description: World shift [dx, dy, dz] of the pressing finger's resting pad before the press is solved (finger IK only), to move the pad off an edge or a protruding nozzle onto the middle of the pressing face. Default none.

inputs.name: rest_point
inputs.description: World point [x, y, z] the pressing finger's tip site is moved to before the press is solved (finger IK only): a grasp that wraps every finger can free one onto the part's pressing face (e.g. the part's press site raised by the pad standoff). Exclusive with rest_offset_m. Default none.

inputs.name: overdrive_m
inputs.description: Extra pad travel past the stroke so the servo keeps pushing at the stop. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: depth_rad
inputs.description: Grip clamp depth of the gripping fingers (the executor's press_targets). Default 0.3.

inputs.name: open_frac
inputs.description: How far the hold pose's own open shape backs every finger off. Default 0.55.

inputs.name: iters
inputs.description: Finger IK iterations. Default 300.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Folder for hold.json, pressed.json, released.json (with `prefix`).

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: File name prefix in out_dir. Default 'press'.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: hold, pressed, released (pose dicts), paths {hold, pressed, released}, joint, finger, direction (world unit vector), stroke_m, pad_travel_m (achieved by the IK along the direction), residual_mm, grip_fingers, issues (e.g. the finger cannot reach the stroke).

tools.name: fit_camera_to_table_plane
tools.title: Fit camera to table plane
tools.summary: RANSAC plane through the depth pixels around the tracked objects gives camera up, pitch, roll and height; cross-checks a GeoCalib estimate and overrules it when it points at the wrong side of the world.
tools.description: GeoCalib reads world-up from horizon lines and upright structure and fails confidently on a featureless white table (measured: +40 deg pitch, looking up, on a clip that plainly looks down). The support surface is the strongest plane that matters, so this un-projects depth pixels in a ring around the object masks, fits a plane by RANSAC, and takes the normal facing the camera as up. If the ring is too small or noisy it falls back to all non-object pixels below the objects' top row on the first frame. With a GeoCalib result passed in it reports which to trust: GeoCalib unless the two disagree by more than 60 deg, or by more than 18 deg when the plane fit is confident (inlier fraction >= 0.55, normal spread <= 12 deg).

inputs.name: depth_npz
inputs.description: estimate_depth output (depths in metres).

inputs.name: masks_dir
inputs.description: Palette label maps frame%05d.png; objects = every non-zero label unless labels is given.

inputs.name: focal_px
inputs.description: Focal length in pixels at the mask resolution.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Object labels that rest on the table.

inputs.name: geocalib
inputs.description: estimate_gravity output to cross-check.

inputs.name: n_frames, stride, tol, grow, keep_out
inputs.description: Frames sampled (5), pixel stride (3), RANSAC tolerance in m (0.008), ring width and keep-out in pixels (30, 4).

outputs.name: plane
outputs.description: gravity_cam, up (vec3d), pitch_deg, roll_deg, camera_height_m, inlier_frac, normal_spread_deg, mode (object_ring | full_surface); plus 'decision' when geocalib was given: source, disagreement_deg, note.

tools.name: fit_object_placement
tools.title: Fit object placement
tools.summary: Optimizes the pose of one object body in a scene (x, y, yaw by default; optionally z, pitch, roll, and a uniform size scale) so that its rendered silhouette through the registered video camera matches the object's video mask, by coarse search then Nelder-Mead on 1 - IoU with hand pixels ignored; writes the scene with the fitted pose.
tools.description: The paper's placement step. Loads the scene, adds the video camera (camera.json, or a camera already in the scene by name), and renders the segmentation of the object's body subtree at the mask resolution for each candidate pose. A fixed root body is moved by writing its pose; a free-jointed body by writing its free joint. Search: the yaw range on a grid combined with random x, y jitter inside the bounds around the start pose (the current pose, or the mask footprint's contact centre when `init_from_mask` is set), then scipy Nelder-Mead from the best candidate. IoU is computed on pixels outside `ignore_mask` only. With `scale` in the parameters the object's mesh and primitive sizes are scaled uniformly about its root (for an object whose size was guessed). Returns the fitted pose in the rig frame, the IoU before and after, the pixel offset of the silhouette centroids, and an overlay image (mask magenta, fitted silhouette green). With out_xml it rewrites the scene so the body starts at the fitted pose. A low final IoU with a good shape means the camera or the size is wrong, not the pose.

inputs.name: scene_xml
inputs.description: The scene (bench with the asset attached, from stage_on_bench).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Root body of the object (for example 'btl_bottle').

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The object's video mask at the camera resolution.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json, its dict, or the name of a camera in the scene.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Pixels excluded from the IoU (hands, arms, occluders).

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: Which of x, y, z, yaw, pitch, roll, scale to optimize. Default ['x', 'y', 'yaw'].

inputs.name: bounds
inputs.description: Half-ranges around the start pose that every search stage respects (coarse grid, yaw scan and Nelder-Mead): {x: 0.15, y: 0.15, z: 0.02, yaw: 180, pitch: 15, roll: 15, scale: 0.3} (metres, degrees, fraction). Give yaw: 20 to keep an object's known facing. Defaults as listed.

inputs.name: init_from_mask
inputs.description: Start x, y at the mask's contact centre on the table (with a camera.json; a scene camera name starts at the current pose). Default True.

inputs.name: n_coarse
inputs.description: Random candidates in the coarse stage (times the yaw grid). Default 48.

inputs.name: n_yaw
inputs.description: Yaw grid size when yaw is optimized. Default 12.

inputs.name: n_refine
inputs.description: Nelder-Mead evaluations. Default 120.

inputs.name: render_scale
inputs.description: Render at this fraction of the mask resolution for speed. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: out_xml
inputs.description: Write the scene with the fitted pose here.

inputs.name: out_png
inputs.description: Overlay image path (needs frame).

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Video frame for the overlay.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Default 0.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: x, y, z, yaw_deg, pitch_deg, roll_deg (rig frame) and scale.

outputs.name: iou / iou_start
outputs.description: Silhouette IoU after and before the fit.

outputs.name: centroid_offset_px
outputs.description: Rendered minus mask silhouette centroid.

outputs.name: out_xml / overlay_png
outputs.description: Written files.

tools.cli: python -m tool_library.skills.fit_object_placement scene.xml btl_bottle mask.png camera.json --out-xml scene_fit.xml --out-png fit.png --frame frame00000.jpg

tools.name: fit_object_poses
tools.title: Fit object poses
tools.summary: Fits one rigid mesh per object into every frame by mask chamfer, inverse-depth and gravity losses, with occlusion-aware freezing, anchor interpolation and wobble removal.
tools.description: Takes the single reconstructed mesh of each object and recovers its camera-frame pose in every frame. The init frame tries all 24 gravity-aligned rotations with rotation and a global scale free and keeps the best after refinement; every other frame warm-starts from its neighbour. Under occlusion the rotation is frozen when too little mask is visible, the pose is carried verbatim when the mask still fits inside the previous silhouette and a hand or another object explains the missing part, low-confidence frames are replaced by slerp between anchors, and deviate-and-return wobbles during an arm sweep are demoted. Output per object: T_seq (N,4,4) camera-frame poses, the solved scale and mesh centre, per-frame IoU, anchors, frozen flags and a visibility range. verts_cam(t) = scale * (V - center) @ R_t.T + t_t.

inputs.name: frames_dir
inputs.description: Folder of frame%05d.jpg.

inputs.name: masks_dir
inputs.description: Palette label maps frame%05d.png (track_objects pred/).

inputs.name: mesh_dir
inputs.description: Folder with <object>.glb/.obj per object (reconstruct_object_meshes).

inputs.name: depth_npz
inputs.description: estimate_depth output (depths in metres).

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Object names, matching the mesh file stems and mask labels.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives <object>.npz per object.

inputs.name: focal_px
inputs.description: Pinhole focal length in pixels (fx = fy).

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: name -> label; default read from result.json beside masks_dir.

inputs.name: gravity_json
inputs.description: estimate_gravity output enabling the gravity loss.

inputs.name: hand_layers_dir

inputs.name: options

inputs.name: python

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: per object: npz path, mean/min IoU, anchors, frozen frames, visible range.

tools.name: fit_placement_through_transparent
tools.title: Fit placement through transparent parts
tools.summary: Grid-then-refine fit of a free body's x, y, yaw (and optionally z) to its video mask through a scene camera, with transparent geoms (alpha below a threshold) made non-occluding, for objects seen through clear drawer fronts, walls or glass.
tools.description: Compiles the scene, hides every geom whose rgba alpha < alpha_max (and that does not belong to the fitted body) by moving it to geom group 5 and disabling that group, and renders MuJoCo segmentation through `camera` at render_scale. The body's pose is searched on a coarse grid over the given half ranges around its initial pose (keyframe 0 when the scene has one) (x, y in metres, yaw in degrees, optional z), then refined by shrinking the grid around the best cell `n_refine` times; the score is the IoU between the body's visible pixels and the mask, with pixels of `ignore_mask` excluded from both. The body must be a free body (its pose is set through the free joint's qpos). With out_xml, the body's pos/quat attributes and its free joint's pose in every keyframe are rewritten in a copy of the scene XML text. Returns the best pose, its IoU, the starting IoU, the number of transparent geoms hidden and an overlay PNG when asked.

inputs.name: scene_xml
inputs.description: Scene MJCF with the camera and the body.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Free body to place.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Binary mask PNG at the camera resolution.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Camera name in the scene.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Pixels to ignore (hands).

inputs.name: half_range
inputs.description: Search half widths {'x': m, 'y': m, 'yaw': deg, 'z'?: m}. Default x 0.03, y 0.03, yaw 30.

inputs.name: alpha_max
inputs.description: Geoms with alpha below this do not occlude. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Grid points per parameter per round. Default 7.

inputs.name: n_refine

inputs.name: render_scale
inputs.description: Render resolution factor. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: out_xml
inputs.description: Write the scene with the fitted pose here.

outputs.description: x, y, z, yaw_deg of the body in the world frame.

outputs.name: iou
outputs.description: Best IoU.

outputs.name: iou_start
outputs.description: IoU at the initial pose.

outputs.name: n_transparent_geoms
outputs.description: Geoms made non-occluding.

outputs.name: visible_px
outputs.description: Rendered body pixels at the best pose (full resolution equivalent).

outputs.name: out_xml
outputs.description: Written scene.

outputs.name: overlay_png
outputs.description: Overlay image.

tools.name: flat_hand_pose
tools.title: Flat hand pose
tools.summary: Lay a hand with straight fingers on a plane: the fingers point along a given direction in the plane and their pads (palm toward the surface) or their backs (palm away: fingers slid under a lid) touch it at a contact point; no inverse kinematics, the wrist is placed from the hand's measured finger thickness.
tools.description: Some contacts are made with the flat of the hand, not with a grasp: fingers slid under a lid near its hinge to lift it, a palm pressing a box flap shut, fingertips pushing a drawer front, a hand sweeping something across the table. Grasp solvers put pads on points and bend the fingers to do it; this skill keeps the fingers straight (every flexion joint at its extended end, abduction zero) and places the wrist so the chosen face of the named fingers is tangent to the plane through `point` with outward normal `normal`, the fingers pointing along `finger_dir` projected into the plane (the direction from the entry edge toward where the contact is). `contact` 'pad' faces the palm to the surface; 'back' faces it away (the lid rests on the backs of the fingers, the hand stays palm down and in the arm's reach). The thumb is 'out' (straight, in the hand's plane), 'curled' (folded under the palm; needs room below), 'up' (raised) or 'auto' (whichever penetrates the scene least). `pitch_deg` tilts the hand about the fingertips' line so only the fingertips touch and the thicker palm clears the table (a lid 35 mm above the table takes 18 mm fingers but not a 45 mm palm); a pitched hand is centred by the pads it really touches with (measured under the fingertips, about 10 mm behind the tip sites at 25 deg), so a press goes through `point` (a point contact transmits no torque: a press off the part's centre tips it). The pose carries grip_fingers, its own open shape (the straight hand, so the planner never curls the fingers into the table before the approach), points and normals (the contact under each finger) for the outcome's pad check, an approach along the normal when that space is free (a press comes from above) and else along the surface (fingers back out from under a lid), contact_side, and press_travel_m (4 mm of pad curl for a pad contact; none for a back contact, which the wrist's motion holds). Verify it like any pose (penetration against the scene, reach with optimize_pose_for_reach / arm_reach_check): the skill knows the plane, not the rest of the scene.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene from hand_scene_from_recon (hand_xml, side, objects...).

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: World contact point on the surface (under the middle of the named fingers).

inputs.name: normal
inputs.description: Outward surface normal at the point (for a lid's underside: pointing down).

inputs.name: finger_dir
inputs.description: World direction the fingers point (projected into the plane).

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Fingers expected to touch (the outcome's pad check). Default ['index', 'middle', 'ring', 'pinky']; the face is always the whole hand's.

inputs.name: contact
inputs.description: 'pad' (palm toward the surface) or 'back' (palm away). Default 'pad'.

inputs.name: thumb
inputs.description: 'out' | 'curled' | 'up' | 'auto' (the mode that penetrates the scene least). Default 'auto'.

inputs.name: pitch_deg
inputs.description: Tilt about the fingertips' line: positive raises the wrist (world up) so only the fingertips touch and the palm clears the table (a hand that does not fit flat under a low lid, a press on a tray's floor). Default 0.

inputs.name: clearance_m
inputs.description: Gap left between the finger face and the plane. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the pose here.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers, points, normals, approach, contact_side, press_travel_m, face_offset_m, thumb, pitch_deg, overlap_mm (hand vs scene at the pose)}: the pose dict every planner and verifier takes.

tools.name: flat_hand_pose_seated
tools.title: Flat hand pose, seated on the surface
tools.summary: Lay a hand with straight fingers on a plane like flat_hand_pose, then seat it: measure the real gap between the fingers' collision geometry (mesh hulls included) and the plane and slide the wrist along the normal until the fingers sit at the requested clearance.
tools.description: flat_hand_pose places the wrist from each finger geom's bounding-sphere radius when the geom is not a capsule; for a hand whose fingers collide as convex mesh hulls that radius is far larger than the hull's thickness, so the pads end 10-15 mm off the surface and a press or a hold never touches. This skill builds the same orientation (palm toward the surface for 'pad', away for 'back'; fingers along finger_dir projected into the plane; optional pitch about the fingertips' line; thumb out, curled, up or the least penetrating) and then measures, for every collision geom of the face (all non-thumb finger links, or only the fingertip links when pitched), its exact support along the direction into the surface: mesh vertices, box corners, sphere, capsule and cylinder analytically, the bounding sphere only for other types. The wrist is moved along the normal so the deepest of them sits clearance_m outside the plane. It assumes the plane is the contact surface near `point` (a face larger than the hand's footprint); it does not check reach (use optimize_pose_for_reach) or physics (execute the subgoal). Returns the pose dict every planner takes, with gap_before_m (where the unseated placement would have left the fingers) and the measured gap after seating.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene from hand_scene_from_recon (hand_xml, side, objects...).

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: World contact point on the surface (under the middle of the named fingers).

inputs.name: normal
inputs.description: Outward surface normal at the point.

inputs.name: finger_dir
inputs.description: World direction the fingers point (projected into the plane).

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Fingers expected to touch. Default ['index', 'middle', 'ring', 'pinky'].

inputs.name: contact
inputs.description: 'pad' (palm toward the surface) or 'back' (palm away). Default 'pad'.

inputs.name: thumb
inputs.description: 'out' | 'curled' | 'up' | 'auto'. Default 'auto'.

inputs.name: pitch_deg
inputs.description: Tilt about the fingertips' line raising the wrist; then only the fingertip links form the face. Default 0.

inputs.name: clearance_m
inputs.description: Gap left between the deepest finger geometry and the plane after seating. Default 0.0005.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the pose here.

tools.name: generate_flat_pinches
tools.title: Generate flat-object pinches
tools.summary: Thumb-versus-finger pinches across a flat object's short or long axis at mid-height (a hard drive, a phone, a plush toy, a lid lying on the table), solved by pose_from_points, screened for fingers in the table and, with bench_scene, for the station's arm (at the grasp, the pre-grasp and any waypoints), then lift-tested.
tools.description: generate_rigid_grasps wraps or pinches an object from its sides at fractions of its height and finds nothing on a part 2-3 cm tall: the finger links reach the table before the pads reach the faces. This skill measures the object's footprint in its own horizontal axes, and for each axis (short first) and each side the thumb takes, places the thumb pad and one or two finger pads on the two opposite faces at `height_frac` of the object's height (never lower than the pad radius plus `table_clear_m` above the table), at the centre of the face and at `along_fracs` of its length, and solves each with pose_from_points from above-behind seeds (pitched, wrist up). Every contact point is ray-cast on the part's own collision shapes from outside along the pinch axis (a rounded part gets pads on its real surface, not on its bounding box), with the normal from two neighbouring rays. A pose whose hand penetrates the table or the object beyond `max_overlap_mm` is dropped, and so is one whose pre-opened hand, on its approach line or while closing, goes more than `max_overlap_mm` into anything other than the part (the walls of a tray or a drawer, a neighbour): rejected.approach counts them. With bench_scene every pose is screened for the arm like generate_rigid_grasps does (arm_waypoints = the carry's displacement), and the best `verify_top` are lift-tested with the executor's full clamp (a ladder of clamp depths and pre-openings, then the wrist seated 2 mm deeper along its approach; a seated pose carries `seat_m`). Every pose carries hold {opposed, opposition_deg, need_n}: the force each planned contact must push to hold the part at 1.5 g tilted 30 deg with realistic (2 cm) twisting friction (hand.grip_hold_quality); pinches that hold with margin rank first, so a pinch line through the centre of mass beats one 30-45 mm off it (a 600 g drive twisted out of those). Returns the ranked poses, the format every grasp verifier and execute_subgoal_plan take (give the list as the subgoal's pose: the executor falls back down it). The hand scene is built once with contact pairs only near the part, every candidate is solved in it, and `time_budget_s` bounds the call: when it runs out the poses found so far come back with a note and the progress counts.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, grasp_body} or its JSON (hand_scene_from_recon); the last object (or grasp_body) is grasped.

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Finger sets opposing the thumb. Default [['index'], ['middle'], ['index', 'middle']] (thumb against the middle finger near one end lifted a 600 g, 24 mm drive that no index pinch lifted).

inputs.name: axes
inputs.description: 'short' and/or 'long': the axis the pinch spans. Default ['short', 'long'].

inputs.name: height_frac
inputs.description: Contact heights inside the usable band (0 = a pad radius above the table, 1 = a pad radius below the top edge: higher rides over the edge, lower puts the thumb in the table). Default [1.0, 0.6].

inputs.name: along_fracs
inputs.description: Positions along the face, as fractions of its half-length from its centre. Default [0, -0.4, 0.4].

inputs.name: table_clear_m
inputs.description: Pad clearance above the table. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: max_overlap_mm
inputs.description: Hand overlap with the object or table allowed in the static pose. Default 2.5.

inputs.name: bench_scene, arm_waypoints, arm_seed
inputs.description: Screen every pose for the station's arm (see generate_rigid_grasps).

inputs.name: verify_top
inputs.description: Lift-test this many of the best poses (0: none), each with a short ladder of clamp depth / pre-opening until one lifts; the working pair is written into the pose. Default 3.

inputs.name: open_frac, press_depth_rad
inputs.description: The pinch's pre-opening and clamp written into every pose (the executor uses them). Defaults 0.1 and 0.12: a flat part is pinched from a nearly closed hand with a light clamp.

inputs.name: grip
inputs.description: 'down' (fingers pointing down into a pinch across the part), 'pencil' (a part thinner than two pads, a pen or closed scissors: clamped at its equator near one end with the fingers lying along it, the wrist behind and above that end) or 'auto' (pencil candidates first when the part is thinner than two pads plus 6 mm). Default 'auto'. Measured limit: on a 13 mm pen the pencil pinches need the contact 40 deg above the equator to keep the thumb tip's back off the table, and they seat but slip after ~4 mm of lift; a pen this thin needs another strategy (a lever, an edge, a tripod from above).

inputs.name: time_budget_s
inputs.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole call: candidates not solved and lift tests not run when it runs out are skipped, and the poses found so far are returned with a note. Default 900; None for no limit.

inputs.name: pair_margin_m
inputs.description: Hand contact pairs are built only for object geoms within the hand's span plus this margin of the grasped part (a scene of 75 ring walls otherwise pays for every pair at every step). Default 0.05; None pairs every object geom.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the ranked list here.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: Current bench state for arm/collision screening: named trajectory.npz or proposal qpos. Defaults to the hand scene's recorded bench_state when available, otherwise the initial keyframe. Explicit object state must match the hand scene.

inputs.name: max_floor_mm
inputs.description: Default 1.5.

inputs.name: max_span_m
inputs.description: Default 0.115.

inputs.name: iters
inputs.description: Default 200.

inputs.name: max_candidates
inputs.description: Default 24.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: grasps (ranked pose dicts with pinch {axis, thumb_side, along, fingers}, hold {opposed, opposition_deg, need_n}, arm, lift), n_candidates, n_feasible, n_arm_feasible, footprint {axes, half_lengths_m, height_m}, progress {candidates_total, candidates_solved, lift_tests_run, lift_tests_planned, elapsed_s, stopped}, note (when the time budget ran out).

tools.name: generate_rigid_grasps
tools.title: Generate grasp candidates for a rigid object
tools.summary: Enumerate and rank grasp poses for a rigid object: pocket wraps from the side and above plus fingertip pinches across its bounding box, each with open, cinched and squeezed finger targets.
tools.description: Measures where the hand holds things (the pocket between the palm face and the curling fingers, from the hand's own kinematics) and the object's extent along its own axes, then places the pocket on the object: side wraps around the object's up axis at a chosen height fraction (palm facing the axis, fingers across it or pointing down it, every yaw step), and top grasps (palm against its top, fingers along several yaws). The up axis is the vertical for an upright part; for a part leaning 3-45 deg (a pipette in a rack) it is the part's own axis (its elongated principal axis, else its body axis nearest the vertical): wraps about the vertical forced a leaning pipette upright and pushed its rack. For objects narrower than 9 cm it also solves thumb-versus-index/middle pinches across each horizontal axis of the bounding box with the fingertip IK solver. Every candidate is screened statically: the OPEN hand must be able to retreat along its own approach axis to a pose that clears the scene by 4 mm, and the cinched hand must touch the object with at least two pads. The cinched hand's contacts are read from the geometry and judged (hold: opposed when two contact groups push at least 100 deg apart with the centre of mass between them; need_n, the force each contact must push to hold the part's weight at 1.5 g tilted 30 deg with 2 cm twisting friction). Survivors are ranked opposed first (with realistic contact a grip whose pads all press one face, the palm on another, holds only by the palm's friction while the wrist pushes: a bar held that way shot out of the hand when the arm pulled it), then by number of touching pads, shallower interpenetration and shorter retreat. With verify=True the top candidates are additionally driven through grasp_lift_test and the ones that lift are returned first. The object is never pre-fitted to a width model: the force-controlled close does the fitting at run time.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor}; the last object is grasped

inputs.name: height_fracs
inputs.description: object-height fractions for side grasps (default [0.5, 0.65])

inputs.name: yaw_step_deg
inputs.description: azimuth step around the object for side and top grasps (default 45)

inputs.name: finger_dirs
inputs.description: finger-axis options for side grasps: 'horizontal', 'down' (default both)

inputs.name: include_top
inputs.description: also generate palm-down grasps (default True)

inputs.name: thumb_oppose_fracs
inputs.description: thumb opposition settings to try, as fractions of the opposition joints' range (default 0, 0.4, 0.8)

inputs.name: min_fingers
inputs.description: cinched pads that must touch (default 2)

inputs.name: include_pinch
inputs.description: also solve thumb-vs-index/middle pinches across the bounding box for objects narrower than pinch_max_width_m (default True)

inputs.name: pinch_max_width_m / pinch_height_frac / pinch_ik_iters
inputs.description: pinch family limits: widest object to pinch (0.09), height fraction of the pinch, or a list of them (0.6; a pinch low on a tall part hangs the curled free fingers into its top on the way down, so every pinch is screened for the open hand's descent along +z and [0.6, 0.85] tries one nearer the top too), IK iterations per seed (240)

inputs.name: verify
inputs.description: run grasp_lift_test on the top `verify_top` candidates (default False)

inputs.name: open_frac
inputs.description: Finger flexion fraction of the OPEN hand during seating and approach (default 0.0, fingers straight, so the palm can come up to a fat object and the fingers wrap it; 0.15 keeps them slightly curled).

inputs.name: verify_top
inputs.description: how many candidates to verify (default 4)

inputs.name: bench_scene
inputs.description: The Stage 2 bench scene.xml: every grasp is screened for the station's ARM (exact IK of the flange at the pre-grasp and the grasp, arm links against the table and the objects) and annotated arm {ok, residual_mm, residual_deg, reason}; arm-feasible grasps rank first. Strongly recommended: a grasp the arm cannot hold is not a grasp of this robot.

inputs.name: arm_seed
inputs.description: Arm joints the screen starts from (default the scene's home).

inputs.name: arm_waypoints
inputs.description: Reach screening along the intended manipulation: legacy world wrist offsets [dx,dy,dz], or {object: free_root_body_name, target_pos: [x,y,z], target_euler_deg: [rx,ry,rz], steps: 8}. Object targets use intrinsic XYZ degrees and absolute WORLD body-frame poses (not object-bottom coordinates); omitted rotation preserves the previous orientation. The hand follows its grasp transform while the object moves, including intermediate rotations. These hypothetical IK states are never executed object motion; the full physical executor remains required.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the ranked grasp list here (a JSON list of poses, as generate_flat_pinches writes it). Default none.

inputs.name: keep_clear
inputs.description: zones no part of the hand may enter, {center, radius} spheres or {min, max} boxes in world metres: the room the other hand needs (the cap above a bottle this hand holds while the other unscrews it). Default none

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: Current bench state for arm/collision screening: named trajectory.npz or proposal qpos. Defaults to the hand scene's recorded bench_state when available, otherwise the initial keyframe. Explicit object state must match the hand scene.

outputs.name: grasps
outputs.description: ranked poses: {side, pos, euler, finger_targets (cinched), finger_targets_open, finger_targets_squeezed, grip_fingers, family, approach, retract_m, overlap_mm, n_touching, hold {opposed, opposition_deg, pair, need_n (N per contact), links}, lift (if verified), arm (with bench_scene)}

outputs.name: n_candidates / n_feasible
outputs.description: how many were tried and how many survived the static screen

outputs.name: object_axis
outputs.description: {axis, tilt_deg}: the up axis the wraps were built about and the part's tilt from the vertical; out_json when written

tools.name: grasp_prior_bodex
tools.title: Grasp prior from BODex
tools.summary: Run BODex force-closure grasp synthesis on the object's own mesh at its settled pose and translate the top seeds into wrist poses and per-joint finger targets for this hand rig.
tools.description: BODex (cuRobo-based dexterous grasp synthesis) runs in its own environment as a subprocess, driven by a job file and returning an .npz of candidate grasps in three stages (pre, grasp, squeeze) with their force-closure error. The object is placed at its current world pose on a table whose top is z=0, so grasps from below are excluded by BODex's own collision world. Each of the best seeds is converted to this library's pose convention: BODex's base_link pose becomes the virtual-wrist pose through the fixed wrist-to-palm transform measured on the compiled hand at rest, and the joint values are mapped by name with a joint sign decided by comparing the URDF's limits with the MJCF ranges (a converted URDF can have every joint mirrored). The GRASP stage is the candidate (fingers at the surface, not pressed in); the squeeze stage rides along as finger_targets_squeezed. Use the result as a set of candidates for optimize_fingertip_contacts and the grasp verifiers, not as a final answer: an articulated target is not a free rigid body and BODex cannot model it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, grasp_body?}; the grasped object must be a mesh for BODex

inputs.name: mesh_path
inputs.description: metric mesh of the grasped object in its body frame (.obj/.stl)

inputs.name: bodex_dir
inputs.description: BODex checkout (github.com/JYChen18/BODex) with cuRobo assets installed

inputs.name: bodex_python
inputs.description: python of the BODex conda environment

inputs.name: hand
inputs.description: 'sharpa' or 'shadow', or {robot_yml, manip_dir, joint_prefix, base_body_suffix, joint_sign ('auto' | 1 | -1)} for another BODex robot config

inputs.name: n_seeds
inputs.description: random restarts (default 20)

inputs.name: top_k
inputs.description: candidates to return (default 8)

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: work folder (job.json, raw BODex output, .npz)

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: subprocess timeout (default 900)

outputs.name: candidates
outputs.description: [{side, pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_squeezed, grip_fingers, grasp_error, dist_error_mm}] best first

outputs.name: n_force_closure
outputs.description: seeds with grasp_error < 0.2

outputs.name: npz
outputs.description: the raw BODex export

requirements: BODex environment (torch, warp-lang, cuRobo, trimesh, pyyaml, coacd) with a GPU

tools.name: grasp_prior_dexgraspnet
tools.title: Grasp prior from DexGraspNet
tools.summary: Run DexGraspNet's annealed force-closure grasp synthesis (its URDF hand model with our dexterous hand) on the mesh of the object or part to grasp, and translate the best grasps into this library's pose convention (wrist pos/euler in the world, finger targets by joint name) as candidates for the stress tests.
tools.description: DexGraspNet (Wang et al.) optimizes hand poses with a differentiable energy: force closure over sampled contact points, contact distance, hand-object and self penetration, joint limits, by simulated annealing over a batch of random initializations around the object. This skill exports the grasp body's collision geometry (its subtree) to an OBJ, writes it as a DexGraspNet object (normalized to its bounding box with the metric scale recorded), runs the synthesis in DexGraspNet's own Python environment through a generated driver (the hand URDF, its contact and penetration point files, batch size, iterations), filters the results by the energy thresholds, and converts each grasp: the URDF root link pose in the metric object frame becomes the wrist pose in the world through the object's current pose, the joint values are mapped by their shared names onto the MJCF hand (with a fingertip-position comparison against MuJoCo's forward kinematics reported, so a mirrored joint is seen), and `finger_targets_squeezed` is the same closure driven 2 mm deeper by the fingertip IK. Candidates come sorted by energy. Use them as a prior: run grasp_lift_test / grasp_hold_test / grasp_turn_test on them in the hand scene before any is executed. Needs a GPU and a DexGraspNet checkout prepared for the hand (DexGraspNet/grasp_generation with utils/hand_model_urdf.py and mjcf/<hand>_contact_points.json).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene dict (hand_scene_from_recon); the grasp_body's subtree is the object.

inputs.name: dexgraspnet_dir
inputs.description: DexGraspNet checkout (contains grasp_generation/).

inputs.name: dexgraspnet_python
inputs.description: Python of the DexGraspNet environment (torch, pytorch3d, TorchSDF, pytorch_kinematics).

inputs.name: hand_urdf
inputs.description: URDF of the hand for pytorch_kinematics (its joint names must match the MJCF hand's, e.g. right_thumb_CMC_FE).

inputs.name: contact_points_json
inputs.description: DexGraspNet contact candidate file for the hand (default grasp_generation/mjcf/sharpa_contact_points.json).

inputs.name: penetration_points_json
inputs.description: Penetration keypoint file (default grasp_generation/mjcf/sharpa_penetration_points.json).

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Grasps optimized in parallel. Default 32.

inputs.name: n_iter
inputs.description: Annealing iterations. Default 3000 (about 5 minutes on one GPU); 6000 for energies that pass DexGraspNet's own thresholds.

inputs.name: top_k
inputs.description: Candidates returned. Default 8.

inputs.name: n_contact
inputs.description: Contact points in the force-closure term. Default 4.

inputs.name: object_mesh
inputs.description: Use this OBJ (in the grasp body's frame) instead of exporting the collision geometry.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Working folder (default next to the scene's bench scene).

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: Default 1800.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Default 1.

inputs.name: coacd_threshold
inputs.description: CoACD concavity threshold for the convex decomposition of the object. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: min_wrist_z
inputs.description: Candidates whose wrist is below this height are dropped (DexGraspNet has no table). Default 0.01.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: candidates: [pose dicts with pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_squeezed, grip_fingers, approach, energy terms, fk_mismatch_mm], n_passing, out_dir, log.

tools.name: grasp_prior_from_video
tools.title: Grasp prior from video
tools.summary: Read the human's grasp off the video at the moment of contact: the approach direction on the table (from the hand mask toward the object mask, back-projected through the calibrated camera), whether the hand came over the top or from the side, the hand's lateral offset, and a ranked list of approach directions to give the grasp skills or to filter their candidates with.
tools.description: A human prior for pose selection. Given the object's mask (its footprint on the table at frame 0 or at the contact frame) and the acting hand's mask at the frame where the hand closes on the object (both at the video resolution; segment_with_text_prompts produces them), the skill back-projects both masks onto the table plane through camera.json, takes the object's footprint centroid and the hand's footprint centroid (the hand mask's lowest rows, where the fingers are, projected at the object's height), and reports the unit approach vector from the hand toward the object in the rig frame, the hand-object distance, the fraction of the hand mask that lies inside the object's silhouette (a large fraction means the hand came over the top), and the hand's angular position around the object. From these it ranks the eight horizontal approach directions plus 'top' and returns them as `approach_dirs` (the format pose_from_points / handle_pinch_pose take) and as a `family` hint (side wrap, top, pinch) for generate_rigid_grasps candidates: keep the candidates whose `approach` points within `tolerance_deg` of the human's. The prior is coarse (a hand mask on a table plane), which is what it is for: picking among verified candidates, never replacing the stress tests.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json (rigcam) of the video camera.

inputs.name: object_mask
inputs.description: Binary PNG of the object at the video resolution.

inputs.name: hand_mask
inputs.description: Binary PNG of the acting hand at the contact frame (the frame where fingers close on the object).

inputs.name: object_height_m
inputs.description: Height at which the hand's footprint is projected (the grasp height on the object). Default 0.05.

inputs.name: tolerance_deg
inputs.description: Angular tolerance for ranking approach directions. Default 45.

inputs.name: top_fraction
inputs.description: Hand-inside-object silhouette fraction above which the grasp is read as from the top. Default 0.5.

outputs.name: prior
outputs.description: approach_xy (unit vector hand -> object), approach_angle_deg, distance_m, hand_over_object_fraction, from_top (bool), family hint, approach_dirs (ranked unit vectors incl. [0,0,1] when from the top), hand_centroid_xy, object_centroid_xy.

tools.name: hand_scene_from_recon
tools.title: Hand scene from reconstruction
tools.summary: Build the floating-hand scene dict the grasp skills and stress tests take (hand_xml, objects, grasp_body, joint_init) from a Stage 2 scene_recon.json, with every object at its current bench pose.
tools.description: Grasp poses are solved on a scene with one floating hand and the objects on a floor at z=0; the bench's world frame is that same frame (table top at z=0, hand wrist joints equal to the world pose), so a pose solved here is used on the bench unchanged. The skill reads the manifest's objects (asset XML, root body), takes each root's pose from the bench scene's keyframe or from a given state (a trajectory frame, so a later subgoal is planned with the objects where the previous one left them), carries the objects' internal joint values over as joint_init, puts the target object last and names the grasped part as grasp_body (a cap, a drawer front, a lid), and picks the hand MJCF of the requested side from the setup folder. Returns the scene dict, also written to out_json for the next tool calls. It records the exact named bench_state so grasp and arm screens use the same object configuration by default; this is input provenance, not physical success evidence.

inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json (paths inside are relative to its folder).

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right'.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Object id from the manifest, or a body name in the bench scene (a part), that the hand will act on.

inputs.name: grasp_body
inputs.description: Body of the part to grasp when it is not the object's root (default: the target's root, or the target itself when it names a part).

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: A trajectory.npz (last frame, or frame given by `frame`) or a qpos list giving the objects' current poses; default the scene's keyframe 0.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame of the state npz to use. Default -1 (last).

inputs.name: hand_xml
inputs.description: Hand MJCF; default <setup>/robot/sharpa_<side>.xml.

inputs.name: setup_dir
inputs.description: Setup folder (default the repository's setup/).

inputs.name: include
inputs.description: Object ids to include as obstacles (default all).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the scene dict here.

outputs.name: scene
outputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects:[{name, xml, pos, quat}], floor, grasp_body, grasp_body_pose (the part's pose the poses are solved against; the planner re-anchors a pose to where the part is at execution), joint_init, bench_scene, target, held_in_air (objects a hand holds in the air at this state -- above the table, touching nothing else, a hand's collision geometry within 3 mm -- marked hold: they keep their pose in the hand scene instead of falling while it settles, and the grasp stress tests treat them as a handover: held where they are until the tested hand has closed, then let go)}; pass it to generate_rigid_grasps, pose_from_points, handle_pinch_pose, push_pose_from_point, the grasp tests.

tools.name: hand_scene_object_state
tools.title: Hand scene with the object's executed joint state
tools.summary: Copy the current values of an object's joints (the root's free joint, the ball joints of a cable, a lid hinge, a drawer slide) from a frame of an executed trajectory into a floating-hand scene's joint_init, so grasp solvers and stress tests see the object in its present shape instead of its built default.
tools.description: A floating-hand scene dict places each object by its root pose only; every internal joint starts at the asset's default. For a rigid object that is enough, but a rope whose root is placed while its cable joints are at zero is a straight cable, and an articulated box has its lid shut, so a pinch solved or stress-tested on any part away from the root is solved against geometry that is not there. This skill opens the bench scene the trajectory was executed in, takes the qpos at the requested frame, collects every joint whose name starts with one of the given prefixes (free joints as 7 values, so a rope's root lands where the bench has it; ball joints as 4 quaternion values, hinge and slide as 1; include_free=false leaves the free joints to the hand scene's own placement), and writes them into the hand scene's joint_init under the same names (the hand scene compiles objects with the bench's joint names). With the root pose already set from the same state, the object then has its executed shape. Optionally it also replaces the scene's grasp_body. Named recorded coordinates are mapped into the bench model. If the hand scene has bench-state provenance, that snapshot is updated too; changes to uncopied object joints are rejected so obstacles cannot silently retain stale states. Rebuild hand_scene_from_recon to update every object. It returns the updated dict and, when asked, writes it as JSON. It does not compile the hand scene; the grasp tool that consumes it does.

inputs.name: hand_scene
inputs.description: Floating-hand scene dict or JSON path (hand_xml, side, objects, joint_init, ...).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench MJCF; named trajectory coordinates are mapped by identity, unnamed trajectories must match its nq.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: npz with qpos [T, nq].

inputs.name: prefixes
inputs.description: Joint-name prefixes of the object(s) whose joints are copied (e.g. the object's id + '_').

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame of the trajectory (default -1, the last).

inputs.name: grasp_body
inputs.description: Replace the scene's grasp_body with this body (optional).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the updated scene here (optional).

inputs.name: include_free
inputs.description: Default True.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: hand_scene (the updated dict), n_joints copied, joints (names), frame, out_json.

tools.name: hand_tool_large_arena
tools.title: Hand tool with a large arena
tools.summary: Run any library skill or verifier that builds floating-hand scenes (pose solvers, grasp generators, stress tests) with the hand scene compiled under a larger MuJoCo arena, so contact-dense objects (perforated racks, tip trays, thin-walled tubes made of many wedges) do not abort the solver with mj_stackAlloc overflow.
tools.description: The floating-hand scenes the grasp tools build pair every hand collision geom with every object geom at condim 6. With an object made of hundreds of small geoms (a perforated rack, a 96-well tip tray, a cup built from wedges) a seed that overlaps the object creates hundreds of contacts and the default arena that MuJoCo sizes from the model overflows inside mj_forward (FatalError mj_stackAlloc), which kills the whole tool call. This wrapper sets <size memory=...> on the base MJCF every hand scene is compiled from (tool_library.common.hand), for the duration of one call of the named tool, then restores it. The tool's own arguments pass through unchanged and its result is returned verbatim with the arena size and the number of hand scenes compiled during the call. Nothing about the physics changes except the memory available for contacts and constraints.

inputs.name: tool
inputs.description: Name of a library skill or verifier that takes a hand scene dict (e.g. pose_from_points, generate_rigid_grasps, grasp_lift_test).

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: Keyword arguments for that tool, exactly as it takes them.

inputs.name: memory_mb
inputs.description: Arena size in megabytes for every hand scene compiled during the call. Default 128 (range 8..4096).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: {tool, memory_mb, hand_scenes_built, narena_bytes (smallest arena of the compiled hand scenes), result (the tool's own return value)}.

tools.name: handle_pinch_pose
tools.title: Pinch pose on a bar or handle
tools.summary: Solve a thumb-versus-finger pinch that straddles a bar-shaped feature (handle, rod, cord segment, scissors ring tube) at a chosen point along it.
tools.description: A bar is a segment with a radius: a drawer handle, a pen, a battery, a rope segment or the tube of a scissors ring. Given its two end points and radius (or the name of a capsule/cylinder geom to read them from), the pad points are placed on opposite sides of the axis at parameter s along it, across a pinch direction that defaults to horizontal-perpendicular to the axis (so the pads come in from the sides, not from above, which is the configuration that can lift). The fingertip IK solver then puts the thumb on one side and the index (plus the middle, offset along the bar) on the other, with seeds back along the approach direction, and the idle fingers are curled. Optionally tilts the pinch direction about the bar's tangent, which is how a rope was pinched from above-and-beside in the knot task. The result is checked with grasp_straddle_test, whose numbers are returned alongside the pose.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor}; the bar belongs to the last object

inputs.name: bar
inputs.description: {p0, p1, radius} in world metres, or the name of a capsule/cylinder geom in the compiled scene

inputs.name: s
inputs.description: where along the bar (0 = p0, 1 = p1) to pinch (default 0.5)

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: pinching fingers, thumb first (default thumb, index, middle)

inputs.name: pinch_dir
inputs.description: direction from the thumb side to the finger side across the bar (default: horizontal, perpendicular to the bar)

inputs.name: tilt_deg
inputs.description: rotate the pinch direction about the bar tangent by this angle (default 0)

inputs.name: finger_spread_m
inputs.description: spacing of index and middle along the bar (default 0.014)

inputs.name: approach_dirs
inputs.description: seed approach directions (default: +z and the thumb-side direction)

inputs.name: iters / yaw_step_deg / pitches_deg
inputs.description: IK budget and seed density

inputs.name: time_budget_s
inputs.description: Stop proposing further IK seeds after this duration, allowing the current seed to finish. Returns ik_search with seeds tried and whether the budget was exhausted. Physical verification is still required.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers, residual_mm, worst_residual_mm, overlap_mm, palm_facing, bar, straddle: {...}}

tools.name: hook_grasp_pose
tools.title: Hook grasp pose
tools.summary: Solve a hook grasp of a part with an opening (a scissor strap, a key ring, a handle lying flat): one or more fingers pointing down through the opening press its inner wall, the thumb outside presses the same wall from the other side, both with their fingertips upright so nothing reaches under the tabletop.
tools.description: A ring or a strap lying flat is too low for pads that close from its sides with the fingers slanted (a pad's centre must stay a pad radius above the table), and no finger gets under it. Its opening is the way in: a fingertip pointing down fits through an opening wider than the fingertip (thin_grasp_diagnosis lists the openings seen from above, with the largest circle that fits), and an upright fingertip touches a wall with the side of its pad at any height above its own radius. The opening is found from above (nonprehensile.openings: the part's top-down occupancy, the enclosed empty regions); `opening` picks one (default the widest). The wall to hook is the one in direction `wall_dir` from the opening's centre (default: each side in turn, the stations' side first). The hooking fingers (`fingers`, default ['index']) touch the inner face of that wall and the thumb its outer face, both at `contact_height_m` above the support (default: tried 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 mm under the wall's top, never under a pad radius + 1 mm), pressing toward each other; an upright fingertip touches a low wall with its distal cap, so the fingertip sites go that cap's offset above the contacts (nonprehensile.tip_cap_offset: 6 mm on the Sharpa index, whose visible tip reaches 12.4 mm past its site). With thumb false the fingers alone hook the wall (a pure hook: the planner pulls along `pull_dir` while rising so the part tips onto them). The fingertip IK (pose_from_points, seeded from above) keeps every link and the visible meshes out of the table; one candidate per sector of wrist heading (`sectors`) is kept when the residual and overlap are within limits. For a round opening every pose is also turned about the opening's vertical axis in 15 deg steps (the same hook on another stretch of wall, kept where the hand stays out of the part): an arm at the bench edge holds a few hand headings only, and the turned copies offer them without another IK; the six the arm holds best are stress-tested. The hooking fingers are the anvil (they hold as posed, a millimetre off the inner wall) and the thumb's clamp presses the wall onto them, so grip_fingers is the thumb (a pure hook clamps the hooking fingers): flexing an upright fingertip swings it off a wall instead of into it. The open shape (finger_targets_open, open_frac) is the widest opening of the grip whose hooking fingertips stay inside the opening with 1.5 mm to spare and whose thumb stays outside the wall, so the hand comes straight down (approach +z) into the opening. Give the poses to the `hook` motion (or grasp_lift) and stress-test them with grasp_lift_test.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output or its json); the part is its last object / grasp_body.

inputs.name: opening
inputs.description: Index into the openings found (widest first), or a world [x, y] inside the opening. Default 0.

inputs.name: wall_dir
inputs.description: [dx, dy] from the opening's centre toward the wall to hook. Default None: eight directions in turn, toward the stations first, until one gives a pose the arm holds.

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Hooking fingers through the opening. Default ['index'].

inputs.name: thumb
inputs.description: Thumb on the wall's outside (default true; false: a pure hook).

inputs.name: contact_height_m
inputs.description: Contact height above the support (default: tried 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 mm under the wall's top, never lower than a pad radius + 1 mm, until one gives a pose).

inputs.name: sectors
inputs.description: Wrist headings about the vertical are split in this many sectors, one candidate each (an arm reaches some headings only). Default 12.

inputs.name: max_residual_mm, max_overlap_mm
inputs.description: Acceptance (defaults 3, 1.5: a finger link resting on a 10 mm wall's top pushes the part away on the way down).

inputs.name: iters
inputs.description: IK iterations per seed. Default 200.

inputs.name: arm_screen
inputs.description: With the hand scene's bench_scene, keep only the candidates the station's arm holds at the pre-grasp, the grasp and the lift (armhand.screen_poses; `arm_dropped` counts the others). Default true.

inputs.name: screen_lift
inputs.description: Run each candidate through the grasp_stress_test ladder in the hand scene (approach, close, lifts of 6, 10 and 15 cm, 4 cm carries in five directions, 25 deg turns, hold; hand.stress_rollout) and drop the ones that fail (listed in `dropped`). Default true.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write {pose, poses, opening, ...} here.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: ok, pose, poses (ranked; pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_open, open_frac, grip_fingers, points, normals, approach [0, 0, 1], pull_dir (a pure hook), anchor, hook {opening, wall_dir, contact_height_m}), openings (all found), opening (the one used), why (when nothing fits: the opening narrower than a fingertip, the wall too low for the thumb, ...).

tools.name: human_grasp_pose_prior
tools.title: Human grasp pose prior
tools.summary: Retargets the demonstrated human hand at the contact frame (EgoDex ARKit joints from read_egodex_episode, or HaMeR meshes) onto the Sharpa hand: the wrist pose by matching the hands' knuckle frames, the fingers by per-finger IK on fingertip targets scaled by finger length, written as a pose json the grasp stress tests and execute_subgoal_plan take.
tools.description: Both hands get the same anatomical frame from four keypoints (common/human_prior.py): origin at the four finger knuckles' centroid, z from the wrist to the middle knuckle, y across the knuckles toward the thumb side on a right hand (the little-finger side on a left hand), x = y cross z out of the palm, which is the Sharpa root's own convention. The fixed mapping from the human frame to the Sharpa root is the Sharpa's anatomical frame measured once from its own sites (a 6 degree tilt and a 9 cm offset from the root to the knuckles); for EgoDex it equals the ARKit wrist transform composed with the axis map Sharpa x = -y, y = +z, z = -x (right) / x = +y, y = +z, z = +x (left) up to a constant 6 degree offset. Each finger's target is the Sharpa finger base plus the human base-to-tip vector, expressed in the hand frame and scaled by the ratio of the two fingers' chain lengths (scaling='per_finger'; 'hand' uses one wrist-to-middle-tip ratio), so a curled human finger gives a curled robot finger of the robot's size; retarget_hand_motion solves the finger joints over a short window ending at the contact frame (warm starts, limits). The knuckles are matched, not the fingertips, so the pads land within about the size difference of the two hands of where the human's were. With a hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon's json) the pose is measured against the objects (overlap with them and with the table, each pad's distance to the grasped body); clear_overlap lifts the hand off the table and backs it out of the object along its approach; snap_to_object then translates the whole retargeted hand, orientation and finger shape kept (the human's grasp aperture), by at most snap_radius_m to where the thumb and its two nearest pads are closest to the object without the hand entering it, because the demonstration and the reconstruction disagree by centimetres (measured 1-10 cm on an EgoDex lego episode). grip_fingers are the thumb plus the pads within contact_tol_m of the object (the close phase must bring the thumb in), or without a scene the thumb plus the fingers the human curled toward it. approach is the direction the human wrist came from over the last approach_frames frames (pads to wrist, as the planner expects). The pose is a PRIOR: it says how the human held the object; the grasp tests decide whether the robot can.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right' (the robot station that takes the grasp).

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: The contact frame (a Stage 1 subgoal's grasp moment, video frame index).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Where the pose json is written.

inputs.name: hands_npz
inputs.description: read_egodex_episode's hands.npz (ARKit joints in the rig frame).

inputs.name: hamer_npz
inputs.description: extract_hand_meshes' hands.npz (alternative source); needs camera and joint_regressor.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json of the video (HaMeR source only).

inputs.name: joint_regressor
inputs.description: MANO J_regressor (.npy or MANO_RIGHT.pkl from HaMeR's _DATA) for the HaMeR source.

inputs.name: hand_xml
inputs.description: The robot hand alone; default <setup>/robot/sharpa_<side>.xml.

inputs.name: setup_dir
inputs.description: Setup folder; default the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: hand_scene
inputs.description: hand_scene_from_recon's scene (json path or dict) to measure the pose against the objects.

inputs.name: grip_fingers
inputs.description: Override the fingers that grip.

inputs.name: scaling
inputs.description: 'per_finger' (default) or 'hand'.

inputs.name: window
inputs.description: Frames before the contact frame retargeted with it (warm start; the first is reported as the preshape). Default 10.

inputs.name: approach_frames
inputs.description: Frames of wrist motion the approach direction is read from. Default 8.

inputs.name: clear_overlap
inputs.description: With a hand scene, back the hand out along the approach until the overlap is at most 2 mm (at most 4 cm). Default true.

inputs.name: contact_tol_m
inputs.description: A pad this close to the grasped body grips. Default 0.015.

inputs.name: snap_to_object
inputs.description: With a hand scene: translate the retargeted hand (orientation and finger shape kept) by at most snap_radius_m to where the thumb and its two nearest pads are closest to the object without entering it; the unshifted position is kept as prior_pos. Default true.

inputs.name: snap_radius_m
inputs.description: How far the snap may translate the retargeted hand (per axis; 0.5x downward) to bring the thumb and its two nearest pads onto the object. Default 0.07.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frame rate of the source (retargeting rate limits). Default 30.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler (intrinsic XYZ, the hand root's world pose = the wrist joints), finger_targets {short joint name: rad}, grip_fingers, approach, finger_targets_preshape, source 'human_prior', frame, residual_mm per finger, finger_scale, human {wrist, tips, knuckle_origin}, robot_tips, and with a scene overlap_mm, cleared_m, tip_to_object_mm}; the input grasp_stress_test, grasp_lift_test and execute_subgoal_plan take.

outputs.name: out_json
outputs.description: The written pose file.

tools.name: human_grasp_seeds
tools.title: Human grasp seeds
tools.summary: Turns the human hand at each Stage 1 subgoal's contact window (EgoDex ARKit joints, an EgoDex .hdf5, or HaMeR meshes) into ranked Sharpa grasp-pose seeds per subgoal: the wrist relative to the object and the finger targets, retargeted through human_grasp_pose_prior / retarget_hand_motion, snapped onto the object, the grip fingers cinched onto its surface, and written as pose lists the executor (pose / pose_candidates), the stress tests and optimize_grasp_pose take.
tools.description: The demonstration already shows how the hand held each part; this skill reads it before any search. For every subgoal whose acting hand starts a contact (grasp_lift, hold, regrasp, pull, open/close_joint, unscrew, screw, tie, fold, or any motion on an object that hand did not touch in its previous subgoal; 'both' gives a seed list per hand) it takes the subgoal's time window (time_window_s x fps, or explicit frames), measures in every frame of the window (and `pre_s` before it) how far the human thumb and nearest finger are from the grasped body's bounding box in the hand scene, and picks up to `frames_per_window` frames: the arrival (the first frame within 1.5 cm of the closest approach), frames after it and the closest one. Each frame is retargeted with human_grasp_pose_prior (knuckle frames matched for the wrist, per-finger IK on fingertip targets scaled by finger length, the hand lifted off the table, backed out of the object along the human's approach and snapped onto the object by at most snap_radius_m, because the demonstration and the reconstruction disagree by centimetres). The grip fingers are then cinched from the human's finger shape until their pads touch the grasped body (avoiding the table and bystanders), giving the closed and squeezed targets the executor clamps from; the human shape is kept as finger_targets_human. Seeds are ranked by a static score: hand overlap with the scene, the thumb's and the next pad's gap to the object, fingers the robot could not bend like the human, and how far the snap moved the hand (a long snap is a warning that Stage 2 misplaced the object). Near-duplicates (8 mm / 10 deg) are dropped. With verify the top seeds of each subgoal are driven through grasp_lift_test and the lifting ones rank first. The seed is a PRIOR: hand it to optimize_grasp_pose (starts=<the seed json>) or execute it after its stress tests.

inputs.name: hamer_npz

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json of the video (HaMeR source).

inputs.name: joint_regressor
inputs.description: MANO J_regressor (.npy or MANO_RIGHT.pkl) for the HaMeR source.

inputs.name: hand_scenes

inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json: hand scenes not given are built with hand_scene_from_recon (target = the object id).

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives seeds_sg<NN>_<side>.json (a ranked JSON list of poses) per subgoal and human_grasp_seeds.json. Default 'poses'.

inputs.name: frames_per_window
