tools.name: identify_moving_joint
tools.title: Identify moving joint
tools.summary: Ranks the slide/hinge joints of an articulated object by rendering each one opened from the video camera and matching edges against the real frame; also reports raw pixel change per projected part face.
tools.description: A four-drawer cabinet has four equally drivable prismatic joints and optimizing the wrong one looks like success. For every candidate joint this finds the part's front face (the geom near the front along the joint axis with the largest face across it), projects it into the video camera for a labelled region, then OPENS that joint alone to its range limit, renders the scene from the video camera and correlates the edge map with the real 'during' frame inside the object's footprint. Raw frame differencing is also reported but is only a prior: a sweeping arm inflates it. Both frames are saved with regions drawn so a vision model can confirm the winner.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF with the articulated object and a camera matching the video.

inputs.name: frame_before
inputs.description: RGB frame with the part at rest.

inputs.name: frame_during
inputs.description: RGB frame with the part moved.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Camera name in the scene, or {'pos','quat','fovy'}.

inputs.name: joint_prefix
inputs.description: Only joints whose name starts with this.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Where to save annotated before/during PNGs and joint_id.json.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: Rest configuration; model default when None.

inputs.name: pad_px
inputs.description: Region padding in pixels (6).

outputs.name: ranking
outputs.description: most_changed joint; ranked list with joint, body, range, bbox, edge_match, pixel_change; image paths.

tools.name: inspect_rope_state
tools.title: Inspect current rope geometry and threading
tools.summary: Read a cable's current recorded centreline, body/material coordinates, spatial crossings, loop apertures, endpoint relations, and observed end passages through a selected material loop.
tools.description: Use a physically executed prefix's scene and trajectory to plan the next deformable manipulation. A passing grasp, in_hand or no_slip proves contact, not topological progress. Returns the actual ordered centreline, cumulative arc length and segment bodies, projected crossings with world coordinates and over/under order, candidate near-planar loop apertures, and each end's plane distance and projected boundary clearance. Candidate loops are discovered in three orthogonal views; loop_bounds can instead select a material arc explicitly as [vertex index + fraction, vertex index + fraction]. These bounds track material, not a fixed world location. To inspect a completed thread attempt, provide history_start and explicit loop_bounds; every recorded frame through frame is checked for the selected endpoint's side change through the moving aperture. Crossings outside the aperture, excessive opening or non-planarity, and insufficient strand clearance are reported separately. All passage results are diagnostic candidates: interpolation cannot prove continuous collision clearance, a hand may not fit through an aperture its rope fits, and a passage alone is not a knot. topology reports the existing four-closure classifier, but final acceptance still requires rope_knot_check and the complete gate suite after release/settling. A single image or static loop is insufficient. This tool never changes scene or state.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MuJoCo scene containing the cable; with no trajectory reads its home keyframe.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Recorded trajectory.npz; use the actual executed prefix, not planned wrist references.

inputs.name: rope
inputs.description: Cable name prefix, required when the scene contains multiple cables.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Recorded frame, default -1 (last).

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: Optional standalone [N,3] centreline for geometric analysis; no simulation or provenance is inferred.

inputs.name: radius_m
inputs.description: Cable radius for diagnostic clearance; default maximum collision capsule radius from the scene, or zero for points-only input.

inputs.name: loop_bounds
inputs.description: Explicit increasing pair of centreline parameters delimiting a material loop arc; omitted discovers candidates.

inputs.name: history_start
inputs.description: First trajectory frame for passage inspection, requires explicit loop_bounds and a trajectory. Checks every recorded frame without decimation.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.description: 'first' or 'last' endpoint for passage tracking, default 'last'; must lie outside loop_bounds.

inputs.name: endpoint_radius_m
inputs.description: Required radius for passage clearance, default rope radius. Supply a larger envelope for a cap or held tool; this is not a full hand collision screen.

inputs.name: max_loops
inputs.description: Maximum discovered loop candidates, default 6 (1..20).

inputs.name: topology
inputs.description: Include the existing four-closure topological classification, default true.

outputs.name: state
outputs.description: diagnostic_only, source, centreline, material_coordinates, endpoints, crossings, loops, passages, topology and limitations. No task-success verdict is produced.

tools.name: make_contact_sheet
tools.title: Make contact sheet
tools.summary: Tile evenly spaced (or chosen) frames of a video or frame folder into one labelled grid image, optionally cropped, so a whole clip or a time window can be read at a glance.
tools.description: Reads a video or a folder of frame%05d images, picks `count` evenly spaced frames inside [start, end] (seconds, or exact `frames` indices), optionally crops every frame to a box given as fractions of the image, resizes each tile to `tile_width`, and tiles them in rows of `columns` with the frame index and timestamp printed in each tile's corner. Returns the sheet path and the frame indices and times used, so a frame seen on the sheet can be fetched at full resolution with extract_frames. Windows and crops are how a vision-language agent zooms into a moment or a region without decoding the whole clip.

inputs.description: A video file, or a folder of frames written by extract_frames (then fps comes from its meta.json or `fps`).

inputs.name: out_path
inputs.description: Where the sheet image is written (.jpg or .png).

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Frames to show, evenly spaced over the window. Default 16. Ignored when `frames` is given.

inputs.name: start

inputs.name: end

inputs.name: frames

inputs.name: tile_width
inputs.description: Width of each tile; height follows the aspect. Default 480.

inputs.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] applied to every tile, as fractions of the frame (0..1) or as pixels of this video's frame (any value > 1; a box running past the frame is refused). Default: the full frame.

tools.name: measure_box_on_table
tools.title: Measure box on table
tools.summary: Fit a rounded-rectangular prism (length, width, height, corner radius, pose) to one or more silhouettes of an object resting on a known table plane, refitting the camera pitch across views.
tools.description: Given a table camera (focal, image size, height above the table, pitch, roll) and one or more binary silhouettes of the same object at different yaws, optimizes [pitch, length, width, corner radius] plus per view [height, outward growth, forward, lateral, yaw] with Nelder-Mead restarts to maximize the IoU between the projected prism's convex hull and each silhouette. share_footprint ties length/width/radius across views (one object), heights may differ (open vs closed); h_bounds per view constrain the height, which the silhouette of a transparent object fixes weakly. Returns the dimensions, each view's pose on the table (forward, left, yaw), the refitted pitch and the per-view IoU. The search runs per view first (yaw grid, then a scaled Powell search) and jointly after. On synthetic silhouettes of a 20 x 14 x 6 cm box at 0.8 m the footprint comes back within about 1 cm; height and pitch trade off against each other under perspective, so seed the pitch from a calibration when one exists and read the IoU before trusting the millimetres. silhouette_from_edges in common/tablecam.py extracts the outline of a dark-edged object on a light surface. Masks may be PNG paths (non-zero = object) or arrays; the camera may be the Stage 2 camera.json (rig frame), its dict, or a common.tablecam camera. With a rig camera every view's pose is also returned in the rig frame (pos_rig of the box's bottom centre on the table, yaw_rig_deg), ready for placing the object. One view cannot fit the pitch: fit_pitch defaults to True with two or more views and False (trust the camera) with one.

inputs.name: views
inputs.type: list[str | {mask: str | ndarray [H, W], init?: dict, h_bounds?: [lo, hi], label?: str}]
inputs.description: Silhouettes of the one object, one per view (frame): a mask PNG path (non-zero pixels = object, as segment_with_text_prompts writes them), or a dict with that path or a bool/uint8 array under 'mask', which may also carry a per-view 'init' {height, yaw_deg, fwd, lat} (m, deg), 'h_bounds' [lo, hi] height bounds in m ([0.005, 0.40] when left out) and a 'label'. All masks must have the same size.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: The camera the masks were seen through: the Stage 2 camera.json path or its dict (rig frame: fx, fy, R_cv, pos; then each view's rig-frame pose is returned too), or a common.tablecam.camera dict (focal_px, width, height, h_above_table_m, pitch_deg, roll_deg). Its pitch is the starting pitch. A camera of another resolution than the masks is rescaled to them.

inputs.name: share_footprint
inputs.description: One object seen in every view: length, width and corner radius are shared, heights may differ (open vs closed). False fits each view's footprint on its own. Default True.

inputs.name: fit_pitch
inputs.description: Refit the camera pitch jointly with the box (needs two or more views at different yaws: one view cannot separate a foreshortening error from a shorter box). Default None = True with two or more views, False with one; True with one view raises.

inputs.name: init
inputs.description: Starting length, width, height, corner_r in metres. Default 0.20, 0.15, 0.06, 0.02.

inputs.name: restarts
inputs.description: Random restarts of the joint search. Default 12.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Random seed of the restarts. Default 1.

outputs.name: fit
outputs.description: length_m, width_m, corner_r_m, pitch_deg, pitch_deg_start, pitch_fitted, mean_iou, views: [label, height_m, grow_m, fwd_m, left_m, yaw_deg, silhouette_iou, and with a rig camera pos_rig (bottom centre on the table) and yaw_rig_deg], x (raw parameters), camera_frame ('rig' | 'table').

tools.name: measure_carry_clearance
tools.title: Measure carry clearance
tools.summary: Per-frame clearance of a carried body to the table top and signed distance to every other body over the carry window.
tools.description: Replays the carry window (given as frames, phase patterns, or the body's own motion window) and on each frame computes the lowest point of the body's geoms above the table top and the minimum signed distance between the body's geoms and each other body's geoms using mj_geomDistance (negative means penetration). Robot bodies are included under their own names, so the clearance to the other hand is reported too. Returns the per-frame table clearance profile, the tightest frame, the nearest bodies sorted by their closest approach, and the height of the carry at its peak. The table top can be given or read from a body named table.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene with collision geometry (distance queries use it).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The carried body.

inputs.name: table_top_z
inputs.description: Table surface height; default from the 'table' body.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Carry window; default the motion window.

inputs.name: others
inputs.description: Bodies to measure distance to; default every other body with geoms.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame stride for the distance queries. Default 1.

outputs.name: measurement
outputs.description: window, min_table_clearance_m with frame/label, peak_height_m, table_clearance [per frame], nearest: {body: {min_dist_m, frame, label}} sorted.

tools.name: measure_joint_trajectory
tools.title: Measure joint trajectory
tools.summary: Per joint and per group: range used, limit proximity, frames on a stop, peak speed and step profile.
tools.description: Groups the robot's scalar joints (per side: end effector, arm, fingers, discovered from the end-effector bodies and the arm welded to each; or explicit groups) and measures each joint's minimum, maximum, used range as a fraction of its limit range, frames within 0.5 degrees of a stop, peak speed in the joint's unit per second and the frame and label where it occurs. Per group it returns the largest per-frame step profile (degrees for hinges) and its 99th percentile, the same signal the joint_speed_check gates on. Also lists the free joints of the robot (a floating wrist) with their translation and rotation steps.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: end_effectors
inputs.description: Hand root bodies; finds the arm and fingers per side.

inputs.name: chains
inputs.description: Explicit joint groups instead.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: measurement
outputs.description: groups: per group peak step, p99, worst frame/label and per joint statistics; fps; n_frames.

tools.name: measure_mask_footprint
tools.title: Measure mask footprint
tools.summary: Back-projects an object's video mask through the registered camera onto the tabletop: the contact line from the mask's bottom edge (where the object meets the table), its width in metres, the apparent height, and the footprint centroid and axes from the full mask, as initial size and pose for a constructor and the placement fit.
tools.description: Two readings of one silhouette. The bottom edge of the mask (lowest mask pixel per column, cleaned of hand pixels with ignore_mask) lies on the table when the object stands on it: back-projected onto z = 0 it gives the near contact line, its centre, its span in metres (the object's width across the view) and the depth of the object. The apparent height is the mask's vertical pixel extent above that contact line converted to metres at the object's depth, an overestimate for objects deeper than tall. The full mask back-projected onto the plane gives a footprint polygon whose area, centroid, principal axes and yaw are right for flat objects (boards, boxes seen from above, lids) and stretched away from the camera for tall ones; `height_guess_m` lifts the plane for that projection when known. Returns everything in the rig frame with the pixel box and a debug overlay. Not a measurement of hidden extents: the far side of a tall object is not visible, so use the width and the contact line as the reliable numbers.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Binary mask PNG (non-zero = object) at the video resolution.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json from register_table_camera or read_egodex_episode.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Pixels to ignore (hands, arms).

inputs.name: height_guess_m
inputs.description: Plane height used for the full-mask footprint projection (half the object's height is a good guess). Default 0.

inputs.name: out_png
inputs.description: Debug overlay: contact line and footprint drawn on the frame (frame needed).

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: The video frame for the overlay.

outputs.name: contact
outputs.description: center_xy (rig), left_xy, right_xy, width_m, depth_m (distance along the optical axis), n_pixels.

outputs.name: apparent_height_m
outputs.description: Mask height above the contact line in metres at the object's depth.

outputs.name: footprint
outputs.description: centroid_xy, length_m and width_m along the principal axes, yaw_deg of the long axis, area_m2, polygon_xy (convex hull) from the full-mask plane projection.

outputs.name: bbox_px
outputs.description: x0, y0, x1, y1 of the mask.

tools.name: measure_motion_timeline
tools.title: Measure motion timeline
tools.summary: Frame-difference motion energy over time for the whole frame and for named regions (default: left and right halves), with the active intervals, the peaks and the frame where motion first and last occurs in each region.
tools.description: Decodes the clip at a stride, converts to grey, blurs, and takes the absolute difference between successive sampled frames. Motion energy is the fraction of pixels whose change exceeds `pixel_thresh`, per region. Regions are boxes as fractions of the frame (or pixels when any value > 1); the defaults are the left and right halves, which on an egocentric table camera separate the two hands' sides. A region is active when its energy is above `active_thresh`; runs shorter than `min_duration_s` are dropped and gaps shorter than `merge_gap_s` are merged. Returns per region the active intervals in seconds, the peak time, the first and last active time and the energy curve (downsampled), plus the whole-frame intervals. Use it to set subgoal time windows, to find when a hand starts and stops acting, to locate a sudden event (a drop, a snap) as an energy spike, and to confirm which side of the frame moved. It measures motion, not identity: anything moving in a region counts, hands and objects alike. On a head-mounted camera the whole frame moves with the head; then compare regions against each other or raise active_thresh.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: A video file, or a folder of frames written by extract_frames.

inputs.name: regions
inputs.description: {name: [x0, y0, x1, y1]} as fractions or pixels. Default {'left': [0, 0, 0.5, 1], 'right': [0.5, 0, 1, 1]}.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Sample every k-th frame. Default 2.

inputs.name: pixel_thresh
inputs.description: Grey-level change that counts as motion. Default 18.

inputs.name: active_thresh
inputs.description: Energy (fraction of changed pixels) above which a region is active. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: min_duration_s
inputs.description: Shortest interval kept. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: merge_gap_s
inputs.description: Gaps shorter than this are merged. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frame rate for a frame folder without meta.json.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Also write the result here.

outputs.name: fps / n_frames / duration_s
outputs.description: Clip facts.

outputs.name: regions
outputs.description: Per region: intervals_s [[start, end], ...], first_active_s, last_active_s, peak_s, peak_energy, energy (downsampled list of [t, e]).

outputs.name: whole_frame
outputs.description: The same for the entire frame.

outputs.name: events
outputs.description: Times of the strongest short energy spikes over the whole frame (largest rises between consecutive samples), up to 10.

tools.name: measure_object_color
tools.title: Measure object color
tools.summary: Dominant RGB colours of an object from its masked video pixels: border-eroded in proportion to the mask's size, shadow-trimmed, k-means over several frames.
tools.description: Reads the frames and the object's label maps, keeps the pixels inside the mask away from its border (mixed edge pixels and a mask that bleeds onto the table would tint the result): the erosion depth adapts to the mask, `erode_frac` of its inscribed radius, between `min_erode_px` and `max_erode_px`, so a 28 mm ring a few dozen pixels across keeps only its core instead of a rim of table-coloured border pixels that outnumber it, while the depth is relaxed when too few pixels would remain. It then drops the darkest third of them (self-shadowed interiors are not the surface colour), and runs a deterministic k-means with luminance-quantile initialisation over up to five frames around a reference frame. The clusters, sorted by weight, are the colours to paint a constructed stand-in with; guessing them from a thumbnail is what this replaces.

inputs.name: frames_dir
inputs.description: Folder of frame%05d.jpg.

inputs.name: masks_dir
inputs.description: Folder of palette label maps frame%05d.png (from track_objects), or one binary mask PNG of the object at ref_frame (from segment_with_text_prompts).

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The object's label value in the label maps; None (or a binary mask file) means every non-zero pixel.

inputs.name: ref_frame
inputs.description: Frame to centre the sampling on. Default 0.

inputs.name: k
inputs.description: Number of colour clusters. Default 3.

inputs.name: n_frames
inputs.description: How many frames to pool. Default 5.

inputs.name: erode_frac
inputs.description: Erosion depth as a fraction of the mask's inscribed radius (its deepest pixel's distance to the border). Default 0.35.

inputs.name: min_erode_px
inputs.description: Smallest erosion depth in pixels (border pixels are mixed on any mask). Default 2.

inputs.name: max_erode_px
inputs.description: Largest erosion depth in pixels (a big object keeps its outer colours; a mask's spill onto the table is a few pixels at any size). Default 12; None for no cap.

outputs.name: palette
outputs.description: The return value is this list itself (not a dict): [{rgb: [r, g, b] in 0..1, weight: fraction}] sorted by weight; clusters under 2% dropped.

tools.name: measure_object_trajectory
tools.title: Measure object trajectory
tools.summary: Motion window, start and end pose, lift, travel, net yaw and speed of a body along a qpos trajectory.
tools.description: Replays the trajectory kinematically and reads the body's world pose on every frame. The motion window is the first to last frame where the body is more than motion_thresh (6 cm) from its start pose, requiring at least min_frames (4) such frames and padded by 3 frames, so fit jitter never counts as motion. Start and end are medians over the first and last 5 frames. Also returns max lift above the start, straight-line start-to-end distance, path length, net yaw change, peak speed, the largest per-frame step with its frame and phase label, and the full position track. Nothing is specific to one object or task.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, labels, fps) or qpos array.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Body to measure.

inputs.name: motion_thresh_m, min_frames, pad
inputs.description: Motion window rule. Defaults 0.06, 4, 3.

outputs.name: measurement
outputs.description: moved, motion_window [first, last] (displaced from the start pose), first_move/last_move (any motion at all), start_pos, end_pos, start_to_end_m, path_length_m, max_lift_m with frame and label, yaw_change_deg, peak_speed_mps, max_step with frame/label, positions [T, 3], phases inside the window.

tools.name: measure_rope
tools.title: Measure rope
tools.summary: Rope mask on a table camera -> ordered centreline in metres, length, radius; joins a mask in pieces, and flags (reliable false + issues) a coiled, crossing or fragmentary cord instead of returning confident wrong numbers.
tools.description: Skeletonizes the mask, builds the 8-connected skeleton graph and takes the longest path through it as the tip-to-tip centreline (spurs from caps and self-contact are dropped by construction). Reads the per-point radius in pixels from the distance transform, lifts the centreline onto the table plane raised by the current radius estimate, converts radii to metres with the per-point optical depth, and iterates until the radius converges (a 2% length correction on a typical bench, silently wrong if skipped). Smooths with an end-held moving average (a plain convolution shortens a rope by half a window per tip), resamples to n_points, and reports length, radius, diameter, the centreline in the table frame and in pixels, the tips, the radius coefficient of variation over the middle 70% and the self-crossings (junctions of the spur-pruned skeleton). A mask in several pieces is joined: pieces smaller than min_fragment_px are dropped, each piece's longest skeleton path is chained to the cord where its end continues the chain's end (gap <= max_gap_px, both turns <= 60 degrees), and the gaps are bridged straight (bridged_gaps_px; they count in the length, not in the radius). reliable is False, with the reasons in issues, when the cord crosses itself, the centreline explains under 75% of the mask area (turns lying on each other), the skeleton has much length off the path, the radius varies more than 35% or a piece could not be joined; then length_m is a lower bound and radius_m is inflated by merged strands. The two tips are unordered unless start_near_px names the end to start from (the plug end, say); radius_m fixes the radius when it is known (a mask blurred wider than the cord).

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Rope silhouette (any segmenter).

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: The table camera (common.tablecam.camera), or a camera.json / dict from register_table_camera or read_egodex_episode; then centreline_rig and points (rig frame, for build_isaac_scene) are returned too.

inputs.name: n_points
inputs.description: Points of the resampled centreline. Default 120.

inputs.name: smooth_win
inputs.description: End-held moving-average window, in skeleton pixels. Default 9.

inputs.name: radius_init_m
inputs.description: Starting radius for the plane lift. Default 0.008.

inputs.name: radius_m
inputs.description: The cord's known radius in metres (from a spec or a sharper frame): used for the plane lift and returned as radius_m, the mask's own estimate as radius_measured_m. Default None (measured).

inputs.name: start_near_px
inputs.description: A pixel (u, v) near the end the centreline should start from (the plug end); tip 'a' is then that end. Default None (whichever end the skeleton search finds first).

inputs.name: max_gap_px
inputs.description: Largest gap bridged between mask pieces, in pixels. Default None = 15% of the image diagonal.

inputs.name: min_fragment_px
inputs.description: Mask pieces with fewer pixels are noise and dropped. Default 30.

outputs.name: measurement
outputs.description: reliable, ok (= reliable), issues; length_m, radius_m, radius_measured_m, diameter_m, centreline_table [n, 3], centreline_px [n, 2], tip_px, radius_cv, self_crossings, coverage (share of the mask the centreline explains), fragments {found, joined, dropped_px}, bridged_gaps_px, bridged_length_m, mask_area_px, bbox_table_m; with a rig camera centreline_rig and points.

tools.name: optimize_fingertip_contacts
tools.title: Cinch fingertips onto the object
tools.summary: Curl each finger of a posed hand inward until its pad just touches the object, producing the closed finger targets a grasp is driven to.
tools.description: Starting from a solved pose, every finger's flexion joints advance in small steps toward the hand's closed synergy while the true gap between that finger's tip geoms and the object is measured with mj_geomDistance (the hand assets ship with contacts off, so the contact list cannot be used). A finger stops at first touch (0.8 mm of interference), and any step that would go deeper than 1.8 mm or that makes the gap worse is reverted: past a point the flexion arc carries the tip back toward the palm, away from the surface. Abduction joints are never moved, so the cinch curls and never spreads the fingers. Optionally also returns a preloaded variant solved with a deeper target interference, which is the correct way to squeeze a pinch (nudging joint angles toward a limit is not).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor}; the last object is the one the fingers close on

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: a pose from pose_from_points / handle_pinch_pose / generate_rigid_grasps

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: fingers to cinch (default: all with tip sites)

inputs.name: touch_mm
inputs.description: target interference per pad (default 0.8)

inputs.name: max_pen_mm
inputs.description: never let a pad go deeper than this (default 1.8)

inputs.name: squeeze_mm
inputs.description: if > 0, also produce finger_targets_squeezed cinched to this deeper interference (default 2.5)

inputs.name: step_rad, max_steps
inputs.description: cinch step and budget per finger

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: the input pose with finger_targets updated, finger_targets_squeezed added, and cinch: {finger: {curled_rad, gap_mm}}

tools.name: optimize_frame_locked
tools.title: Optimize frame-locked
tools.summary: CEM over rigid end-effector offsets inside phase windows, applied with a smooth bump and re-solved by IK, with every frame outside the windows left exactly as recorded.
tools.description: Each edit names a frame window (phase patterns or a frame range) and the offsets to search: dx, dy, dz (metres, world) and dyaw_deg (about the world up axis through the hand), each with bounds. A candidate applies offset x bump(t) across the window (bump rises and falls with a smoothstep over ramp frames, so joint speed and the frames outside are untouched), solves the end-effector chain on each edited frame and then the arm chain bolted to it (position-only when the weld carries no torque), and hands the full qpos to evaluate(Q) -> {gates, terms}. Candidates rank by failed gates then reward (optimize_reward_cem). Carried objects can be listed so they ride the hand's displacement over the window. Returns the best trajectory, its offsets and evaluation. The timeline, the phase labels and the untouched frames are preserved by construction.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: The verified-or-nearly trajectory.

inputs.name: end_effector
inputs.description: Hand root body (its chain is solved first).

inputs.name: arm_tip
inputs.description: Body the arm chain ends at; default found through the weld to the end effector.

inputs.name: edits
inputs.description: Windows and bounded offsets to search.

inputs.name: evaluate
inputs.description: Verifies a candidate trajectory.

inputs.name: carried
inputs.description: Free bodies that ride the hand on those frames.

inputs.name: iterations, population, elite, seed
inputs.description: CEM controls. Defaults 6, 12, 3, 0.

inputs.name: weights
inputs.description: Reward weights per term.

outputs.name: best
outputs.description: qpos [T, nq], params, gates, gates_failed, terms, reward, ik_worst (pos m, rot deg), n_evals, history.

tools.name: optimize_grasp_pose
tools.title: Optimize grasp pose
tools.summary: Cross-entropy search over a grasp's pose parameters (wrist roll about the approach, tilts about the pinch line and across it, offsets along the approach and the pads' line, the opening, the press depth), starting from human seeds, given poses or a grasp family's own candidates (rigid wraps and pinches, bar/cable-link pinches, plate-edge pinches, flat pinches), with a static and arm-reach screen first and the REAL grasp stress tests run in parallel processes; returns the best passing pose, or the failure classes of the best tries.
tools.description: Replaces the hand search of one candidate per call. The agent names the hand scene (the object, the part and the hand), the grasp family and the stress tests the subgoal needs; the skill does the rest. Starts: `starts` (a pose, a list, or a json file of poses: human_grasp_seeds' seeds, an earlier result, a deliberately rough guess) and, unless family is 'seeds', the family's generator run in the worker pool: 'rigid' = generate_rigid_grasps (pocket wraps and thumb pinches), 'bar' = handle_pinch_pose at several points along the bar and tilts about it (handles, rods, a cable or rope link: the grasp body's own capsule/cylinder geom, never the chain hanging from it), 'plate' = plate_edge_pinch_pose on each in-plane edge of the part's thinnest box geom, 'flat' = generate_flat_pinches (parts lying flat 1-3 cm tall); 'auto' picks by the grasp body as a whole (thinner than 24 mm across and twice as long, with a capsule/cylinder of at most 12 mm radius -> bar; a slab at most 12 mm thick with sides three times that -> plate; else rigid). Each candidate is a start perturbed by nine parameters in a frame at the grip pads (a = approach, p = pinch line, q = a x p): roll about a, tilt about p (keeps the pinch contact), tilt about q, offsets along a, p and q, the way in tipped toward above or the side (approach_up), the approach opening (open_frac, replacing the start's own open shape) and press_depth_rad. A perturbed hand re-closes its grip fingers from the posed shape until the pads touch the grasped body (hand.cinch_fingers, table and bystanders avoided). Generated starts cover distinct grasp families within the budget; after the first batch, isolated squeeze/opening/approach probes preserve seated contact geometry before the broader coupled search. Screens, cheap first: the closed hand overlaps the scene by at most max_overlap_m (grip pads excused against the part), the thumb and another grip pad within 2 mm of it (prehensile grips), the open hand 3 and 6 cm back along the approach clear of everything (the executor reaches in from there), outside keep_clear; then, with bench_scene, the station's arm (armhand.screen_poses: exact flange IK at the grasp, the pre-grasp and every arm_waypoints offset, arm links against the table and objects). Survivors run the stress tests by calling the library verifiers themselves (default grasp_lift_test and grasp_hold_test; any Grasp Stress Test by name with test_args) in `workers` worker processes of its own, or through `launcher` (a command prefix such as a cluster wrapper) for more CPUs. The score rewards passed tests and partial progress (the share of the commanded lift achieved, low slip and drift) and penalises screen failures by how far off they are; a Gaussian per start is refit to the elite candidates each iteration and the search stops at the first iteration with a passing pose (or at max_evals). Nothing is loosened: a pose passes only when every requested test passes unchanged. The result is a pose json the executor and stress tests take (with stress_tests to copy into the manifest) and the ranked passing poses as pose_candidates; when nothing passes, the failure classes of the best tries (screen reasons, arm reasons, each test's first failing phase) and a hint say what to change: another family, a non-prehensile motion for a part too thin for the pads, the stations, or the scene.

inputs.name: hand_scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon's json or dict): the object, its grasp_body and the hand side.

inputs.name: family
inputs.description: 'auto' (default), 'rigid', 'bar', 'plate', 'flat', or 'seeds' (only the given starts).

inputs.name: starts
inputs.description: Start poses: a pose, a list, or a json file holding a pose or a list (human_grasp_seeds' seeds_sgNN_<side>.json, generate_rigid_grasps' out_json).

inputs.name: tests
inputs.description: Grasp Stress Tests every pose must pass. Default ['grasp_lift_test', 'grasp_hold_test']; add 'grasp_shake_test' for a carry, 'grasp_turn_test' (with test_args joint) for a turn.

inputs.name: test_args
inputs.description: {test name: keyword arguments} for the tests (e.g. {'grasp_turn_test': {'joint': 'cap_hinge'}}).

inputs.name: lift_heights_m
inputs.description: Heights for the lift tests. Default [0.06, 0.10, 0.15].

inputs.name: bench_scene
inputs.description: Stage 2 bench scene.xml (or the station-moved scene): screen every candidate for the station's arm before its stress tests.

inputs.name: arm_waypoints
inputs.description: Reach screening along the intended manipulation: legacy world wrist offsets [dx,dy,dz], or {object: free_root_body_name, target_pos: [x,y,z], target_euler_deg: [rx,ry,rz], steps: 8}. Object targets use intrinsic XYZ degrees and absolute WORLD body-frame poses (not object-bottom coordinates); omitted rotation preserves the previous orientation. The hand follows its grasp transform while the object moves, including intermediate rotations. These hypothetical IK states are never executed object motion; the full physical executor remains required.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: Bench state for the arm screen: trajectory.npz (last frame) or qpos. Defaults to the hand scene's recorded bench_state when available, otherwise the initial keyframe. Explicit object state must agree with the hand scene; rebuild hand_scene_from_recon after physical motion.

inputs.name: bar
inputs.description: Family 'bar': the capsule/cylinder geom name or {p0, p1, radius}; default the grasp body's own thinnest capsule/cylinder.

inputs.name: plate_geom
inputs.description: Family 'plate': the box geom; default the grasp body's thinnest box.

inputs.name: keep_clear
inputs.description: Zones ({center, radius} or {min, max}, world m) no part of the hand may enter (room for the other hand).

inputs.name: bounds
inputs.description: Override parameter ranges: roll_deg, tilt_pinch_deg, tilt_cross_deg, off_approach_m, off_pinch_m, off_cross_m, approach_up, open_frac, press_depth_rad (each [lo, hi]).

inputs.name: iterations / population / elite_frac / max_evals / max_starts
inputs.description: Search budget: 8 iterations of 16 candidates, the best quarter refit, at most 128 candidate evaluations, 6 starts.

inputs.name: seed_time_budget_s
inputs.description: Per bar-family IK solve budget (default 30 seconds; None for exhaustive seeds). A running seed may finish after the budget. Reports searched seed scope; every accepted pose still passes all requested physical tests. Supplied starts are verified before fallback family generation.

inputs.name: max_overlap_m
inputs.description: Closed-hand overlap allowed by the screen (pads excused against the part; the executor fails a hand 8 mm in). Default 0.008.

inputs.name: prehensile
inputs.description: Require the thumb and another pad on the part (default true; false for a one-sided push or press pose).

inputs.name: workers
inputs.description: Parallel processes (default: CPUs available - 1, at most 8).

inputs.name: launcher
inputs.description: Command prefix that runs a worker batch elsewhere (a cluster wrapper); the batch runs `python -m tool_library.skills.optimize_grasp_pose --worker in.json out.json` there with its own pool. Needs a shared filesystem.

inputs.name: launcher_batches
inputs.description: Batches sent through the launcher at once. Default 2.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Random seed. Default 0.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the best passing pose here and the ranked passing poses to <stem>_passing.json; when nothing passes, the best try goes to <stem>_best_try.json (a start for the next attempt, not a pose to execute).

inputs.name: checkpoint_json
inputs.description: Optional atomic search journal. Saves completed evaluations, generated starts, pending jobs and CEM/RNG state after bounded batches. This agent-writable file is not verification evidence; resumed passing candidates are physically rechecked.

inputs.name: resume
inputs.description: Resume checkpoint_json with identical inputs (default false). Changed parameters, input files, compiled hand/bench physics, tool-library code or runtime reject the checkpoint. Budgets are total across resumptions, not added per call.

inputs.name: stop_file
inputs.description: With checkpoint_json, an existing marker requests a cooperative stop. The current batch finishes and workers close normally. Returns ok=false, status=incomplete, pose=null, passing=[]; no passing pose file is written. Remove the marker before resuming. An individual verifier or seed solve is not interrupted, so this is not a wall-clock deadline.

inputs.description: Maximum jobs per checkpoint batch (default workers). Requires checkpoint_json. Changes execution grouping only; the population, budgets and every requested check remain unchanged.

tools.name: optimize_pose_for_reach
tools.title: Optimize pose for reach
tools.summary: Search rotations of a hand pose about an axis that preserves its contact (the pinch line between the pads, the surface normal of a push, or the object's vertical) for the orientation the station's arm can reach with the smallest residual, optionally along a planned joint sweep or a set of waypoints, and return the re-oriented pose with its reach margins.
tools.description: A grasp is a contact set, not a wrist orientation: a pinch may be turned about the line through its pads and a fingertip push about its surface normal without changing what touches what, and a wrap about the object's axis within limits. The arm, however, reaches only some orientations at a given place. This skill takes a pose from any grasp tool, the bench scene and side, picks the contact axis (`axis`: 'pinch' uses the two grip pads, 'normal' the palm normal (the pads' contact normal for a push), 'vertical' the world z, or an explicit [x, y, z] through `pivot`), samples both signs and every enabled axis in `step_deg` steps before larger turns within their ranges, then descends on every enabled axis (the primary, the tilt about the pads' line, an opt-in roll) until the worst residual stops improving, and for each candidate solves the arm (position and the home-pose mount rotation, multi-start) at the pose and, when `sweep` is given, at the pose carried through a joint sweep (joint name, from, to, in the bench scene, with the hand following rigidly or level) or through `waypoints` (world offsets). Candidates whose turned hand penetrates the scene (a pinky into a box wall), or whose arm holds it only by running into the table, an object or its own hand (the executor's arm screen, armhand.ArmProbe: every arm link's hull at the solved arm), at the pose, along the path or on the way in (the pre-grasp `approach_m` back along the pose's approach, where the executor's reach ends, and half way down), are infeasible, and so is one whose pre-grasp the arm cannot reach within the transit tolerance. Objects are where `state` puts them (default the hand scene's recorded bench_state, else the keyframe); rebuild the hand scene from the episode so far once parts have moved. On the sweep, among the feasible candidates that reach, the smallest turn wins of those whose worst-case residual is within 1 mm (2 deg of tilt) of the best, so a pose that reaches unturned stays unturned (when none reaches, the best worst-case residual wins); the descent from there moves only for a candidate that reaches where it does not, or for a residual lower by more than that. Its finger targets are kept, its approach vector is rotated (kept along the surface normal, or in the surface, for a one-sided contact). Pose anchors follow the current materialized part as in the executor; returned poses carry their new anchor to prevent a second transform. A hand scene's recorded bench_state is the default state, and an explicitly inconsistent object state is rejected. co_sides requires actual contact with the moving part in this state; a parked hand or a hand holding its stationary base cannot be attached to the moving part. Screen the complete intended manipulation, not just the initial contact: use a joint sweep for mechanisms or held-object waypoint dictionaries for subsequent translation AND rotation. A rigid grasp follows the part's orientation; level following keeps wrist orientation and follows the contact centroid, so contact must be proved again during physical execution. This finite sampled screen is necessary, not a continuous-motion or task-success certificate. Re-verify the result with the stress tests: a rotated pinch may seat differently. With axis='normal' and parallel coplanar recorded contacts, the pivot/tilt line uses the surface points, the supporting plane normals stay fixed, and rotations that move recorded points off the plane are rejected. When the target part is identified by sweep or anchor, every named grip finger must also remain within max_contact_gap_m of its collision geometry at every nominal path state; metadata alone cannot prove contact.

inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF (reach is a property of the station).

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right'.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Pose dict or json from a grasp tool (pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers, approach).

inputs.description: The hand scene the pose was solved in (to locate the pads for the 'pinch' axis); default: pads from the bench scene at the pose.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: 'pinch' | 'normal' | 'vertical' | [x, y, z]. Default 'pinch' when the pose has two or more grip fingers, else 'normal'.

inputs.name: pivot
inputs.description: Point the axis passes through (default: the grip pads' centroid, or the wrist).

inputs.name: range_deg
inputs.description: Half-range of the search. Default 60.

inputs.name: step_deg
inputs.description: Default 10.

inputs.name: sweep
inputs.description: {joint, to, hand_follows: 'rigid'|'level', steps: 6, co_sides: []}: evaluate both moving-part geometry and wrist motion. At least one sample per 10 degrees / 1 cm. Optional from must match state. co_sides names hands already holding this moving part in state; their wrists and arms are screened too.

inputs.name: waypoints
inputs.description: World wrist offsets, or {object, target_pos, target_euler_deg, steps} for held free-body transforms (same convention as optimize_grasp_pose arm_waypoints). Include downstream orientation/placement targets when choosing a grasp.

inputs.description: Second search axis through the pivot: 'pads_line' (the line through the pads; a push keeps its pads on the surface when the hand tips about it), 'fingers', [x, y, z] or None. Default 'auto' = pads_line for a push, none for a pinch.

Rebuild the hand scene from the episode so far when a part has moved; an explicit contradictory object state is rejected.

tools.name: optimize_reward_cem
tools.title: Optimize reward (CEM)
tools.summary: Cross-entropy method over named bounded parameters, ranking by (number of failed gates, weighted reward); returns the best candidate and its evaluation.
tools.description: Samples parameter vectors from a Gaussian clipped to the bounds (initial mean at the centre or a given start, initial std a quarter of the range), evaluates each with the user's function, which returns boolean gates and real-valued terms, ranks by the number of failed gates and then by the weighted sum of terms (weights default to 1; give negative weights to penalize), and refits mean and std to the elite fraction with a std floor (2% of the range) and optional smoothing. Supports integer parameters (rounded), a deterministic seed, early stop when every elite passes all gates and the reward has stopped improving, an evaluation budget, and a history of every candidate for inspection. The paper's trajectory optimizer used this with terms such as object tracking error, penetration, smoothness and clearance.

inputs.name: evaluate
inputs.type: callable(params: dict) -> {gates: dict[str, bool], terms: dict[str, float], ...}
inputs.description: Builds and verifies one candidate.

inputs.name: bounds
inputs.description: Parameter ranges.

inputs.name: weights
inputs.description: Reward weights per term (higher reward is better).

inputs.name: integers
inputs.description: Parameters rounded to integers.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Initial mean.

inputs.name: iterations, population, elite, seed, max_evals
inputs.description: Defaults 8, 16, 4, 0, unlimited.

inputs.name: std_floor_frac, smoothing, patience
inputs.description: Defaults 0.02, 0.1 and 2 (iterations without improvement, all gates met, before stopping early).

inputs.name: log
inputs.description: Progress printer.

outputs.name: best
outputs.description: params, gates, gates_failed, terms, reward, evaluation (the full return of evaluate), iteration, n_evals, history (every candidate).

tools.name: overhang_pinch_pose
tools.title: Overhang pinch pose
tools.summary: Solve an edge pinch of a flat part (a phone, a card, a plate) where a hand can get under its edge: the grip fingers under the part where it overhangs the table's edge (or where its end is tilted up), deeper than the thumb on its top, so the pinch also carries the part's moment, with an approach from beyond the edge.
tools.description: A part thinner than about two pad radii cannot be pinched from its sides where it lies (thin_grasp_diagnosis); where it overhangs the support's edge, or where one end is tilted up (tilt_up), fingers fit under it. A pinch there holds only if it carries the part's moment about the pinch: the thumb on the top `thumb_inset_m` in from the edge and the grip fingers on the underside deeper, at `finger_inset_m` (default from the moment balance F_thumb (f - t) = m g (d_com - f) with the thumb pressing at most 5 N, nonprehensile.overhang_need; up to 15 mm deeper when the part overhangs farther than that needs). The contact points come from rays onto the part's own geometry. The hand scene's floor is made the bench table as the finite box it is (nonprehensile.with_table_floor, from the scene's bench_scene or `bench_scene`), so the fingers below the tabletop beyond its edge are not counted as in the table, and the result carries that scene (`hand_scene`) for the stress tests. With `overhang_m` the part is first moved along `edge_dir` in the hand scene until it overhangs that much: the pose for where a slide will leave it (it records the part's pose it was solved for as `anchor`, and the executor re-anchors it to where the part really ends). For each finger direction in `finger_yaws_deg` (the finger axis turned about the vertical from straight in under the edge; an arm often reaches a slanted entry only) the fingertip IK is seeded palm-up with the fingers pointing in (for a raised end also with the hand in front of the edge and the fingers curled down and in under it: under a tilted part there is room for fingers, not a palm), and the approach is written: the pre-grasp straight above the pose, over to above the point where the open hand is clear of the part, straight down beside it to the pinch height, then in along the fingers (`approach` +z, `approach_waypoints`). A candidate is kept when its worst pad residual is under `max_residual_mm`, its overlap with the part and the table (visible meshes included) under `max_overlap_mm`, every grip finger's pad clears the table's edge (or top, for a raised edge) by 3 mm, and the open hand touches neither on the way in nor while it closes: the pose carries the opening it was checked with (`open_frac`, the widest rung of the executor's ladder 55-15 % the executor keeps (narrower only where the open fingers would be in the table at the pose), whose slide in does not sweep into the part and whose close does not swing a finger through it; a thumb opened 55 % over a 12 mm box curled into its end face and shoved it 14 mm). Candidates are ranked by residual and overlap; give them all to the plan entry (pose_candidates) so the executor picks the one the arm holds.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output or its json); the grasped part is its last object / grasp_body.

inputs.name: edge_dir
inputs.description: [dx, dy]: horizontal outward direction of the part's edge to pinch (toward the table edge it overhangs, or toward its raised end).

inputs.name: overhang_m
inputs.description: Solve for the part slid along edge_dir until it overhangs the table's edge this far (default None: as it lies).

inputs.name: raised
inputs.description: The edge is raised above the support (a tilted part) instead of overhanging its edge: the fingers' clearance is their height above the table; the part is held where it is in the hand scene (another hand presses it). Default false.

inputs.name: grip
inputs.description: 'edge' (default: fingers under, thumb on top), 'sides' (a raised end only: thumb and fingers across the part on its two side faces, near the raised end where they stand a pad radius + 1 mm above the table; under a tilted part there is room for fingers, not for a palm; such a pinch resists the part's weight about the line through its pads only by the pads' torsional friction: on 7-11 mm boxes 14-15 cm long tilted 30 mm it held on the bench but failed the stress ladder, lift or turn_roll, so expect few or no candidates for a long part) or 'auto' (edge, else sides).

inputs.name: s

inputs.name: thumb_inset_m, finger_inset_m
inputs.description: Insets from the edge (defaults: pad radius + 3 mm; from the moment balance).

inputs.description: Thumb positions along the edge tried with each direction, from the fingers' centre (a turned hand puts its thumb to one side). Default [0, 0.012, -0.012].

inputs.name: bench_scene

inputs.name: iters

inputs.description: Write {pose, poses, hand_scene, ...} here.

tools.name: package_stage3_episode

tools.summary: Turn one passing execute_subgoal_plan run into the Stage 3 deliverable: trajectory.npz and phases.json, the manifest built from the executor's own outcomes (one entry per executed segment, bound to the pose each segment actually used), grasp stress tests run on those poses with their evidence, the episode audits, stage4_task/ from write_stage4_config, sim_video.mp4; then the manifest check and the Stage 1 goal gate.
tools.description: Everything in the manifest comes from the execution, not from the caller: frames, motion, side, object, release, expectations and measured outcomes from the executor's report and outcomes.json, the plan entry each segment ran, and for every segment that holds a part in the fingers the executor's selected pose and the hand scene of its actual starting state, on which the stress tests are run (default grasp_stress_test; `stress_tests` maps a motion or a subgoal index to other library stress tests, e.g. a turn or slide test). The audits episode_physics_check, robot_self_collision_check and arm_reach_check run on the executed scene and trajectory, stage4_handoff_check on the written task folder. A failed test or audit is written as failed and reported; nothing is forced to pass. trajectory_manifest_check and stage1_goal_gate are run at the end and returned, so a result with ok true is ready for finish (which re-checks everything independently). Two-hand segments (motion 'both') are packaged per hand. Deformables simulated in Isaac Sim: `isaac_episode` is the execute_isaac_deformables run on this very execution (its report's sha256 binding must name this scene and trajectory); its recording, deformables.json, MuJoCo mirror and video are copied into the workspace and stage4_task/, the manifest gets a deformables block, and the goal gate runs on the mirror.

tools.name: physics_informed_retargeting
tools.title: Physics-informed retargeting iterations
tools.summary: Stage 3 method module (the first after the agent): annealed sampling-based optimization in MuJoCo Warp on a GPU iterates hand commands along a reference (the agent's best physical attempt, an earlier method's tracking reference, or the demonstrator's hands) until the objects follow it under contact physics, with contact guidance; the result is checked on the bench's own rigid runtime and written as a tracking reference plus an execute_subgoal_plan plan of track_reference entries.
tools.description: Physics-informed retargeting (the sampling retargeting of Pan et al., 'SPIDER: Scalable Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting', 2025, run from its own checkout and environment; nothing of it is copied here): hundreds of control samples around the reference are rolled out in parallel in MuJoCo Warp, scored by how closely the object follows the reference, and annealed over iterations (DIAL-MPC), re-planned along the motion. Reference: `reference` (an earlier method's tracking reference), else the agent's best physical attempt in the workspace (tracking.reference_from_attempt: the execute_subgoal_plan folder whose executed entries cover the most Stage 1 subgoals, its commanded reference with one segment per executed entry); with source='human' the demonstrator's hands (EgoDex hands.npz, or HaMeR) mapped onto the Sharpa by matching anatomical hand frames, the objects following the plan or a given track, segmented by Stage 1's time windows. Preparation (sample-agnostic): the manipulated object grounded on what lies under it, fingertips within 2 cm of it in the interaction window put on its surface one pad radius out, the thumb re-derived at the antipode of the finger contacts (contact guidance). The optimizer runs at the bench's own 2 ms step with the bench's actuation limits (0.8 N m fingers, 40 N / 3 N m wrist) and contact parameters; the sampling `profiles` are tried in order (refine: small noise around the reference, held to it; explore: larger) and each result's commands (the executed wrist plus the servo push re-expressed for the bench's wrist stiffness, the finger commands) are rolled out once on the bench's rigid runtime as the executor will run them (tracking.BenchTracker: home start, joint-rate ceilings, arms coupled); the profile whose objects stay closest to the reference there is written. Outputs: reference.npz (tracking reference), plan.json (track_reference entries with the segments' Stage 1 indices and expectations), report.json. The harness runs the plan with execute_subgoal_plan (a trusted execution), packages it with package_stage3_episode and runs finish's verifiers, exactly as for an agent's plan; the agent may call it the same way. Limits: one free rigid object per acting hand (articulated objects, cables and a second object in one hand are refused with the reason), the reference decides which contacts are tried, a GPU and the checkout (models.spider_dir, environments.spider) are needed; without them the call returns ok false with `unavailable` and the next method module runs.

tools.name: pin_pose
tools.title: Pin pose
tools.summary: Hand poses that steady a part, or one link or end of a cable, while the other hand acts: fingertip, two-finger or flat-hand presses onto its top (or given grip candidates), kept out of the zones the other hand needs and reachable by this station's arm, ranked; the input of a `pin` plan entry.
tools.description: A steadying hand must hold the part still AND leave the other hand its room: a wrap around a bottle that reaches up to the cap is in the way of the hand turning the cap, and a press on a free cable end that the station's arm cannot hold steadies nothing. Press mode samples the part's top surface (vertical rays on its own collision geoms, keeping hits whose normal points up; or the `points` given), and at each point poses the families asked for: 'flat' (flat_hand_pose: straight index and middle fingers, pads down, pitched so only the fingertips touch, in `n_dirs` finger directions), 'tip' (push_pose_from_point: the index finger pointing into the surface, straight down and tilted 30 deg toward each of four directions) and 'palm' (flat_hand_pose unpitched: the whole flat hand on a large top). Grip mode ranks the given `candidates` (any grasp tool's poses; for a rigid part without candidates generate_rigid_grasps is called with the zones as keep_clear, wrapping low on the part; the best grips are driven through their approach and close, and one that shoves the part more than 1 cm is dropped). Every candidate is judged in the hand scene: no hand geom more than max_overlap_m into the scene, including pressing pads along the approach; a grip is judged against everything but its part), the posed hand pushed along the press direction meets the part with an intended pressing finger within 1 cm (the pose is corrected to first contact and the executor presses from that contact), and its collision geometry, at the pose and along the approach, at least clear_margin_m out of every keep_clear zone: {center, radius} spheres, {min, max} boxes, {p0, p1, radius} capsules (the swept cylinder of a cap and the fingers turning it), and {hand_pose, side, sweep?: {point, axis, deg}} (the OTHER hand placed at its own pose in the bench scene, optionally turned about an axis through a range: the volume a hand turning a cap sweeps). With bench_scene and side every surviving candidate is screened for this station's arm (armhand.screen_poses: the arm holds the hand at the pose and the pre-grasp, without running into the scene) and the arm's links must also stay out of the zones. Ranked: feasible first, then the larger zone margin (up to 5 cm), a press square to the support (its normal nearest the vertical, in 10 deg steps), more pressing pads (two pads cannot roll a round part from under them as one fingertip can), the nearer to the part's centre (or to `prefer_point`; the first press point is also taken on the crest), the smaller overlap. Each pose carries pin_mode, its press normals and points, the approach, and pin {family, point, normal, keep_clear_mm, overlap_mm, press_offset_mm, reach}; a `pin` entry takes it as its pose (force_n sets the press).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon dict or its JSON path) of the pinning hand; the part is its grasp body unless `body` names one.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The body to pin (hand-scene name, the bench name: a cable link such as '<rope>_ropeB_first'). Default the hand scene's grasp body.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: 'press' (default) or 'grip'.

inputs.name: families

tools.name: place_arm_stations
tools.title: Place arm stations
tools.summary: Search a common shift of both arm stations (their roots and the hands' home pose) toward or away from the objects for the placement at which the arms reach the most task objects with the most margin, and write the bench scene with the stations moved.
tools.description: The bench's arms hold a palm-down hand only in a band about 0.4-0.6 m in front of their stations, and a clip recorded in another session can put the objects 20-30 cm outside it (fitting the arm after the hand hides this behind centimetres of gap at the wrist). When object_reach_check fails, this skill moves both stations by the same (dx, dy), keeping their separation and orientation and keeping each hand on its flange at home, and scores every candidate by exact arm IK of the flange (the executor's solver) at each object: palm down above it, palm down pitched 45 degrees, fingers in from the side, each at the object and 3 cm around it. The stations stay where they are when every object's centre is reached; otherwise the shift reaching the most probe points (the smallest among equals) wins. The scene is written as a new file next to the input with the shift recorded in `place_arm_stations.json`; use it for every Stage 3 tool and the Stage 4 task folder. Prefer no shift: use it when an object or a destination (`points`) is out of reach, and report the shift. Generic probes do not know the grasp: when the task's hand poses are known, pass them as `poses` (each with the arm that must hold it and the displacements it must also be held at, e.g. the carry to a slot); the shift is then ranked first by how many of those poses their own arm holds exactly at the grasp, the pre-grasp and every waypoint without hitting anything (the executor's screen), then by the probes. `sides` limits the probes to the arms that act.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF (Stage 2 scene.xml).

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Bodies the arms must reach (default: every free object).

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: World points the hand must also reach: destinations of carries and places (the box a lid goes onto), measured like objects (hover above, pitched, from the side).

inputs.name: dy_range
inputs.description: Shifts toward the objects (+y) tried, metres. Default [-0.15, 0.45].

inputs.name: dx_range
inputs.description: Lateral shifts tried. Default [0, 0] (none).

inputs.name: step_m
inputs.description: Grid step. Default 0.025.

inputs.name: poses
inputs.description: Hand poses the shift must serve: [{pose: <pose json path or dict>, side?: 'right'|'left' (default the pose's own side), waypoints?: [[dx,dy,dz], ...] displacements from the grasp the same arm must also hold (a lift, the carry's goal)}].

inputs.name: sides
inputs.description: Arms whose reach counts for objects and points. Default both.

inputs.name: stations
inputs.description: Stations that move: both (default, keeping their separation) or one, e.g. ['right'] to bring only the right arm closer to a part the left arm's layout already serves.

inputs.name: out_xml
inputs.description: Default <scene dir>/scene_stations.xml.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: shift [dx, dy] of this call, stations_moved, station_shifts {side: [dx, dy]} (each station's total from the setup, carried over from a previous call whose scene this one moved further), scene (the written file), reached {object: n points reached of 5}, poses_held (per pose at the chosen shift: ok, residual, reason), before {...}, candidates [{shift, reached, poses_held, worst_mm}], note.

tools.name: place_egodex_camera_for_reach
tools.title: Place EgoDex camera for reach
tools.summary: Searches the EgoDex head camera's foot position (x, y) and yaw on the bench so every Stage 1 object, back-projected from its frame-0 mask through the camera, lands inside a station arm's reachable band with margin and clear of the robot at home; returns the cam_xy (and yaw) to give read_egodex_episode, re-frames camera.json / hands.npz / episode.json, and re-checks the result with the exact arm IK.
tools.description: An EgoDex episode is filmed by a head camera with no fixed place on our bench: read_egodex_episode stands its foot at cam_xy (default (0.019, 0.05)) and points the rig's y along the view. Moving that foot moves every object rigidly, and whether the arms reach them is not monotonic in the shift (fixing one object can push two others out), so this skill searches it instead of the agent. Each object's footprint comes from its mask (measure_mask_footprint: the contact line's centre pushed back by half the object's width along the view, radius half the width, height the apparent height or a given one) or is given in metres. The arms' reach is precomputed once as a field: for each station, the arm IK residual of a palm-down hand hover_m above the object's top (object_reach_check's palm-down test, the same solver) on a grid over the table, turned into a signed distance to the band's edge; this is stricter than object_reach_check, which also accepts a level hand beside the object, because a pick from above needs the palm-down reach. A candidate placement (dx, dy, yaw about the camera foot) scores each object by its centre's distance inside the better station's band; candidates that put an object off the table's near edge or under the robot's home pose are rejected. The choice is the smallest move whose worst object is at least margin_m inside the band, else the placement with the largest worst-object margin. The result is then checked with the exact solver (palm-down hover and fingers-in, as object_reach_check does) before and after. With an episode folder it writes camera.json, hands.npz and episode.json re-framed to the new foot and yaw (read_egodex_episode takes cam_xy but not a yaw), a top view of the band with the objects before and after, and the reach field for reuse. Object positions already staged in a scene move by the returned `transform` (apply_transform). Masks must be of objects standing on the table: a part on top of another (a cap on a bottle) back-projects far behind it and drags the camera; leave it out with exclude. Objects lying on the table (cords, ribbons, cloth: Stage 1's deformables) go in `flat`. The camera stays where it is when that placement already gives every object its margin and clearance; otherwise `reason` says what it violated.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives placement.json, reach_field.json, placement.png and, with episode_dir, the re-framed camera.json, hands.npz, episode.json.

inputs.name: episode_dir
inputs.description: read_egodex_episode's out_dir (camera.json, episode.json, hands.npz).

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json instead of episode_dir (its foot pos[:2] is the current cam_xy).

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Frame-0 object masks: a folder of <id>.png (hands*.png is the ignore mask) or {id: png}.

inputs.name: footprints

inputs.name: heights
inputs.description: {id: height m} overriding the apparent heights read off the masks.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these mask ids are placed: the Stage 1 objects the hands manipulate. Other masks in the folder (helper masks, static fixtures such as a dispenser the robot never touches) are ignored. Default every mask.

inputs.name: flat
inputs.description: Mask ids of objects lying flat on the table (Stage 1's deformable cords, ribbons, cloth): their footprint is the whole mask projected onto the table, 2 cm high, split into zones along its length (one per 12 cm, ids '<id>@k') that must each be reachable, instead of a standing object's contact line and apparent height (a lying ribbon across the frame would read as a 19 cm tall column).

inputs.name: exclude
inputs.description: Mask ids to leave out: parts that do not stand on the table (a cap on a bottle back-projects far behind it), extra masks of one object. A mask covering two or more others (a union) is skipped automatically, as is one hidden by the hands.

inputs.name: x_range / y_range

inputs.name: yaw_range_deg

inputs.name: xy_step_m / yaw_step_deg

inputs.name: hover_m

tools.name: plan_knot_moves
tools.title: Plan knot moves
tools.summary: Search the sequences of over-moves (pick a link, carry it just clear of the strands to a landing point, set it down) that tie a cable on the table into a knot (an overhand / trefoil by default), each move predicted follow-the-leader and checked by its crossing order, keeping only pinches and landings this bench's arms hold; returns `lay` plan entries for execute_subgoal_plan and the crossings each move must leave.
tools.description: A hand holding a rope end cannot pass it UNDER a strand on the table (a fingers-down pinch stands about 0.18 m tall, a lifted span leaves less than 0.1 m), but every crossing a knot needs can be made by laying rope OVER rope: an end that must go under a strand is tied by laying that strand over the end. The planner works on the cable's centreline at a state (a trajectory frame or the scene keyframe): the vertices of construct_rope's links, the segment lengths and, for every crossing, which strand is on top. A move picks one link, lifts it, carries it along a straight path or, for an end, through one via point (a straight rope's first loop, a tail swept round a crossing) and sets it down. Its prediction (common/knotplan.py) is follow-the-leader with friction: a segment the move stretches is pulled back to its length by moving both its ends (the least motion that keeps the rope inextensible), slack rope does not move, the rope bends round the hand with a radius, rope that moved lies on top of rope that did not, a tail slid through a crossing keeps its order there; pinning or overlapping moves are refused, and so is a move that would close a loop tighter than a thick rope lies (18 cm of rope, or 10 radii, between a crossing's two visits) or stack two crossings on one spot. Measured on an executed 40 cm carry of a 1.55 m, 3.2 cm cable end: pure follow-the-leader 0.20 m mean from the executed rope, this model 28 mm with the crossing order right. The knot is read from the predicted diagram exactly as rope_knot_check reads a real rope (knot.check; knot.quick_type screens), and each move's crossing ORDER is recorded (knot.crossing_order: 'a+ b- c+ a- b+ c-' is an overhand, a nested 'a b c c b a' a fold). An overhand is searched first as its own three over-moves (knotplan.overhand_search: a link near one end laid across the other strand, the loop; a link near the other end laid over the loop, its tail on top; a later piece of the loop laid over that tail; landings are tried just past every strand, however far, and on rings around the link), then, for anything else, by beam search: states ranked by the largest set of pairwise interleaved crossings (three only when they alternate over and under, as a trefoil's do), the free tail length at the ends and the cost (moves, carry length, a via, a change of hand, a pin, distance from the human's moves when `prefer` gives them); the beam keeps at most a third per crossing order. A pick must lie flat (no crossing on it or its neighbours, no raised link two away), nearly straight and 5 cm clear of other strands (the pads straddle the link; a pinch next to a raised link ran the thumb into it), a landing `land_clear_m` (3.5 cm) clear. Reach: one pinch per side (`pinch_poses`: a pinch with its `bar` record, best one proved by grasp stress tests such as optimize_grasp_pose family 'bar'; without one it is solved here: a level thumb-index pinch, the hand leaning in from its station, carried to a clear link the arm holds it at and optimized there with lift and hold tests: measured, a level unoptimized pinch lost a 0.86 kg cable at the start of the carry, the optimized one carried it) is carried rigidly to each candidate link, either way round, leaning 20 degrees along the link if needed, and the station's arm must hold it (6-DoF IK of the flange) at the pre-grasp, the grasp, lifted, at the via, over and at the landing and after the retreat. With `allow_pins` a move may have the OTHER hand pin a link 3-12 links away with its pinch (a grip `pin` entry before it, a `release` after): the drag stops there. Every plan found is re-screened with the arm checked against the scene (armhand.screen_poses) and simulated on the cable alone (common/ropesim.py: the cable's own asset on the table in the episode's contact physics, the link carried as the executor's lay carries it; 10-11 mm mean from executed ropes on the bench); plans whose simulated cable is not the knot are dropped and the simulated crossing orders become the entries' expect_order. Of the rest, the cheapest with the widest landing margin (the share of landings 2 cm around the planned one that still give the knot in the prediction) comes first. Execute the first move (its entries share an index), then call again from the executed trajectory (closed loop): a lay whose expect_order fails left other crossings than planned; drop expect_order to accept the rope as it lies and plan on from it. `moves` skips the search and plans the moves YOU give (from the video, or the rest of an earlier plan re-planned from the executed rope): each is predicted, screened for reach and simulated the same way, and the entries say what crossing order each must leave. When no full tie is found (or the given moves stop early) the result is `partial`: the furthest sequence, with its predicted orders, to execute and plan again from.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF the state belongs to (Stage 2 scene.xml, or an executed scene_physics.xml).

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos) to read the cable from; None: the scene keyframe.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame of the state. Default -1.

inputs.name: rope

inputs.name: goal

inputs.name: sides
inputs.description: Hands that may act. Default ['left', 'right'].

inputs.name: pinch_poses
inputs.description: {side: pose dict or JSON path}: a verified pinch on one of the cable's links with its `bar` {p0, p1, radius}.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 manifest: used to build a hand scene and solve the pinch for a side without one.

inputs.name: max_moves
inputs.description: Longest sequence searched. Default 3.

inputs.name: beam
inputs.description: States kept per depth. Default 8.

inputs.name: lift_m
inputs.description: Carry height of the picked link above the table in the prediction (the executor lifts it clear of the strands under its path). Default 0.05.

inputs.name: prefer
inputs.description: Per move, what the human did: {side, link (body name) or end ('first' | 'last': the B_first or B_last end), target [x, y]}; leaving it costs.

inputs.name: bounds
inputs.description: [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax] where rope may land. Default: the table top 3 cm in from its edges.

inputs.name: time_budget_s
