tools.name: plan_subgoal_keyframes
tools.title: Plan subgoal keyframes
tools.summary: Turn one Stage 1 subgoal (motion, hand, object, a verified hand pose, targets) into keyframes on the bench scene: reach, descend, close, lift, carry, set down, let go, joint sweeps, screw bites, pours, wrist presses that seat press-fit parts, two hands acting on two parts at once, one hand pinning a part while the other acts, two hands lifting one cable, a second object in the same hand, a cable link laid over or dragged across other strands; with the phases they form and what the simulation must show afterwards (`expect`).
tools.description: The planner starts from a state of the bench scene (its keyframe, or a frame of an executed trajectory so a subgoal continues from where the previous one really ended) and writes full-qpos keyframes with hold and transit durations. Motions follow Stage 1's vocabulary: grasp_lift (open hand to the pre-grasp along the pose's approach, down to the pose, close, lift), hold (the same without the lift), carry / place / insert (the carried object is moved rigidly with the wrist to target_pos, or onto / over another body; place adds a set-down, a let-go and a retreat), release, open_joint / close_joint / pull / push / press with a joint (the hand follows the moving part while the joint sweeps to its target: `hand_follows` 'rigid' = the wrist rides the part like a pinch that turns with a lid; 'level' = the wrist keeps its orientation and the pads of the grip fingers, or a world `follow_point`, ride the part, for fingertips that lift a lid from below or hook a drawer, since an arm cannot roll its hand 100 degrees with a lid and a level hand stays in reach), push / pull / press without a joint (a straight stroke from a pose along a direction), unscrew / screw (bites of bite_deg about the yaw joint with the lift joint following the pitch, opening and turning back between bites), pour / tilt (rotation about an axis through a pivot, by default the object's top over the target; `keep` leaves the object turned), cut (with scissors already held: the open blades are carried, keeping their orientation, so a rope's join (`join`: its equality name from Stage 2 cut_joins, or `cut_point`) comes in from beyond the tips and sits on the blades' bisector at `cut_s_frac` of the blade length, then the gripping fingers close the blades -- pressed `close_depth_rad` past the holding grip, or to explicit `finger_targets_close`; expect: severed + the scissors still in hand; without a join it just shuts them, expect joint_target closed. The rope parts only through the executor's cut rule), press_seat (a press-fit part pushed home by the WRIST: a palm or flat-finger pose on the part, the wrist reference driven travel_m past the contact while the wrist force cap on that axis is force_n, at most the library's 40 N; expect seated = the part's root at its seat height within seat_tol_m), the thin-part moves (common/nonprehensile.py; thin_grasp_diagnosis says which one a part needs): slide (upright fingertips behind the part push it along the table, mode 'push', or pads pressed on its top drag it with a force-capped wrist press, mode 'drag'; a slide_contact_pose; how far: `overhang_m` past the table's edge along `direction` (refused when its centre of mass would come within 12 mm of the edge), `distance_m` or `target_pos`; expect displaced, overhang, upright, released), edge_pinch / overhang_grasp (an overhang_pinch_pose: grip fingers under the overhanging edge deeper than the thumb on top, the hand coming down beside the part and in under it; refused, with the slide that fixes it, when the part overhangs less than the pose needs; then a grasp_lift), tilt_up / pivot (a press pose on the overhanging end: pressed down far enough that the far end rises `lift_m` about the table's edge, the press force capped at `force_n`; with `hold` (default) the hand keeps pressing into the next entry, where the other hand closes on the raised end (`hold` with an overhang_pinch_pose solved with raised true, grip 'sides': the raised end's side faces stand a pad radius above the table, under it there is room for fingers but not a palm), then this hand's `release` and the other hand's grasp_lift (no pose: it holds); expect end_raised. A side pinch of a raised end holds the part's weight only by the pads' torsional friction: on parts under about 1 cm it rarely passes the stress ladder, and overhang_pinch_pose says so; slide + edge_pinch is the move that holds), hook (a hook_grasp_pose: fingers down through an opening, the thumb on the wall's outside, straight down and lift; without the thumb it pulls along the pose's pull_dir while it rises), strip_pinch (a pinch across an arch of a flat strip: the thumb on the strip where it arches over something, a fingertip slid in under the arch, then lift; no pose tool holds one yet, so the pose comes from handle_pinch_pose or pose_from_points, stress-tested); each of them expects no finger more than 2 mm into the table (table_clear), regrasp, home, wait, and both (two hands on two different parts in one rollout: {motion: 'both', hands: {left: entry, right: entry}, sync: 'start'|'end'|'keyframes'}; each hand's entry is planned from the same start, the plans are merged on one time line, labels join the two phases 'left: ... | right: ...', expect = each hand's own plus untouched bystanders and hands_apart), pin (one hand steadies a part, or one link or end of a cable, while the OTHER hand acts: a press pose (flat_hand_pose pads down, push_pose_from_point, pin_pose) comes down on it and the WRIST presses force_n (default 20 N, never above the 40 N cap) from where the posed hand first meets it, with the wrist force on that axis capped at force_n; a grip pose (a pinch, a wrap) closes on it instead. The pin lasts through the following entries (the executor keeps the pinning hand's commands, press reference and force cap) until a release of that hand, and every one of those entries expects `pinned`: the part within tol_m (default 2 mm) and rot_tol_deg (3) of where the pin left it on EVERY frame, the pinning hand still on it; a pinning hand may only release, go home or wait), lift_together ({hands: {left: {object, pose, hand_scene}, right: {...}}, lift_m}: both hands close on two links of ONE object, a heavy cable, in the same keyframes and lift it by the same offsets, so a SPAN rises (the end can pass under it), the load is shared and the spacing kept; expect per hand rise, the link in hand (its pads on the link or its neighbours) and no_slip, plus `spacing` within spacing_tol_m, 2 cm). Each pose's approach_waypoints are visited; a hand with fewer waypoints waits open at its last point. t_reach / t_descend / t_close / t_grip may be set on lift_together or per hand; each synchronized stage uses the slower hand's duration. approach_controls reports the applied waypoint offsets and timings so repairs can be checked before physics. carry_together (both hands holding links of one object move by the same `offset`, or so their links' midpoint reaches `target_pos`; expect each link at its own target, in hand, the spacing kept), grasp_more (a hand that holds one object takes a second with its FREE fingers: the pose's grip_fingers, e.g. second_grasp_pose's middle, ring and pinky inside a cup, must not overlap the fingers holding the first, which keep their press; the hand carries the first object to the new pose and closes only the free fingers; `state.in_hand` records which fingers hold what, later carries, places and lifts move every object the hand holds and expect `also_in_hand`, and a release or place naming one of them opens only its fingers), lay (one over-move of a cable lying on the table, the moves plan_knot_moves plans to tie a knot: a pinch on one link, the link lifted just clear of the strands under its path (its underside 12 mm above the highest, at least 3 cm up, or `lift_m`), carried through `via` [[x, y], ...] to `target_pos` [x, y] (where the link's body origin lands), SET DOWN there, the fingers opened with the wrist still and the hand backed out along the pose's approach (a hand that moves while it opens drags the rope); expect the link at its target in x-y, released, at rest, `expect_order` (the crossing order the move must leave, knot.crossing_order's code, kinks dropped) and `knot` on the last move), drag (the same with the link held 8 mm off the table, so the rope slides: a pull-through or tuck of a tail along itself). Carry/place heights from on / over / into come from the bodies' real collision geometry (the support's highest surface under the carried part's footprint, studs included, and the part's own lowest point), never bounding spheres. A hand pose is a dict or a JSON path from the grasp skills; it may carry `finger_targets_open` (its own open shape, used instead of the 55% opening), `open_frac`, `press_depth_rad` (how far past the closed targets the grip fingers' flexion is driven; a negative value drives them that far toward extension instead, spreading what they hold open: scissor rings; the pose's finger_targets_squeezed still win where they flex deeper; a one-sided grip, no thumb opposing the grip fingers, presses by 4 mm of pad travel, and when that flexion would lift its pads off their surface, a fingers-down fingertip on a strip, the fingers stay as posed and the wrist presses 4 mm along the contact normal instead, and the hand reaches and descends with those grip fingers as posed rather than opened, since opening them pushes the pads into the surface) and `approach_waypoints` (world offsets from the pose visited between the pre-grasp and the pose, for a hook that goes over a bar and down behind it); the grip memory (closed, pressed and opened finger targets, what each hand holds) is carried in `state` between calls. The keyframes go to chain_subgoals / rollout_keyframes_physics; `expect` goes to subgoal_outcome_check. Labels are '<side>: <phase>' as Stage 4 wants them.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF (Stage 2 scene.xml).

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: {index, motion, side, object (body name), pose (dict|json path), lift_m, approach_m, t_reach / t_descend / t_close / t_grip (positive seconds for grasp_lift, hold, articulated grasp approaches and grip-mode pin; defaults 2.0 / 0.8 / 0.5 / 0.3, so contact can be slowed after impulse feedback), t_open / t_retreat (positive release seconds, defaults 0.5 / 0.8; duration_s scales their total unless either is explicitly set), settle_s (nonnegative stationary physics after release, default 0.5; included in the release outcome and recorded episode), target_pos|on|over|into, offset, height_m, via_height, into (a container body: the carried object's lowest point lands on the container's highest surface under the object's footprint at its centre -- the inner floor, or the sloped wall where the object reaches it -- + `offset`, `clearance_m` 3 mm), on (a body: the carried object's lowest point lands 2 mm above the highest collision surface of that body under the object's footprint, studs and rims included, measured from the real geometry, plus `offset` [dx, dy, dz] in metres (no compensation offset is needed); `height_m` is the travel height of the carry, not the landing height; `set_down_s` (default 1.0) controls a place's final descent time, `placement_force_n` bounds its contact and release effort (default at least 10 N, enough for object weight plus 5 N, always within the configured wrist limit); `carry_rise_m` how far a place lifts the wrist above the higher of itself and the target on the way, default 0.05; `lift_dir` [x, y, z] (a grasp_lift's way out: the part drawn out from under an overhang toward the operator while it rises) or `lift_path` [[dx, dy, dz], ...] (offsets from the grip visited in order, e.g. out first, then up; the rise expected is half the last offset's height); `via_rise_m` a carry's rise above the higher of its two ends on the way (instead of an absolute via_height); `arm_path: 'joint'` plans a carry's or place's transfer (not its set-down) in arm joint space, so an arm parked in a configuration that cannot follow the straight carry changes configuration in the air) | over (the same target without the set-down), target_pos (a world position of the carried object's root), target_euler_deg or turn {axis, deg} (a carried object's orientation at the destination; carries and places keep it by default), keep (a tilt that stays turned instead of returning to level), joint, target, hand_follows ('rigid'|'level'), follow_point, yaw_joint, lift_joint, angle_deg and pivot (rotate: the part is turned on the table about the vertical through pivot, default its centre, by pushing the pose's face around it; positive = counterclockwise from above), turns, pitch_m, bite_deg, regrasp_lift_m (an unscrew's open hand rises this far off the cap before turning back and comes down again after: fingers left on the cap's top edge drag it back; default 0.006), direction, distance_m, angle_deg, axis, pivot, release, duration_s, expect (overrides), with (a body, or a list of bodies, that rides along with the part this subgoal moves and is not a disturbed bystander: the toy inside the drawer being shut), open_frac / finger_targets_open / press_depth_rad / press_travel_m (grip settings that override the pose's own; a negative press_depth_rad extends the grip fingers from their closed targets instead of clamping, e.g. to spread scissor rings), reanchor ('full' default: the pose follows its part's whole motion since it was solved; 'yaw': translation and turn about the vertical only, for a cylinder that rolled about its own axis; 'translate'; 'none'), and for `cut`: join (a rope join's equality name) | cut_point [x, y, z], cut_s_frac (0 pivot .. 1 tip, default 0.5), approach_m (0.03), position (true), via [[x, y, z], ...], close_depth_rad (0.6) | finger_targets_close {joint: rad}, close_s (1.2), hold_s (0.6), joint (the scissors' hinge); for `press_seat`: pose (palm or flat fingers on the part), seat_depth_m | seat_z | seat_on + seat_offset_m, force_n (default and ceiling 40 N), travel_m (default: from where the hand first meets the part, seat depth + force/10000 N/m + 2 mm, at most 0.05), settle (default true: the pose is rocked up to 15 deg about the line across its fingers and shifted up to 12 mm in the press plane until its first contacts surround the part's centre, as a compliant hand settles; a point contact off the centre tips a press-fit part and jams it; expect.press.settle records it), direction ([0, 0, -1]), press_s (1.0), hold_s (0.8), approach_m (0.05), seat_tol_m (0.0015); for `both`: hands {left: entry, right: entry} (each a full entry with its own motion, object, pose ...), sync ('start' default | 'end' | 'keyframes'), hand_clearance_m (0.005); for `slide`: direction [dx, dy], overhang_m | distance_m | target_pos, mode ('push' | 'drag', default the pose's slide_mode), force_n (drag press, default 2.5x what the friction needs, at least 15 N, at most 40), extra_m (0.004); for `edge_pinch`: lift_m (0.08); for `tilt_up`: lift_m (the far end's rise, default a fingertip thickness + 8 mm), force_n, hold (true), edge_dir, press_point; for `hook`: lift_m, pull_m (a pure hook's pull, 0.012); for `strip_pinch`: lift_m (0.06); any of them max_table_pen_m (0.002); for `pin`: object (part, link or cable end), pose, mode ('press' | 'grip'; default press for a pose whose grip fingers have no thumb), force_n (20), direction (default minus the pose's contact normal), tol_m (0.002), rot_tol_deg (3), stay_tol_m (0.01: how far placing the pin may shift the part); for `lift_together`: hands {left: {object, pose, hand_scene, approach_m}, right: {...}}, lift_m (0.08), lift_dir | lift_path, spacing_tol_m (0.02), duration_s; for `carry_together`: offset [dx, dy, dz] | target_pos (the two held links' midpoint), via_rise_m, duration_s; for `lay` / `drag`: object (a cable link), pose (a pinch on it), target_pos [x, y], via, lift_m, expect_order, knot, approach_m (0.06), lift_s (0.6), carry_s (1.6), set_s (0.6), open_s (0.6), retreat_m (0.06); for `grasp_more`: object (the second object), pose (grip_fingers = the free fingers; finger_targets_open = their insertion shape), lift_m (0), approach_m (0.05)}.

inputs.description: Start state: a trajectory.npz (frame `frame`), a qpos list, or None for the scene keyframe.

inputs.name: fps

inputs.name: auto_via

tools.name: plate_edge_pinch_pose
tools.title: Plate edge pinch pose
tools.summary: Solve a thumb-versus-fingers pinch across the edge of a thin box geom (a lid, panel, board or cover) with the thumb pad on one face, the finger pads on the other and the palm and knuckles kept outside the edge.
tools.description: Reads the plate from a box geom in the hand scene: its thin axis is the face normal, `edge` names the local in-plane axis and sign of the edge to pinch, `s` the point along that edge (0..1) and `inset_m` how far in from the edge the pads sit. The thumb target lies on the `thumb_face` side ('up' = the face whose normal points up in the world, 'down' the other), the other grip fingers on the opposite face, spread along the edge by `finger_spread_m`; every target is a pad radius (+1 mm) off its face. Fingertip IK (the library's damped least squares with the collision-escape null-space task) is run from every wrist seed backed off along the outward edge normal (tilted up by `seed_up`), one seed at a time, and a solution is accepted only when its worst pad residual is under `max_residual_mm` and every hand link except the middle and distal phalanges stays at least `min_out_m` outside the edge, so the palm never lies over the plate, and the hand opened to `open_frac` at the pose (as planners open it before closing) keeps `open_floor_clear_m` off the floor, so a plate lying low over a table can still be reached. With `pivot` (a hinge line) the palm closest to the line wins, so turning the plate with the hand is mostly a rotation of the hand. With `finger_axis_max_deg` the fingers must point into the plate within that angle. Among accepted solutions the self-collision-free solutions (the visible finger meshes intersecting by at most 1 mm, closed and opened; the fingers with no target are folded and spread clear) win, then the smallest hand-object overlap, then the largest outside margin. The pose carries `approach` = the outward edge normal tilted up, so planners and stress tests bring the open hand in from the side of the edge rather than from above. Records surface points and outward normals separately from pad-centre targets, and anchors them to the materialized plate body so joint-following planners retain the actual contact reference. Assumes the plate is a box geom whose thinnest half-size is its thickness.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, ...} (hand_scene_from_recon output).

inputs.name: geom
inputs.description: Name (or unique name suffix) of the plate's box geom in the hand scene.

inputs.name: edge
inputs.description: Edge to pinch as a signed local in-plane axis: '+x', '-x', '+y', '-y' (or '+z'/'-z' when z is in-plane).

inputs.name: s
inputs.description: Position along the edge, 0..1 along the remaining in-plane local axis. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: inset_m
inputs.description: Distance of the pads in from the edge. Default 0.014.

inputs.name: thumb_face
inputs.description: 'up' or 'down': world-up face or the other one for the thumb. Default 'up'.

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Grip fingers, thumb first. Default ['thumb', 'index', 'middle'].

inputs.name: finger_spread_m
inputs.description: Spacing of the opposing fingers along the edge. Default 0.018.

inputs.name: min_out_m
inputs.description: Required clearance of palm and proximal links outside the edge. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_residual_mm
inputs.description: Worst accepted pad residual. Default 3.

inputs.name: seed_up
inputs.description: Upward tilt of the seed and approach direction (added to the unit edge normal). Default 0.3.

inputs.name: yaw_step_deg / pitches_deg / back_m / iters
inputs.description: Seed sweep density, seed back-off and IK iterations per seed (45, [-60,-30,0,30,60], 0.12, 200).

inputs.name: finger_axis_max_deg
inputs.description: Largest angle between the hand's finger axis (palm to middle knuckle) and the inward edge normal; e.g. 35 keeps the fingers pointing into the plate so the hand pivots with a hinged plate instead of swinging over it. Default None (any).

inputs.name: finger_dir
inputs.description: World direction the finger axis is compared with under finger_axis_max_deg (default: into the plate, minus the edge normal); use it to match the direction an arm can present the hand from.

inputs.name: pivot
inputs.description: {point, axis}: the hinge line the plate turns about (world). When given, solutions whose palm lies closest to that line win (after overlap), so the hand mostly rotates instead of swinging through an arc when the plate turns. Default None.

inputs.name: max_pivot_dist_m
inputs.description: With pivot: reject solutions whose palm is farther than this from the hinge line. Default None.

inputs.name: open_frac
inputs.description: Opening fraction the planners use before closing (H.open_targets). Default 0.55.

inputs.name: open_floor_clear_m
inputs.description: Clearance every hand geom of the OPENED hand may reach into the floor at the pose: the deepest hand-floor contact distance must be at least this (negative = penetration). Default -0.001.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the pose here.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_squeezed, grip_fingers, points (surface), normals, targets (pad centres), anchor, approach, press_depth_rad, residual_mm, worst_residual_mm, overlap_mm, outside_m, edge_point, n_seeds, n_accepted, self_overlap_mm, n_self_collision_free}.

tools.name: port_urdf_asset
tools.title: Port URDF asset
tools.summary: URDF (ArtiCraft, PartNet-Mobility, hand-written) to a metric MJCF asset: all geometry and colours, slide/hinge joints with limits, damping and friction, handle sites, and a joint/footprint info sheet.
tools.description: Parses the URDF with the standard library, finds the root link, and emits one MJCF body per link nested by the joint tree. Geometry comes from the <visual> elements (or <collision> with geometry='collision'); boxes, cylinders, spheres and meshes are kept with their origins and material colours, every length multiplied by `scale`; mesh files are copied beside the XML. prismatic -> slide and revolute/continuous -> hinge joints keep their axis and limits (scaled for slides) and get the damping, frictionloss and armature given; fixed joints merge the child into its parent's frame; a floating joint (below the root by construction) raises ValueError, since MuJoCo allows free joints only on top-level bodies: port that link as its own asset. URDF inertials are kept when present. The root body is fixed to the world by default or given a freejoint. A default contact class (condim 4, friction 0.8, solref 0.004) makes the surfaces graspable. The info sheet lists joints, per-link handle sites (the longest cylinder on each moving link), the carcass footprint and the drawer measurements (front face, bin interior, bin floor) when the link follows the ArtiCraft cabinet naming (front/bottom/side_*/back panels).

inputs.name: urdf
inputs.description: Path of the URDF file.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Directory for <name>.xml, meshes and <name>_info.json.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Asset/root body name. Default 'articulated'.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Multiplier applied to every length. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: joint_damping
inputs.description: Damping on every moving joint. Default 3.0 (a drawer slide).

inputs.name: joint_frictionloss
inputs.description: Dry friction on every moving joint. Default 0.4.

inputs.name: joint_armature
inputs.description: Armature on every moving joint. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: fixed_base
inputs.description: Root fixed to the world (True) or on a freejoint. Default True.

inputs.name: geometry
inputs.description: 'visual' (default) or 'collision': which URDF elements become geoms.

inputs.name: moving_mass
inputs.description: Override mass for every moving link (kg); None keeps the URDF inertials.

inputs.name: pos
inputs.description: World position of the root. Default [0, 0, 0].

inputs.name: yaw_deg
inputs.description: World yaw of the root. Default 0.

inputs.name: include_floor
inputs.description: Add a floor plane and lights. Default False.

outputs.name: xml
outputs.description: The MJCF asset.

outputs.name: info_json
outputs.description: <name>_info.json with everything below.

outputs.name: joints
outputs.description: name, type (slide|hinge), axis, range, parent, child, origin_m for every moving joint.

outputs.name: handles
outputs.description: link -> {site, centre_m, radius_m, length_m} for links with a cylinder handle.

outputs.name: drawers
outputs.description: link -> front/bin measurements when the ArtiCraft panel names are present.

outputs.name: footprint_m
outputs.description: Root link's box extents in x, y, z.

tools.name: pose_from_points
tools.title: Hand pose from fingertip points
tools.summary: Solve a dexterous-hand wrist pose and finger joints that put each named fingertip pad on its own labelled surface point, keeping the rest of the hand out of the object.
tools.description: The pose is solved, not searched. Each finger that is given a surface point and outward normal gets a target one pad thickness outside the surface; damped-least-squares inverse kinematics over the six virtual wrist DoF and every finger joint drives the fingertip sites onto those targets from a multi-start sweep of wrist seeds (back along the approach direction, over yaw and pitch). After a quarter of the iterations, interpenetration of the hand with the objects (the pads excepted: pressing the part is their job) and with the floor (pads included, and the hand's visible meshes against the floor plane, as the Stage 3 penetration audits judge it) is pushed out in the null space of the fingertip task; overlap_mm reports the same. Seeds are ranked by worst residual (to 2 mm), then deepest overlap (to 5 mm), then how squarely the palm faces the object. Fingers without a point are curled into the palm. The recorded approach (pads to wrist; the planner reaches in and backs out along it) is, for a one-sided contact (the normals agree: a press, a push, a cradle), the outward normal when the hand moved 3, 6 and 10 cm out along it stays clear of the scene and the floor (a fingertip pressing a strip comes down from above), else the pads-to-wrist direction in the surface plane (fingers slid under a lid); for an opposed grasp the pads-to-wrist direction. Works with any hand MJCF that follows the virtual-wrist and fingertip-site naming convention described in common/hand.py (Sharpa and Shadow hands included). Kinematic only: contact forces are measured afterwards by the grasp verifiers. The hand gets contact pairs only with the object geoms within its own span of the targets (pair_region 'auto') and the IK evaluates kinematics and collisions without the constraint solver, so a scene of many small parts (three magnetic rings, 75 geoms) costs well under a millisecond per iteration; `time_budget_s` caps the seed sweep and the result reports how many seeds ran.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects:[{name, xml, pos, yaw_deg}], floor} - the last object is the one being grasped

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: surface points for the fingers that must touch, keys from thumb/index/middle/ring/pinky

inputs.name: normals
inputs.description: outward surface normals at those points

inputs.name: standoff_m
inputs.description: fingertip-site standoff from the surface so the pad, not the site, rests on it (default: the pad radius plus 1 mm, read from the hand)

inputs.name: approach_dirs
inputs.description: directions the wrist seeds start back along (default: mean normal and +z)

inputs.name: palm_face_at
inputs.description: point the palm should face when ranking seeds (default: the target centroid)

inputs.name: parallel_fingers
inputs.description: pin abduction to zero and the thumb to its opposition convention

inputs.name: curl_free
inputs.description: flexion fraction for fingers without a point (0 leaves them open)

inputs.name: iters, yaw_step_deg, pitches_deg, seed_back_m
inputs.description: IK budget and seed sweep density

inputs.name: seeds
inputs.description: explicit wrist seeds [(pos, euler), ...] instead of the sweep (a family of orientations the arm can reach, from arm_workspace_map)

inputs.name: fix_orientation
inputs.description: keep each seed's wrist orientation and solve only the wrist position and the fingers (fingers that must stay level under a thin lid). Default false

inputs.name: clear_overlap
inputs.description: for a one-sided contact, back the hand out along the surface normal until the fingers (pads included) just touch, so a contact made with the back of the fingers (palm down under a lid) is placed on the finger's back; the pose records cleared_m and contact_side. Default true

inputs.name: time_budget_s
inputs.description: stop trying further wrist seeds after this many seconds (scene build included) and return the best pose so far with a note; progress {seeds_tried, seeds_total, elapsed_s} is in the result either way. Default None (every seed)

inputs.name: pair_region
inputs.description: which object geoms get hand contact pairs: 'auto' (default) those within the hand's own span of the target points (nothing the posed hand can reach is left out; a scene of many small parts no longer pays for every pair), a {center | points, radius_m} region, or None for every object geom

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: optional file to write the pose to

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler (intrinsic XYZ), finger_targets {joint: rad}, grip_fingers, approach (unit, pads to wrist: for a one-sided contact the outward surface normal when the hand can back out along it, else the pads-to-wrist direction in the surface plane), approach_kind (normal | along_surface | pad_to_wrist), points, normals, targets, residual_mm per finger, worst_residual_mm, overlap_mm (deepest overlap: non-pad geometry in the objects, any geometry or visible mesh in the floor), palm_facing, standoff_m, progress {seeds_tried, seeds_total, elapsed_s, stopped}, note (when the time budget cut the seed sweep short)}; the input every grasp verifier takes

tools.name: preview_keyframes
tools.title: Preview keyframes
tools.summary: Render a subgoal's planned keyframes (no physics) as one labelled sheet from a chosen camera and list where the plan itself drives a hand through the other hand or through an object it is not handling, in seconds.

Takes the keyframes of plan_subgoal_keyframes (or its json), sets the scene to each keyframe's qpos, renders it from a named scene camera or a free camera looking at the handled object, tiles the frames with their phase labels, and runs the plan collision sweep on the interpolated reference (hand-hand and hand-vs-bystander interpenetration deeper than 4 mm, with frame and geom names). Use it to check an approach, a swing or a carry visually before spending a physics rollout, and to see why a rollout reported plan_collision.

inputs.name: allowed_bodies

inputs.name: width

Works at the initial state or at any qpos. The bounds come from the geoms' bounding radii, so they are quick and slightly loose.

tools.name: probe_video

tools.name: push_pose_from_point
tools.title: Push pose from a surface point
tools.summary: Construct a hand pose whose extended finger points straight into a surface at a given point, for pushing an object with the fingertip.
tools.description: A push is not a grasp: the finger's direction is part of the intent. The posture is fixed (one finger extended, the others curled, thumb tucked), the wrist rotation is constructed so the finger axis (knuckle site to tip site) points along minus the surface normal, the wrist position follows analytically so the tip site lands one pad thickness outside the point, and the single remaining freedom, roll about the finger axis, is swept in 10 degree steps and ranked by non-pad interpenetration with the scene and then by knuckles-up (palm normal downward). Nothing is searched iteratively, so the result is deterministic and takes well under a second.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects:[{name, xml, pos, yaw_deg}], floor}

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: surface point to push at

inputs.name: normal
inputs.description: outward surface normal at the point; the finger will point along -normal

inputs.name: finger
inputs.description: pushing finger (default index); its axis runs from the knuckle site (or the tip link's parent joint) to the tip site

inputs.name: standoff_m
inputs.description: tip-site standoff from the surface (default 0.015)

inputs.name: posture
inputs.description: override of the fixed posture as fractions of joint range (None = joint at 0)

inputs.name: roll_step_deg
inputs.description: roll sweep step about the finger axis (default 10)

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: {side, pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers:[finger], residual_mm, overlap_mm, palm_facing (down-facing cosine), finger_alignment (cosine of finger axis with -normal)}

tools.name: rank_grasps_q1
tools.title: Rank grasps by Ferrari-Canny Q1
tools.summary: Close each candidate grasp on the object in physics, read the simulator's contact set, and rank the candidates by the Ferrari-Canny Q1 force-closure quality and a press-versus-grip ratio.
tools.description: For every pose the hand is placed open, the fingers are driven to the closed (or squeezed) targets and the scene settles; the hand-object contacts (positions, normals, forces, friction) are read from MuJoCo and turned into a 6-D wrench hull with 8-edge friction cones, torques normalised by the object's radius. Q1 is the radius of the largest origin-centred ball inside that hull: Q1 > 0 means force closure. press_frac = |sum F| / sum |F| tells a press (all fingers pushing the same way, ~1) from a grip (~0). Candidates are sorted by Q1 descending, then press_frac ascending, then number of contacts. Static and cheap, so it is the right first filter before the driven stress tests; it does not replace them, because a servo-held grasp can have force closure at rest and still slip under motion.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, grasp_body?}

inputs.name: poses
inputs.description: candidates with pos, euler, finger_targets (and optionally finger_targets_squeezed)

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: settle time after closing (default 0.5)

inputs.name: use_squeezed
inputs.description: close to finger_targets_squeezed when present (default True)

inputs.name: min_force_N
inputs.description: ignore contacts weaker than this (default 0.05)

outputs.name: ranked
outputs.description: [{index, q1, press_frac, n_contacts, fingers, total_force_N, force_closure}] best first

outputs.name: best
outputs.description: index of the best candidate with force closure

tools.name: reachable_contact_search
tools.title: Reachable contact search
tools.summary: Samples candidate contact points on a part (a face of a box geom, or points you give), builds a flat-hand pose at each, turns it for reach along the planned motion, and ranks the reachable ones by a criterion such as the farthest from a hinge: the answer to 'where can the arm act on this part'.
tools.description: Reach is a property of where the contact is, not only of how the hand is turned. A lid lifted near its hinge needs a force the base cannot take, farther out the arm cannot reach; the right contact is the farthest point the arm still reaches. This skill takes the bench scene, the side, the hand scene and either explicit `candidates` [{point, normal, finger_dir}] or a `face` of a box geom (`geom`, `face` in +x/-x/+y/-y/+z/-z, `n` points along each edge, `inset_m` from the edges) sampled in world coordinates with the outward normal. For every candidate it builds `flat_hand_pose` (contact 'pad' or 'back', `pitch_deg`, `fingers`, `thumb`), runs `optimize_pose_for_reach` with the given `sweep` (a joint motion the hand must follow, rigid or level) and `waypoints`, and records the worst residual, the overlap and the score: `score` is 'far_from' or 'near' a `ref_point` (a hinge, the base), or 'residual'. Reachable candidates (within `pos_tol_m`, no overlap beyond `max_overlap_m`) come first, ranked by the score; the best pose is written to `out_json`. The physics is still to be proved by executing the subgoal: this finds where a contact can be made, not whether it moves the part. Automatic finger directions cover several headings in the surface plane around the actual configured station. A bounded search visits distinct contact locations before extra headings/modes at the same point and reports location coverage separately from the number of pose variants evaluated. For a mechanism, sweep.hand_follows='auto' compares rigid and level following independently and returns the chosen mode in best.hand_follows; use that explicit mode in the plan and verify physical contact throughout execution. For carried objects, include later translation and orientation targets in waypoints before choosing an initial grasp. Sampled contacts use the hand scene's recorded bench_state by default; after parts move, rebuild the hand scene from the episode so far. An explicit inconsistent object state is rejected. co_sides must already contact the moving part in that state, not be parked at home or holding its stationary base. Absence of a witness proves neither unreachable geometry nor an upstream reconstruction error. For a joint sweep, contact_drive reports whether pressure at the sampled surface can produce the requested signed joint effort, including a conservative bound on tangential and angular friction. Reachable contacts that drive by pressure rank before contacts requiring friction, and those before contacts that cannot drive. This assumes unilateral contact on that face; it does not establish actual contact, sufficient force, or passive motion. Opposing-thumb grasps are not rejected from a single face normal. require_drive explicitly assumes the sampled face is the only contact force source (no incidental thumb, edge or other contacts) and excludes candidates whose unilateral wrench cone cannot drive, while retaining them in the diagnostic rows.

inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right'.

inputs.name: hand_scene

inputs.description: [{point, normal, finger_dir}] explicit contacts (world).

inputs.name: n

inputs.name: inset_m
inputs.description: Keep this far from the face's edges. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: finger_dir
inputs.description: Explicit world finger direction. If absent, search heading_samples headings around the actual station-to-contact projection in the face plane.

inputs.name: heading_samples
inputs.description: Automatic in-plane finger headings. Default 4 (90-degree spacing, refined by range_deg). Explicit finger_dir on a candidate is respected without extra headings.

inputs.name: contact
inputs.description: 'pad' or 'back' for flat_hand_pose. Default 'back'.

inputs.name: pitch_deg
inputs.description: flat_hand_pose pitch. Default 10.

inputs.name: fingers

inputs.name: thumb

inputs.description: Total search budget (300 seconds), shared across sampled contacts. Finishes the current candidate's complete path before returning partial results. None permits an unbounded search. Absence of a witness is inconclusive.

inputs.name: require_drive
inputs.description: Default False. Opt into the assumption that ONLY the recorded grip-finger contacts on the sampled face supply force, excluding incidental thumb/edge contacts: exclude poses whose unilateral wrench cone cannot drive. Reach remains separately reported. Does not reject declared opposing-thumb contacts; execution is still required.

tools.name: read_egodex_episode
tools.title: Read EgoDex episode
tools.summary: Opens an EgoDex episode (hdf5 + mp4): writes the first frame (or a strided set), the head camera as camera.json in the rig frame via the table plane found from the fingertip heights, the task text, and the 2D hand joints per frame.
tools.description: EgoDex stores the camera intrinsics (camera/intrinsic), the per-frame camera pose and 3D skeleton (transforms/*, ARKit world, gravity-aligned y-up) and the task description in the file attributes. The table plane is the horizontal plane through the low percentile of all fingertip heights over the episode minus a pad (fingertips touch the table during every task); the rig frame is built from it: z up, y the chosen frame's optical axis projected onto the plane, x = y cross z, origin so that the camera's foot lands at `cam_xy` (default (0.019, 0.05): the robot mounts 5 cm behind the camera foot, since a head camera 0.3 to 0.4 m up with a 72 degree lens would otherwise see the parked robot hands in the middle of the frame). Writes frame%05d.jpg files, camera.json (fx, fy, cx, cy, fovy_deg, pos, quat_wxyz, R_cv in the rig frame; the frame's own pose), episode.json (task, description, objects named by the dataset, n_frames, fps, table height, rig transform world<-rig, fingertip pixels at the frame) and hands.npz (every joint's 3D rig position and 2D pixel per frame).

inputs.name: hdf5
inputs.description: The episode's .hdf5.

inputs.name: mp4
inputs.description: The episode's .mp4; default: same stem as the hdf5.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives frames, camera.json, episode.json, hands.npz.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: The frame whose camera pose defines the rig frame and camera.json. Default 0.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Also write every k-th frame; 0 writes only `frame`. Default 0.

inputs.name: cam_xy
inputs.description: Camera foot in the rig frame. Default [0.019, 0.05].

inputs.name: tip_percentile
inputs.description: Percentile of fingertip heights taken as the tabletop. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: tip_pad_m
inputs.description: Fingertip centre height above the surface when touching. Default 0.008.

outputs.name: frames
outputs.description: Written frame files (the chosen frame first).

outputs.name: camera
outputs.description: camera.json content in the rig frame.

outputs.name: episode
outputs.description: task, description, dataset objects, n_frames, fps, width, height, table_height_world, rig {R_world_rig, origin_world}, fingertips_px at the frame, hands_npz.

tools.name: reconstruct_object_meshes
tools.title: Reconstruct object meshes
tools.summary: SAM 3D Objects on the best frame of each tracked object: a textured .glb mesh, its predicted pose, and the anchor frame used.
tools.description: A rigid object needs one good reconstruction, not one per frame. For each label the anchor frame is chosen by solidity x temporal mask consistency x relative area, penalising overlap with the hands, so a frame where the object is whole, still and unoccluded wins. SAM 3D Objects then reconstructs the masked crop into a textured mesh with mesh post-processing and texture baking, and the object-to-camera similarity it predicts is saved beside it. Requires the gated SAM 3D Objects checkpoints.

inputs.description: Folder of frame%05d.jpg.

inputs.name: masks_dir
inputs.description: Palette label maps frame%05d.png.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives <name>.glb, <name>_pose.json, <name>_anchor.png, <name>_mask.png.

inputs.name: sam3d_repo

inputs.name: anchor_frame
inputs.description: Force this frame instead of picking one.

inputs.name: seed, min_area
inputs.description: Sampling seed (42) and minimum mask area in pixels (200).

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: per object: anchor frame, glb path, pose json path, mask area.

tools.name: refit_to_real_rig
tools.title: Refit to real rig
tools.summary: Flange pose path -> smooth, rate-limited, table-safe joint trajectory for a real arm, with branch-reset handling.
tools.description: Fits the arm chain above flange_body to the given pose path with a damped least squares IK tuned for real arms (per-axis rotation weights with the roll axis soft, trust-region warm starts, position primary). A frame whose warm solution is more than 30 mm or 20 degrees off triggers a multi-start search; a better branch is adopted and blended over the previous 12 frames. The joint trajectory is then smoothed with a zero-phase Savitzky-Golay filter, clamped to rate_max_deg_s (180 deg/s), and checked by forward kinematics against the table: frames where the flange (or the given hand point) falls below table_top_z + floor_margin are raised and re-solved. Optionally the path is first transformed by a rigid offset (sim-to-real base registration) and clamped above the table. Writes an npz with the joint trajectory, residuals and timestamps when out_path is given.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene containing the arm (the real arm's kinematics and limits).

inputs.name: flange_body
inputs.description: Body whose pose the path describes.

inputs.name: positions, rotations
inputs.description: Target pose path.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frame rate of the path.

inputs.name: table_top_z, floor_margin_m
inputs.description: Table safety floor for the flange or hand point. Default margin 0.01.

inputs.name: hand_point
inputs.description: Lowest point of the hand in the flange frame to keep above the floor.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Rigid transform applied to the path first.

inputs.name: rate_max_deg_s
inputs.description: Controller joint-rate ceiling. Default 180.

inputs.name: joint_ranges_deg
inputs.description: Real stops tighter than the model's.

inputs.name: seed_q
inputs.description: Starting posture for the first frame.

inputs.name: out_path
inputs.description: Write qpos, residuals, time stamps.

inputs.name: smooth_window
inputs.description: Default 9.

inputs.name: max_floor_passes
inputs.description: Default 3.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: qpos [T, n], joint_names, residual {pos_mm max/p95, tilt_deg max, roll_deg max}, resets (frames), floor_fixes (frames raised), max_rate_deg_s, out_path.

tools.name: register_camera_hand_overlay
tools.title: Register camera by hand overlay
tools.summary: Estimates the video camera's pitch, yaw, roll, height and foot position in the setup's rig frame by rendering the robot hands at the home keyframe through candidate cameras and maximising their overlap with the human hand masks, optionally held to a table-plane (gravity + depth) prior; writes camera.json in register_table_camera's format and a check image.
tools.description: The setup's home keyframe is the pose every demonstration starts from, so the human hands in a frame where they rest at the start and the robot hands at home should cover the same pixels. The skill renders the robot hands' visible meshes (no arm: at home it is outside the ego view) as projected convex hulls, which needs no OpenGL, and scores a camera by 1 - IoU with the human hand mask plus a symmetric chamfer term that keeps the score informative when the silhouettes do not overlap yet. Human pixels on the elbow side of each robot hand's wrist are ignored, because a hand-and-arm mask (SAM 3's 'hand' prompt returns the forearm too) has no robot counterpart. The search is a coarse grid over yaw and the foot position (x, y) at the initial pitch, roll and height, then Nelder-Mead over all six numbers from the best grid cells, inside a box around the initial guess. A table prior (pitch, roll from gravity; height from a depth plane: estimate_gravity, fit_camera_to_table_plane) adds a Gaussian penalty with the given sigmas. Accuracy depends on how close the demonstrator's hands are to the robot's home pose. With masks that match it (the home hands rendered through a known camera) the estimate lands within 1-3 degrees and 1-3 cm, and pixels on the table move by 0.4-1.3 cm (median) with a table prior, 1-5 cm without; the residual is a real ambiguity, not the optimiser: both hands lie at about one depth, so yaw trades against the sideways foot position and pitch against height at almost the same overlap. On the paper's bench footage the resting hands sit about 10 cm inward, 8 cm forward and on the cloth (10 cm below the home hands); the overlap then stays below IoU 0.6 and the estimate is worse than a reasonable initial guess. So the result is gated: below min_iou (0.7) the overlay is REJECTED, camera.json is the initial guess with the prior's pitch, roll and height, and the rejected estimate is kept for inspection. hand_pose='on_table' with fit_spread=True models hands resting on the cloth and spread differently from home. Writes camera.json (width, height, fx, fy, cx, cy, fovy_deg, pos, quat_wxyz, R_cv, pitch_deg, yaw_deg, height_above_table_m, plus source, accepted, the overlap and the search settings) and camera_check.png (table grid, human mask outline in red, robot hands at the written camera in blue).

inputs.name: hand_mask

inputs.name: table_prior

tools.name: reinforcement_learning_tracking
tools.title: Reinforcement-learning residual tracking
tools.summary: Stage 3 method module (the third after the agent): a residual tracking policy is trained with proximal policy optimization on the bench's own rigid runtime (CPU MuJoCo, the executor's servo physics) to keep every part the reference moves on its reference pose (position and orientation, so in-hand rotations count), episodes starting where the reference first loses the object and moving earlier (a reset curriculum); the trained policy's deterministic rollout over the whole episode is written as a tracking reference and its track_reference plan.
tools.description: Residual reinforcement learning for demonstration tracking (as in ManipTrans, Li et al. 2025, and DexMachina, Mandi et al. 2025: a policy that corrects a kinematic reference under contact physics), with a reset curriculum from the demonstration's own states (DemoStart, Bauza et al. 2024), trained in this library's numpy PPO (common/ppo.py: Gaussian tanh-MLP policy and value function, clipped surrogate, GAE, Adam, observation normalization). Reference: `reference` (an earlier method's tracking reference), else the agent's best physical attempt (tracking.reference_from_attempt); it is put on the bench as the executor will run it (tracking.BenchTracker). Action every act_s: per acting station six arm-joint offsets and one grip offset on the reference's commands (scaled by action_scale_arm_rad / action_scale_grip_rad), interpolated linearly from the previous action across the interval. Observation: the episode phase, every tracked part's position error, rotation error (rotation vector) and velocity, every tracked joint's error, the previous action. Reward per interval: the mean over its frames of exp(-50 x position error) + 0.5 x exp(-3 x rotation error) per part (and exp(-10 x joint error) per joint), minus the action's size, hand penetration past 3 mm and hand-object force past 12 N (the gates' contact spike audit allows 15 N); an episode ends with -2 when a part is more than 10 cm off its reference. Episodes of episode_s start from the reference's own integration states at action boundaries, first just before the frame where the unrefined rollout first loses a part (2 cm / 20 deg) and widening toward the start as the policy succeeds. Every eval_every iterations the deterministic policy runs the whole episode from the start; the best such rollout (by its worst mean and end error) is kept, and written only when its whole-episode cost beats the unrefined reference's (`improved`), as reference.npz, plan.json (track_reference entries) and report.json with the training curve. The harness executes the plan with execute_subgoal_plan, packages it and runs finish's verifiers, as for an agent's plan; the agent may call it the same way. CPU only, in `workers` processes. Limits: a residual policy corrects a reference whose contacts are roughly right; training time grows with the episode's length (max_minutes ends training with the best policy so far).

tools.name: sampling_mpc_refinement
tools.title: Sampling-based MPC refinement
tools.summary: Stage 3 method module (the second after the agent): predictive-sampling model-predictive control on the bench's own rigid runtime (CPU MuJoCo, the arms and hands, the executor's servo physics) re-plans a residual on a tracking reference every replan_s: candidate residuals over a short horizon are rolled out in parallel from the current physics state, scored by how closely every part the reference moves follows it (position and orientation, so in-hand turns count), and the best is executed; writes the refined tracking reference and its track_reference plan.
tools.description: Predictive sampling (Howell et al., 'Predictive Sampling: Real-time Behaviour Synthesis with MuJoCo', 2022; the planner MuJoCo MPC runs) on the same simulator the executor and the gates use, so there is no gap between the model the plan is optimized in and the one it is judged in. Reference: `reference` (an earlier method's tracking reference), else the agent's best physical attempt in the workspace (tracking.reference_from_attempt). It is put on the bench as the executor will run it (tracking.BenchTracker: from the Stage 2 home state, the joint-rate ceilings, the arms coupled with the executor's settings and arm planner). The decision variable is a residual on the commands, a piecewise-linear spline with a knot every knot_s: per acting station six arm-joint offsets (which move the hand rigidly) and one grip offset (added to every flexion joint of that hand's fingers, clipped to their ranges). At every replan_s the knots inside the horizon are sampled around the current nominal (samples - 1 Gaussian perturbations plus the nominal itself), each candidate is rolled out over horizon_s from the complete integration state the previous step left (rigid_robot.servo_rollout, in `workers` processes), and scored per frame by 10 x position error (m) + 0.5 x rotation error (rad) of every free part the reference moves, 2 x the error of every articulated joint it moves, hand penetration past 3 mm, hand-object force past 12 N (the gates' contact spike audit allows 15 N) and the residual's size; the best candidate's first replan_s is executed and becomes the start of the next step. The refined commands are rolled out once from the start and compared with the unrefined ones by the same cost over the whole episode; the better of the two is written (`improved` says which) as reference.npz, the track_reference plan.json and report.json. The harness executes the plan with execute_subgoal_plan, packages it and runs finish's verifiers, as for an agent's plan; the agent may call it the same way. CPU only. Limits: the residual corrects a reference whose contacts are roughly right (it does not invent a new grasp), and the work grows with the reference's length (max_minutes stops refining; the rest of the episode then keeps the reference's own commands).

tools.name: search_subgoal_variants
tools.title: Search subgoal variants
tools.summary: From an execution whose earlier subgoals passed, run many variants of the failing subgoal's parameters as parallel physical trials (Latin hypercube, then cross-entropy refits on the best), rank them on subgoals passed, the Stage 1 goals and the measured shortfall of the failed checks; when a variant passes, continue the search on the next failing subgoal from its state (backtracking to another passing variant if that one dead-ends). Returns the best plan and its execution folder to re-execute and package.
tools.description: Each trial is an ordinary execute_subgoal_plan run with resume=True from a copy of the prefix execution, restarting at the target subgoal (from_subgoal), so the subgoals before it are not simulated again and everything after it is run as planned until the next failure. A variant changes only named keys of the target plan entry: `knobs` maps a key (for a two-hand entry 'left.<key>' / 'right.<key>') to [lo, hi] (absolute value), {low: [...], high: [...]} (absolute vector), {delta_low: [...], delta_high: [...], default: [...]} (added to the entry's value, e.g. a place offset; `pose_shift_m` with a delta translates the entry's grasp pose file, so the hand lands elsewhere on the part), {scale: [lo, hi], default: x} (multiplies the entry's value, e.g. duration_s) or {choices: [...]} (e.g. arm_path [null, 'joint'], or alternative pose files). Without knobs they are proposed from the failed checks and the motion (the grasp pose's position, timing and press depth for rise/in_hand/pads_touching/no_slip; place offset, set-down time, contact force and release timing for at_target/at_rest/released/upright; approach and carry heights and a joint-space transfer for penetration and reach; durations, travel and force for joints, slides and seats); when no variant of them passes, a second level searches what led into the failure together with them: the destination of the carry before it and the descent, closing time and press of the grasp that holds the same object (trials restart at that grasp, since how the object sits in the hand decides where it lands). The first round is a Latin hypercube of `population` variants; each further round samples a Gaussian (categoricals: frequencies) refitted to the `elite` best, with a variance floor. A trial is ranked by (plan subgoals passed, Stage 1 goals met when every subgoal passed and scene_semantic_json is given, fewer failed checks, smaller normalized shortfall: e.g. target error / 5 mm, slip / 5 mm, penetration / 1 mm, missing rise / 10 mm). With dig=true, once a variant passes the target, the next failing subgoal of the best such variant becomes the target (its knobs proposed from its own failure), up to max_depth subgoals; when a deeper target finds no passing variant, the search backtracks once to the next passing variant of the level above. Budgets: max_evals trials, max_minutes wall time, eval_timeout_s per trial, `workers` trials at a time. Gates are not changed or relaxed: every trial is judged by the executor's own checks, and the result is a candidate: re-execute the best plan with execute_subgoal_plan (resume=True in the returned folder reuses its segments) so the harness records the execution, then package_stage3_episode and finish.

tools.name: seat_grasp_for_lift
tools.title: Seat a grasp for lifting
tools.summary: Search the small seat a pose solved exactly at contact needs to lift: the wrist moved 0-4 mm deeper along its approach, with the clamp depth and pre-opening, judged by the approach-close-lift rollout in the hand scene and by the hand's visible overlap with the part and the table.
tools.description: Contact solvers (pose_from_points, generate_flat_pinches, handle_pinch_pose) put the pads exactly on the surface. The bench arm holds the hand where it is commanded (the hand scenes carry the hand's weight the same way), so a pinch whose pads only touch may close without wedging the part, and a seat a few millimetres deeper along the approach is worth trying before the pose is given up. With realistic pad contact (2 cm twisting, 1 mm rolling patches) a seat rarely decides it (a tripod on a thin pen lying on a table can lift at no seat, the closing thumb rolling the pen out), so every configuration is reported with why it failed. For each seat depth (shallowest first) and each clamp depth / pre-opening of the ladder, the hand is placed at the seated pose, its static overlap is measured (collision and visible meshes, pads included: the visible overlap with the part and the table must stay within max_visible_mm), and the shared stress rollout runs approach, close and lift. The first configuration that lifts wins: its pose is returned with `pos` moved, `seat_m`, `press_depth_rad` and `open_frac` written, ready for the executor. Every tried configuration is reported. Assumes the pose's approach vector points away from the part (the grasp tools' convention).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output) holding the part as it is now.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Hand pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers, approach, ...} or its json.

inputs.name: seats_mm
inputs.description: Seat depths along the approach, shallowest first. Default [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].

inputs.name: press_depths
inputs.description: Clamp depths (rad past touch). Default [the pose's own or 0.12, 0.25].

inputs.name: open_fracs
inputs.description: Pre-openings. Default [the pose's own or 0.2].

inputs.name: lift_heights_m
inputs.description: Commanded lifts. Default [0.04, 0.08].

inputs.name: max_visible_mm
inputs.description: Largest visible overlap of the seated hand with the part or the table. Default 4.0.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the seated pose here.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: ok, pose (seated; None when nothing lifts), seat_m, press_depth_rad, open_frac, lift_mm [per commanded height], tried [{seat_mm, press_depth_rad, open_frac, visible_mm, ok, first_fail, lift_mm}].

tools.name: second_grasp_pose
tools.title: Second grasp pose (finger allocation)
tools.summary: Pose for taking a SECOND object with the free fingers of a hand that already holds one (the first cup between thumb and index, the second on middle, ring and pinky dipped inside it and spread), searched with the first object riding the hand, so the two grasps are designed together; the input of a `grasp_more` plan entry.
tools.description: The two grasps of one hand cannot be chosen apart: the first object rides the hand to the second, so where the first grasp put it decides whether the free fingers can reach the second at all (a cup pinched between thumb and index hangs exactly where the other three fingers would dip). Given the first grasp (`first_pose`, one pose or a list of candidates: then the PAIRS are ranked; or its pad points, and the first grasp is designed in the second's wrist family) and the second object, the free fingers are the fingers the first pose's grip_fingers leave (or `free_fingers`). Family 'inside' (an open container: a cup, a bowl, a box): the free fingers go in together through the mouth, straight, and spread by their abduction joints against the inner wall (abduction is the grip: curling three fingers inside a cup retracts the tips and presses one wall, tipping it). The search turns the hand so the free fingers point into the mouth (straight down, and tilted by `tilts_deg` toward 8 directions) at every `yaw_step_deg` about the free fingers' axis, and puts their tip centroid `depth_m` below the rim on the mouth's axis. Every candidate is judged with the first object carried rigidly from its grasp (lifted lift1_m) to the new wrist pose: the first object must clear the second, the table and every bystander by clear_m and tilt at most max_first_tilt_deg; the hand (insertion shape: the spreading fingers turned a third of the way inward) must clear the second object, the table and the bystanders by clear_m, also along the approach (approach_m back along the free fingers' axis, the first object riding along); sweeping the abduction from the insertion shape to the spread, at least two free fingers must meet the inner wall, from opposite sides (the spread target lies past the wall, so the servos press it). With bench_scene the surviving poses are screened for the station's arm down the clearance ranking, in batches, until top_k pass. Ranked by the smallest clearance (larger first), then the first object's tilt. The pose carries finger_targets (the free fingers spread, the held fingers as the first grasp clamps them), finger_targets_open (the free fingers together: the insertion shape), grip_fingers = the free fingers, press_depth_rad 0 (the spread presses; no flexion clamp), the approach, the first grasp it was designed with (`first_pose_index`) and its numbers. By default, a bounded multi_object_hold_test search verifies the ranked pairs and modest first-grip clamp variations, preserving actuator/contact limits. Every returned candidate includes its exact first_pose. Full rigid-arm episode verification is still required.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon) holding both objects, as they lie before the first grasp.

inputs.name: first_pose
inputs.description: The first grasp (pose dict or JSON path), or a list of candidates.

inputs.name: first_object
inputs.description: Body of the first object (the one the first pose grasps).

inputs.name: first_points, first_normals
inputs.description: With first_pose None: the first grasp's pad points and outward normals ({thumb: [x, y, z], index: ...}); the first grasp is then DESIGNED with the second: pose_from_points with the wrist held in the family the second grasp uses (the free fingers, straight, pointing down or tilted 25 deg), every first_yaw_step_deg (30) about the vertical, kept only when the executor's clamp presses every pad into its surface.

inputs.name: second_object
inputs.description: Body of the second object.

inputs.name: free_fingers
inputs.description: Fingers for the second grasp (default: those the first pose's grip_fingers leave).

inputs.name: family
inputs.description: 'inside' (default; the only family so far).

inputs.name: depth_m
inputs.description: How far below the rim the free fingertips go. Default 0.025.

inputs.name: lift1_m
inputs.description: The first object's lift before the transfer (it rides at this height). Default 0.04.

inputs.name: yaw_step_deg
inputs.description: Turn about the free fingers' axis between candidates. Default 15.

inputs.name: tilts_deg
inputs.description: Tilts of the free fingers' axis from straight down. Default [0, 15, 30].

inputs.name: max_first_tilt_deg
inputs.description: How far the first object may tilt from its grasp orientation. Default 20.

inputs.name: clear_m
inputs.description: Clearance of the hand and the first object from the second and the scene. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: approach_m
inputs.description: Approach distance (checked). Default 0.05.

inputs.name: bench_scene, side, state
inputs.description: Screen each pose for the station's arm (state: the bench state, a trajectory.npz or a qpos).

inputs.name: top_k
inputs.description: Poses returned. Default 5.

inputs.name: verify_physics
inputs.description: Default True: only return pairs passing the default multi-object hold stress test. False returns geometric/reach candidates requiring separate stress validation.

inputs.name: max_physics_trials
inputs.description: Maximum combined hold trials across poses and clamp variations. Default 12.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the best pose here (the ranked list to <stem>_all.json).

inputs.name: first_yaw_step_deg
inputs.description: Default 30.0.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: {ok, pose (with `first_pose`: the first grasp it was designed with), poses [ranked, each with `second_grasp` {first_pose_index, yaw_deg, tilt_deg, clear_mm, first_tilt_deg, wall_fingers, reach}], first_poses, n_candidates, rejected {reason: count}, free_fingers, mouth}.

tools.name: segment_source_frame
tools.title: Segment a source video frame on CPU
tools.summary: Fixed OpenCV GrabCut inside a selected object's box on a decoded video frame; CPU fallback for source masks.
tools.description: Decodes the video frame itself, uses the supplied pixel box as GrabCut initialization, and writes a binary mask and lossless source frame. No proposed mask, synthetic render, or processor can be supplied. Inspect the result; source provenance does not prove correct object identity or segmentation accuracy. Invoke directly through the harness for reference evidence, not inside run_python. Existing masks can be copied without changing their bytes. Multiple separate visible instances can use separate calls; do not union or paint accepted masks after the call.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: Original source video, matching the run input.

inputs.name: frame_index
inputs.description: Zero-based source frame index.

inputs.name: box
inputs.description: Pixel box [x0, y0, x1, y1], with background outside it.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives source.png, mask.png and recipe.json.

outputs.name: result

tools.name: segment_with_text_prompts
tools.title: Segment with text prompts
tools.summary: SAM 3 on every frame: the union of all instances of the given prompts as one binary mask per frame, and optionally one mask per instance.
tools.description: For each frame, each prompt is segmented with SAM 3 and all instances above the score floor are merged into a single mask (255 = matched). This is the mask a video eraser needs: name the hands and arms and every object the simulation re-creates, and the result marks exactly the pixels to remove. Frames can be downscaled for speed; masks are returned at full resolution. With `instances` each instance above the floor is also written as its own mask (instances/<prompt>/frame%05d_<k>.png, k by descending score) with its score, box and area in meta.json: several same-coloured parts (identical bricks) get one mask each without a detect-then-track detour. Instance numbers are per frame (ranked by score), not identities tracked through the video: track_objects does that.

inputs.name: frames_dir

inputs.name: prompts

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Receives frame%05d.png masks and meta.json.

inputs.description: Instance confidence floor. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: downscale
inputs.description: Detect at this fraction of the resolution. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Image checkpoint version: 'sam3' (default). SAM 3.1 multiplex video checkpoints are not supported by this image tool.

requirements: Hugging Face access to facebook/sam3 (or its already cached checkpoint)

tools.name: slide_contact_pose
tools.title: Slide contact pose
tools.summary: Pose the hand to slide a part across the table (to make it overhang the edge, or to bring it against a stop): flat fingertips pressed on its top that drag it by friction, or a fingertip pushing one side face; with the friction check that says whether a drag can move it at all and with how much press.
tools.description: A drag works when the pads' friction beats the support's: mu_hand N > mu_support (N + m g), so it needs a press N > mu_support m g / (mu_hand - mu_support) (the hand's contact friction is the library's 1.2, the part-table friction the larger of the two geoms', as MuJoCo combines them); the press must fit under the 40 N wrist cap with margin (slide.drag_within_wrist_cap: 1.5 x the press <= 40 N; a drag that does not fit is still returned, flagged). Mode 'drag' lays the straight index, middle and ring fingers on the part's top over its centre of mass (so the drag does not turn it), pitched `pitch_deg` so only the fingertips touch (flat_hand_pose), the fingers pointing along `finger_dir` (default: against the slide, the hand trailing behind the part's centre as a person pulls a phone toward them); candidates turn the fingers about the vertical (`yaws_deg`) and pitch them steeper (an arm at a bench edge holds a fingers-down hand far more often than a flat one), returned as `poses` for the plan entry's pose_candidates (the executor keeps the ones its arm holds). Mode 'push' stands the index and middle fingertips upright just behind the side face that faces away from the slide, their caps a pad radius plus 1 mm above the table (on a part lower than that they meet its top edge), one candidate per sector of wrist heading. Mode 'auto' (default) pushes when the contact slope allows it (tan of the angle under 0.6 / mu_support: a 5 mm part still, a 1.5 mm strip not) and drags otherwise; the drag rides on the pads' friction margin over the support's, which on this bench (1.2 against the table's 1.0) let the pads slide 6 cm over a 170 g slab pressed with 21 N. Mode 'press' gives the drag's flat fingertips at contact_point with no slide: the press pose of tilt_up. The pose carries slide_mode and the friction numbers; give it to the `slide` motion with the direction and how far (overhang_m, distance_m or target_pos).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output or its json); the part is its last object / grasp_body.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: [dx, dy]: where the part is to go.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: 'auto' (default: push when the contact slope allows, else drag), 'drag', 'push', or 'press' (the drag's flat fingertips at contact_point with no slide: the press pose of tilt_up).

inputs.name: finger_dir
inputs.description: Drag: the direction the fingers point (default minus direction).

inputs.name: fingers
inputs.description: Drag / press: fingers on the top. Default ['index', 'middle', 'ring'] (a flat hand); one finger gives an upright fingertip on the contact point (a strip or a small part, where a flat hand's other fingers would press the table).

inputs.name: pitch_deg
inputs.description: Drag: the hand pitched so only the fingertips touch (tried first; 45, 60 and 30 follow). Default 45.

inputs.name: yaws_deg
inputs.description: Drag: finger directions tried, degrees about the vertical from finger_dir. Default [0, 30, -30, 60, -60, 90, -90, 120, -120, 180].

inputs.name: contact_point
inputs.description: Drag: world xy (or xyz) to press at (default: over the part's centre of mass).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the pose here.

outputs.name: pose
outputs.description: The first candidate: hand pose (pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_open, grip_fingers, points, normals, approach) plus slide_mode, slide {direction, mu_hand, mu_support, mass_kg, drag_force_n (the press a drag needs; None: a drag cannot move it), drag_within_wrist_cap, height_m, push_contact_deg, why}, and poses (every candidate, for pose_candidates).

tools.name: solve_arm_ik
tools.title: Solve arm IK
tools.summary: Damped-least-squares IK for the joints above any body, limit-aware with null-space rest pull, for one target or a path with warm starts and retries.
tools.description: Builds the chain of hinge and slide joints between the world and the target body, then iterates a damped least squares step on the position error (and the rotation error as an axis-angle, scaled by rot_weight) with a per-step cap. Joints on a limit that would move further out are removed from the Jacobian for that step; a hinge whose range spans a full turn is treated as unlimited. A rest posture is pulled in the null space. For a path each frame starts from the previous solution and, when a frame does not converge within the tolerances, retries from the previous frame's solution and from perturbed postures, keeping the best. A point in the body frame can be given as the controlled point (an attachment point rather than the body origin). Returns the joint trajectory and per-frame residuals. Any robot, any chain.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Body the chain ends at.

inputs.name: positions
inputs.description: World targets for the body (or point).

inputs.name: rotations
inputs.description: World target rotations; None for position-only.

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: Controlled point in the body frame. Default the origin.

inputs.name: rest
inputs.description: Posture pulled in the null space.

inputs.name: q0
inputs.description: Starting joint values; default the scene's qpos0.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.description: Restrict the chain to these joints.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Default 0.

inputs.name: qpos_base
inputs.description: Default None.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: qpos [T, n] joint values in chain order, joint_names, qadr (qpos columns), pos_err_m [T], rot_err_deg [T], ok (all frames within tolerance), worst frame.

tools.name: stage_on_bench
tools.title: Stage on bench
tools.summary: Attaches asset MJCFs into an existing robot world at poses given in the rig frame (origin between the two arm bases on the table top, x along the baseline, y into the work).
tools.description: A fitted trajectory is expressed relative to the robot, so objects are staged relative to the robot too: the rig frame has its origin at the midpoint of the two arm roots projected to the table top, x from the left base to the right base, y into the workspace and z up. Each asset is attached through a frame at origin + R_rig @ (x, y, z) with its orientation in the rig frame (yaw only by default; roll_deg / pitch_deg for an object lying on its side or flipped, composed as R = Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll), the convention fit_object_placement reports; or a full quat), with a name prefix, so the bench's joints and qpos layout are unchanged for every body that was already there (a recorded qpos still replays). The rig frame can also be passed explicitly for single-arm or custom benches.

inputs.name: world_xml
inputs.description: Robot world MJCF.

inputs.name: assets
inputs.description: [{'name', 'xml', 'x', 'y', 'z'=0, 'yaw_deg'=0, 'pitch_deg'=0, 'roll_deg'=0 | 'quat'=[w,x,y,z], 'joints'={joint: value}}] in rig coordinates (metres, degrees). The orientation is R = Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll) in the rig frame (roll_deg 180 lays a phone whose body frame has its back up screen up), or 'quat' (w, x, y, z) for any rotation; give one or the other. 'joints' sets the asset's initial joint values (an open lid, a pulled drawer) in the scene's keyframes, joint names as in the asset (the prefix is added). Other keys are refused.

inputs.name: out_xml
inputs.description: Output MJCF.

inputs.name: arm_roots
inputs.description: Body names of the (left, right) arm bases used to derive the rig frame. Default ('robot_left_arm_root', 'robot_right_arm_root').

inputs.name: table_top_z
inputs.description: Height of the rig origin (table surface). Default 0.0.

inputs.name: rig
inputs.description: Explicit {'origin': [x,y,z], 'R': 3x3 columns x,y,z} overriding the derivation. The DexAgent setup scene's world frame IS the rig frame: pass origin [0,0,0] and the identity.

inputs.name: cameras
inputs.description: {name: camera.json path or dict} cameras to write into the world (for example {'video_cam': 'camera.json'}): pose, fovy and, when the dict has width and height, the camera's resolution (its image size, so renderers keep its aspect).
