tools.name: thin_grasp_diagnosis
tools.title: Thin grasp diagnosis
tools.summary: Decide from geometry whether a part lying on the bench (a phone, a card, scissors, a strap, a flat ribbon) can be pinched or wrapped where it lies, and if not, name the primitive that makes it graspable (slide it to overhang the edge and pinch it from below, tilt it up, hook it through an opening, gather a strip into an arch) with the numbers it decided on.
tools.description: Every grasp skill assumes the pads can close on the part's sides or get under it. The hand's own sizes decide that (read from its collision capsules: pad radius, fingertip thickness, thumb-index span), against the part as it lies (its footprint and height above its support, the gap under it from rays cast up from the support, its through-openings from above, how far it overhangs or stays inside each table edge, its mass and the friction it has on the support). Verdicts: side_pinch (height >= pad radius + 1 mm off the table + 2 mm under the top edge: 10 mm for the Sharpa hand), pinch_under (a gap a fingertip thick + 2 mm), wrap, edge_pinch (the overhang the moment balance needs: fingers under the part deeper than the thumb on top, the thumb pressing at most 5 N, the finger a radius plus 3 mm past the table's edge; and no more overhang than keeps the centre of mass 12 mm on the table), slide (to the nearest table edge: a drag with pads pressed on its top needs the hand's friction 1.2 above the support's and a press N = mu_s m g / (mu_h - mu_s) within the 40 N wrist cap; a push needs a side face taller than a pad radius + 2 mm), tilt_up (pressing the overhanging end about the edge raises the far end by the lever ratio), hook (an opening wider than a fingertip + 3 mm; the thumb outside when the wall is 10 mm tall), strip_pinch (a flexible chain thinner than a side pinch needs). `recommend` orders the plans that work, with the tools that build their poses, or says nothing in the library makes it graspable (then report the task blocked with these measurements). Call it before trying grasps on a thin or flat part.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF (Stage 2 scene.xml).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The part: an object's root body or a part of it (its subtree is measured).

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: Which hand ('left' or 'right'); its sizes are read from the scene. Default 'right'.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: A trajectory.npz (last frame) or a qpos: the part where an earlier subgoal left it. Default the scene's keyframe.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: geometry {height_m, support, footprint, edges {+x|-x|+y|-y: {overhang_m, edge_distance_m}}, under {max_gap_m, at}, openings [...], mass_kg, mu_support, flexible}, hand {pad_radius_m, tip_thickness_m, finger_thickness_m, span_m}, verdicts {side_pinch, pinch_under, wrap, edge_pinch, slide, tilt_up, hook, strip_pinch: {ok, why, ...numbers}}, graspable_as_lies, recommend [{plan, why}].

tools.name: trace_rope_waypoints
tools.title: Trace rope along waypoints
tools.summary: Coiled or self-crossing cord mask + ordered pixel waypoints along it -> centreline in metres routed through the mask's middle between the waypoints, with the crossings found and the upper strand lifted, ready for construct_rope / construct_plug_cable / build_isaac_scene.
tools.description: For cords measure_rope refuses (coils, loops, crossings). Snaps each waypoint to the nearest mask pixel within snap_px (a waypoint with no mask pixel that close stays where it is: an occluded stretch), builds an 8-connected pixel graph of the mask whose step cost is the step length times 1 + centre_weight x (1 - min(dt / r_px, 1)) with dt the distance transform and r_px the cord's half width, and routes each leg between consecutive waypoints by Dijkstra (scipy). Unconnected legs are bridged straight. A leg whose route is longer than max_detour times the straight distance plus 4 cord widths is reported as a possible jump to another turn (add a waypoint there). The radius is the median distance-transform value along the routed pixels converted to metres at each point's depth (or radius_m when given); the pixel path is lifted onto the plane z = radius (rig frame for a camera.json, table frame for a common.tablecam camera), smoothed with an end-held moving average of smooth_win pixels and resampled to n_points. Crossings are the plan-view intersections of non-adjacent segments; at each the strand named by `over` ('later' default, 'earlier', or a list per crossing) is raised by 2 x radius x (1 + lift_margin) under a cosine bump of lift_span_m. Reports the 3D minimum gap between non-adjacent stretches after lifting (negative = the laid cord starts interpenetrated, an issue). Assumes the cord lies on the table plane except where it crosses itself.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Binary cord silhouette at the camera resolution.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json (or its dict) in the rig frame, or a common.tablecam camera dict (then the result is in the table frame).

inputs.name: waypoints_px
inputs.description: Ordered pixels along the cord from end a to end b (at least 2). Put one every few centimetres and one on each side of every crossing.

inputs.name: n_points
inputs.description: Points of the resampled centreline. Default 120.

inputs.name: radius_m
inputs.description: Known cord radius in metres; default None = measured from the mask.

inputs.name: snap_px
inputs.description: Largest distance from a waypoint to the mask it is snapped across. Default 15.

inputs.name: centre_weight
inputs.description: Extra step cost away from the mask's medial axis. Default 4.0.

inputs.name: max_detour
inputs.description: A leg routed longer than this times its straight distance (plus 4 cord widths) is reported. Default 2.5.

inputs.name: smooth_win
inputs.description: End-held moving-average window over the routed pixels. Default 9.

inputs.name: lift_crossings
inputs.description: Raise the upper strand at every crossing. Default True.

inputs.name: over
inputs.description: Which strand is on top at a crossing: 'later' (default), 'earlier', or one of them per crossing in order along the cord.

inputs.name: lift_margin
inputs.description: Extra lift as a fraction of the cord diameter. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: lift_span_m
inputs.description: Arc length of the cosine bump around each crossing. Default 0.04.

outputs.name: trace
outputs.description: ok, issues; frame ('rig' | 'table'); centreline [n, 3] metres (lifted at crossings); points (= centreline, rig frame only, for build_isaac_scene); centreline_px [n, 2]; length_m; radius_m; radius_measured_m; legs [{i, from_px, to_px, routed_px, straight_px, bridged, detour}]; crossings [{s_a_m, s_b_m, xy, lifted}]; min_self_gap_m; snapped [{i, moved_px, on_mask}].

tools.cli: python -c "from tool_library.skills.trace_rope_waypoints import trace_rope_waypoints; print(trace_rope_waypoints('mask.png', 'camera.json', [[u0, v0], [u1, v1]]))"

tools.name: track_objects

tools.summary: SAM 2 video tracking of every detected object from its best seed frame, forward and backward, into per-frame label maps.
tools.description: Takes a detection scan, picks the seed frame (the sampled frame that found the most keywords, ties broken by the highest minimum score), seeds SAM 2's video predictor with each keyword's box there, and propagates through the clip in both directions, one object at a time so tracks never swap identities. Writes a palette label map per frame (pixel value = object label, 1..K in keyword order), a binary mask video per object, an overlay video, and result.json with per-object coverage. Objects missing at the seed frame are reported, not silently dropped.

tools.name: write_stage4_config
tools.title: Write Stage 4 config
tools.summary: Assemble the folder Stage 4 consumes: scene.xml with its assets, trajectory.npz (with the servo commands), the human and sim videos, the Stage 3 subgoal expectations, the executable Stage 3 plan (plan.json; Stage 4 does not re-execute it on the rigid runtime), and stage4.json with end effectors, per-phase anchors, the objects to randomize with their carriers, releases, resting relations and clearance-sized ranges, cameras, table, inpaint prompts and robot materials.
tools.description: Stage 4 re-anchors every hand frame to an object or the world and lets carried objects ride the hand; it needs to know which phase is anchored to what. This skill walks the Stage 3 phases per side in order and emits the segment list with the rule Stage 4 enforces (an anchor changes only through a blend over the phase in which it changes): reaching blends world -> object, grasp/lift/hold phases stay on the object, a carry blends from the carried object to its destination, an unanchored let-go or retreat stays with what the hand held, a return home blends back to world; phases are walked in time order and a label that recurs in several frame ranges gets a segment per range; a two-hand phase ('left: X | right: Y') gives each hand its own anchor. Per object, the carrier is the hand whose own lift/carry/set-down phase names that object and the release is that hand's first let-go phase naming it, never a later phase merely anchored to it (the hand stacking the next brick on it); an object that travels under 2 cm has no carrier. What a released object rests on or in (`rests_on` / `inside`, so a stacked goal follows the brick it is stacked on; `next_to` for a part set down at a world target within group_clearance_m of another randomized part, the part or its hand, so it keeps its place beside it) comes from the Stage 3 plan entry (`on`, `into`, the expectation's `on`), else the anchor of its release phase, else the contacts holding it up in the final state; the carrier's set-down phases that were anchored to the world are then anchored to that body. Objects whose geometry comes within group_clearance_m of each other while both still sit at their start (a pile of bricks, a brick lifted past its neighbour) move together (attached_to the group's first uncarried member). A 'deformable' that is a single free body (a plush toy) is randomized like a rigid one. Ranges default to half each object's start clearance to its nearest neighbour, 5 mm to 3 cm, with a yaw range scaled to match (3 to 15 degrees, and at most the shift range divided by how far the object reaches from its origin, so no point of a large object moves farther than the shift); `ranges` overrides per object. An object sharing its asset with another (a cap on its bottle) is attached_to it. For the physics replay of augmented episodes the folder gets trajectory_manifest.json (the manifest's executed subgoals with frames, plan and expect; rebuilt from the executor's outcomes.json when the manifest is not written yet), the servo commands as `reference` in trajectory.npz (from the same rigid runtime recording), the scene's screw-thread / cut / connector-latch rules, and checks.physics_replay. The executable plan goes to plan.json (stage4.json reexecute.plan): one entry per executed plan entry of the execution folder, in order, as it ran (its segment's keyframes.json, else the matching entry of `plan` or of the manifest), every hand pose inlined (the pose that ran first, then the other candidates the plan offered) with the object pose it was solved against (`anchor`), and its frame window in the trajectory; with the screw-thread / cut / latch rules. Without an execution folder that adds up to the trajectory no plan is written (a warning says why) and Stage 4 only warps. An object carried more than once (put down by one hand and picked up by the other, or handed over) gets every carrier and release in order (`carrier` and `release` as lists). A Stage 2 object whose root is fixed to the world (an articulated object's frame, a cabinet) can be randomized as a whole (fixed_bases=true); a cable or rope with a free root is randomized as one rigid piece (`deformable`: Stage 4 turns it about its middle, with a yaw range that moves its ends no farther than the shift range, and settles it before re-executing the plan on it). The video camera comes from Stage 2's camera.json with its full intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy at its image size), the wrist views from the scene's cameras under the hand bodies, the table from the scene's table geom, erase prompts from Stage 1's object names. Robot materials use the sharpa / yam presets. Copies scene.xml and the assets it references into the task folder with relative paths.

inputs.name: episode_dir

inputs.name: out_dir

inputs.name: human_video

inputs.name: sim_video

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Not read: the scene is always the one the execution recorded (episode_dir/scene_physics.xml, which already holds place_arm_stations' stations); accepted for call compatibility.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 manifest for the erase prompts (default: next to the Stage 2 manifest).

inputs.name: num_samples
inputs.description: Randomized episodes to keep. Default 3.

inputs.name: ranges

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Task name (default the run name).

inputs.name: manifest

inputs.name: physics_replay

inputs.name: group_clearance_m
inputs.description: Objects closer than this while still at their start move together (default 0.01; 0 disables grouping).

inputs.name: plan

inputs.name: fixed_bases

tools.name: above_check
tools.title: Above check
tools.summary: The centre of one body is higher (world z) than the centre of another, optionally by at least a margin.
tools.description: A cheap relation for 'the lid is on the box' or 'the cup sits on the tray' that does not need the two to touch. Compares world-frame body positions, after settling by default. `min_gap` demands a height difference (metres); zero accepts any ordering.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: The body expected higher.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: The body expected lower.

inputs.name: min_gap
inputs.description: Required height difference. Default 0.

inputs.name: settled
inputs.description: Judge after settling (default) or at the initial state.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; z_top; z_bottom; gap_m.

tools.name: actuator_limit_integrity_check
tools.title: Actuator limit integrity check
tools.summary: Every robot actuator of a scene has the setup's transmission, gains, bias, control range, force range and gear, the robot joints keep their actuator force caps, and no extra actuator drives a robot joint.
tools.description: Stronger fingers or wrists make any grasp hold: a finger servo with ten times the gain, a widened force range or a second actuator on the same joint squeeze an object no real hand could. The reference actuators come from a setup folder (default: the repository's setup/scene.xml). Each reference robot actuator is matched to the scene by name; its target joint (by name), gain/bias/dynamics types and parameters, gear, ctrllimited/ctrlrange, forcelimited/forcerange and actlimited/actrange must equal the reference within a relative tolerance. Each robot joint's actuatorfrcrange (jnt_actfrclimited, jnt_actfrcrange) must equal the reference, and any scene actuator not in the reference whose transmission acts on a robot joint, body, site or tendon is reported as extra. The executor's own runtime caps (limit_hand_forces) are applied later and are not part of the scene.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: rel_tol
inputs.description: Allowed relative difference of every parameter. Default 1e-6.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; n_actuators compared; changed [{actuator, field, reference, scene}]; missing; extra (actuators on robot joints the setup does not have); joint_caps_changed; worst (largest gain or force-range ratio scene/reference).

tools.name: actuator_mapping_check
tools.title: Actuator mapping check
tools.summary: Every actuator drives an existing joint/site/body/tendon with valid ctrl and force ranges (a position servo's ctrlrange inside its joint's range, no dead actuator), the robot's actuators come first and contiguously (matching the setup's list when given), and every non-robot actuator is listed with its ctrl slot.
tools.description: Stage 3 and Stage 4 address the robot through ctrl: ctrl[:56] are the two hands' servos on the bench. An object asset that brings its own actuators (EgoDex magnetic rings add three adhesion actuators after the robot's 56) changes nu, and code that sizes or slices ctrl as robot-only breaks; an actuator inserted before or between the robot's shifts every robot command. The check compiles the scene, assigns each actuator to the robot or not by its target's name (joint/site/body/tendon carrying the robot prefix), and fails: robot actuators that are not the first block of ctrl; a robot actuator list that differs in count, names or order from the `reference` scene's (setup/scene.xml) or from `expected_robot_nu`; ctrllimited with ctrlrange[0] >= ctrlrange[1] and forcelimited with an empty forcerange; a position servo whose ctrlrange reaches beyond its limited joint's range by more than `range_tol` (it drives the joint into its stop); an actuator with zero gain and zero bias (it does nothing); and, when `allow_non_robot` is False, any non-robot actuator. Non-robot actuators are always listed with their ctrl indices and targets.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Scene whose robot actuators (names, order) must be reproduced, e.g. setup/scene.xml.

inputs.name: expected_robot_nu
inputs.description: Number of robot actuators expected (setup.yaml robot.actuators: 56).

inputs.name: allow_non_robot
inputs.description: Accept actuators that drive non-robot parts (listed either way). Default True.

inputs.name: range_tol
inputs.description: How far a servo's ctrlrange may exceed its joint range (rad or m). Default 0.01.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot elements. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; nu; robot_nu; robot_ctrl_slice [first, last+1]; non_robot: [{index, name, trntype, target}]; actuators: [{index, name, robot, trntype, target, ctrlrange, joint_range, problem}] (problems first); worst.

tools.name: anchored_cord_pull_test
tools.title: Anchored cord pull test
tools.summary: Force-only trial on a scene: the free end of a cord whose other end is anchored to a fixed object is pulled horizontally away from the anchor with a capped, ramped force; the anchored end must stay put, the anchor body must not move, and the cord must end taut (end-to-end distance close to its length).
tools.description: Loads the scene at keyframe `key` (gravity on, the robot held by its own actuators at the keyframe ctrl), finds the cord's links as the chain of bodies between anchored_body and free_body (nested bodies, as MuJoCo cables build them; or the given chain_bodies) and its length as the summed distance between consecutive link origins at the keyframe. It checks that an active weld or connect ties anchored_body to a body that cannot move (not the world), then applies a force on free_body along the horizontal direction from the anchored end to the free end at the keyframe (or `direction`), ramped to pull_force_N over ramp_s and held for hold_s. Verdict: the anchored end moves at most tol_anchor_m, the anchor body does not move, the state stays finite, and at the end the end-to-end distance is at least taut_frac of the cord's length while the free end has travelled (the pull acted). Assumes the cord lies free to straighten (nothing else holds it).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF with the anchored cord.

inputs.name: anchored_body
inputs.description: The cord's end link held by the anchor.

inputs.name: free_body
inputs.description: The cord's free end link (the one a hand pulls).

inputs.name: chain_bodies
inputs.description: The cord's links in order, when they are not nested bodies. Default None

inputs.name: pull_force_N
inputs.description: Peak pulling force, newtons. Default 0.5

inputs.name: ramp_s
inputs.description: Ramp time to the peak force, seconds. Default 0.5

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Time the peak force is held, seconds. Default 1.5

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Pull direction (normalised); default horizontal from the anchored end to the free end. Default None

inputs.name: tol_anchor_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed motion of the anchored end, metres. Default 0.005

inputs.name: taut_frac
inputs.description: End-to-end distance / cord length required at the end. Default 0.9

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe to start from. Default 0

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here as JSON. Default None

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; anchor {equality, type, other_body}; length_m; end_to_end_start_m; end_to_end_end_m; taut_ratio; anchored_end_max_motion_m; anchor_body_motion_m; free_end_travel_m; finite; params.

tools.name: appearance_texture_check
tools.title: Appearance texture check
tools.summary: Every object has at least one visible geom whose colour is not MuJoCo's default grey or that carries a texture Stage 4 can render; every texture and mesh file the MJCF names exists and loads; a texture on a geom that cannot carry it (a primitive, a mesh without UV coordinates) is reported because Stage 4's Cycles export silently drops it.
tools.description: Stage 4 renders the scene photo-realistically from the compiled model: a geom's colour is its rgba, or its material's rgba when the geom keeps the default (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1); a 2D texture is exported only for mesh geoms with texture coordinates, and Cycles drops a missing image without an error. So an object built without colours renders as default grey, and a textured material put on a box or on a mesh without UVs renders as its plain (often white) rgba. The check (1) parses the MJCF for every <texture file=...> and <mesh file=...>, resolving them as MuJoCo does (compiler assetdir/texturedir/meshdir relative to the file) and opening each texture image; (2) for each object (Stage 2 manifest objects, else top-level non-robot bodies) lists its visible geoms (groups 0-2, alpha > 0) with their effective colour and whether a texture survives; an object fails when none of its visible geoms has a non-default colour or a surviving texture, or when it has no visible geom at all; a dropped texture is an issue naming the geom. Compiling is attempted after the file checks, so a missing file is reported rather than raised.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF path (the files are resolved relative to it).

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json naming the objects. Default: top-level non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these objects (ids or body names).

inputs.name: visual_groups
inputs.description: Geom groups Stage 4 renders. Default [0, 1, 2].

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; files {textures, meshes, missing, unreadable}; objects [{id, n_visible, colours, textured, verdict}]; dropped_textures [{geom, why}].

tools.name: arm_branch_flip_audit
tools.title: Arm branch flip audit
tools.summary: Windows in which an arm's joints travel far (an IK elbow or wrist branch switch) while its flange stays nearly still in position and orientation.
tools.description: Covers what arm_reach_check (joint speed above 180 deg/s, weld residual) and joint_speed_check (per-frame budget) miss: a slow branch switch that respects every per-frame speed. For each arm (bench stations via episode.robot_parts; other robots: joints on bodies whose name contains '_arm') it slides windows of each length in window_s over the episode and measures the largest joint excursion inside the window (max - min of any one joint, degrees) against the flange's largest displacement from its pose at the window start (millimetres and degrees). A window where a joint swings at least min_joint_deg while the flange stays within max_flange_mm and max_flange_deg is a branch switch (the configuration changed, the end effector did not). Default 45 degrees against 30 mm and 15 degrees, windows 0.5 s and 2 s. Reports the worst window per arm with the joint that swung, its frames and phase labels, and the sign changes of each joint inside it (an elbow or wrist joint crossing zero is the usual signature).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: window_s
inputs.description: Window lengths in seconds. Default [0.5, 2.0].

inputs.name: min_joint_deg
inputs.description: Joint excursion that counts as a swing. Default 45.

inputs.name: max_flange_mm, max_flange_deg
inputs.description: Flange motion under which the swing served nothing. Defaults 30 mm, 15 deg.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, frames, labels, joint, joint_excursion_deg, flange_mm, flange_deg}; arms {side: worst window measurements}.

tools.name: arm_jerk_check
tools.title: Arm jerk check
tools.summary: Second difference of every arm joint per frame against a replayable budget.
tools.description: Takes the arm joint groups of a trajectory (discovered from the end-effector bodies or named explicitly; with neither, the scalar joints of robot bodies whose body or joint name contains '_arm', one group per side, so the hand's wrist and finger joints are never held to the arm budget), computes the frame-to-frame change of the per-frame step (the discrete acceleration) in degrees per frame squared, and fails when any joint exceeds the budget, 3.0 deg/frame^2 at 30 fps scaled to the trajectory's frame rate. Reports the worst frame and phase label per group and how many frames are over the budget, so the fix can target one transit instead of smoothing the whole episode.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or the qpos array.

inputs.name: end_effectors
inputs.description: Finds the arm chain per side.

inputs.name: chains
inputs.description: Explicit joint groups instead.

inputs.name: limit_deg
inputs.description: Budget in deg/frame^2 at 30 fps. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies, used to find the arm joints when neither end_effectors nor chains is given. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per group: max, limit, p99, worst frame and label, frames over the limit.

tools.name: arm_reach_check
tools.title: Arm reach and weld check
tools.summary: For each arm, the residual between its flange and the hand bolted to it on every frame (position and rotation of the fixed mount), the arm's joint speed and configuration jumps, and how close its joints run to their limits. A disconnected or twisted wrist fails.
tools.description: The hand is bolted to the arm's flange: on every frame the hand root must sit exactly where the arm's joints put the flange, through the fixed mount calibrated in the trusted setup's home state. The delivered trajectory cannot supply its own calibration. This verifier measures the mount residual (position mm, rotation deg) on every frame, the peak arm joint speed and any one-frame configuration jump, and the smallest margin of every arm joint to its range. Physical recordings additionally check actual velocities at every integrator step, including the initial velocity; brief between-frame overspeed cannot hide in the rendered frame rate. Missing or malformed physical velocity evidence fails. Proposal-only diagnostics retain the frame-difference check. It fails when the residual exceeds `pos_tol_m` / `tilt_tol_deg` on any frame (defaults 2 mm / 2 deg: a visible gap or twist at the wrist), or a joint moves faster than `max_joint_speed_deg_s`, and reports the worst frame with its label. execute_subgoal_plan (couple_arms) plans the arm with the hand and passes it by construction; an episode whose arms were fitted afterwards usually does not. With `poses` it screens candidate wrist poses for the arm of `side` (exact IK, same tolerances) and, at each solved arm, checks the arm's links (convex hulls) against its own hand, the other station, the table and the objects at the scene's keyframe (the executor's arm screen): an arm that holds the hand only by running a link 8 mm into its own palm fails here, not in the executor's dry run. Poses may be dicts, pose json paths, or a json holding a list (generate_* out_json).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz with the arm joints filled (omit when checking poses).

inputs.name: poses
inputs.description: Candidate wrist poses ({pos, euler, finger_targets}) to test for reach instead of an episode: dicts, pose json paths, or one json file holding a pose or a list of them; returns which the arm of `side` can reach without its links running into its own hand or the scene.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right' for the poses mode.

inputs.name: arm_collision
inputs.description: Poses mode: also check the solved arm's links against its own hand, the other station, the table and the objects (default true; a pose with a hit fails and names the link).

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: Poses mode: the scene state the poses are checked in (where the objects and the other station are): a trajectory.npz (its last frame) or a qpos; default the scene's keyframe.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Weld position tolerance. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: tilt_tol_deg
inputs.description: Weld rotation tolerance. Default 2.

inputs.name: max_joint_speed_deg_s
inputs.description: Arm joint speed that fails (a branch flip shows here). Default 180.

inputs.name: limit_margin_deg
inputs.description: Warn when a joint runs closer than this to its stop. Default 2.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.description: Deprecated: baseline-relative acceptance is rejected; each episode must meet absolute limits.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Trusted setup directory providing the calibrated mount.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, failed, per side {mount, pos_err_mm {max, mean, worst_frame, label}, tilt_err_deg {...}, frames_over, peak_joint_speed_deg_s, speed_frames_over, limit_margin_deg, joints_at_limit}. Poses mode: ok, reachable [indices], issues, poses [{index, source, ok, reach_ok, pos_err_mm, rot_err_deg, arm_qpos, arm_hits [{geoms, depth_mm, what}], own_hand_mm}].

tools.name: arm_workspace_map
tools.title: Arm workspace map
tools.summary: Samples a grid of wrist positions over the table for one or several hand orientations and reports, per orientation, the region the station's arm reaches (residual below tolerance), its far edge in y, and whether given points of interest (an object's part, a handle) are inside; a map image shows the reachable cells.
tools.description: Reach is a property of the station, not the pose: the same hand orientation is reachable at 0.5 m and not at 0.65 m, and at the same place a level hand is reachable where a fingers-down hand is not. Before choosing a grasp or a strategy, ask this verifier where the work can happen. For each named orientation (`orientations`: 'palm_down' (fingers forward +y), 'palm_up', 'fingers_down' (palm toward the other station), 'fingers_in' (level, palm down, fingers pointing across the table toward the other station), 'fingers_in_palm_up', 'palm_in' (vertical, fingers forward, palm toward the other station), or any euler [rx, ry, rz] of the hand root, whose local z runs along the fingers and local x is the palm normal) it solves the arm's IK (position plus the home-pose mount rotation, multi-start) on a grid of (x, y) at heights `z_m` and marks the cells whose residual is within `pos_tol_m` / `tilt_tol_deg`. The report names, per orientation, the reachable fraction, the far edge (largest reachable y at each x band), and, for every point in `points`, whether it is reachable with that orientation and the residual there. The side's own orientation convention is handled (a right-hand 'fingers_in' points -x, a left-hand one +x). Solved cells are cached on disk per (robot signature, side, orientation, cell): the signature hashes only what reach depends on (the arm chain's placement and joints, its home posture, the hand mount and the solver settings), so a Stage 2 scene that adds objects to the default setup reuses the cache shipped for the default setup (tool_library/assets/arm_workspace_cache.json, the default grid for both stations), and a repeated call on any station answers from the user cache ($DEXAGENT_CACHE_DIR, else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/dexagent, else ~/.cache/dexagent) instead of re-solving for minutes.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left' or 'right'.

inputs.name: orientations
inputs.description: Names or eulers. Default ['palm_down', 'fingers_in', 'fingers_down', 'palm_in'].

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: {label: [x, y, z]} wrist positions to classify (an object's edge, a handle).

inputs.name: x_range
inputs.description: [min, max] in metres. Default [-0.4, 0.4].

inputs.name: y_range
inputs.description: Default [0.1, 0.9].

inputs.name: z_m
inputs.description: Height(s) of the wrist. Default 0.12.

inputs.name: step_m
inputs.description: Grid step. Default 0.1 (a 9 x 9 grid per orientation: about a minute per orientation on a busy node when solved, instant from the cache; 0.05 is four times finer and slower).

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Default 0.015.

inputs.name: tilt_tol_deg
inputs.description: Default 15.

inputs.name: out_png
inputs.description: Map image (one panel per orientation and height).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Report.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: True (default): read the shipped and the user cache, write new cells to the user cache; a path: read and write that json file (the shipped cache is still read); False: solve every cell.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok (every requested point reachable with at least one orientation), per orientation: euler, reachable_fraction, far_edge_y {x: y}, cells [[x, y, z, pos_err_mm, rot_err_deg]], points {label: {ok, pos_err_mm, rot_err_deg}}; best_orientation per point; verdict; cache {hits, solved, file, signature}.

tools.name: articulated_joint_travel_test
tools.title: Articulated joint travel test
tools.summary: Pulls each slide/hinge joint of an articulated asset through its range with a capped force on the moving part, both ways, and reports the fraction of travel reached.
tools.description: Loads the MJCF (or the info sheet port_urdf_asset wrote) and, for each requested joint (default: every limited slide or hinge), runs two trials from the initial state: a force of up to force_N along the joint axis in world frame (torque of up to torque_Nm about it for a hinge) applied with xfrc_applied on the child body, at the handle site when the info sheet names one, ramped over 0.5 s and held for `seconds`; then the opposite force for the same time. It records the travel fraction reached toward each limit, the time to 80% of the range, and the displacement of the root body named by the info sheet's root_body (a free-based cabinet must not slide more than root_slip_m; None when no root body is named, so not measured). With hold_root (default) a free root is welded to the world for the test, as a hand or the table holds it. Passes when every joint reaches min_fraction of its range in both directions and the root, when measured, stays put. Hinges whose range is unlimited are measured against one full turn.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF path, or the info dict/json from port_urdf_asset (gives handle sites and joint names).

inputs.name: joints
inputs.description: Joint names to test. Default: every limited slide/hinge.

inputs.name: force_N
inputs.description: Cap on the pull for slides. Default 10.

inputs.name: torque_Nm
inputs.description: Cap on the torque for hinges. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Hold time per direction. Default 3.

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Fraction of the range to reach each way. Default 0.8.

inputs.name: root_slip_m
inputs.description: Allowed root displacement (measured only for the info sheet's root_body). Default 0.005.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

inputs.name: hold_root
inputs.description: Weld a free root body to the world for the test (a hand or the table holds a drawer unit or a box while its part is moved). Default True.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Every tested joint travelled both ways and the root (when measured) stayed put.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence naming the joints that failed, if any.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: per joint: type, range, forward {fraction, t80_s, q_end}, back {fraction, t80_s, q_end}, root_slip_m (None when not measured), ok.

tools.name: articulation_axis_semantics_check
tools.title: Articulation axis semantics check
tools.summary: For every Stage 1 articulation (prismatic, revolute, screw, free part), finds joints of the matching MuJoCo type in the object and checks their world axis, opening direction and hinge location at keyframe 0 against the direction words of the Stage 1 description (vertical, horizontal, left-right, toward the operator, along the long axis, the back wall, down and left in the image).
tools.description: A drawer whose slide opens away from the operator, a lid hinged on the front wall instead of the back, or a screw cap on a horizontal axis still compile and pass a joint-travel test, and Stage 3 then pulls in the wrong direction. Stage 1 states each articulation in words (articulation.joint_type and .axis). The check maps joint_type to MuJoCo joints in the object's bodies (prismatic -> slide, revolute -> hinge, screw -> a hinge and a slide, free_part -> a free joint or a weld on a part; other -> not judged) and reads cues from the axis text: intrinsic axis cues use the first clause; directional clauses and parentheticals are conditioned on opening or closing when specified. Conditions about changing object poses are not axis constraints. 'vertical', 'up', 'down' -> axis within angle_tol_deg of world z; 'horizontal' -> within angle_tol_deg of the table plane; 'left-right', 'side to side', 'image's horizontal' -> along the camera's horizontal (world x without a camera); 'toward the operator/camera/person' -> the opening direction (the joint's larger range side) points to -y within 60 deg, 'away from the operator', 'into the work' -> +y. Directions explicitly describing closing are reversed before checking opening; toward-and-away travel without an opening condition checks the unsigned operator axis. Contradictory or unresolved opening/closing cues fail with that reason. 'long axis' -> along the longest dimension of the object's fixed body (skipped when its two largest dimensions are within 15%); 'back/rear/far' or 'front/near' with 'wall/edge/side' -> the hinge anchor lies on that side of the fixed body's centre; '<up|down|left|right> in the image' (with a camera) -> the projected opening direction lies within 90 deg of the combined image direction (Stage 1's image words are approximate). An articulation passes when some joint of the right type satisfies every cue; no cue means only the type is judged. Assumes the rig frame (operator at -y, z up).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: semantic
inputs.description: scene_semantics.json (Stage 1).

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json mapping Stage 1 ids to bodies.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json for image-direction cues and the image horizontal.

inputs.name: angle_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed angle between a joint axis and a cued axis. Default 30.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; articulations [{id, joint_type, cues, candidates [{joint, type, axis, open_dir, anchor, failed}], verdict}].

tools.name: articulation_check
tools.title: Articulation check
tools.summary: An object declared articulated is built with at least one hinge or slide joint that has a usable range, not as a rigid free body.
tools.description: Stage 1 decides what moves; stage 2 must build it that way. A drawer added as a rigid mesh passes every geometric check and still cannot open. For each named object the verifier collects the bodies that belong to it (the body itself and everything whose name starts with its slug) and looks for hinge or slide joints on them. It fails when there is none, when the object is a free rigid body instead, or when the joint has a degenerate range (`min_travel`: 3 mm for a slide, 5 degrees for a hinge, summed over the object's joints of a kind so a sprung contact split into stages counts). It also drives each joint across its range and reports whether the moving part actually displaces, which catches a joint attached to the wrong link.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Names of the objects that must be articulated.

inputs.name: min_travel
inputs.description: Smallest joint range accepted: metres for slides, radians for hinges. Default 0.003 m / 0.087 rad.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per object: joints [{joint, type, range, travel, moves_part_m}], verdict in {articulated, no mechanism, rigid free body, degenerate range}.

tools.name: asset_path_portability_check
tools.title: Asset path portability check
tools.summary: Every mesh, texture, height field, skin and include path of an MJCF resolves relative to the scene's folder and exists; absolute or machine-specific paths, missing files and paths escaping the allowed root fail.
tools.description: A scene that names its meshes by absolute path opens only on the machine that wrote it: a reused scene copied into a repository or another run keeps pointing at the original checkout, and the copy silently depends on files that are not shipped with it. The check reads the MJCF as text (following <include> files), resolves every file attribute the way MuJoCo does (meshdir / texturedir / assetdir from <compiler>, relative to the main model's folder), and fails a reference that is absolute, starts with '~', uses backslashes or a drive letter, does not exist, or (when `root` is given) resolves outside `root`. A compiler meshdir/texturedir/assetdir that is absolute fails the same way. Each failing reference is reported with the relative path that would replace it, so the fix is a search-and-replace. Works on the file alone; nothing is compiled.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file path (an XML string has no folder to be relative to).

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Folder every referenced file must stay inside (e.g. the run or repository root); default: no containment rule.

inputs.name: max_listed
inputs.description: Rows kept in the report per problem kind. Default 20.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; n_refs; counts {absolute, missing, outside_root, machine_specific}; bad: [{tag, name, file, resolved, problem, suggest}]; worst: the first bad reference.

tools.name: asset_scene_consistency_check
tools.title: Asset / scene consistency check
tools.summary: For every object of scene_recon.json, the bodies of its recorded asset_xml are the bodies the scene has under that object's root: Stage 3 builds its hand scenes from the asset file, so an asset that lacks a part the scene has (a cable's plug) or has parts the scene lacks hides them from every grasp tool.
tools.description: Compiles each object's `asset_xml`, takes its body names, and finds the object's bodies in the scene: the subtree of its `root_body` (plus the bodies the entry lists). The scene names an asset's bodies with a prefix (<prefix>_<asset body>, the prefix stage_on_bench gave it), found from the root body. Issues: an asset body the scene does not have, a scene body of the object the asset does not have (both with names), an asset that does not compile, a root body missing from the scene. Deformables simulated only in Isaac (no MuJoCo body) and objects without an asset are skipped and reported.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: The Stage 2 scene.xml.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json (objects with id, root_body, asset_xml, bodies).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, objects {id: {prefix, asset_bodies, scene_bodies, missing_in_scene, missing_in_asset}}, skipped {id: reason}.

tools.name: badqacc_reset_audit
tools.title: BADQACC reset audit
tools.summary: Frames where many degrees of freedom snap back to qpos0 or a keyframe at once (MuJoCo's silent reset after a bad acceleration), and frozen stretches where the whole state stops changing across phases.
tools.description: No other audit looks for this. For every frame t it compares the state with qpos0 and with every keyframe: a qpos entry 'snaps' when it was more than from_tol away from the reference on frame t-1 and within eps of it on frame t. A frame where at least min_dofs entries snap and they are at least min_frac of the entries that were away, and they jump at least five times farther than they moved the frame before, is a reset (a physics run never lands thirty joints exactly on their initial values by chance, and an interpolation that ends on qpos0 arrives with an ordinary step). It also measures runs of frames whose entire state is bit-identical to the previous frame: a physics-executed episode never repeats exactly, so a frozen run that crosses a phase boundary (the plan moved on, the state did not) or lasts longer than freeze_max_s is the executor's guard copying the last good frame forward after an instability. Reports each reset frame with the reference it snapped to and how many entries snapped (robot joints and objects separately), and the frozen runs.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in (qpos0 and keyframes come from it).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: min_dofs
inputs.description: Fewest snapped qpos entries that make a reset. Default 6.

inputs.name: min_frac
inputs.description: Fewest snapped entries as a share of those that were away from the reference. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: How close to the reference counts as on it. Default 1e-6.

inputs.name: from_tol
inputs.description: How far from the reference an entry must have been the frame before. Default 1e-3.

inputs.name: freeze_min_frames
inputs.description: Shortest frozen run that counts when it crosses a phase boundary (at 30 fps). Default 3.

inputs.name: freeze_max_s
inputs.description: A frozen run longer than this fails anywhere. Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {frame, label, reference, snapped, robot_snapped, object_snapped}; resets (list); frozen_runs (list of {first, last, labels}).

tools.name: battery_seat_test
tools.title: Battery seat test
tools.summary: Seated battery must stay in its sprung slot; a battery released mid-insertion must be ejected by the spring.
tools.description: Builds a combined model of a battery case slot and a cell (the cell's XML is attached under the prefix 'bat_'), then runs two trials from posed initial states with no forces applied afterwards. Seated: the cell is placed on the compressed spring plate behind the bump; after 1.5 s its drift must be under 1 mm and the spring must still hold more than half its seated compression. Eject: the cell is placed 2 mm deeper with the button end tilted 25 degrees up, clear of the bump, and released; after 0.8 s the spring must have re-extended (under 1 mm left) and the cell must have travelled more than 6 mm down the slot. Both must hold for the slot to pass. This is how the case's bump height, spring preload and slot clearance are checked to be a mechanism rather than a cosmetic recess.

inputs.name: case_built
inputs.description: The dict construct_battery_case returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: battery_built
inputs.description: The dict construct_battery returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: slot
inputs.description: Which slot to test. Default 0.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Both the seated and the eject trials passed.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence with the drift and the ejection distance.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: slot, seated {drift_mm, spring_holds_mm, ok}, eject {thrown_mm, spring_after_mm, ok}.

tools.name: bead_on_cable_slide_test
tools.title: Bead on cable slide test
tools.summary: Force-only trial of a holed bead on a cable: pushed coaxially at the cable's free tip it must thread on, slide along the cable, come to rest against the cable's fat stop section (a cap or bead column) without passing it, and stay threaded under a sideways push.
tools.description: Rebuilds the cable straight with tool_library.common.cable from the given cross-section (radius, length, segments, stop section of cap_radius over cap_length at end b; or reads them from a construct_rope params JSON), pins both ends to the world with welds (on end links made 1e4 times heavier: a weld's give is about F tc^2 / m, which on a thin cord's 0.03 g end link let a 0.2 N push swing the whole 'pinned' cable 10 cm), switches gravity off, and inserts the bead asset (any MJCF whose bead body has a free joint; its actuators, contacts, assets and equalities are copied along) with its bore axis along the cable, its centre a few millimetres beyond the free tip (end a). Phase 1 pushes the bead along +x with a speed-regulated force capped at push_force_N: it must pass the tip (thread on), travel at least half of the thin section, and stop with its centre before the start of the stop section and no more than half its height plus the stop radius plus 2 mm short of it. Phase 2 keeps the axial push and adds lateral_force_N sideways: the bead centre must stay within the bore radius plus tol_m of the cable's current centreline (it is threaded, not resting beside the cable). While the bead is at rest (below 1 cm/s) no bead-cable contact may penetrate deeper than max_penetration_m; the transient peak of impacts is reported, not judged. Assumes the bead's bore axis is a principal axis of its body frame (bead_axis) and its collision geoms are distributed symmetrically about the bore (their mean position is the bore centre).

inputs.name: bead_xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the bead asset (one free body; e.g. construct_magnetic_ring with magnet_force_N 0).

inputs.name: bore_radius
inputs.description: Radius of the bead's hole, metres (the free radius the cable passes through).

inputs.name: bead_height
inputs.description: Length of the bead along its bore axis, metres.

inputs.name: bead_body
inputs.description: Name of the bead body; None takes the first top-level body with a free joint. Default None

inputs.name: bead_axis
inputs.description: Bore axis in the bead body frame: 'x', 'y' or 'z'. Default 'z'

inputs.name: cable_params_json
inputs.description: A construct_rope params JSON to read radius, cap_radius_scale, cap_length_b, density, friction and stiffness from (its length is replaced by cable_length). Default None

inputs.name: cable_radius
inputs.description: Cable radius, metres (required without cable_params_json).

inputs.name: cap_radius
inputs.description: Radius of the stop section at end b, metres; None or <= cable_radius for no stop. Default None

inputs.name: cap_length
inputs.description: Length of the stop section at end b, metres (0 for none). Default 0.04

inputs.name: cable_length
inputs.description: Length of the straight test cable, metres. Default: the stop section plus 15 cm (at least 0.16)

inputs.name: segments
inputs.description: Capsule segments of the test cable. Default 24

inputs.name: push_force_N
inputs.description: Cap on the axial push, newtons. Default 0.05

inputs.name: push_speed
inputs.description: Target sliding speed of the push, m/s. Default 0.08

inputs.name: lateral_force_N
inputs.description: Sideways push in phase 2, newtons. Default 0.2

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Slack on the threaded-distance bound, metres. Default 0.0007

inputs.name: max_penetration_m
inputs.description: Deepest allowed bead-cable penetration, metres. Default 0.001

inputs.name: timestep
inputs.description: Simulation timestep, seconds. Default 0.002

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Folder for the merged test MJCF; None uses a temporary folder. Default None

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here as JSON. Default None

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; cable_pin_drift_m (how far the pinned cable ends moved; over 1 cm voids the trial); insertion {passed_tip, travel_m, final_gap_to_stop_m, stopped_at_stop, has_stop}; lateral {max_offset_from_centreline_m, bound_m, threaded}; max_penetration_m (while the bead is at rest, judged); peak_transient_penetration_m (impacts, reported); params used; merged_xml.

tools.name: bimanual_pose_clearance_test
tools.title: Two-hand pose clearance test
tools.summary: Put the left and right hands at their grasp poses and along their open-hand approach paths in one model and fail when the two hands come closer than a minimum distance anywhere.
tools.description: Every hand scene holds one hand, so two grasps solved separately on neighbouring parts (two magnetic rings 3 cm apart, a bottle and its cap, a box and its lid) can each pass every grasp test and still drive the hands into each other on the bench (measured on the EgoDex rings: palm into palm 14.8 mm and index into the other hand's fingers 17.9 mm, seen only in the bench physics). Both hands (with the collision hulls the bench uses) are placed by their wrist poses, which share the bench's world frame, and the smallest distance between any collision geom of one hand and any of the other is measured with mj_geomDistance: (1) both hands at their poses with the executor's closed targets and its clamp; (2) the left hand coming down its approach (approach_m back along the executor's retreat axis, open shape, n_samples steps) and closing while the right hand holds its pose, (3) the same with the roles swapped, and (4) both approaching together. Fails when any phase gets closer than min_clearance_mm; the issue names the phase, the step, the two closest geoms and how far they are apart (negative = interpenetration).

inputs.name: left_pose / right_pose
inputs.description: the two grasp poses (world frame) or their JSON

inputs.name: left_scene / right_scene
inputs.description: optional hand scenes: their hand_xml are used (default setup/robot/sharpa_<side>.xml)

inputs.name: min_clearance_mm
inputs.description: smallest allowed hand-hand distance (default 10: two 2 mm / 2 deg calibration errors at a 0.1 m lever)

inputs.name: approach_m
inputs.description: pre-grasp distance along each retreat axis (default 0.08, the executor's)

inputs.name: n_samples
inputs.description: steps along each approach (default 12) and the close (4)

inputs.name: check_approach
inputs.description: also check the approach phases (default True)

inputs.name: approach_sides
inputs.description: hands whose approach is checked (default both; ['right'] when the left hand is already holding and does not move)

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: the hands keep min_clearance_mm everywhere

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: the phase, step and geoms that came too close, and what to change

outputs.name: min_clearance_mm
outputs.description: the smallest hand-hand distance over every phase

outputs.name: phases
outputs.description: per phase: min_mm, at (step), closest geom pair, ok

tools.name: bimanual_sync_gate
tools.title: Bimanual sync gate
tools.summary: For every Stage 1 subgoal whose acting_hand is 'both', both hands act inside overlapping time windows (not one after the other, not one hand alone).
tools.description: A demonstration in which two hands press a lid, close two flaps or carry two bricks at once is not reproduced by one hand doing it and then the other. For each Stage 1 subgoal with acting_hand 'both', the manifest entries that cover it give the window (their frame span); a hand is active when it actually touches one of the subgoal's objects (Stage 1 object_refs resolved through scene_recon; 1 mm contact margin), so a left hand that keeps holding the battery holder while the right hand presses counts. A simultaneous two-hand entry {motion: 'both', hands: {left: {...}, right: {...}}, sync} is subject to the same physical contact evidence. The subgoal passes when both hands are active together for at least min_overlap_s. A sequential deviation cannot waive that requirement. The issue names the two activity spans, or the hand that never acts.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 scene_semantics.json.

inputs.name: trajectory_manifest_json
inputs.description: Stage 3 trajectory_manifest.json.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: The delivered trajectory npz.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json; default the manifest's scene_recon.

inputs.name: min_overlap_s
inputs.description: Time both hands must be active together, s. Default 0.2.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; subgoals [{index, goal, entries, window, active {left, right}, overlap_s, sequential_deviation, ok, note}].

tools.name: body_contact_window_check
tools.title: Body contact window check
tools.summary: On the frames of an executed episode, named body pairs must stay in contact (a carried ring kept on two held rings, a part kept on its support) and other pairs must be apart at the end or at some frame (two held parts pulled apart).
tools.description: Replays the qpos of an executed trajectory (npz with 'qpos', optional 'subgoal') in the scene it was executed in and, on every evaluated frame, runs forward kinematics and collision detection and lists the contacts between the subtrees of each named pair (a body and every body rigidly or jointedly below it, so a ring's magnet child counts as the ring). A pair is 'touching' on a frame when some contact between the two subtrees has distance <= tol_m (contacts inside a geom margin count, so attraction zones of magnets register). touching pairs must touch on at least touch_frac of the frames (default all); apart pairs must have no contact closer than apart_m at the frame 'end' (default), on 'any' frame or on 'all' frames. Frames are a [start, end] window, or the frames whose subgoal index matches (the trajectory must then carry a 'subgoal' array), or all frames. Returns ok, issues naming the pair, the frame and the distance, and per pair the touching fraction, the first frame it lost contact and the closest distance.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz with qpos [T, nq] (and optionally subgoal [T]).

inputs.name: touching
inputs.description: Body pairs that must stay in contact. Default []

inputs.name: apart
inputs.description: Body pairs that must not be in contact (see apart_at). Default []

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [start, end] frame window (inclusive), or None.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Evaluate the frames whose subgoal index equals this, or None. Raises when the trajectory has no 'subgoal' array.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Contact distance below which a pair touches. Default 0.002

inputs.name: touch_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of frames a touching pair must touch. Default 1.0

inputs.name: apart_m
inputs.description: Smallest contact distance an apart pair may have. Default 0.0

inputs.name: apart_at
inputs.description: 'end', 'any' or 'all' frames for the apart pairs. Default end

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Evaluate every stride-th frame (the last frame always). Default 1

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.
