outputs.description: ok; issues; frames [start, end]; n_evaluated; touching {pair: {frac, first_lost_frame, max_gap_frame, min_dist_m}}; apart {pair: {apart_ok, closest_m, frame}}.

tools.name: box_enclosure_check
tools.title: Box enclosure check
tools.summary: A box-like object must enclose a cavity: from the centre of its interior, rays must hit its own bottom and all four side walls within its extent, the interior must be hollow (sample points not inside any of its geoms), and the top is reported as open or closed (a lid); a slab with a hinged panel, or a solid block, fails with the missing faces named.
tools.description: Collects the object's bodies (the named body with its subtree, or every body with the name as prefix) and their collidable or visible geoms, builds the object's axis-aligned extent in its root body frame, and takes the interior centre at mid height. Hollowness: a grid of interior sample points (the extent shrunk by `wall_margin`) is tested for containment in the object's box, cylinder, sphere and capsule geoms (mesh geoms by their bounding sphere); the cavity fraction must exceed `min_cavity`. Faces: rays cast from the centre along -z, +x, -x, +y, -y in the object frame must hit one of the object's geoms before leaving the extent; +z tells whether the top is closed. With `expect_top` ('open' | 'closed' | None) the top state is also checked. Reports the face hits with distances, the cavity fraction, the interior size, and one issue per missing face. Meant for cardboard boxes, trays, drawers, bins and gift boxes; a cup is a vessel (vessel_containment_test), not a box.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model (an asset or the whole scene).

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: Root body name or name prefix of the box.

inputs.name: min_walls
inputs.description: Side walls required (of 4). Default 4.

inputs.name: require_bottom
inputs.description: Default True.

inputs.name: expect_top
inputs.description: 'open', 'closed' or None (not checked).

inputs.name: min_cavity
inputs.description: Fraction of interior sample points that must be empty. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: wall_margin
inputs.description: Shrink of the extent for the interior samples. Default 0.012.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State to evaluate; default keyframe 0 or qpos0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; faces: {bottom, x_pos, x_neg, y_pos, y_neg, top: {hit, geom, distance_m}}; cavity_fraction; interior_size_m; n_geoms; top_state.

tools.name: box_enclosure_check_tiled_bottom
tools.title: Box enclosure check (tiled bottom)
tools.summary: A box-like object must enclose a cavity: rays from the centre of its interior must hit its own bottom and all four side walls, the interior must be hollow, and the top is reported open or closed; the bottom may be tiled from several thin slabs (a rounded-rectangle dish), whose union sets the interior extent.
tools.description: Fork of box_enclosure_check for containers whose floor is not one box geom but a tiling of thin horizontal slabs (a rounded-rectangle glass dish built from a centre slab plus side strips, a tray with a segmented base). Collects the object's bodies (the named body with its subtree, or every body with the name as prefix) and their visible or collidable geoms, expresses every box geom in the root body frame, finds the largest thin horizontal box near the lowest point, then takes as the bottom the UNION of every thin horizontal box whose underside lies within `tile_tol` of that slab's underside and whose top is within `tile_tol` of its top. The interior extent is the union's footprint and the wall height is the tallest geom rising from inside it. Hollowness: a 7x7x5 grid of interior points (extent shrunk by `wall_margin`) is tested for containment in the object's primitive geoms; the cavity fraction must exceed `min_cavity`. Faces: rays from the interior centre along -z, +x, -x, +y, -y (object frame) must hit one of the object's geoms before leaving the extent (+2 cm); +z tells whether the top is closed, checked against `expect_top`. Reports face hits with distances, cavity fraction, interior size, the bottom tiles used, and one issue per missing face.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model (an asset or the whole scene).

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: Root body name or name prefix of the box.

inputs.name: min_walls
inputs.description: Side walls required (of 4). Default 4.

inputs.name: require_bottom
inputs.description: Default True.

inputs.name: expect_top
inputs.description: 'open', 'closed' or None (not checked).

inputs.name: min_cavity
inputs.description: Fraction of interior sample points that must be empty. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: wall_margin
inputs.description: Shrink of the extent for the interior samples. Default 0.012.

inputs.name: tile_tol
inputs.description: How close in height another slab must be to join the bottom tiling. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State to evaluate; default keyframe 0 or qpos0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; faces: {bottom, x_pos, x_neg, y_pos, y_neg, top: {hit, geom, distance_m}}; cavity_fraction; interior_size_m; bottom_tiles; n_geoms; top_state; walls_found.

tools.name: cable_drag_test
tools.title: Cable drag test
tools.summary: Drags a cable by capped end forces (lift, swing, drop, tension, loop) and checks inextensibility, span and self-collision.
tools.description: Loads a cable built by construct_rope. First it drops the cable as a vertical coil (turns 1.96 radii apart, i.e. just touching, 1 cm up) and counts the contacts between non-neighbouring segments as the turns rest on each other: a cable that cannot touch itself falls through its own turns and cannot be knotted. Then it resets the cable straight and runs the thread driver: settle, lift one end 22 cm with a <= 0.9 N spring-damper pull, swing it in a circle whose radius scales with the span, lower it, let go, pull both ends apart to 92% of the nominal length, then cross the ends into a loop. Every step records the centreline length (stretch), the end-to-end span and the count of self-contacts between non-adjacent segments. CABLE OK requires max stretch under 5%, max span at most 102% of the nominal length and at least one self-contact in the coil drop or the drag. A cable that stretches is under-constrained; one that never touches itself cannot be knotted. The pull is a force on the end link's centre of mass, damped with that point's own velocity (MuJoCo's cvel is the velocity at the cable's overall centre of mass, which on a thin light cord turned the damping into a spin feedback that went unstable within seconds), so cords down to 1.25 mm radius run at the asset's timestep. Every phase, the coil drop included, fails loudly on a MuJoCo bad-acceleration reset.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_rope returned, the path of its <name>_params.json, or any MJCF holding a cable (a path, or a dict with just 'xml'): the cable's links are found in the model (the longest chain of ball-jointed bodies under a free root, or the one named after built['name']) when the dict does not list bodies.first / segments / last, and its length, radius and start are read from the model when there is no params_json.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: z of the cable's resting centreline; the lift is measured from it. Default: one radius above the asset's own floor (z = 0).

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Time the cable is left to land on the floor before the trial. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: span
inputs.description: Working span for the swing radius (0.35 x span). Default: the cable length.

inputs.name: out_mp4
inputs.description: Also render the trial to this video.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: True when the verdict is CABLE OK.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: CABLE OK / CABLE SUSPECT with the numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: max_force_N, max_stretch_pct, max_span_m, self_contacts, nominal_length_m, drag_self_contacts, coil_drop {coil_radius_m, coil_turns, max_self_contacts}.

outputs.name: video
outputs.description: The rendered mp4 when out_mp4 was given.

tools.name: camera_hand_overlay_check
tools.title: Camera hand overlay check
tools.summary: Renders the robot hands at the setup's home keyframe through the registered video camera and compares them with the hand masks of frame 0 (overall IoU and per-hand centroid offsets): the paper's hand-overlay check that the camera is registered to the footage, for recordings that start with the hands at home.
tools.description: The bench recordings start with both hands resting at the setup's home pose (keyframe 'home': palm down at the bottom corners of the ego frame), and the station positions and home pose were fitted to them, so the rendered home hands must land on the hands in the first frame when the camera is right; a camera registered to other footage or with a wrong pitch shows as an offset. The hands are rendered by segmentation from the scene (default: the setup's scene.xml) at its home keyframe (or keyframe 0) through camera.json, split into left and right; the hand mask of frame 0 (any segmenter, e.g. masks/hands.png) is split into connected components, each assigned to the nearer rendered hand. The overall IoU must be at least min_iou and each matched hand's centroid must be within max_offset_frac of the image diagonal and, unless it overlaps well (IoU 0.6), its rendered area must be within area_band of the frame's (a wrong focal length or height scales the hands). When the check applies, an empty hands mask fails (a wrong mask path or a missed segmentation). A recording that does not start at home cannot be judged: start_at_home=None applies the check only when camera.json says source 'setup' (the bench camera); footage from other sessions (source given, estimate, egodex) starts wherever the person's hands were and is reported as not applicable unless start_at_home=True.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json path or dict.

inputs.name: hands_mask
inputs.description: Binary mask of the hands in frame 0 (masks/hands.png).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene whose robot is rendered. Default: the setup's scene.xml.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (home keyframe name). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: start_at_home
inputs.description: Whether frame 0 shows the hands at the home pose. Default None: true for source 'setup' cameras.

inputs.name: min_iou
inputs.description: Smallest overall IoU. Default 0.4.

inputs.name: area_band
inputs.description: Accepted robot/frame hand area ratio per hand when its IoU is below 0.6 (a wrong focal length or height scales the hands). Default [0.5, 2.0].

inputs.name: max_offset_frac
inputs.description: Largest centroid offset per hand, as a fraction of the image diagonal. Default 0.06.

inputs.name: min_area_px
inputs.description: Mask components smaller than this (at the camera resolution) are noise. Default 200.

inputs.name: max_side
inputs.description: Render at most this many pixels on the long side (masks are compared at that size). Default 960.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; applicable; iou; hands [{side, robot_px, human_px, iou, centroid_offset_px, offset_frac}]; image [w, h].

tools.name: camera_registration_check
tools.title: Camera registration check
tools.summary: Checks a registered video camera (camera.json): its intrinsics and extrinsics agree with each other, the scene's camera of the same name is the same camera, its height, pitch and roll are those of a camera over a table, and the table plane it implies lies under every object mask's contact line (below the horizon, in front of the camera, within range and on the table).
tools.description: Every Stage 2 placement is a back-projection through the video camera onto the table plane, so a camera registered to the wrong footage, with a stale focal length or with the scene's copy out of sync silently puts every object in the wrong place at the wrong size. The check reads camera.json (rigcam convention: fx, fy, cx, cy, R_cv, pos, quat_wxyz) and: (1) consistency - fovy matches fy and the height, fx = fy within 2%, the principal point within 10% of the image centre, R_cv a rotation, quat_wxyz the same rotation in MuJoCo's convention, and any recorded pitch/yaw/height_above_table equal to what R_cv and pos give; (2) the scene camera (scene_camera, default video_cam) has the same pose (pos_tol_m, angle_tol_deg) and fovy; (3) plausibility - height above the tabletop in height_band, optical axis pitched pitch_band below horizontal, |roll| at most max_roll_deg, and the optical axis meets the table within max_range_m; (4) with masks, each object mask's lowest pixels (where it stands on the table) lie below the table plane's horizon line, and back-projected onto z = 0 they land in front of the camera, within max_range_m and on the table (the scene's table geom, else setup.yaml's table) grown by table_margin_m. Masks may be a dict {id: path}, a list of paths or a folder (every PNG except those named hands*).

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json path or dict.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF whose camera must equal camera.json and whose table bounds the contacts.

inputs.name: scene_camera
inputs.description: Name of the scene's video camera. Default 'video_cam'.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Object masks of frame 0: {id: png}, [png], or a masks/ folder.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder for the table extent when no scene is given. Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: height_band
inputs.description: Camera height above the tabletop, metres. Default [0.15, 2.0].

inputs.name: pitch_band
inputs.description: Optical axis below horizontal, degrees. Default [5, 89.9].

inputs.name: max_roll_deg
inputs.description: Largest roll about the optical axis. Default 20.

inputs.name: max_range_m
inputs.description: Farthest table point a contact may back-project to. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed scene-camera position difference. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: angle_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed scene-camera orientation / fovy difference. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: table_margin_m
inputs.description: Margin around the table for back-projected contacts. Default 0.05.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; camera {height_m, pitch_deg, yaw_deg, roll_deg, fovy_deg, axis_range_m}; consistency {...}; scene_camera {pos_diff_m, angle_diff_deg, fovy_diff_deg}; masks [{id, contact_v, horizon_v, contact_xy, range_m, on_table, verdict}].

tools.name: camera_visibility_audit
tools.title: Camera visibility audit
tools.summary: The manipulated objects and the acting hands project inside the video camera's image (camera json or a scene camera) on the frames that matter: while an object moves or is touched, while a hand touches one.
tools.description: No other audit looks through the camera. The camera is a camera.json (width, height, fx, fy, cx, cy, pos, quat_wxyz in MuJoCo's convention: looking along its -z, y up; Stage 2 writes one) or a camera of the scene by name (default: 'video_cam' when the scene has it, else 'ego'; intrinsics from its fovy and width x height). On every frame each free object's centre of mass and each hand's palm are projected; the point counts as out of view when it is behind the camera or farther than outside_frac (default 0.2) of the image size beyond its border: a palm or object centre a little past the edge still shows most of the body, one a fifth of the image beyond it shows none (the paper's executed episodes reach 0.16 at the edges of egocentric frames). Frames that matter: for an object, those where it moves faster than 1 cm/s or a robot hand touches it; for a hand, those where it touches a free object. It fails when an object or hand is out of view on more than max_out_frac (default 0.25) of its frames that matter, or for a contiguous stretch longer than max_out_s (default 1 s). Reports per body the share of frames out of view, the longest stretch and its first frame and phase label.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json path or dict, or the name of a scene camera. Default 'video_cam' if present, else 'ego'.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: width, height
inputs.description: Image size for a scene camera without a resolution of its own. Default 640 x 480 (the human video's size matters: pass the Stage 2 camera.json when the video is not 4:3).

inputs.name: outside_frac
inputs.description: How far beyond the image border, as a share of the image size, a centre may lie and still count as in view. Default 0.2.

inputs.name: max_out_frac
inputs.description: Largest share of frames that matter out of view. Default 0.25.

inputs.name: max_out_s
inputs.description: Longest contiguous stretch out of view. Default 1.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, out_frac, longest_out_s, first_out_frame, label}; bodies {name: frames that matter, out of view, longest stretch}; camera.

tools.name: collision_visual_alignment_check
tools.title: Collision-visual alignment check
tools.summary: For every visible, non-colliding geom of every object, measures how far its surface lies outside the object's collision geoms and flags exposed visual parts that stick out of the physics by more than a tolerance (a collision primitive smaller than the mesh it stands for, a visual mesh moved off its collider).
tools.description: When a collision primitive is smaller than the visual mesh it stands for, the hand visibly sinks into the object (or the object into the table) with no contact at all: the Sharpa palm box once left the visible palm 17 mm outside physics. Each object (the Stage 2 manifest's objects, else every top-level non-robot body) is posed at keyframe 0. For each visible geom that does not collide (group 0-2, alpha > 0), its surface points (mesh vertices, or samples of a primitive) are measured against the object's collision geoms: signed distance to each (primitives exactly, meshes as their convex hull, which is what MuJoCo collides), keeping the nearest. A point counts as exposed when it lies more than tol_m outside every collision geom AND more than tol_m outside the convex hull of all the object's collision geometry, so decorations enclosed by the object (the parts inside a computer case, a spring in a slot, a straw in a bottle) are not reported. Thin decorations (a geom whose smallest extent is below thin_m: wires, labels, stripes) are skipped. A geom fails when its worst exposed point is beyond tol_m and at least min_frac of its points are exposed; a small geom (largest extent below decoration_m) that no collision geom comes near is a loose decoration and only warned about.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json naming the objects. Default: top-level non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these objects (ids or body names).

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed visual surface outside the physics, metres. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: thin_m
inputs.description: Visual geoms thinner than this are decorations and skipped, metres. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: min_frac
inputs.description: Smallest fraction of a geom's points that must be exposed for it to fail. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: decoration_m
inputs.description: A geom smaller than this (largest extent) that no collision geom touches at all is a loose decoration (a plug, a sticker): reported as a warning, not a failure. Default 0.015.

inputs.name: ignore
inputs.description: Geom or body names (substrings) not to judge.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; warnings (loose decorations); geoms [{geom, body, object, n_points, max_out_m, exposed_frac, verdict}]; skipped (thin or no collision); worst (largest exposed distance, m).

tools.name: color_match_check
tools.title: Colour match check
tools.summary: The dominant surface colour of a constructed object is within a distance of the colour palette measured from the video.
tools.description: Constructed objects are painted with measured colours, never invented ones. The verifier gathers every visible geom of the object (the body and the bodies named with its prefix), weights each colour by the geom's volume so a large carcass counts and a small handle does not, takes the dominant colour, and compares it with the closest entry of the measured palette in RGB. A distance above `max_dist` (0.30 in 0..1 RGB) fails. Only the dominant surface is judged: a palette measured over an object's whole mask says nothing about small hardware such as a pull.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: Body name or name prefix of the constructed object.

inputs.name: palette
inputs.description: Measured colours: [{rgb: [r,g,b], weight}] or plain [r,g,b] triples in 0..1.

inputs.name: max_dist
inputs.description: Largest accepted RGB distance. Default 0.30.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; dominant_rgb; closest_palette_rgb; dist; colours: every colour with its volume share.

tools.name: combined_hold_state_test
tools.title: Combined hold from recorded state
tools.summary: Test every object retained by one hand from an executed grasp_more state, with the real rigid arm and actual finger commands.
tools.description: Replays recorded controls to the specified frame without resetting object or hand coordinates. From that complete simulator state, the unchanged bounded arm/finger controller holds and moves each arm joint three degrees in both directions. Every rigid object must remain in hand, clear of external supports, within 20 mm and 15 degrees of its initial wrist-relative pose, with penetration at most 3 mm. Use the final frame of a successful grasp_more segment after lifting every object clear of its support. The manifest independently binds the frame and complete retained-object set to the trusted execution history. This tests the actual combined hold; multi_object_hold_test remains useful for candidate search before the first grasp. Flex objects and dynamic mechanism equalities are currently unsupported.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: The executed rigid scene_physics.xml.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Complete actual trajectory.npz with dense control/state recording.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Last frame of the grasp_more segment, with all held parts lifted.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: left or right.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: All objects still retained by this hand, in acquisition order.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, prefix replay and per-object continuous stress measurements.

tools.name: compile_determinism_check
tools.title: Compile determinism check
tools.summary: Compiles the scene several times in this process and once in a fresh interpreter in another working directory and compares a stable hash of its sizes and key arrays; optionally compares with a recorded hash and rebuilds the scene twice with its builder to catch unseeded randomness.
tools.description: Stages hand scenes to each other by file: Stage 2 verifies a scene, Stage 3 executes it, Stage 4 randomizes it. If the file compiles to a different model later (a mesh rewritten in place, an include edited, a builder that draws random numbers without a seed), every verdict reached on the earlier model is void and nothing says so. The check fingerprints the compiled model: its sizes, its options and a digest of each key array (body masses and poses, joint ranges, geom sizes and contact parameters, mesh vertices, actuators, equalities, keyframes), rounded to 1e-9. It compiles `repeats` times in-process and, with `fresh_process`, once more in a new interpreter started in another directory, and fails on any difference, naming the arrays (MuJoCo's in-process asset cache can serve a mesh rewritten within the same second, which only the fresh interpreter sees). With `expected_hash` (the hash a manifest recorded when the scene was verified) it fails when the scene has changed since. With `rebuild` (a callable, or a command line list, that regenerates `scene`) it runs the builder twice and fails if the two rebuilt models differ.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file path.

inputs.name: repeats
inputs.description: In-process compiles to compare. Default 2.

inputs.name: fresh_process
inputs.description: Also compile in a fresh interpreter in another working directory. Default True.

inputs.name: expected_hash
inputs.description: Hash recorded earlier for this scene (the report's 'hash').

inputs.name: rebuild
inputs.description: Builder that rewrites `scene`: a function of no arguments, or a command line run twice.

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: Time limit per subprocess (fresh compile, builder run). Default 300.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; hash (of the file's current content: the fresh interpreter's when it ran); in_process_hash; n_compiles; fresh_process_hash; differences: [{between, arrays}]; rebuild: {hashes, differing_arrays}; sizes.

tools.name: contact_check
tools.title: Contact check
tools.summary: Two bodies are in contact, at the initial state or after the scene settles.
tools.description: Asserts a task relation such as 'the cup rests on the tray'. Contacts are read from MuJoCo's own collision detection, so the answer is what the physics sees, not a distance heuristic. By default the scene is settled first (2 s) because that is the state the robot will meet; `settled=False` judges the authored initial state. Two bodies that are both fixed to the world never produce contacts in MuJoCo, so that case is reported as such instead of as a false failure. Names resolve by exact name, slug, or unique assembly-part suffix.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: First body.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Second body.

inputs.name: settled
inputs.description: Judge after settling (default) or at the initial state.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time. Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; in_contact; both_static (contact impossible); contacts: all pairs touching either body.

tools.name: contact_exclusion_audit
tools.title: Contact exclusion audit
tools.summary: Lists every way a scene can stop the robot from touching what it should touch (an <exclude> between a robot body and an object or the table, a missing or softened hand-table pair, an explicit robot pair with a gap or spongy solver parameters, object or table collision bits the arm cannot see, an object parented to or welded to a robot body) and fails on any.
tools.description: Contact is how DexAgent's objects move: a scene in which the hand passes through an object or the forearm through the table produces trajectories that look fine and cannot happen. The audit reads the compiled scene and the setup's reference (default: the repository's setup/): (1) every <exclude> body pair, failing when one side is a robot body and the other an object or the table, and when a robot-robot exclude is not in the reference; (2) the reference's explicit robot-table <pair>s (the hands collide only through pairs), which must all be present with the same condim, friction, solref, solimp, margin and gap; (3) every explicit pair between a robot geom and a non-robot geom, failing on a gap that exceeds the margin by more than gap_tol_m (penetration without force), a solref time constant above max_timeconst_s or a direct stiffness below min_stiffness, an impedance dmax below min_dmax, or condim 1 (frictionless); (4) the contype/conaffinity bits: each object geom that collides with the table must also collide with the robot arm's collision geoms, and the table geom must keep the reference's bits; (5) an object body whose parent is a robot body (MuJoCo filters parent-child contact and the object rides the hand) and an equality constraint between a robot body and an object (a glued object). Global contact switches (option flags) are physics_options_check's job.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: gap_tol_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed gap - margin of a robot pair, metres. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: max_timeconst_s
inputs.description: Largest allowed solref time constant of a robot pair. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: min_stiffness
inputs.description: Smallest allowed direct stiffness (negative solref) of a robot pair, N/m. Default 1000.

inputs.name: min_dmax
inputs.description: Smallest allowed solimp dmax of a robot pair. Default 0.5.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; excludes [{body1, body2, verdict}]; table_pairs {expected, present, changed}; robot_pairs_checked; bad_pairs; masked_geoms (object geoms the arm cannot collide with); parented_objects; robot_object_equalities.

tools.name: contact_force_check
tools.title: Contact force check
tools.summary: Normal force between a holder's subtree and a held body stays in a working range over the hold window (for a posed or stress-tested grasp; on frames of an executed episode, whose contacts carry penetration from the servo clamp, read finger_servo_saturation_audit and contact_impulse_spike_audit instead).
tools.description: For each frame of the window it writes the pose into the scene, runs a forward pass and sums the contact normal force over every contact between a geom of the holder's subtree (a hand with all its fingers) and a geom of the held body's subtree. The frame passes when the total is inside [min_n, max_n]; the window passes when at least hold_frac of its frames pass and the first and last frames do. Also reports how many distinct finger bodies touch (enclosure), the mean force, and the frame of the weakest hold. A bench scene is loaded as the executor runs it (its hand-object and hand-table contact pairs); a scene without robot hands uses its own collision geometry. The forces are those of the scene's solref/solimp, so compare them against the object's weight, which the report includes.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene with collision geometry on hand and object.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: Root body of the hand (its subtree counts).

inputs.name: held
inputs.description: Body being held (its subtree counts).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Hold window: frame indices or phase-label patterns. Default all frames.

inputs.name: min_n, max_n
inputs.description: Working force range. Defaults 0.3 and 50.

inputs.name: hold_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of window frames that must be in range. Default 0.9.

inputs.name: min_bodies
inputs.description: Distinct holder bodies that must touch (2 = a pinch). Default 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; force per frame summary (min, mean, max N), frames in range, weakest frame and label, bodies in contact, object weight N, max_depth_mm (deepest hand-object penetration over the window: sub-millimetre for a seated grip; the posed force is that depth times the pair stiffness, so a wrap whose palm the wrist presses 0.7 mm in reads 60-90 N).

tools.name: contact_impulse_spike_audit
tools.title: Contact impulse spike audit
tools.summary: Contact force spikes from inverse dynamics (objects stopped or launched by a contact at many times their weight, hands decelerated hard on contact) and from the executor's force logs when the episode carries them.
tools.description: contact_force_check bounds the holding force in a window and episode_physics_check the object speed; neither looks for impulses. Objects: on frames where the object's subtree has a contact within margin_m plus its travel over the frame (the executor's contact model), the contact force it needed, M |a_com - g| by central difference, must stay under max_force_ratio times its weight (default 4: a drop of a few centimetres onto a hard surface reads 2, a slam 5 and more). Hands: the wrist body's linear acceleration (central difference) on frames where the hand touches an object or the table (or did one frame before) must stay under max_hand_acc (default 8 m/s^2; a hand stopping from 0.3 m/s within a frame reads 9). Logs: when the trajectory carries the executor's 'wrist_force_n' (or 'hand_object_force_n'), a frame whose value exceeds log_ratio (default 4) times the median of the surrounding second and log_floor_n (default 15 N) is a servo hit. Reports the worst spike per body with its frame and phase label.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, fps, labels; optional wrist_force_n, hand_object_force_n).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: margin_m
inputs.description: Contact distance that counts (plus the frame's travel). Default 0.003.

inputs.name: max_force_ratio
inputs.description: Allowed contact force on an object, in multiples of its weight. Default 4.

inputs.name: max_hand_acc
inputs.description: Allowed wrist acceleration on contact frames, m/s^2. Default 8.

inputs.name: log_ratio, log_floor_n
inputs.description: Spike rule on logged forces: above ratio x local median and above the floor. Defaults 4, 15 N.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, frame, label, value, limit, unit}; objects {name: peak force ratio, frame}; hands {side: peak contact acceleration, frame}; logs {key: peak, frame}.

tools.name: contact_margin_gap_check
tools.title: Contact margin/gap check
tools.summary: Margins and gaps are judged under the semantics this MuJoCo actually has (measured on a probe): no collidable pair pushes from farther than `max_active_m` (bodies float, fingers stop short), no negative values, and every body an adhesion actuator pulls has a margin so it attracts before touching.
tools.description: The classic reading of MuJoCo's margin and gap (contacts detected inside margin, pushing only inside margin - gap, so margin == gap detects without force) is not what MuJoCo 3.x does: measured on two spheres, the two geoms' margins add up, a contact pushes as soon as the distance is below that margin, and gap only adds an inactive band beyond it (detected up to margin + gap, no force). So margin == gap, written to 'detect early without pushing', keeps the contact active and repels inside the margin: an object rests that far above its support and fingers stop that far short. And a margin of 0 detects nothing before touching, so an adhesion (magnet) actuator, which acts through its body's contacts, cannot attract from a distance. The check measures the semantics once (`margin_semantics` in the report), then for every collidable geom or explicit pair with a non-zero margin or gap computes, against the geoms it can collide with, the distance at which the contact starts pushing and the distance at which it is detected, and fails a geom whose contacts with margin-free geoms (supports, hands) push from farther than `max_active_m`, an explicit pair that does, negative margins or gaps, and adhesion bodies whose geoms have no margin; two margin-carrying geoms (studs of two bricks) push from the sum, which is a note since they rarely face each other. Geoms of adhesion bodies may push from their margin by design (the magnet range). At keyframe `key` it also lists the contacts that are already pushing across a gap (dist > 0) as evidence.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: max_active_m
inputs.description: Largest distance at which a contact may start pushing, metres. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe for the evidence of contacts pushing across a gap. Default 0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; margin_semantics {combine, gap_band, version}; geoms: [{geom, body, margin, gap, adhesion, worst_active_m, worst_detect_m, partner, problem}]; pairs: [{pair, margin, gap, problem}]; hovering: [{geom1, geom2, dist_m, active_m}]; worst.

tools.name: contactless_motion_audit
tools.title: Contactless motion audit
tools.summary: An object travels or turns beyond settling while no robot part touches it, directly or through a chain of touching objects, and it is not in free fall: air grasps and ghost carries.
tools.description: No existing audit relates object motion to robot contact over a whole episode (contact_force_check judges one hold window given by hand). On the scene as the bench executor runs it (hand-object pairs), each frame of each free object is classified as robot-connected when the robot touches it within margin_m (default 3 mm) or touches an object that is, recursively, or an engaged object-object constraint links it to one (a toy in a drawer the hand pulls, a cap on a bottle the hand carries). A constraint between the robot and the object does NOT connect: holding must be by contact. Frames in free fall (no contact at all, acceleration within 3 m/s^2 of gravity) are excluded; free_fall_plausibility_audit judges those. On the remaining unconnected frames, per run of consecutive moving frames (speed above 1 cm/s or 5 deg/s), the object body's net travel and rotation from its pose before the run are measured (a body rocking in place gets nowhere; parts hinged on it, a lid falling shut, are not the object moving). A run that starts within settle_s (default 1 s) of the last robot connection is settling (a released object dropping into place, a cylinder rolling to rest) and may travel up to settle_m / settle_deg (defaults 40 mm, 90 deg); any other run may travel up to move_m / move_deg (defaults 10 mm, 10 deg). Reports the worst run per object with its frames, phase labels, travel and frames since the robot last touched it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels, optional eq_active).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: margin_m
inputs.description: Contact distance that counts as touching. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Time after the last robot contact during which motion is settling. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: settle_m, settle_deg
inputs.description: Allowed net travel / rotation of a settling run. Defaults 0.04, 90.

inputs.name: move_m, move_deg
inputs.description: Allowed net travel / rotation of any other contactless run. Defaults 0.01, 10.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, frames, labels, travel_mm, rotation_deg, since_robot_frames, settling}; objects {name: worst run}.

tools.name: deformable_dimension_check
tools.title: Deformable dimension check
tools.summary: Measures each rope/cable object's length along its links and its radius at keyframe 0 and compares them with the measured centreline (a measure_rope result, or a length and radius), and, when the measurement has a centreline in the rig frame, how far the simulated rope lies from it.
tools.description: A rope built 30% short cannot make the knot the video makes, one built twice as thick does not fit the loop, and one laid 10 cm off the measured centreline starts where the hands do not reach. The rope objects are found as deformable_topology_check finds them (manifest deformables named rope/cable/..., else chains of linked bodies). Length: the polyline through the link centres in chain order plus half a link at each end (capsule/cylinder half-length; for other links half the spacing). Radius: the median capsule/cylinder/sphere radius of the links. Both are compared with the measurement: `measurement` is a measure_rope output (dict or json path with length_m, radius_m and optionally centreline_rig / points) or {length_m, radius_m}. The relative length error must be within length_tol and the radius error within radius_tol; with a rig-frame centreline, the mean distance from the link centres to it must be at most centreline_tol_m. With several ropes, `rope` names the one measured. A measurement measure_rope marked reliable: false (a coil, a crossing, an unjoined piece) fails the check with its reasons: its length is a lower bound.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: measurement
inputs.description: measure_rope output (json path or dict) or {length_m, radius_m[, centreline_rig]}.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json naming the deformable objects.

inputs.name: rope
inputs.description: The rope object to judge when the scene has several (id or root body).

inputs.name: length_tol
inputs.description: Allowed relative length error. Default 0.15.

inputs.name: radius_tol
inputs.description: Allowed relative radius error. Default 0.35.

inputs.name: centreline_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed mean distance of the links from a rig-frame centreline, metres. Default 0.03.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; rope id; n_links; length_m {scene, measured, rel_err}; radius_m {scene, measured, rel_err}; centreline_mean_dist_m.

tools.name: deformable_integrity_audit
tools.title: Deformable integrity audit
tools.summary: Cables, ropes and ribbons (capsule or box link chains) keep their length, never pass through themselves or another strand of the same cable (at a frame or between frames), and do not sink into the table or the hand.
tools.description: No other audit models a chain. Chains are found in the scene: runs of at least min_segments nested bodies each carrying one capsule (or cylinder), or one box (the flat ribbon links construct_multi_strand_cable builds), joined by ball joints (or two or three hinges), as a MuJoCo cable composite builds them, and runs of free capsule bodies linked by connect / weld equalities; a chain starts at a free end or at a branch, so each strand hanging off a multi-strand cable's junction is a chain of its own. A box link's axis is the one that runs toward its neighbour (a ribbon link may be wider than long) and its radius across the chain is its half-thickness. Per frame: (1) stretch: for constraint-linked segments, the gap between the linked anchors relative to the segment length may not exceed stretch_frac (default 0.1); (2) self-interpenetration, for segments at least two apart in a chain and for every pair of segments of two strands of one cable: the distance between two capsule axes may not fall below the sum of their radii by more than pen_m (default 2 mm, a rope pressed on itself in a knot compresses about 1 mm); two boxes may not overlap (separating-axis depth) by more than pen_m or half the thinner link's thickness, whichever is smaller (a ribbon lying through another overlaps by its whole thickness, two strips pressed together by a fingertip by 0.2 mm); (3) table: no segment's lowest point (a box's lowest corner) more than pen_m under the tabletop over the table; (4) hand: no hand collision geom more than hand_pen_m (default 4 mm) inside a segment (the scene as the bench executor runs it). Between frames: (5) self-crossing, on the same pairs as (2): for two segments that are close on consecutive frames, the side of each axis relative to the other flips (the signed volume of their four end points changes sign) while their closest points lie inside both segments at a distance under the sum of the radii: one passed through the other. A scene without a chain passes with a note. Reports the worst event per rule with frames, phase labels and segments (a pair of strands is named 'A x B').

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: min_segments
inputs.description: Shortest run of capsule or box links that counts as a chain. Default 4.

inputs.name: stretch_frac
inputs.description: Allowed anchor gap of a constraint link, as a share of the segment length. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: pen_m
inputs.description: Allowed self- and table interpenetration. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: hand_pen_m
inputs.description: Allowed hand-segment interpenetration. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Check every n-th state for rules 1-4 (rule 5 uses every pair). Default 1. Whole-episode audits use every recorded physics substep when available; explicit frames select video frames.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {rule, chain, frames, label, segments, value}; chains {name: kind, profile (capsule | box), segments, radius_m (a box's half-thickness), width_m (boxes), length_m, per-rule maxima}.

tools.name: deformable_rest_check
tools.title: Deformable model and rest check
tools.summary: Independently simulates every reconstructed cable at rest and checks all links for drift, penetration and invalid dynamics; rejects unsupported deformable representations.
tools.description: The MuJoCo cable path (a cord that a subgoal cuts, built with construct_cuttable_rope, and older MuJoCo cable reconstructions) supports flexible cable chains, including declared branches and severable joins. It does not certify a rigid proxy as cloth or a volumetric soft body. Topology is checked separately. Deformables simulated in Isaac Sim (entries with simulator 'isaac') are left out here: isaac_deformable_rest_check re-measures them from their cord specification and settled poses.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Placed scene MJCF.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: Scene reconstruction manifest.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Unforced settling duration. Default 1.

inputs.name: max_mean_drift_m
inputs.description: Maximum mean link drift. Default .02.

inputs.name: max_link_drift_m
inputs.description: Maximum single link drift. Default .05.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, objects with independently measured link drift and penetration; scope=mujoco_cable_simulation.

tools.name: deformable_shape_gate
tools.title: Deformable shape gate
tools.summary: A rope or cable's centreline on a frame (the last by default) against a target centreline (discrete Frechet distance) and/or target positions of its two ends.
tools.description: The goal predicate for a rope laid into a shape ('the rope runs left to right across the table', 'the brass end rests at the left'). The cable's segment bodies (construct_rope names them <prefix>B_first, <prefix>B_<i>, <prefix>B_last) give its centreline on the decision frame. The centreline and the target polyline are both resampled to n points by arc length and compared with the discrete Frechet distance, which respects the order along the rope (a rope folded back on itself does not match a straight target the way a point-cloud distance would); unless ordered, the rope may run either way along the target. planar (or a [k, 2] target) compares x, y only. target_ends {first, last} checks the end segments, swapped when that fits better and ordered is false. The issue names the largest deviation's location.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: rope
inputs.description: Cable name prefix (e.g. 'red_rope'); default the only cable.

inputs.name: target_points
inputs.description: Target centreline [k, 3] (or [k, 2] planar), m.

inputs.name: target_ends
inputs.description: {'first': [x, y, z], 'last': [x, y, z]} (either may be left out), m.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Frechet distance tolerance, m. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: ends_tol_m
inputs.description: End position tolerance, m. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: ordered
inputs.description: The rope's first segment must match the target's first point. Default false.

inputs.name: planar
inputs.description: Compare x, y only. Default false.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame to judge. Default -1 (the last).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; frame; segments; frechet_m; end_errors_m; ends_swapped.

tools.name: deformable_topology_check
tools.title: Deformable topology check
tools.summary: For every rope/cable object (a chain of linked bodies), checks the topology of its link graph (number of strands and of free ends), that every link after the first is jointed to its neighbour (no fused segments), that no active equality pins a link to the world, the table, a mocap body or the robot at the initial state, that non-adjacent links can collide with each other (a knot needs self-contact) and that no two non-adjacent links interpenetrate at keyframe 0.
tools.description: The paper checks deformables for topology. A rope modelled as a MuJoCo chain (cable composite, construct_rope, construct_cuttable_rope) can go wrong silently: two cables meant to be joined left as two strands, a link without a joint that makes a stiff rod of part of the rope, an end welded to the table or to a gripper mocap at the start, self-collision masked off so the rope passes through itself and no knot can hold, or a centreline that crosses itself at rest. Rope objects are the Stage 2 manifest's deformable objects whose skill, id or root name says rope/cable/thread/string/cord/wire, else any top-level object whose bodies form a chain of at least min_links linked bodies. The link graph has the object's geometry-carrying bodies as nodes and parent-child links plus equality constraints between links active at keyframe 0 as edges: its connected components are strands, its degree-1 nodes ends (a closed loop has none). Expected: expected_strands strands and expected_ends ends (default 1 and 2, or the object's declared `topology` in scene_recon.json, which the report lists under `declared`). Self-contact: the fraction of non-adjacent link pairs whose contype/conaffinity allow contact and that no <exclude> removes must be positive when require_self_collision; interpenetration: capsule/cylinder/sphere links closer than -self_tol_m (segment distance minus radii) at keyframe 0 while at least min_gap_links apart along the chain.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json naming the deformable objects.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these objects (ids or root body names).

inputs.name: expected_strands
inputs.description: Connected strands per rope object. Default 1; an object whose scene_recon.json entry has `topology: {strands, ends}` (a ribbon of three strands joined at one end: strands 1, ends 3) is held to that instead.

inputs.name: expected_ends
inputs.description: Free ends per rope object. Default 2 per strand (0 for a loop).

inputs.name: require_self_collision
inputs.description: Non-adjacent links must be able to touch. Default True.

inputs.name: self_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed interpenetration of non-adjacent links at rest, metres. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: min_gap_links
inputs.description: Links this many apart along the chain count as non-adjacent. Default 2.

inputs.name: min_links
inputs.description: Bodies a chain needs to count as a rope without a manifest. Default 5.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; ropes [{id, n_links, strands, ends, fused_links, pinned, self_collision_frac, interpenetrations, verdict}].

tools.name: detachable_part_release_test
tools.title: Detachable part release test
tools.summary: Force-only trial of a part (a pen cap, a plug, a press-fit lid) that is welded to a press-fit slide until it has been pulled its release travel: it must stay seated under gravity and a brief tug, stay coaxial while welded, slide to the release travel under a hand-sized pull, and, once the weld is switched off by the release rule, leave the base freely.
tools.description: The asset carries the removable part as its own free body, welded by an equality constraint to a carrier on a slide joint of the base (the press fit is the slide's frictionloss); an executor switches the weld off once the slide has travelled release_travel_m. This verifier emulates that rule with forces only, with the base held in place (a free base is re-pinned every step; a fixed base needs nothing). Four trials, each from the initial state: (1) seated hold: gravity turned to pull the part straight off along the slide axis for hold_s, the slide must stay below a quarter of the release travel; (2) brief tug: a pull of sub_force_frac times the slide's frictionloss for sub_pull_s must not reach the release travel; (3) weld holds coaxial: a sideways force with the weld active must not move the part off the axis by more than max_coaxial_drift_m; (4) pull-off: pull_force_N along the axis until the slide reaches release_travel_m (within pull_s), then the weld is switched off and the same sideways force must carry the part at least separate_m off the axis. When expose_site is given (a nib tip, a nozzle), it must lie inside one of the part's geoms at the start (covered) and outside all of them after the pull-off (exposed). The sideways direction is the one perpendicular to the axis closest to world up, so the part is lifted, not pushed into a support. Only slide joints are judged; geoms other than box, sphere, cylinder, capsule and ellipsoid are treated as their bounding sphere for the covered/exposed test.

inputs.name: xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the asset (or a scene) containing the base, the slide, the weld and the free part.

inputs.name: equality
inputs.description: Name of the weld equality that holds the part on the carrier (the release rule switches it off).

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: Name of the press-fit slide joint the carrier moves on (positive q = off).

inputs.name: part_body
inputs.description: Name of the removable part's free body.

inputs.name: release_travel_m
inputs.description: Slide travel at which the release rule frees the part, metres (> 0).

inputs.name: expose_site
inputs.description: Optional site the part covers when seated and must uncover once removed (a nib tip). Default None.

inputs.name: pull_force_N
inputs.description: Pull along the axis in the pull-off trial, newtons. Default 4.0.

inputs.name: pull_s
inputs.description: Time allowed to reach the release travel, seconds. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: sub_force_frac
inputs.description: Brief tug as a fraction of the slide's frictionloss. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: sub_pull_s
inputs.description: Duration of the brief tug, seconds. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Seated-hold duration with gravity along the axis, seconds. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: lateral_force_N
inputs.description: Sideways force on the part (weld-active and after release), newtons. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: lateral_s
inputs.description: Duration of the sideways force, seconds. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: separate_m
inputs.description: Required off-axis distance of the freed part, metres. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_coaxial_drift_m
inputs.description: Allowed off-axis drift while the weld is active, metres. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: cover_margin_m
inputs.description: Margin added to the part's geoms in the covered/exposed test, metres. Default 0.0005.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional path for the JSON report.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All four trials (and the cover/expose test when asked) passed.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and which parameter of the asset or the test to change.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence: DETACH OK or DETACH FAILED with the numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: seated_hold {q_end}, brief_tug {force_N, q_max}, weld_holds_coaxial {perp_drift_m}, pull_off {released, t_release_s, q_at_release, perp_separation_m, t_separate_s, covered_before, exposed_after}, axis_world, hold_force_N.

tools.name: drawer_receive_and_close_test
tools.title: Drawer receive-and-close test
tools.summary: Opens a drawer's slide joint, drops a free item over the exposed bin, checks it rests inside the bin, then pushes the drawer shut with a capped force and checks it closes with the item enclosed.
tools.description: Composes a test world from two MJCF files: the drawer asset (a fixed or free root with a slide joint whose child body is the drawer bin, e.g. port_urdf_asset output) and an item asset with a free joint (a plush toy, a cube, any rigid or soft body). A free drawer root is held fixed by removing its free joint. The slide joint (the first slide joint, or `joint`) is set to `open_frac` of its range. The exposed part of the bin is the part of the moving body's geometry that lies beyond the fixed geometry along the joint axis (world-space geom AABBs); the item is dropped from `drop_height` above the bin's top over the middle of that exposed part and settles for `settle_s` under gravity. It must end inside the moving body's local bounding box (between its floor and rim, within its walls) and at rest (speed below `rest_speed`). Then a force of `close_force_N` is applied to the drawer along the closing direction for `close_s`: the joint must return to within `close_tol_frac` of its closed stop, and the item must still be inside the bin and inside the fixed housing's extent along the axis (enclosed). Assumes the drawer opens toward +q of the slide joint and that the closed stop is the lower limit.

inputs.name: drawer_xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the drawer asset (slide joint on the bin body).

inputs.name: item_xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the item; its first body must carry a free joint.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: Slide joint name in drawer_xml; default the first slide joint.

inputs.name: open_frac
inputs.description: Opening as a fraction of the joint range. Default 0.9.

inputs.name: drop_height
inputs.description: Gap between the bin's top and the item's lowest point at release. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Settling time after the drop. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: close_force_N
inputs.description: Capped pushing force along the closing direction. Default 10.

inputs.name: close_s
inputs.description: Pushing time. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: close_tol_frac
inputs.description: Closed when q <= lower + this fraction of the range. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: rest_speed
inputs.description: The item counts as at rest below this speed. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional path for the report.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: The item rested inside the open bin and stayed enclosed after the drawer closed.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and what to change (bin size, opening, force).

outputs.name: joint
outputs.description: The slide joint tested.

outputs.name: exposed_m
outputs.description: Length of the bin exposed at the opening, along the axis.

outputs.name: item_extent_m
outputs.description: The item's bounding box size.

outputs.name: bin_local_bounds
outputs.description: lo/hi of the bin body's geometry in its own frame.

outputs.name: rest
outputs.description: inside, speed, item position in the bin frame after settling.

outputs.name: close
outputs.description: q_end, closed, inside_bin, enclosed after pushing.

tools.name: drop_rest_test
tools.title: Drop-and-rest test
tools.summary: Drops a free object onto a floor from several tilted orientations and checks that each time it comes to rest within the settle time and then stays put (the rest criteria of end_state_rest_audit).
tools.description: Loads the asset MJCF, finds its free body (or `body`), adds a floor plane at z = 0 when the asset has none, and for each drop orientation (roll, pitch, yaw in degrees about the world axes) places the body so its lowest collision point is `drop_height` above the floor, at rest. It simulates `settle_s`; over the last `rest_window_s` of that the body must move slower than `rest_speed_m_s` and turn slower than `rest_deg_s`; then it simulates `check_s` more and the body's peak motion from where it was must stay under `settle_m` and `settle_deg`, the same numbers end_state_rest_audit applies to a Stage 3 episode's last frame. A body that rocks on a curved underside, rolls away or keeps spinning fails with the drop and the numbers. Every joint of the asset other than the free joint keeps its springs and limits. Lowest points come from each collision geom's world-axis extent (exact for spheres, ellipsoids, boxes, capsules and cylinders; the bounding sphere for meshes).

inputs.name: asset_xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the object asset (one free body, optional floor).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The free body to drop; default the first body with a free joint.

inputs.name: drops
inputs.description: Drop orientations in degrees. Default five: level and four tilts up to 40 deg.

inputs.name: drop_height
inputs.description: Gap between the lowest collision point and the floor at release. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Time to come to rest after the release. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: rest_window_s
inputs.description: Final stretch of settle_s over which speed is measured. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: rest_speed_m_s
inputs.description: Largest speed at rest. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: rest_deg_s
inputs.description: Largest turn rate at rest. Default 15.

inputs.name: check_s
inputs.description: Time simulated on after settle_s. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: settle_m
inputs.description: Largest peak motion during check_s. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: settle_deg
inputs.description: Largest peak rotation during check_s. Default 2.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; body; drops [{orientation_deg, final_speed_m_s, final_turn_deg_s, check_peak_mm, check_peak_deg, rest_z_m, ok}]; worst.

tools.name: dynamics_consistency_audit
tools.title: Dynamics consistency audit
tools.summary: Inverse dynamics on free objects: on frames with contacts, the force each object needs (mass x (acceleration - gravity)) must lie in the cone its contacts can push with; a hand constraint is no support.
tools.description: No other audit relates an object's acceleration to its contacts (contact_force_check sums normal force in a hold window, episode_physics_check bounds speed and jumps). For each free object and frame, the external force it needs is F = M (a_com - g) (subtree mass M, centre-of-mass acceleration by central difference). The contacts of its subtree within margin_m (default 3 mm) on that frame and its two neighbours (an impact between frames counts), on the scene as the bench executor runs it, each contribute a friction pyramid (normal plus or minus mu along two tangents, mu from the contact, capped at mu_cap), and a contact of a body with an adhesion actuator (a magnet) may also pull, up to that actuator's force. Non-negative least squares finds the closest force the contacts can produce; the remainder divided by M is the unexplained acceleration. Frames without any contact are left to free_fall_plausibility_audit; frames where an object-object or object-world constraint (a cap on its thread) is engaged are skipped, because a constraint pushes and pulls. It fails when the unexplained acceleration exceeds acc_tol (default 4 m/s^2) on at least min_frames consecutive frames (default 2), and when a robot-object constraint is engaged for more than attach_frames frames (the object rides on a constraint to the hand: an attach). Reports the worst run per object with frames, phase labels, the needed force and the contacts present.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels, optional eq_active).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: margin_m
inputs.description: Contact distance that counts. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: acc_tol
inputs.description: Unexplained acceleration that fails, m/s^2. Default 4.

inputs.name: min_frames
inputs.description: Consecutive failing frames that make a run. Default 2.

inputs.name: mu_cap
inputs.description: Largest friction coefficient credited to a contact. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: attach_frames
inputs.description: Frames a robot-object constraint may be engaged before it counts as an attach. Default 3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, frames, labels, unexplained_m_s2, needed_force_n, contacts}; objects {name: frames judged, worst unexplained acceleration, frame}; attaches.

tools.name: end_state_rest_audit
tools.title: End state rest audit
tools.summary: At the end every object is at rest (still over the last frames), stays put when the scene is simulated on from the last frame, and is supported by the scene rather than propped by the robot.
tools.description: episode_physics_check fails an object that touches nothing at the last frame; this audit checks what that misses. (1) Rest: over the last rest_window_s (default 0.3 s) each free object's body moves slower than rest_speed_m_s (default 2 cm/s) and turns slower than rest_deg_s (default 15 deg/s). (2) Stable: the scene as the bench executor runs it is simulated for settle_s (default 1 s) from the last frame with every robot joint held; each object's peak motion must stay under settle_m (default 3 mm) and settle_deg (default 2 deg): an object balanced on a rim or sliding down a slope moves. (3) Released: objects the robot still touches at the last frame (within 1 mm) are simulated again with every robot contact removed; one that then moves more than settle_m / settle_deg was propped by the hand, unless it is listed in allow_held (a task that ends holding). Reports per object the final speed, the settle motion and whether the robot props it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Window whose last frame is judged as the end. Default all.

inputs.name: rest_window_s
inputs.description: Final stretch over which speed is measured. Default 0.3.

inputs.name: rest_speed_m_s, rest_deg_s
inputs.description: Speed limits at rest. Defaults 0.02, 15.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Simulated time after the last frame. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: settle_m, settle_deg
inputs.description: Allowed peak motion while simulating on. Defaults 0.003, 2.

inputs.name: allow_held
inputs.description: Objects allowed to end in the hand (fnmatch). Default none.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst; objects {name: final speed m/s and deg/s, settle peak mm / deg, touched_by_robot, propped peak mm / deg}; notes (the propped-by-robot rule skipped when the scene without robot contact cannot be built).

tools.name: episode_physics_check
tools.title: Episode physics check
tools.summary: Realism audit of an executed episode: finite state, no object faster than a hand can move things, no object jumping between frames, no interpenetration beyond a few millimetres between hands and objects or between objects, nothing left floating at the end, and the hands' servos never forced far off their commands.
tools.description: Replays the episode frame by frame (kinematics + collision detection on the physics scene with the hand-object contact pairs) and measures: per free object its peak speed and the largest single-frame displacement; the deepest hand-object/hand-table and object-object interpenetration on every frame; at the last frame every free object's support (contact with something below it, or its lowest point at the table within tolerance); and, when the episode carries the rollout diagnostics, the worst wrist tracking error and the frames where it exceeded the limit. Thresholds are generous for real manipulation and tight for artefacts: an object moving at 4 m/s, a 3 cm jump in one frame or a pad 1 cm inside a surface only happen when the simulation was forced. The report lists the offending frames and bodies.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz (qpos, labels, fps, optional diagnostics).

inputs.name: max_speed_mps
inputs.description: Default 4.0.

inputs.name: max_jump_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed per-frame displacement of an object. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: max_pen_m
inputs.description: Allowed interpenetration. Default 0.008.

inputs.name: max_track_m
inputs.description: Allowed wrist tracking error. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame stride for the collision replay. Default 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, failed, objects {name: {peak_speed, max_jump, jump_frame}}, penetration {hand_object_mm, object_object_mm, worst_frame, worst_pair}, floating_at_end, tracking {max_mm, frames_over}.

tools.name: equality_constraint_check
tools.title: Equality constraint check
tools.summary: Every weld and connect has a unit relative quaternion and a meaningful torquescale, every active equality is satisfied at the initial state, and each equality's active flag matches what the scene or its episode intends (a fresh MjData re-activates every weld whose eq_active0 is set).
tools.description: Equalities hold the hands on the arms and the mechanisms together, and they fail silently. A weld whose relative quaternion is zero (eq_data written as [0]*11 at run time) has no defined orientation; a weld written through MjSpec with the default data gets torquescale 0 and holds position only, so a part welded to the world spins about its anchor; only the robot's arm-to-hand welds are position-only by design (both bodies carry the robot prefix). The check compiles the scene and, at keyframe `key`, measures every weld / connect residual itself (position error of the anchor, and the rotation error of a weld whose torquescale is not 0) plus joint-equality residuals; an active equality violated by more than `pos_tol_m` / `rot_tol_deg` at the start snaps its bodies on the first step. Intended state: `expect_active` ({equality name or 'body1|body2': bool}) is compared with eq_active0; and with a `trajectory` (npz with qpos, optional eq_active / eq_active_start / eq_names), every non-robot weld/connect that the recorded qpos violates by more than `release_tol_m` / `release_tol_deg` on some frame must have been released in the recording: if the scene starts it active and the trajectory records no eq_active, replaying the episode from a fresh MjData re-engages it (a removed cap snaps back onto its bottle); if eq_active is recorded, its frames are used. A recorded eq_active_start that differs from eq_active0 is reported the same way.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe of the initial state. Default 0 (qpos0 without keyframes).

inputs.name: expect_active
inputs.description: {equality name or 'body1|body2': True/False} the scene must start with.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz (qpos [T, nq], optional eq_active [T, neq], eq_active_start, eq_names).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] frames of the trajectory to scan. Default all.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Scan every stride-th frame. Default 5.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Residual an active equality may have at the start, metres. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Rotation residual an active weld may have at the start. Default 2.

inputs.name: release_tol_m
inputs.description: Residual on a trajectory frame that means the equality was released. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: release_tol_deg
inputs.description: Rotation residual that means a weld was released. Default 10.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; equalities: [{name, type, body1, body2, active0, torquescale, robot_pair, pos_err_m, rot_err_deg, problem}]; trajectory: {n_frames, recorded_eq_active, released: [{name, first_frame, max_pos_err_m}]}; worst.

tools.name: execution_scene_integrity_check
tools.title: Execution scene integrity check
tools.summary: Compare execution objects, mechanisms and initial state with the independently compiled Stage 2 scene.
tools.description: Permits only canonical rigid robot conversion, contact-pair construction and source-proven unspecified rigid contact defaults. Explicit compliance, object mass, inertia, geometry, friction, joints, actuators, tendons, constraints, contact exclusions and initial states must remain the same. The reference comes from the trusted Stage 2 input, never the submitted runtime scene.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Executed runtime MJCF.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Trusted Stage 2 scene reconstruction manifest.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Runtime recording; its first object state must equal the trusted initial state.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, compared.

tools.name: final_pose_check
tools.title: Final pose check
tools.summary: Final position (and optionally yaw or full rotation) of a body against the demonstration's or a target, judged on the last frame.
tools.description: Reads the body's pose on the last frame of the trajectory (optionally the median of the last n frames to ignore a settling jitter) and compares it with the same body's last pose in a reference trajectory or with an explicit target. Fails when the position error exceeds pos_tol (0.10 m by default, the paper's task gate) or when the rotation error exceeds rot_tol_deg, measured as yaw about the up axis for objects that stand on a table or as the full geodesic angle when full_rotation is set. Also reports the path-tracking error against the reference as information, never as the gate.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: The rollout to judge.

inputs.name: body

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Demonstration trajectory; its last frame is the target.

inputs.name: target_pos, target_yaw_deg
inputs.description: Explicit target instead of a reference.

inputs.name: pos_tol
inputs.description: Default 0.10.

inputs.name: rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Rotation gate; None skips rotation. Default 30.

inputs.name: full_rotation

inputs.name: settle_frames
