tools.name: finger_press_in_hand_test
tools.title: Finger press in hand test
tools.summary: Hold an object in a posed hand, lift it (and optionally tilt it), then press a sprung part of it (a spray pump head, a trigger, a button) with one finger several times; pass when the part travels through its stroke on every press, springs back on every release and the object stays put in the hand.
tools.description: Physics rollout in the floating-hand scene. The hand comes in with its open shape (the pose's finger_targets_open, else every finger backed off by open_frac) from approach_m back along its retreat axis (the pose's approach, else back along the fingers, as the executor does), closes over close_s to the grip clamp (press_targets of the gripping fingers, the executor's clamp; the pressing finger stays on its resting targets), seats, lifts the object by lift_m and, when `tilt` = {axis, deg} is given, turns the wrist about that world axis through the object's grip point. Then `cycles` times: the pressing finger ramps to the pressed targets (pressed_pose's finger targets for that finger) over press_s and holds, the joint value is read; it ramps back and holds, the joint value is read. The object's position in the wrist frame is tracked from the end of the lift/tilt. Verdicts: DROPPED (the object did not rise with the hand or lost the grip), STALLED (a press moved the joint less than min_travel_frac of its range: the finger cannot push the spring, or its push goes into the grip), STUCK (a release left the joint more than return_frac of its range away from rest), SLIPPED (the object drifted more than drift_max_mm in the hand while pumping), PUMPED. The finger servos and wrist are force-capped by the hand scene's defaults, so a press that only works with more force fails.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, grasp_body?} or its JSON path; the held object is the last object (or grasp_body).

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Hold pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers (without the pressing finger), finger_targets_open?} (finger_press_targets' hold).

inputs.name: pressed_pose
inputs.description: Pose whose finger_targets hold the pressing finger's pressed joint targets (finger_press_targets' pressed).

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: The pressed part's slide or hinge joint (full name or unique suffix).

inputs.name: finger
inputs.description: Pressing finger; default pressed_pose['press_finger'], else 'index'.

inputs.name: cycles
inputs.description: Press-release cycles. Default 3.

inputs.name: lift_m
inputs.description: Lift before pumping. Default 0.06; 0 keeps the object on its support (a button on a resting box).

inputs.name: tilt
inputs.description: {axis: world [x, y, z], deg: angle} wrist turn after the lift (pumping a tilted sprayer). Default none.

inputs.name: press_s, release_s, dwell_s
inputs.description: Finger ramp times and the dwell at each end. Defaults 0.4, 0.4, 0.3.

inputs.name: min_travel_frac
inputs.description: Required joint travel per press as a fraction of its range. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: return_frac
inputs.description: Allowed joint offset from rest after a release, as a fraction of its range. Default 0.25.

inputs.name: drift_max_mm
inputs.description: Allowed object drift in the wrist frame while pumping. Default 8.

inputs.name: approach_m
inputs.description: How far back along the retreat axis the open hand starts. Default 0.06; 0 places it open at the grasp.

inputs.name: close_s
inputs.description: Default 0.6.

inputs.name: open_frac
inputs.description: Default 0.55.

inputs.name: depth_rad
inputs.description: Default 0.3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, verdict, issues, measured {joint, range, rest, presses: [{travel_mm, frac}], releases: [{offset_mm}], drift_mm_max, lift_achieved_mm, tilt_achieved_deg, fingers_at_end, contact_force_N, press_finger_on_part}.

tools.name: finger_servo_saturation_audit
tools.title: Finger servo saturation audit
tools.summary: During carry phases, the smallest finger torques that let the grasp's actual contacts carry the object (gravity and the measured acceleration) stay below the finger servos' torque cap for most of the hold.
tools.description: contact_force_check sums the contact force in a window; it cannot tell a grip that needs its full torque from one with reserve, and the executor's position servos sit at the cap either way. For each carry window (lift, carry, transport phases of a hand, object named in the label or touching the hand) and each judged frame (every `stride`-th; frames where the object also touches a support are skipped), the contacts between the robot and the object within margin_m (the scene as the bench executor runs it) each get a friction pyramid (mu from the contact, capped at mu_cap) plus torsional and rolling friction bounded by the contact's own coefficients times its normal force: the physics the episode was executed in (spin_m / roll_m override them; spin_m=0.005, roll_m=0 judges against a realistic fingertip pad). A linear program finds contact forces that balance the object's weight and inertial force (mass x (acceleration - gravity)) and zero net torque about its centre of mass while minimising the largest finger-joint torque as a fraction s of each joint's cap (torque = J^T f through the finger's contact Jacobian; palm contacts load the arm, not a finger). Caps: the actuator's forcerange when the scene limits it, else finger_cap_nm (default: the bench hand's 0.8 N m that the executor applies at run time), times the actuator gear. A frame whose contacts cannot balance the load at all (residual above 20% of the weight) is reported, not judged. It fails when s >= sat_frac (default 0.95) on at least hold_frac (default 0.6) of a window's judged frames. Reports per window the median and peak s and the joint that limits. The hand-scene grasp stress tests judge the same measure with the same thresholds (hand.ServoReserve), so a grasp they pass is not failed here for holding only at the torque cap.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: finger_cap_nm
inputs.description: Finger joint torque cap when the scene sets none. Default the bench hand's 0.8 N m.

inputs.name: sat_frac
inputs.description: Share of the cap that counts as saturated. Default 0.95.

inputs.name: hold_frac
inputs.description: Share of judged frames that must be saturated to fail. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: margin_m
inputs.description: Contact distance that counts. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: mu_cap
inputs.description: Largest friction coefficient credited. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: spin_m, roll_m
inputs.description: Torsional / rolling friction length credited per contact (torque <= value x normal force). Default None: the contact's own coefficients.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Judge every n-th frame of a window. Default 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, object, frames, saturated_frac, median_s, peak_s, limiting_joint}; windows; unbalanced frames.

tools.name: flat_press_drag_test
tools.title: Flat press-and-drag test
tools.summary: Lay a posed hand on a free object (sponge, cloth pad, eraser, card), press it down onto its support and drag the wrist sideways in physics; pass when the object slid along with the hand, stayed flat on the support and stayed under the pads.
tools.description: For wiping and scrubbing motions, where the hand does not close around the object but holds it against the table by friction. The hand is teleported above the pose along its approach axis with its posed fingers, descended onto the pose, pushed a further press_m into the object along its contact normal as the executor's wrist press goes (the pose's mean normal; the approach axis when it records none; default: the pose's press_travel_m when positive, else 4 mm) and then translated by travel_m along a horizontal direction in steps, with the wrist and finger servos of the hand rig in contact physics. The object (scene grasp_body, else the free body of the last scene object) must move at least min_fraction of the wrist travel along the direction, must not rise more than max_lift_mm or tilt more than max_tilt_deg (a pad that flips or rides up on the fingers is no wipe), and a hand geom must still touch it at the end. A hand that never touches the object reports STALLED, a hand that skates over it SKATED, an object that tips or lifts TIPPED.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene {hand_xml, side, objects:[{name, xml, pos, quat|yaw_deg}], floor, grasp_body?} or the JSON file hand_scene_from_recon writes.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Hand pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, press_travel_m?, approach?} (flat_hand_pose, pose_from_points), or its JSON file.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: World direction of the drag; its vertical part is dropped.

inputs.name: travel_m
inputs.description: Wrist travel along the direction. Default 0.04.

inputs.name: press_m
inputs.description: Extra wrist travel into the object after contact, along the pose's mean contact normal (else back along its approach). Default: pose press_travel_m if > 0, else 0.004.

inputs.name: approach_m
inputs.description: Start height above the pose along its approach axis. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Duration of the drag. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Required object travel / wrist travel. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: max_lift_mm
inputs.description: Largest allowed rise of the object. Default 5.

inputs.name: max_tilt_deg
inputs.description: Largest allowed tilt of the object. Default 15.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, verdict, measured {object, travel_m, object_moved_m, fraction, lateral_m, max_lift_mm, max_tilt_deg, contact_start, contact_end, peak_wrist_force_n}.

tools.name: flip_cap_snap_test
tools.title: Flip-cap snap test
tools.summary: Pries a microtube's flip cap open with a ramped force under its tab and presses it shut again; measures the pop force, the opening and the reclosed angle.
tools.description: Rebuilds the tube from its parameters into a one-well rack so it has a holder, pins the tube with a constant 10 N downward force, and ramps a pry force under the cap tab (3 N/s up to 7 N) until the cap fold angle passes 6 degrees; the force at that moment is the measured pop force (compare with built['snap_force_N']). The cap is left to fall open, then a press_force_N press at the tab, where a thumb lands, closes it. Passes when the cap opened past 80 degrees and reclosed to within 8 degrees of shut. The same trial works on any cap that exposes <tube>_fold and <tube>_flex joints, a <tube>_tab geom and a <tube>_capface body.

inputs.description: The dict construct_microtube returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: pry_force_N

inputs.name: press_force_N
inputs.description: The closing press on the tab. Default 8.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Trial length. Default 9.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: PASS/FAIL with the angles.

tools.name: fold_box_fold_test
tools.title: Fold-box fold test
tools.summary: Pushes every crease of a folding carton shut at its panel edge, measures the fold angles and panel interpenetration, then lets gravity reopen it.
tools.description: Loads a carton built by construct_fold_box and runs the fold-box driver: rest, push the walls up, push the inner flaps over, push the outer flaps over, hold, then all forces off. Pushes are 1.2 N at each panel's far edge along the panel's own normal and ease off over the last 25 degrees so the joint limit is not slammed. For a style='lid' box the single lid hinge is swung open instead. Measured: max wall angle, max flap angle, the worst interpenetration among the box's own panels (contacts of other objects are ignored), and the angle the walls fell back open by with the hands off. Passes when the walls (or the lid) reach more than 85 degrees under the push and the worst panel interpenetration stays under 1.5 mm.

inputs.name: out_mp4

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

tools.name: force_closure_check
tools.title: Force-closure check
tools.summary: Close a posed hand on the object in physics and check that the resulting contact set has force closure (Ferrari-Canny Q1 above a threshold) rather than being a one-sided press.
tools.description: The hand is placed open at the pose, the fingers are driven to the closed or squeezed targets, and the scene settles. The hand-object contacts from the simulator (position, normal, force, friction) form a 6-D wrench hull with 8-edge friction cones; Q1 is the largest ball around the origin inside it, and force closure means Q1 > 0. The check also fails when the contacts all push the same way (press_frac above press_max, a press that can hold nothing against gravity), when fewer than min_fingers pads are in contact, or when the close itself moved the object more than move_max_mm. This is the static companion of grasp_lift_test: cheap enough to run on every candidate, not sufficient on its own.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, grasp_body?}

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: {pos, euler, finger_targets, finger_targets_squeezed?, grip_fingers?}

inputs.name: q1_min
inputs.description: minimum Q1 (default 0.01)

inputs.name: press_max
inputs.description: maximum |sum F|/sum|F| (default 0.85)

inputs.name: min_fingers
inputs.description: pads that must touch (default 2)

inputs.name: move_max_mm
inputs.description: allowed object motion during the close (default 15)

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: force closure with opposing contacts and a quiet close

outputs.name: q1 / press_frac / n_contacts / fingers / total_force_N / object_moved_mm
outputs.description: the measurements

tools.name: free_body_policy_check
tools.title: Free body policy check
tools.summary: Every Stage 1 object a hand moves (role manipulated or tool) must be a free body in the scene, not welded to the world, the table or the robot and not a mocap body; every object Stage 1 calls static must be fixed; containers and targets may be either and are reported.
tools.description: A manipulated object built without a free joint (or welded to the world by an active equality, or made a kinematic mocap body) can never be picked up, and an object parented to a robot body rides the hand without any grasp; a 'static' object left free can be knocked away and become a support the robot must balance. Stage 1 objects (scene_semantics.json) are mapped to bodies through scene_recon.json (else by id). An object is free when its root body or one of its ancestors below the world carries a free joint, and fixed otherwise; equality welds and connects active at keyframe 0 between the object and the world, the table, a fixed object or the robot make it held. Rules: role manipulated or tool -> free and not held (a part attached to a free object by a weld, such as a cap on its bottle's thread, is free when that object is); role static -> fixed unless static_may_be_free; container/target -> reported only. Deformable objects are judged on their root body; a deformable whose scene_recon.json entry declares `anchored_to` (a cord end held under a fixed object) may be welded to that fixed object's body.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: semantic
inputs.description: scene_semantics.json (Stage 1) with each object's role.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json mapping Stage 1 ids to root bodies.

inputs.name: static_may_be_free
inputs.description: Accept free bodies for role 'static'. Default False.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; objects [{id, role, root, free, held_by, mocap, under_robot, verdict}].

tools.name: free_fall_plausibility_audit
tools.title: Free fall plausibility audit
tools.summary: On every frame where a free object touches nothing and no constraint holds it, its acceleration must be gravity's: hovering, falling too slowly or drifting sideways fails.
tools.description: episode_physics_check checks only the final frame for floating objects; this audit checks every frame. For each free object it marks the frames where the object's subtree has no contact within margin_m (default 3 mm, plus the distance it travels in a frame) on that frame and both neighbours, on the scene as the bench executor runs it (hand-object pairs included), and no equality constraint holds it to another object or the world (constraints are taken as engaged from a recorded eq_active, else when their residual is under 3 mm / 3 deg). On those free frames the centre-of-mass acceleration (central second difference) must equal gravity within acc_tol (default 3 m/s^2). Runs of at least min_frames such frames that fail are reported as hovering (speed under 2 cm/s), falling too slowly, or accelerating sideways, with their frames, phase labels and mean acceleration. A constraint from the robot to the object is not support: the hand must hold by contact.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels, optional eq_active).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: margin_m
inputs.description: Contact distance under which the object counts as touching. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: acc_tol
inputs.description: Allowed |a - g| on a free frame, m/s^2. Default 3.

inputs.name: min_frames
inputs.description: Shortest failing run reported. Default 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, frames, labels, kind, mean_acc}; objects {name: free frames, worst |a - g|}.

tools.name: free_joint_object_check
tools.title: Free joint object check
tools.summary: Each object meant to move has exactly one free joint, on its root body; extra free bodies of an object are tied to it by an equality unless they are the declared separate pieces of a group object (`parts`); no free joint is nested below a top-level body; static objects, the table and the robot have none.
tools.description: An object that should be picked up but whose root has no free joint is welded to the world, and Stage 3 can never move it; a part that is a separate free body without an equality to its object (a cap that should be screwed on, a lid that should be hinged) lies loose and falls off; a free joint below another body does not compile (MuJoCo: 'free joint can only be used on top level', naming only the first), which an attach into the wrong parent produces; a fixture (a rack, a shelf, the table) with a free joint slides when touched. The check reads the scene through MjSpec so every nested free joint is listed even when the scene does not compile, then compiles it and, per object (from a scene_recon.json, or the top-level non-robot bodies), counts the free joints among its bodies. `moving` objects (default: the recon's rigid objects whose Stage 1 role is 'manipulated' or 'tool', read through the recon's scene_semantic link) must have one free joint on their root body; every further free body of an object must be connected to another of its bodies by an equality constraint, except the pieces a group object declares in its scene_recon.json entry under `parts` (a tower of loose bars, a pile of cards: Stage 1 `pieces`), which are separate free bodies by design; when Stage 1 says the pieces are loose, every declared part must have its own free joint, and a declared part that is not a body of the scene is reported. Undeclared extra free bodies still fail. `static` objects, the table and robot bodies must have no free joint.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: scene_recon.json path or dict, or a list of object ids / dicts; default: top-level non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: moving
inputs.description: Object ids that must move freely; default from the recon's types and Stage 1 roles (none without a recon).

inputs.name: static
inputs.description: Object ids that must not have a free joint. Default [].

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; nested_free: [{joint, body, parent}]; objects: {id: {root, root_free, n_free, free_bodies, untied_free_bodies, parts, moving, static}}; worst.

tools.name: friction_parameter_check
tools.title: Friction parameter check
tools.summary: Checks the sliding, torsional and rolling friction of every object and table collision geom and of every explicit contact pair the setup does not have against plausible ranges, and the damping and friction loss of object free joints, so a 3.0 friction that makes any grasp hold (or a syrupy free joint that keeps a released object in place) is caught.
tools.description: MuJoCo combines two geoms' friction by taking the larger, so one sticky geom (friction 3.0) makes every contact it has hold; torsional and rolling friction are lengths (m): 1.0 means an object cannot spin in a pinch at all. Rules: each non-robot collidable geom's sliding friction within [min_slide, max_slide] (default 0.01-2.0; rubber on rubber is about 1-2), torsional at most max_torsional (0.05 m) and rolling at most max_rolling (0.01 m). Explicit <pair>s that the setup scene also has (the hand-table pairs) are left to contact_exclusion_audit; other pairs that touch a robot geom are capped at the executor's own hand-object pair friction (pair_cap, default [1.2, 1.2, 0.02, 0.001, 0.001]: hand.HAND_PAIR_FRICTION as build_execution_model writes it), pairs between non-robot geoms at the geom limits. Object free joints must have damping at most max_free_damping and no friction loss (both act on the object against the world, holding it wherever a hand leaves it). The table geom must keep the setup's friction.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder for the reference table and pairs. Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: min_slide
inputs.description: Lowest sliding friction accepted. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: max_slide
inputs.description: Highest sliding friction accepted. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: max_torsional
inputs.description: Highest torsional friction of a geom, metres. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: max_rolling
inputs.description: Highest rolling friction of a geom, metres. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: pair_cap
inputs.description: Cap on the 5 friction values of robot pairs not in the setup. Default [1.2, 1.2, 0.02, 0.001, 0.001], the executor's own hand-object pair friction.

inputs.name: max_free_damping
inputs.description: Highest damping on an object's free joint (N s/m). Default 0.01.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; geoms_checked; pairs_checked; bad_geoms [{geom, body, friction, why}]; bad_pairs; bad_joints; table {reference, scene}; worst (largest sliding friction seen).

tools.name: geom_count_budget_check
tools.title: Geom count budget check
tools.summary: Counts the collision geoms of each object and, more to the point, how many object collision geoms lie within one hand's reach of each other; a cluster above the budget (72 ring-wall geoms made each hand-scene step 15 ms and grasp search time out) fails with a simplification to apply.
tools.description: Every hand collision geom gets an explicit contact pair with every object collision geom in a hand scene and in the executor, so the cost of a step grows with the number of object geoms a hand can be touching at once: three 25-geom magnetic rings in a 6 cm cluster made each hand-scene step take 15 ms (552 contacts with the hand among them) and the grasp searches ran past 15 minutes, while a 100-geom meal box spread over 20 cm stayed under 4 ms. The check takes the collision geoms of the non-robot objects (an MJCF bench scene, or a hand-scene JSON / dict compiled the way the grasp tools compile it), counts them per object and by type, and for each geom counts the object geoms whose bounding sphere reaches into a sphere of `reach_m` (a hand's grasp envelope) around it. The largest such cluster above `max_local_geoms` fails, naming the objects in it and how to simplify them (fewer wall segments, a convex decomposition with a handful of hulls, primitives merged); `max_object_geoms` optionally caps each object too. With `measure=True` it also times mj_forward with a hand at the densest cluster (hand scene) or the paired execution model (bench scene); the time is reported, never judged, because it depends on the machine.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF bench scene, or a hand-scene JSON path / dict ({hand_xml, side, objects: [...]}).

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: scene_recon.json (or list) naming the objects of an MJCF scene; default: its top-level non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: reach_m
inputs.description: Radius of a hand's reach around a geom, metres. Default 0.06.

inputs.name: max_local_geoms
inputs.description: Largest number of object collision geoms within one reach. Default 48.

inputs.name: max_object_geoms
inputs.description: Optional cap on one object's collision geoms. Default None.

inputs.name: measure
inputs.description: Also time mj_forward (reported only). Default False.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; objects: {id: {n_collision_geoms, by_type}}; densest: {count, center_geom, objects: {id: n}, reach_m}; n_object_geoms; n_hand_pairs_estimate; timing_ms (when measured); worst.

tools.name: goal_contact_gate
tools.title: Goal contact gate
tools.summary: Two named bodies (with everything attached below them) are in contact at the end of a window of an executed episode, optionally on a fraction of all its frames, or are apart (a goal 'touches', 'against', 'separated from').
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'slide the brick until it touches the yellow brick', 'the sponge stays in contact with the table' and 'the cap is separated from the bottle'. The trajectory's qpos is replayed in the execution model of the scene it was executed in (hand hulls paired with every object, as the Stage 3 executor runs it); on the window's last frame every geom of the two subtrees is given a detection margin of tol_m, collision detection runs, and the pair touches when some contact between them is closer than tol_m (default 4 mm: reconstructed parts carry millimetre errors, while the misses this gate exists for are centimetres short). When they do not touch, the gap is measured up to 5 cm and reported, so a push that stopped 13 mm short says so. throughout requires contact on at least min_frac of the window's frames (every stride-th frame). apart inverts the test: no contact closer than apart_m at the end. Two parts of one articulated object that the scene excludes from collision (a lid and its box) are measured by the geometric distance of their primitive geoms instead. 'table' names the support surface. Correct episodes pass: a resting contact sits inside the margin on every frame; a displacement that stops short of the target body fails however far it moved.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels, optional subgoal).

inputs.name: body_a
inputs.description: First body (its subtree counts).

inputs.name: body_b
inputs.description: Second body, or 'table'.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window; the end is the last frame.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames whose npz subgoal index matches.

inputs.name: throughout
inputs.description: Also require contact on min_frac of the window. Default false.

inputs.name: min_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of frames for throughout. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Contact distance that counts as touching, m. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: apart
inputs.description: Require the bodies to be apart at the end instead. Default false.

inputs.name: apart_m
inputs.description: Smallest allowed distance for apart, m. Default tol_m.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame step for throughout. Default 2.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues (frame, gap, what to change); end_frame; touching_at_end; end_gap_m; touch_fraction and first_lost_frame for throughout; gap_m for apart.

tools.name: goal_language_coverage_check
tools.title: Goal language coverage check
tools.summary: Compiles every Stage 1 subgoal goal and task_success with the goal language Stage 3's stage1_goal_gate uses, without a scene, and lists each clause it cannot turn into a measurement, so Stage 1 rephrases it while it still can.
tools.description: Stage 3 accepts an episode only when stage1_goal_gate measures every clause of the Stage 1 goals (held, clear of a support, above an opening, inside or on an object, upright, unmoved, closed/open, released, knotted ...). A clause it cannot measure ('upright in the pinch' before the vocabulary knew it, 'gently', 'nicely') makes Stage 3 unpassable whatever the robot does. This check runs the same compiler on the Stage 1 file alone: object names resolve against Stage 1's objects and parts, and only the language is judged (a clause that needs the scene to resolve, such as which drawer is meant, is left to Stage 3; any other error of the compiler fails the check). Each uncovered clause is reported with its sentence and the measurable phrasings to use instead.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The scene_semantics.json to check.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues (one per uncovered clause, or per goal the compiler failed on, naming the JSON path); clauses {path: [clause, covered]}.

tools.name: grasp_approach_open_test
tools.title: Open-hand approach test
tools.summary: Check that the open hand can be driven into the grasp pose without knocking the object away or burying its collision geometry in the scene.
tools.description: A grasp is not just its final pose: opening the fingers at the grasp position sweeps them through the very thing being grasped (measured on a cord: teleporting the open hand onto the solved wrist shoved it 15 mm sideways and every later lift was the hand chasing an object it had already knocked away). The hand starts 90 mm back along its retreat axis with the pose's recorded opening (or the executor's floor-clear opening), settles, and follows approach waypoints with the executor's rate-limited motion. Passes when the object moved less than nudge_max_mm and every physics substep stays below the penetration cap, including grip pads and self-contact; visible hand meshes against the floor are checked at 60 Hz.

tools.name: grasp_carry_profile_test
tools.title: Carry profile replay test
tools.summary: Replay the planned carry's own wrist motion (accelerations and orientation changes, read from a trajectory segment, a keyframes JSON or a wrist path) on the grasp in its hand scene and fail when the object slips or turns in the hand.
tools.description: The generic carry test shakes every grasp the same way; the carry the plan will actually execute can be faster, turn the object upside down or swing it round a corner. The test closes the hand as the executor does (open-hand descent, close, torque-capped clamp), lifts lift_m, then replays the carry: the world wrist path of the acting hand over the selected frames (a trajectory npz with its labels, frames [first, last] or the first run labelled '<side>: carry...'; or keyframes chained with quintic legs; or an explicit wrist path) is applied as motion RELATIVE to its first frame, expressed in the hand's frame, so the object sees the same accelerations and the same orientation sequence relative to gravity as on the bench even when the hand scene's pose was re-anchored by a yaw. The servo commands are interpolated between frames at the source's fps as the executor does, and the wrist chain is re-based when it pitches past 60 deg (as the executor does). With isolate (default) the floor and every other object stop touching the hand and the object from the lift on, and equality welds that tie the object to the rest of the scene are released (the bench carries a cap only after its thread let go), so only the grasp holds it and the replay cannot run it into the hand scene's bystanders. Fails when the object's drift in the wrist frame passes drift_max_mm, its turn passes turn_max_deg, or no finger touches it at the end. Reports the path's peak speed, acceleration and turn rate, the wrist tracking error, and the frame of the worst slip.

tools.name: grasp_closing_rotation_test
tools.title: Closing rotation test
tools.summary: Close the hand on the object exactly as the executor does and fail when the object turns or slides while the fingers close, before any lift.
tools.description: A grasp can lift in the hand scene and still be wrong: if one pad reaches the object long before its opposing pad, the closing fingers push the object round and it is held in a different pose than planned (measured on the bench: a cream lego brick turned 34-49 deg during closing although every lift test passed, then slipped out of the pinch). The hand starts open on its pre-grasp (approach_m back along the executor's retreat axis, the executor's open shape), descends in 0.8 s, closes to the pose's closed targets (0.5 s + 0.2 s) and to the executor's clamp (0.3 s + 0.3 s), with the torque-capped finger servos, elliptic cones, no-slip iterations and a gravity-compensated hand of the hand scene. The grasped body's rotation and displacement are tracked from the moment the fingers start to close (the open-hand descent is grasp_approach_open_test's job) to the end of the clamp hold, together with the time each finger first touches it. Fails when the largest rotation exceeds max_rot_deg or the largest displacement exceeds max_shift_mm; the issue names the finger that touched first and the lag to its opposing pad. The defaults sit above what accepted bench grasps do (a pinch that pushes the object into place before the opposing pad meets it: up to 12.6 deg and 26.5 mm on the executed closes of ten accepted episodes, which this test reproduces with a median difference of 0.5 deg and 1.2 mm over 25 grasps) and below a grasp that turns the object out of its planned pose.

tools.name: grasp_hold_test
tools.title: Grasp hold test
tools.summary: Close on the object, lift, and hold still; pass when the object's slip rate in the hand is below a threshold and at least one pad is still on it.
tools.description: The hand approaches with the executor's opening and motion. Every physics substep checks contact penetration, including grip pads and self-contact; visible mesh penetration of the support is checked at 60 Hz. More than 3 mm fails regardless of lift or hold success. After closing and lifting, the wrist is commanded to stay put for hold_s while every simulated state is checked. Slip rate is the maximum displacement from the hold's initial relative position divided by hold duration, so a slip that later recovers cannot disappear. Rigid held links must also stay within the episode audit's 15 degree relative rotation limit. Articulated objects are measured at the contacted link and material contact point; ball-joint bending is reported without judging its angle. Also reports contact force and pads at the end.

tools.name: grasp_lift_test
tools.title: Grasp lift test
tools.summary: Close the posed hand on the object by driving its actuators and lift; pass when the object rises with the hand at every commanded height.
tools.description: The hand approaches with the executor's opening and motion. Every physics substep checks contact penetration, including grip pads and self-contact; visible mesh penetration of the support is checked at 60 Hz. More than 3 mm fails regardless of lift or hold success. The hand approaches open, closes until the grip pads are on the object with real force (or to the full press target), seats for 0.5 s, then the wrist is driven up to each height in turn. A height passes when the object rose more than lift_frac of it. This is the single most informative grasp test: a pose that looks seated statically and still fails it is pressing, not gripping (both pads above the object's centre line, or one finger loaded and the others in the air). With maintain_N > 0 the grip fingers keep closing while the contact force is below it. While the hand alone carries the object, the finger servos' reserve is judged as finger_servo_saturation_audit judges an episode (the smallest share of the finger torque caps with which the hand's contacts carry it, every executor frame): a grasp that holds only with a finger servo at 95% of its cap or more on 60% of the hold fails at 'servo_reserve' (a drive pinched 29 mm off its centre lifted with the thumb's abduction servo at 110% of its cap).

tools.name: grasp_mass_friction_robustness_test
tools.title: Mass and friction margin test
tools.summary: Make the grasped object heavier (default x1.3) and its contacts with the hand slipperier (default x0.7), then run the executor's grasp, a lift, a hold and five carry moves; fail when the grasp no longer holds.
tools.description: Reconstructed objects carry estimated masses and friction coefficients, and the real ones differ: a grasp that holds exactly at the estimate is one surprise away from dropping the object. The test scales the mass and inertia of every body the lift carries by mass_scale and the sliding and torsional friction of the grasped geoms and of their hand contact pairs by friction_scale, then drives the executor's grasp (open-hand descent, close, torque-capped clamp), lifts lift_m, holds hold_s (slip rate below slip_max_mm_s) and carries the object shake_m out and back along up, forward, back, left and right in move_s per leg (drift in the wrist frame below drift_max_mm). With compare_nominal the same ladder is first run unscaled, so the issue can say whether the margin or the grasp itself is the problem. A part on a fixed asset cannot be lifted, so the test reports applicable=False with ok=True.

tools.name: grasp_opposition_test
tools.title: Contact opposition test
tools.summary: Close the hand as the executor does and check that the hand-object contacts include two opposing groups whose normals face each other across the object's centre, so the grasp is a squeeze and not a hook or a press against the table.
tools.description: After the executor's close (pre-grasp, descent, close, torque-capped clamp) the hand-object contacts are read from the simulator over a 0.1 s hold (a torque-capped pad chatters on a light object, so one step is not a reading) and grouped by link (each finger, the palm). A group counts when its normal force reaches min_force_N; its direction is the force-weighted mean of its contact normals (pointing into the object) and its point the force-weighted contact centroid. The test takes the two groups whose directions are furthest apart and requires (1) at least two loaded groups, (2) an opposition of at least min_opposition_deg: the angle between their normals, or, when the normal forces share a common push (fingertips on a rim pressing down and in while friction carries the weight), the angle between their components across that push, (3) the object's centre of mass on the inner side of both contact planes ((c - p) . n >= -com_margin_frac x object size: the pads span the object rather than both pressing one side), and (4) while the object still rests on its support (it did not rise, or lift_m is 0), a press fraction |sum F| / sum |F| of the hand's normal forces no higher than max_press_frac (a hand whose forces all push one way, into the table, is leaning on the support, not gripping). A single-finger hook, a flat press from above and a grasp that only pins the object against the table all fail. With lift_m > 0 and a free object the hand then lifts it lift_m and the verdict is taken on the LIFTED contacts (only the hand holds it then: a claw that cradles a toy touches it only after the lift, a grasp that leans the object on the table loses it); when it does not rise (a cap still on its thread, a grasp that does not lift) the seated contacts are judged and a note says so.

tools.name: grasp_pose_noise_test
tools.title: Grasp pose noise test
tools.summary: Re-run the executor's close, lift and hold with the hand pose off by a calibration-sized error (default 2 mm and 2 deg) in several random directions; fail when any perturbed grasp drops or slips.
tools.description: A real arm puts the hand within a couple of millimetres and degrees of its command, so a grasp that only works at the exact pose will fail on the bench as soon as the calibration is off. The test draws n_trials wrist errors of exactly pos_noise_mm and rot_noise_deg in random directions (seeded, in antithetic pairs: +e and -e), applies each to the pose (translation, and a rotation about the wrist origin where a flange error acts, or about the pads' centroid with pivot='pads'), and runs the executor's grasp on each: open-hand descent from the pre-grasp, close, torque-capped clamp, a lift of lift_m (0.8 s, +0.3 s) and a hold of hold_s. A trial passes when the object rose more than half the lift, slipped less than slip_max_mm_s during the hold and a finger still touches it. The unperturbed pose is run first: when it fails the issue says so and points to grasp_lift_test. Passes when at least min_pass_frac of the perturbed trials pass (default all). A part on a fixed asset cannot be lifted, so the test reports applicable=False with ok=True.

tools.name: grasp_release_clean_test
tools.title: Clean release test
tools.summary: Grasp the object, set it back down and let go exactly as the executor's release does; fail when opening the hand or backing away flings, drags, lifts or tips the object.
tools.description: A grasp is also judged by how it ends: fingers that open INTO the object, a squeezed object that springs out of a releasing clamp, or a hand that backs away while a pad still drags on the object knock the placed object off its target (a release flick). The hand closes as the executor drives it (pre-grasp, descent, close, torque-capped clamp), lifts lift_m, comes back down until the object is set_down_m above where it rested (the executor's set-down clearance, measured on the object so in-hand slip during the lift does not ram it into its support), then releases as SubgoalPlanner._release does: the fingers go to the executor's open shape in 0.5 s (+0.3 s), the wrist backs off retreat_m along retreat_dir in 0.8 s (+0.2 s), and the scene settles for settle_s with the hand away. Measured from the moment before the fingers open: the object's horizontal slide and its spin about the vertical (an object that merely drops onto its support neither slides nor spins), its tip (its attitude against gravity at the end compared with how it rested before the grasp, so settling flat from a tilted hold is not a tip but landing on its side is), its largest rise (dragged up with the hand), its peak speed, and whether the hand still touches it at the end. Fails when any passes its limit or the hand is still on it; the issue names the phase (opening or retreat) where the object moved.

tools.name: grasp_shake_test
tools.title: Grasp carry-and-turn test
tools.summary: Hold the object, lift it, then carry it out and back in five directions and turn the wrist about three axes; pass when the object's drift in the wrist frame stays small.
tools.description: The hand approaches with the executor's opening and motion. Every physics substep checks contact penetration, including grip pads and self-contact; visible mesh penetration of the support is checked at 60 Hz. More than 3 mm fails regardless of lift or hold success. After the close-until-held and a short lift, the wrist translates shake_m out and back along up, forward, back, left and right, then rotates turn_deg and back about roll, pitch and yaw. Drift is the change of the object's position in the WRIST frame since seating, so an object that travels with the hand has not slipped however far it moved in the world. Each move and turn must keep the drift under drift_max_mm. This is the test that catches grasps which lift but rotate in the hand.

tools.name: grasp_slide_pull_test
tools.title: Grasp slide-pull test
tools.summary: Close the posed hand on a part that slides on a prismatic joint (drawer, tray, slider), translate the wrist along the joint axis by a set distance in physics, and pass when the part followed the hand, the pads stayed on it and no sibling joint of the same object was dragged along.
tools.description: The slide counterpart of grasp_turn_test. The hand scene is the floating-hand scene of hand_scene_from_recon (the last object holds the joint). The object's root is held still (as a brace or the bench would hold it); the open hand descends along the pose's approach axis onto the pose, closes to the pose's finger targets, presses to its squeezed targets, then the wrist is translated in steps along the joint axis in world frame (sign from `direction`: +1 moves the joint toward its upper limit) by `travel_m` with the fingers fixed. The verdict compares the joint's travel with the wrist's: PULLED when the fraction reaches `min_fraction` and at least one hand geom still touches the part at the end; SLIPPED / LOST / STALLED otherwise. Every other slide or hinge joint of the same object is watched: if one moves more than `sibling_tol` (m or rad) the hand caught the wrong part (a neighbouring drawer's handle) and the test fails with its name. Peak wrist force is reported against the hand's force cap.

inputs.description: Floating-hand scene {hand_xml, side, objects, floor, joint_init, grasp_body}; the last object holds the joint.

inputs.name: travel_m
inputs.description: Distance the wrist moves along the joint axis. Default 0.08.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: +1 toward the joint's upper limit (open), -1 toward the lower. Default +1.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Duration of the stroke. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Joint travel / wrist travel needed to pass. Default 0.8.

inputs.name: sibling_tol

inputs.name: approach_m

tools.name: grasp_slide_pull_test_preshaped
tools.title: Preshaped grasp slide-pull test
tools.summary: Drive a posed hand onto the handle of a sliding part with its own pre-grasp finger shape and approach path (a hook that drops in behind a bar), close, translate the wrist along the joint axis in physics, and pass when the part followed the hand and stayed in contact.
tools.description: A fork of grasp_slide_pull_test for grasps whose open hand cannot reach the pose: a finger hooked behind a drawer bar standing a few centimetres proud of the front, where the default 55% opening lays the finger on the housing instead of behind the bar. The pre-grasp finger shape is the pose's `finger_targets_open` when present, otherwise the closed shape opened by `open_frac` (0 = arrive closed, 0.55 = the default opening of the other tests); the fingers that do not grip stay curled. The wrist starts `approach_m` back along `approach_dir` (default the pose's own approach axis), visits the `approach_waypoints` (world offsets from the pose, as the subgoal planner takes them) and lands on the pose, then the fingers close to the pose's targets and press to its squeezed targets. The object's free root is held still (the bench, or the other hand, holds the housing). The wrist is then translated along the joint axis (sign from `direction`) by `travel_m` in steps with the fingers fixed. Verdict as in grasp_slide_pull_test: PULLED when joint travel / wrist travel reaches `min_fraction` and a hand geom still touches the part at the end; STALLED / LOST / SLIPPED otherwise. It also reports where the hand first touched the part during the approach and the deepest hand penetration into any object on the way, so a path that scrapes the housing is visible. Assumes the floating-hand scene convention of hand_scene_from_recon (the last object holds the joint).

tools.name: grasp_straddle_test
tools.title: Pinch straddle test
tools.summary: Check geometrically that a pinch has the bar between its two pads, on opposite sides and below the centre line, rather than both pads resting on top of it.
tools.description: Four conditions on the two fingertip sites of a posed hand relative to a bar (axis point, direction, radius): the pad-to-pad direction is roughly perpendicular to the axis (|cos| < 0.5; two pads lined up along a cord are not either side of it); the pads are on opposite sides of the axis in the cross-section plane (a sign test); the axis passes through the middle 70% of the pad segment within 2 mm, with each pad within a pad radius of the bar; and neither pad is above the bar's centre line, because the contact force runs from the pad centre toward the object centre and pads riding high only press it down (measured on a cord: pads 3 mm high held 7 N, the hand rose 50 mm, the cord stayed). tools.name: grasp_stress_test
tools.title: Grasp stress ladder
tools.summary: Drive a posed hand through approach, close, lift, carry, turn and hold in one continuous physics rollout and fail at the first phase the object is nudged, dropped, slips or drifts.
tools.description: Every phase goes through the hand's position actuators, never by teleporting onto the object. The open hand first settles back along its own retreat axis and descends to the pose (the object must not be nudged more than 20 mm); the fingers then ramp toward the press target and stop at the first configuration where the grip pads are on the object with more than 12 N (else the full press is used); after seating, the wrist lifts 60, 100 and 150 mm (each must raise the object more than half the commanded height), carries it 40 mm out and back along up, forward, back, left and right, turns 25 degrees about roll, pitch and yaw (object drift in the wrist frame below 30 mm), and holds still for 0.8 s (slip rate below 10 mm/s). Drift is measured in the wrist frame because a held object keeps a constant offset however far the hand travels. With maintain_N > 0 the grip fingers keep closing while the measured contact force is below that value, since a position servo bleeds off grip force as the object beds into the pads. Returns every phase's numbers and the name of the first failing phase. While the hand alone carries the object, the finger servos' reserve is judged as finger_servo_saturation_audit judges an episode (the smallest share of the finger torque caps with which the hand's contacts carry it, every executor frame): a grasp that holds only with a finger servo at 95% of its cap or more on 60% of the hold fails at 'servo_reserve' (a drive pinched 29 mm off its centre lifted with the thumb's abduction servo at 110% of its cap).

tools.name: grasp_stress_test_preopen
tools.title: Grasp stress test with a chosen pre-grasp opening
tools.summary: Run the approach, close, lift, carry-shake, turn and hold phases of a posed hand on an object from a chosen pre-grasp finger opening, so grasps of thin objects lying on a support (pens, cards, cables) are tested the way they are executed when a wide-open thumb would hit the support.
tools.description: The library's other grasp stress tests open the hand as the executor does (the pose's finger_targets_open or open_frac, else 55%, closed further until the open fingers clear the floor). For a thin object lying on a table (a pen, a rod, a card edge) a wide-open thumb swings below the object's centre line, lands on the table and is held there by friction, so the close never reaches the object even though the pose itself is sound. This verifier runs the same physics rollout (the shared stress_rollout of common/hand.py: approach along the pose's approach axis, close until held, then the selected phases) with the pre-grasp opening fixed to `open_frac`, or to the pose's own `open_frac`, or 0.55, so an opening can be tried before it is written into the pose. The executor (plan_subgoal_keyframes) honours the same `open_frac` key on the pose, so a pose that passes here is executed with the opening it was tested with. Passes when every selected phase passes: seated with at least one finger in contact, each commanded lift raises the object by lift_frac of the command, drift and slip under their limits. While the hand alone carries the object, the finger servos' reserve is judged as finger_servo_saturation_audit judges an episode (the smallest share of the finger torque caps with which the hand's contacts carry it, every executor frame): a grasp that holds only with a finger servo at 95% of its cap or more on 60% of the hold fails at 'servo_reserve' (a drive pinched 29 mm off its centre lifted with the thumb's abduction servo at 110% of its cap).

tools.name: grasp_table_support_dependence_test
tools.title: Support dependence test
tools.summary: Close the hand as the executor does, then take the table and every neighbouring object away from the grasped object and fail when the hand alone cannot keep it in place.
tools.description: A pose can look held only because the object still rests on something: the table under a hand that presses from above, a neighbouring brick in a stack, a lid sitting on its box. A lift test does not always expose it, since a wedged object can be dragged up with its neighbour or slide along it. Here the hand closes exactly as the executor drives it (pre-grasp, descent, close, torque-capped clamp, elliptic cones, no-slip, gravity-compensated hand); the support the object had at that moment is recorded (normal force from the floor and from each other body), then the object is made weightless, the floor and every other object stop colliding with it and with the hand (they float in place, gravity-compensated), its weight is ramped back over ramp_s so the hand takes the load as a slow lift would load it, and the wrist holds still for hold_s more. Passes when the object's drift in the wrist frame stays under drift_max_mm, its turn under turn_max_deg, and a finger still touches it at the end. A part on a fixed asset (no free joint up its tree) is held by its joint, so the test reports applicable=False with ok=True.

tools.description: Using a held object (pouring, wiping, pressing a trigger, a tool meeting resistance) loads the grasp with torques that a lift never applies, and a two-pad pinch that lifts cleanly can spin like an axle about the line between its pads. tools.title: Grasp turn test
tools.summary: Close the posed hand on a part that moves on a joint (a cap, a knob, a lid on a hinge; a drawer on a slide), drive the wrist along the joint's motion (an arc about a hinge, a translation along a slide) by a set amount in physics, and pass when the part followed the hand without the hand losing it.
tools.description: The stress test for a grasp whose job is torque. The hand scene is built with the object's root held fixed (a bottle steadied by the other hand, a cabinet on the floor) and the fingers are driven to the pose's closed and then pressed targets; the wrist is then servoed through an arc about the joint's axis (its world axis through the joint's world anchor, read from the model) in small steps, keeping the fingers' commands fixed and letting the hand rise with any thread coupling. It measures the joint angle reached against the angle the hand swept, the slip (sweep minus turn), the peak wrist force the arc needed, the pad contacts at the end, and whether any finger lost the part. Passes when the part turned at least `min_fraction` of the sweep and the hand still holds it at the end. Fails name the reason: SLIPPED (pads skate on the part), LOST (the hand came off), FLUNG (the part ran ahead of the hand: flicked, not held), STALLED (the joint did not move at all: wrong axis, joint blocked, or the pose presses the part sideways). Missing initial contact is reported as NO_CONTACT, not evidence of a blocked joint. Progress is signed along the requested direction; opposite motion cannot pass. Every simulated substep checks the same 3 mm hand/object/self penetration limit as the other grasp stress tests, including grip pads, with visible support penetration checked at 60 Hz. Runs on the same scene dict the grasp skills take.

inputs.name: joint

inputs.name: sweep_deg
inputs.description: Angle the hand swings about a hinge axis. Default 90.

inputs.name: sweep_m
inputs.description: Distance the hand travels along a slide axis. Default 0.08.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: +1 or -1 about the joint axis. Default +1.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Duration of the sweep. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Required turn / sweep. Default 0.8.

inputs.name: max_fraction
inputs.description: Turn / sweep above which the part ran ahead of the hand (FLUNG, not held); a jump of more than three sweep steps in one step also counts. Default 1.25.

inputs.name: hold_root
inputs.description: Hold the object's free root during the test by making it 10^4 times heavier (default true).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, verdict, measured {sweep_deg, turned_deg, fraction, slip_deg, lost_at_deg, pads_end, peak_wrist_force_n, peak_wrist_torque_nm, joint_before_close (the joint as the open hand arrives), joint_start (after the close, where the sweep is measured from), close_moved (deg or mm the close itself moved the part), joint_end}.

tools.name: grasp_turn_test_keep_state
tools.title: Grasp turn test (start state kept, rigid or level follow)
tools.summary: Like grasp_turn_test, but it reports the joint values the parts start the sweep at (the hand scene's joint_init after the close), and the wrist can follow the part rigidly or level: close the posed hand on a part that moves on a joint (a cap, a knob, a lid on a hinge; a drawer on a slide), drive the wrist along the joint's motion (an arc about a hinge, a translation along a slide) by a set amount in physics, and pass when the part followed the hand without the hand losing it.
tools.description: Fork of grasp_turn_test. Both keep the hand scene's joint_init start state (a lid's folded skirt flap, a part set half open) through the root-holding mass change; this fork also reports that start state (state_start: the object joint values after the press) and adds follow='level': the wrist keeps its orientation and its position rides a follow point (the mean of the hand-part contacts after the press, or the grip fingers' distal links when nothing touches) as that point turns about the hinge, which is how the subgoal executor drives open_joint with hand_follows='level' (pads that drag or lift a lid without the hand rolling with it). follow='rigid' is the original arc. The stress test for a grasp whose job is torque. The hand scene is built with the object's root held fixed (a bottle steadied by the other hand, a cabinet on the floor) and the fingers are driven to the pose's closed and then pressed targets; the wrist is then servoed through an arc about the joint's axis (its world axis through the joint's world anchor, read from the model) in small steps, keeping the fingers' commands fixed and letting the hand rise with any thread coupling.
