tools.name: hand_contact_pair_mask_check
tools.title: Hand contact pair mask check
tools.summary: The hands collide only through explicit contact pairs; checks that the pairs a scene has, plus the ones the Stage 3 executor will add, respect each object geom's own contype/conaffinity intent (a magnet shell meant only for ring-ring contact must not become solid to the hand) and that every solid object geom gets a pair with each hand.
tools.description: The Sharpa hands ship with contype/conaffinity 0 and touch objects only through <pair>s: the executor (episode.build_execution_model) pairs every hand collision geom with every object geom whose contype or conaffinity meets the hand's contact bits (hand.hand_may_touch with HAND_CONTACT_BITS, MuJoCo's own rule), unless the geom or its class opts out with the suffix 'nohand'; it names unnamed geoms itself, so they are paired too. Two failures follow. A geom whose bits do not include the bits the table and arm use (the 'solid' bits, read from the table's collision geom, default 1) is meant for special contacts only, e.g. the EgoDex rings' magnet shell with its own bit; a hand pair makes that invisible shell solid to the fingers, which then grip a sphere around the ring instead of the ring. And a solid object geom that gets no pair (its bits miss the hand's, or it opts out) lets the hand pass straight through it. With include_executor_pairs (default) the executor's rule is applied on top of the scene's explicit pairs; with False only the explicit pairs count and every solid object geom must be paired with every collision geom of each hand. An unpaired solid geom that lies inside the paired geoms of its own body (within cover_tol_m: the support feet of a battery inside its can) is covered and needs no pair. Hand geoms are those whose name contains hand_geom_pattern.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: include_executor_pairs
inputs.description: Add the pairs build_execution_model will add (object geoms the hand's contact bits meet and that do not opt out with 'nohand', x the hand's collision geoms). Default True.

inputs.name: hand_geom_pattern
inputs.description: Substring naming the hands' collision geoms. Default '_collision_hand_'.

inputs.name: solid_bits
inputs.description: contype/conaffinity bits of ordinary solid contact. Default: the table geom's bits (1 without a table).

inputs.name: sides
inputs.description: Hands that must reach the objects. Default: every hand found.

inputs.name: cover_tol_m
inputs.description: An unpaired solid geom lying within this distance inside the paired geoms of its body (support feet inside a can) needs no pair of its own, metres. Default 0.002.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; hands {side: n collision geoms}; solid_bits; pairs {explicit, executor}; special_paired [{geom, bits, source}]; unpaired [{geom, side, why}]; objects_geoms_checked.

tools.name: hand_joint_rate_audit
tools.title: Hand joint rate audit
tools.summary: Finger joint chatter (rapid back-and-forth reversals) and finger joint accelerations; finger speed itself is joint_speed_check's.
tools.description: joint_speed_check covers finger speed (0.30 rad/frame at 30 fps), so this audit covers what it misses on the same joints. Chatter: for every finger joint it marks the frames where the joint reverses direction with both the step before and the step after larger than amp_rad (default 0.01 rad, above servo noise), and counts reversals inside every window of window_s (default 0.5 s); max_reversals or more (default 6, i.e. six turnarounds in half a second) is a finger vibrating against a contact or a grip command toggling, which on hardware is audible buzzing and wears the tendons. Acceleration: the raw second difference of each finger joint against max_acc_rad_s2 (default 150 rad/s^2; the paper's executed episodes peak near 70 when a contact makes or breaks): a finger that reverses at full speed in one frame. Fingers come from the bench hands (episode.robot_parts) or, for other robots, the actuated joints of the hand bodies. Reports per hand the worst joint for each rule with its frames and phase label.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: amp_rad
inputs.description: Smallest step on both sides of a reversal that counts (at 30 fps). Default 0.01.

inputs.name: window_s
inputs.description: Window for counting reversals. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: max_reversals
inputs.description: Reversals in one window that make chatter. Default 6.

inputs.name: max_acc_rad_s2
inputs.description: Raw second-difference limit. Default 150.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, joint, kind, frame, label, value}; hands {side: max reversals per window, peak acceleration, joints}.

tools.name: hand_object_contact_consistency_check
tools.title: Hand-object contact consistency
tools.summary: With metric hand joints from the demonstration (EgoDex hands.npz), the fingertips must reach each object's reconstructed surface at first contact, including a physically replayed previous support motion when measured tracking supports one. Unexplained gaps remain failures.
tools.description: For every Stage 1 object, the first subgoal whose acting hand grasps, holds, pushes, pulls, presses or opens it (motion in a fixed set) gives a time window (time_window_s, converted to frames with the episode fps). The object's collision and visible material is measured per geom: analytic primitives, convex collision mesh hulls, and actual visual mesh triangles. Empty spaces between walls are not filled. Over the window the acting hand's fingertips (all five for the gap, thumb, index and middle for the depth inside; both hands for 'both') come closest to that surface at some frame; the smallest fingertip-to-surface distance must be at most `tol_m`. A failed initial-surface comparison can also be checked against an internally replayed previous articulated support motion, anchored to measured fingertip tracking and initial physical contact. Only bounded force on that support joint is applied; carried objects move through physics. Replay states are aligned to the source time window; no supplied object poses or arbitrary joint sweeps count. This narrow consistency witness does not prove robot execution feasibility. An object Stage 1 says a hand already holds at the first frame (initial_state) whose first contact starts there is skipped with that reason: the scene must start it at rest. The report gives, per object, the window, the closest frame and fingertip, the gap and the offset from the surface to the fingertip (which direction the object would have to move). Objects the hands never act on, or whose first window falls outside the joints' frames, are listed as skipped. Without hands.npz (a video without metric hand joints) the check does not apply and says so. A group object (its scene_recon.json entry lists its separate pieces under `parts`) is measured against the surface of all its pieces, so the gap is to the nearest piece, which the report names (`part`).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene.xml (objects at their fitted frame-0 poses; keyframe 0 used when present).

inputs.name: hands_npz
inputs.description: hands.npz from read_egodex_episode (names, rig_xyz [T, J, 3]) in the scene's rig frame. None: not applicable.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 scene_semantic(s).json (subgoals with acting_hand, motion, object_refs, time_window_s).

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json (object id -> root_body).

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frames per second of the joints; default: episode.json next to hands.npz, else 30.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed fingertip-to-surface gap at the closest frame. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_penetration_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed depth of a fingertip inside any material component over the contact window. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: pad_s
inputs.description: Seconds added on both sides of the window. Default 0.3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, applicable, objects {id: {subgoal, frames, closest_frame, fingertip, gap_m, offset_m, ok, part (group objects: the nearest piece)}}, skipped {id: reason}.

tools.name: hand_object_relative_jitter_audit
tools.title: Hand-object relative jitter audit
tools.summary: High-frequency jitter of a held object relative to the hand during hold phases: the residual of the relative pose after a short smoothing filter, peak and RMS.
tools.description: held_object_slip_audit measures low-frequency drift; this audit measures the high-frequency part. For every run of phases in which a hand holds an object (labels with grip, lift, carry, hold, set down, lower, place, pour, insert, turn, twist; object named in the label or the one touching the hand on most of the run), the object's position and orientation in the hand's wrist frame are high-passed by subtracting a Savitzky-Golay fit (quadratic, smooth_frames, default 9 at 30 fps, 0.3 s), which keeps slow slip and seating and removes nothing a real grasp does. The residual's peak and RMS must stay under peak_mm / rms_mm (defaults 3 mm, 1 mm; the paper's executed episodes peak at 1.1 mm) and peak_deg / rms_deg (defaults 4 deg, 1.5 deg). Reports the worst window per hand and object.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: peak_mm, rms_mm
inputs.description: Allowed positional jitter. Defaults 3, 1.

inputs.name: peak_deg, rms_deg
inputs.description: Allowed rotational jitter. Defaults 4, 1.5.

inputs.name: smooth_frames
inputs.description: Savitzky-Golay window at 30 fps (odd). Default 9.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, object, frames, labels, peak_mm, rms_mm, peak_deg, rms_deg, peak_frame}; windows.

tools.name: height_check
tools.title: Height check
tools.summary: The world-z of a body's centre lies within [lo, hi], with half a millimetre of slack.
tools.description: Measures the body's height for you and compares it with the band. The band should be stated relative to the scene's own table top, which is rarely z = 0; pass `relative_to` (a body name) to express lo and hi as offsets from that body's centre instead of absolute heights. Half a millimetre of slack keeps a band copied from a printed measurement from failing on rounding.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The body to measure.

inputs.name: lo
inputs.description: Lower bound.

inputs.name: hi
inputs.description: Upper bound.

inputs.name: relative_to
inputs.description: Measure relative to this body's centre height.

inputs.name: settled
inputs.description: Judge after settling (default) or at the initial state.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; z (measured value compared with the band); reference_z.

tools.name: held_object_slip_audit
tools.title: Held object slip audit
tools.summary: During carry phases the held object's pose relative to the hand drifts no more than a tolerance from where it sat when the carry began.
tools.description: No audit measures in-hand slip on the delivered episode (the grasp stress tests run on a hand scene, the executor's per-subgoal outcome is written at execution time). For every run of phases whose label says the side carries (carry, transport; consecutive runs of the same hand and object, e.g. carry up / across / down, are joined), with the object named in the label or, when it names none, the object touching that hand on most of the run, the object's pose is expressed in the frame of the hand's wrist body on every frame. An articulated object (a cable or ribbon of linked segments, a box with a hinged lid) is judged at the link the hand holds, the body of the object its contacts touch most on the carry's first frame that has any (the deepest contact breaks a tie), and at the point those contacts touch, not at its root: a fingertip dragging the end link of a ribbon moves that link, while the ribbon's junction 10 cm away swings with the rest of the strand (a false 108 mm). The turn of a cable link (a segment on a ball joint) is reported but not judged: it is the cable's local bend and twist under the pad, which no fingertip or pinch holds. The drift is the largest distance and rotation from that relative pose at the carry's first frame. It fails above slip_m (default 20 mm) or slip_deg (default 15 deg). Lift phases are left out by default: the grip seats while the object leaves its support (the paper's executed episodes seat by up to 13 mm there); pass words to include them. Reports the worst window per hand and object with the frame where the drift peaks.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: slip_m, slip_deg
inputs.description: Allowed drift of the relative pose. Defaults 0.02 m, 15 deg.

inputs.name: words
inputs.description: Phase words that mark a carry. Default ['carry', 'transport'].

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, object, body (the link judged), frames, labels, drift_mm, drift_deg, turn_judged, peak_frame}; windows (all, with drift).

tools.name: held_through_window_gate
tools.title: Held through window gate
tools.summary: On every frame of a window the object is held: touched by the hand on at least two links with opposing contact normals and not supported by the table ('in_hand'), or touched by the hand and not moving ('fixed', a steadying hold).
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the battery is held in the right fingers' and 'the bottle is carried over the mug'. Each frame of the window (every stride-th) is loaded in the execution model, whose hand hulls are paired with every object, and collision detection runs with a 1 mm margin on the hand and the object. A frame counts as held in mode 'in_hand' when hand links touch the object on at least min_links distinct bodies, two of the contact normals are at least opposing_deg apart (a pinch, a wrap, two hands squeezing a lid) and the object does not touch the table (allow_table for a rope whose rest still lies on the cloth); in mode 'fixed' when any hand link touches it, and over the window the object moves less than stay_tol_m / stay_tol_deg. The window passes when at least min_frac of the frames are held, the longest run of unheld frames is at most max_gap_s (a drop and re-catch fails) and the last frame is held. The hand is a side ('left', 'right'; both when None) or an explicit list of body names or name prefixes.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The held object (its subtree).

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: 'left', 'right', or None for either hand.

inputs.name: hand_bodies
inputs.description: Body names or prefixes that make up the hand, instead of side.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: 'in_hand' or 'fixed'. Default in_hand.

inputs.name: min_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of frames that must be held. Default 0.9.

inputs.name: max_gap_s
inputs.description: Longest allowed run of unheld frames, s. Default 0.25.

inputs.name: opposing_deg
inputs.description: Angle two contact normals must span. Default 100.

inputs.name: min_links
inputs.description: Distinct hand links touching. Default 2.

inputs.name: allow_table
inputs.description: Allow table contact while held (a rope). Default false.

inputs.name: stay_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed motion in 'fixed' mode, m. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: stay_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed rotation in 'fixed' mode, deg. Default 8.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame step. Default 1.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; mode; frames; held_fraction; longest_unheld_s; longest_unheld_from; end_links; end_opposing; end_on_table; moved_m and rotated_deg in fixed mode.

tools.name: hinge_drive_check
tools.title: Hinge drive check
tools.summary: On an executed episode, a hinged part (a lid, a flap, a door) turned through a required angle while a holder (a hand) was on it, without falling back, so the turn was driven by the hand rather than flung or dropped.
tools.description: The physics proof for a part moved about its hinge by a hand that does not grasp it: fingers hooked under a lid, a flat hand lifting a flap, a fingertip pushing a door. Such contact is one-sided and intermittent, so a hold-force window (contact_force_check) under-reads it and a floating-hand turn test cannot reproduce the arm-carried hand. The check replays the window frame by frame in the scene as the bench executor runs it (hand-object contact pairs added; a scene without robot hands uses its own collision geometry), counts a frame as touching when any holder collision geom is within `contact_tol_m` of the part (contact margins raised to the tolerance for the replay), and measures the part's joint: its travel in the driven direction (inferred from the net change unless `direction` is given), the largest fall-back below its best progress, the share of the forward travel made on frames with the holder on the part or within `lag_frames` after (the driven fraction), the share of touching frames and the longest stretch without contact. Passes when the travel reaches `min_travel_deg`, the fall-back stays under `max_backslide_deg` and the driven fraction reaches `min_driven_frac`. Issues name what failed and what to change.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene the trajectory belongs to (a bench scene, or any scene with the holder and the part).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, labels, fps) or a qpos array.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: The hinge (or slide) the part moves on.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: Root body of the holder (its subtree counts: a hand with its fingers).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Window: frame indices, or phase-label patterns. Default all frames.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: +1 or -1: the sign of the joint change the hand drives. Default: the sign of the net change.

inputs.name: min_travel_deg
inputs.description: Required travel in the driven direction (degrees, or mm for a slide). Default 20.

inputs.name: max_backslide_deg
inputs.description: Largest fall-back below the best progress (degrees / mm). Default 5.

inputs.name: min_driven_frac
inputs.description: Required share of the forward travel made while the holder touched the part. Default 0.8.

inputs.name: contact_tol_m
inputs.description: Gap below which the holder counts as on the part. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: lag_frames
inputs.description: Frames after a touching frame whose travel still counts as driven (the part's momentum). Default 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; measured {frames, direction, joint_start, joint_end, travel, best, backslide and its frame, driven_frac, contact_frac, longest_gap_frames, unit}.

tools.name: hinged_lid_closure_test
tools.title: Hinged lid: rests open, closes, stays shut
tools.summary: Three force-only trials on a box with a hinged lid (and optional skirt crease): the lid stays where frame 0 left it, a capped hinge torque swings it shut (then folds the skirt down), and released it stays seated shut under gravity.
tools.description: Loads a standalone asset MJCF (with its floor) and runs three trials from qpos0. REST: no forces for rest_s seconds; the lid and skirt must stay within tol_deg of their initial angles (an open lid lying folded back must not creep). CLOSE: a speed-limited torque on the lid joint toward closed_deg, capped at torque_factor times the lid subtree's gravity torque about the hinge (or torque_Nm), for close_s seconds, then a capped torque on the skirt joint toward skirt_closed_deg; both must reach their closed angle within tol_deg. HOLD: all torques removed for hold_s seconds; the lid and skirt must stay shut within tol_deg and the base must not slip more than root_slip_m at rest or after release. Torques act on the joints directly (qfrc_applied), so the trial judges the mechanism and its stops, not a grasp. Returns ok, issues and every measured angle.

inputs.name: xml
inputs.description: Standalone asset MJCF (built with include_floor on).

inputs.name: lid_joint
inputs.description: Name of the lid hinge joint.

inputs.name: skirt_joint
inputs.description: Name of the skirt crease joint, or None. Default None.

inputs.name: closed_deg
inputs.description: Lid joint value when shut. Default 0.

inputs.name: skirt_closed_deg
inputs.description: Skirt joint value when folded down. Default 90.

inputs.name: torque_Nm
inputs.description: Fixed closing torque; None = torque_factor x gravity torque. Default None.

inputs.name: torque_factor
inputs.description: Multiple of the moving part's gravity torque. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: rest_s
inputs.description: REST trial length, s. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: close_s
inputs.description: Seconds per closing push. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: HOLD trial length, s. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: tol_deg
inputs.description: Angle tolerance, deg. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: root_slip_m
inputs.description: Allowed base translation during REST and HOLD (the pushes may shift a free base), m. Default 0.01.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; rest: initial/final angles and drift; close: reached angles and torques; hold: final angles and drift; root_slip_m.

tools.name: holds_at_video_end_check
tools.title: Holds at video end check
tools.summary: From the final frame, hold the robot still and run gravity: the object must stay in hand (or stay put where it was placed).
tools.description: Takes the trajectory's last frame (or any frame), freezes every robot joint by writing the pose back each step, and runs the scene's physics for settle_s seconds. The body passes when its displacement over that time stays under drop_tol (1 cm by default) and its rotation under 10 degrees; if the pose has it resting on something (placed, not held) the same test says whether the placement is stable. Any object that falls, slips out or is squeezed out by over-closed fingers fails. Reports the drift, how many robot bodies touch the object, and whether the object is in contact with the table at the start (held vs placed). Requires the scene's collision geometry and masses. The robot is pinned through its joints' qpos (every joint of a body with robot_prefix); a mocap-driven hand has no joints and stays at the model's mocap pose, not the frame's, so pose its mocap bodies in the scene first.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene with collision geometry.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Object that must stay held or placed.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: Hand root body; reported contact count uses its subtree.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame to test from. Default -1 (the end).

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Physics time. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: drop_tol_m, rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Defaults 0.01 m, 10 deg.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Bodies with this prefix are pinned. Default 'robot_'.

inputs.name: noslip_iterations
inputs.description: No-slip solver passes during the settle, so soft-contact creep is not read as a drop. Default 10.

inputs.name: rigid_armature
inputs.description: Default 1000.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; drift_m, rot_deg, held (robot contacts at start), on_table, contacts at end, frame tested.

tools.name: inertia_validity_check
tools.title: Inertia validity check
tools.summary: Every body's inertia is positive (semi-)definite and satisfies the triangle inequality, no moving body has zero or negative mass, and each moving rigid part's radius of gyration fits its own geometry (no placeholder inertias).
tools.description: MuJoCo refuses some impossible inertias at compile time, but a model edited at run time, an inertia clamped by boundmass / boundinertia / balanceinertia, or a placeholder copied from a URDF (diaginertia 1e-6 on a 300 g box, or 1 kg m^2 on a cup) compiles and then spins too freely or not at all. The check works on rigid parts: bodies welded together without a joint count as one part (the part of a body is its weld root). For every body it checks finite non-negative mass, non-negative principal inertia and the triangle inequality I1 + I2 >= I3. For every part that moves (its root has joints), it checks that the part, with what it carries, weighs more than `min_mass_kg`, that its composite inertia about its centre of mass is positive definite when it can rotate, and and, for a part that turns freely (free or ball joint, where only its own inertia resists turning), that its largest radius of gyration sqrt(I_max / m) lies between `rg_ratio_min` and `rg_ratio_max` times the half-extent of the part's geometry at the initial state (a solid sphere gives 0.63, a rod 0.58, a cube 0.82). Across each joint the mass ratio of the two parts must stay under `max_mass_ratio`, beyond which the solver is ill-conditioned. Parts without geometry (wrist slide/hinge carriers) are only checked for mass and definiteness, and an intermediate link lighter than 1% of what it carries (the massless 'virtual link' between two axes of a finger joint) only for the mass it carries.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: min_mass_kg
inputs.description: Smallest mass of a moving part. Default 1e-6.

inputs.name: rg_ratio_min
inputs.description: Smallest radius of gyration / part half-extent. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: rg_ratio_max
inputs.description: Largest radius of gyration / part half-extent. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: max_mass_ratio
inputs.description: Largest mass ratio between the two parts a joint connects. Default 1e6.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe giving the pose the part extents are measured at. Default 0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; bad_bodies: [{body, mass, inertia, problem}]; parts: [{part, bodies, mass_kg, principal_inertia, half_extent_m, rg_ratio, problem}] (problems first); worst; n_moving_parts.

tools.name: initial_keyframe_state_check
tools.title: Initial keyframe state check
tools.summary: Keyframe 0 exists with finite values of the right sizes, puts every robot joint at the setup's home pose (wrist positions moved with their station), and the objects are settled at it: simulated briefly with the robot held still, no object may drift, tilt or open beyond a few millimetres or degrees.
tools.description: Stage 3 and Stage 4 start every rollout from keyframe 0. A scene without a keyframe starts the robot at qpos0 (arms folded, hands at the origin) and the objects wherever the XML put them; a keyframe whose objects are not at rest (the hand-built cup example starts tilted and settles 47 mm) makes the first frames of every trajectory a settling transient that Stage 3 mistakes for its own action. The check: (1) at least one keyframe, with key_qpos (nq), key_ctrl (nu) and mocap entries finite; (2) every robot joint matched to the setup (default: the repository's setup/) equals the setup's home within tol_joint, the hands' wrist slides allowed to move by their station root's displacement from the setup (stage_station_integrity_check decides whether that displacement is legitimate); (3) servo targets in key_ctrl that differ from the joint values they drive are reported as a warning (the executor overwrites ctrl; a plain reset-and-step drives the hand to them), or as an issue with ctrl_must_match; (4) from keyframe 0 the scene is stepped for settle_s seconds with every robot joint clamped at its home value, and each object with a free joint must stay within drift_tol_m and tilt_tol_deg, each object hinge/slide within joint_tol of its keyframe value (half of it warns). A bad acceleration that makes MuJoCo reset the simulation (a part away from the weld or joint holding it) fails.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder holding the home keyframe. Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Seconds simulated with the robot held. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: drift_tol_m
inputs.description: Largest object translation while settling, metres. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: tilt_tol_deg
inputs.description: Largest object rotation while settling, degrees. Default 3.

inputs.name: joint_tol
inputs.description: Largest object hinge (rad) / slide (m) change while settling: [hinge, slide] or one number. Default [0.25, 0.01] (a falling lid moves far more; a flap sagging onto its stop less); half of it is reported as a warning.

inputs.name: tol_joint
inputs.description: Allowed robot joint difference from home, rad or m. Default 1e-4.

inputs.name: ctrl_must_match
inputs.description: Fail (not warn) when key_ctrl servo targets differ from the keyframe's joints. Default False.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; warnings; keyframe {n, name, nq, nu}; home {compared, off [{joint, scene, home}]}; ctrl_mismatch [{actuator, ctrl, joint_value}]; settle {object: {drift_m, tilt_deg}}; joints {joint: change}; worst (largest drift, m).

tools.name: ink_round_trip_test
tools.title: Ink round-trip test
tools.summary: A nib in contact marks the board, a nib in the air does not, a jump is not joined, and a pad wipe clears the mark; all read off the live texture.
tools.description: Loads a board built by construct_whiteboard and drives its InkSurface with world points: a 60% width stroke on the face (gap 0) must raise the darkness of its bounding rectangle above min_ink; the same stroke at `air_gap_m` above the face must leave the darkness under max_ghost; two dabs far apart on the board must not produce a connecting line (the midpoint rectangle stays clean); a pad wipe over the first stroke must bring its rectangle back under max_ghost. With render=True the texture is uploaded to a MuJoCo renderer and the frame's dark pixel count over the board must change between the inked and wiped states. Works on any asset that exposes surface_geom and texture names in its built dict.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_whiteboard returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: air_gap_m
inputs.description: Height of the no-contact stroke. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: min_ink
inputs.description: Darkness a contact stroke must reach. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: max_ghost
inputs.description: Darkness allowed after an air stroke or a wipe. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: wipe_passes
inputs.description: Back-and-forth passes of the pad over the stroke. Default 20 (one pass takes 16% of the ink).

inputs.name: render
inputs.description: Also check the texture reaches a rendered frame. Default True.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All four texture checks (and the render check) passed.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence with the darkness numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: darkness after contact stroke / air stroke / jump / wipe, and the rendered dark pixel counts.

tools.name: ink_trace_check
tools.title: Ink trace check
tools.summary: Replay an executed episode frame by frame on a writable surface's live ink texture (nib sites ink where they touch it, felt pads lighten what they cover) and check that named regions end inked or clean.
tools.description: Writing and erasing are outcomes on a texture, not on a body pose, so the subgoal outcome check cannot see them. This verifier resolves the surface geom and its texture in the compiled scene (suffix match, so an asset attached under a prefix is found), resets the texture to its pristine state, and walks the trajectory: on every frame each nib site inks the surface where its gap to the writing face is at most `max_gap_m` (joined to its previous inked sample unless the jump is larger than `max_jump_m`, so a lift-and-move draws nothing), and each pad geom whose bottom face lies flat within `pad_gap_m` of the face lightens the rotated rectangle it covers by `efficiency` per frame (one pass does not erase; back-and-forth wiping does). Regions are rectangles in WORLD x/y on the surface (converted to the surface's own frame at frame 0), each with an expectation 'inked' (ink fraction >= min_ink) or 'clean' (<= max_ink), judged after replaying up to `at_frame` (default the last frame), so 'the 4 was written' and 'the 4 was wiped off' are separate gates on one replay. It also reports per nib the frames in contact and the inked path length, and writes the final texture as a PNG for a look. Assumes the surface is a box geom whose +z face is the writing face and whose texture maps its x/y extent (the construct_whiteboard convention, shared through tool_library.common.ink.InkSurface).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene (the scene the episode was executed in).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq]) or the qpos array.

inputs.name: surface_geom
inputs.description: Writing-face geom name (or its unprefixed suffix, e.g. 'board_panel').

inputs.name: texture
inputs.description: Its live texture name (or suffix, e.g. 'board_ink').

inputs.name: nibs
inputs.description: Site names that write (or suffixes). Default: every non-robot site whose name ends with 'tip'.

inputs.name: pads
inputs.description: Box geoms whose bottom (-z) face wipes (felt pads). Default none.

inputs.name: regions
inputs.description: [{name, rect: [x0, x1, y0, y1] world metres, expect: 'inked'|'clean', min_ink? (default 0.02), max_ink? (default 0.004), at_frame? (int, default last)}]. At least one: with none nothing is judged and the check fails.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] frame window to replay. Default the whole episode.

inputs.name: nib_radius_m
inputs.description: Ink line radius. Default 0.0018.

inputs.name: max_gap_m
inputs.description: Largest nib height above the face that still inks. Default 0.0012.

inputs.name: max_jump_m
inputs.description: Largest step between inked samples that is joined. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: pad_gap_m
inputs.description: Largest pad-face height above the surface that wipes. Default 0.0025.

inputs.name: efficiency
inputs.description: Fraction of the remaining ink one frame of pad contact removes. Default 0.16.

inputs.name: ink_rgb
inputs.description: Ink colour 0-255. Default [18, 18, 22].

inputs.name: board_rgb
inputs.description: Blank colour 0-255. Default [249, 249, 246].

inputs.name: out_png
inputs.description: Write the final texture here.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; regions {name: {expect, ink, at_frame, ok}}; nibs {site: {contact_frames, first, last, inked_path_m}}; pads {geom: {contact_frames}}; n_frames; png.

tools.name: insertion_depth_gate
tools.title: Insertion depth gate
tools.summary: Depth of A along an insertion axis past B's entry plane (a drive in its slot, a plug in its port, a battery in its cell) reaches a minimum depth or a minimum fraction of A's length; without an axis, A is seated inside B's envelope and touches it.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the drive sits in the top slot', 'the plug tip is fully inside the port' and 'the tray front is flush with the stack'. axis is the insertion direction in B's root frame; the entry plane is perpendicular to it through `entry` (a point in B's frame), by default B's outer face on the side A comes from (the extent of B's collision geoms along -axis). A's leading point, centre of mass and trailing point along the axis come from exact support functions of its collision geoms. With min_depth_m the chosen point (leading, com or trailing) must be at least that far past the entry plane (a negative value allows a part that stops just short: flush within that much); otherwise min_fraction of A's length along the axis must be past it. Without an axis the gate checks that A's centre lies inside B's collision extent in B's frame (more than half inserted along whichever axis it entered) and that A touches B; table contact is reported but allowed, since a slot with an open floor lets the part rest on the table.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The inserted body A.

inputs.name: receiver
inputs.description: The body B it goes into (holder, case, socket).

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: Insertion direction in B's frame; None for the envelope test.

inputs.name: entry
inputs.description: A point of the entry plane in B's frame, m. Default B's outer face.

inputs.name: min_depth_m
inputs.description: Required depth of `point` past the entry plane, m.

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Required fraction of A's length past the plane when no min_depth_m. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: 'leading', 'com' or 'trailing'. Default leading.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last]; decided on the last frame.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Decide on this frame instead.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; mode ('axis' | 'envelope'); depth_m; inserted_fraction; length_along_axis_m; axis_world; com_in_B, B_lo, B_hi, depth_inside_m in envelope mode; touches_B; touches_table.

tools.name: inside_container_gate
tools.title: Inside-container gate
tools.summary: A's centre of mass is inside B's interior volume and A rests on B below its rim band (not on the rim, not on the table) at the end of a window; optionally A's whole footprint lies within B's.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the cup stands on the inner bottom of the bowl' and 'the toy rests inside the tray'. On the decision frame B's frame is its root body's pose with the axis nearest to vertical taken as up; B's interior is the extent of B's collision geoms along those axes (exact support functions of boxes, cylinders, capsules, spheres, ellipsoids and mesh vertices). A passes when (1) its mass-weighted centre lies inside B's footprint (shrunk by xy_margin_m) and between B's floor and rim height (+ com_above_rim_m for a part taller than the container), (2) at least one A-B contact lies below the rim band (the top max(rim_band_min_m, rim_band_frac x depth) of B), so A rests on B's inner floor or walls and not balanced on the rim, and (3) A does not touch the table. entirely additionally requires A's footprint inside B's. A cup that ends on a bowl's rim fails (2) and usually (1); a toy dropped beside the tray fails (1) and (3).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The contained body A.

inputs.name: container
inputs.description: The container body B (its subtree: a drawer's tray, a bowl).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last]; decided on the last frame.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Decide on this frame instead.

inputs.name: rim_band_frac
inputs.description: Rim band as a fraction of B's depth. Default 0.15.

inputs.name: rim_band_min_m
inputs.description: Smallest rim band, m. Default 0.004.

inputs.name: xy_margin_m
inputs.description: Shrink B's footprint by this much for the centre test, m. Default 0.

inputs.name: com_above_rim_m
inputs.description: How far A's centre may sit above the rim, m. Default 0.

inputs.name: entirely
inputs.description: Require A's whole footprint inside B's. Default false.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; com_in_B; B_interior_lo/hi; com_inside_xy; com_inside_height; contacts_with_B; contacts_below_rim; rim_band_m; touches_table; entirely_inside_footprint.

tools.name: isaac_deformable_rest_check
tools.title: Isaac deformable rest check
tools.summary: Re-measures every deformable a Stage 2 scene simulates in Isaac Sim from its files: the cord specification and its settled link poses, the settling report (no PhysX errors), drift from the laid centreline, chain connectivity and stretch, self-interpenetration, sinking into the table or a rigid object, no MuJoCo copy, and the settled cord's silhouette through the camera against the object's mask.
tools.description: The Isaac Sim counterpart of deformable_rest_check and deformable_topology_check: deformable objects are simulated in Isaac Sim only, so their rest state is the one build_isaac_scene settled, and nothing written in scene_recon.json about it is taken on trust. For every entry with type deformable and simulator 'isaac' (or skill build_isaac_scene): isaac.cord_json must load as an isaac_cord specification with settled link_poses (one centre and one unit quaternion per link, finite); n_links, segment_m, length_m and radius must agree with each other and with the measured centreline (points); isaac.report_json must say ok with no PhysX invalid transforms or errors. From the poses: (1) drift of every link from where the cord was laid (the points resampled into its links): mean <= max_mean_drift_m (0.02) and max <= max_link_drift_m (0.05), as the MuJoCo rest check; the report's and the entry's claimed mean drift must match the recomputed one within 5 mm; (2) connectivity: neighbouring links meet at their joint (each link's end against the next link's start within max(2 mm, 10% of a link)): one chain, two free ends, no torn or fused link; neighbouring centres at most 10% further apart than one link; (3) self-interpenetration at rest: capsules (the PhysX geometry, trimmed cylinder plus radius) at least two links apart overlap by at most self_tol_m (2 mm), as deformable_topology_check; (4) the table: no link's lowest point more than pen_m (3 mm) below the table top of scene.xml; (5) rigid objects and the robot: no link's axis point deeper than pen_m inside a collidable geom of scene.xml at keyframe 0; (6) no MuJoCo copy: scene.xml has no body named like the cord's or the entry's MuJoCo cable (<name>B_first...) and none of the entry's root_body / bodies; (7) placement: the settled centreline drawn as a tube of the cord's radius through camera.json is scored against the object's mask by centreline (the thin-object score of silhouette_iou_check: both skeletons widened to a common tolerance) with the demonstrator's hands (masks/hands.png) left out; below min_iou (0.25) fails. Scope: cords (capsule chains); cloth and volumetric soft bodies are not certified.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene.xml (the MuJoCo bench and rigid objects).

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json (paths relative to it).

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json; default the recon's camera_json.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Hand mask left out of the silhouettes; default masks/hands.png next to the recon.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these object ids.

inputs.name: max_mean_drift_m
inputs.description: Largest mean link drift while settling. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_link_drift_m
inputs.description: Largest single link drift. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: pen_m
inputs.description: Allowed sinking into the table or a geom. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: self_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed overlap of capsules two or more links apart. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: min_iou
inputs.description: Centreline silhouette score floor. Default 0.25.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, objects {id: {cord, n_links, segment_m, mean_drift_m, max_link_drift_m, claimed_drift_m, joint_gap_m, link_stretch, self_overlap_m, below_table_m, inside_geom {geom, depth_m}, iou, plain_iou}}; scope=isaac_cord.

tools.name: isaac_export_check
tools.title: Isaac export check
tools.summary: Opens a USD stage written by build_isaac_scene (or its soft-body variant) in Isaac Sim's Python and compares every exported static geom's pose with the MuJoCo scene at the export state, plus the export.json record with the scene even without Isaac; skips the Isaac part with ok and a note when Isaac is not configured.
tools.description: Deformable objects are simulated in Isaac Sim on a stage exported from the MuJoCo scene; if the scene is re-placed after the export, or the export used another state or a wrong quaternion order, the cord lies on a table and objects that are no longer where MuJoCo has them, and nothing fails. The check (1) reads the export.json next to the USD (the geoms build_isaac_scene exported, by name, with their poses) and compares each with the same geom of `scene` at `qpos` (default its keyframe 0, the export's own default) - this needs no Isaac; (2) when an Isaac Sim Python is configured (`isaac_python` or DEXAGENT_ISAAC_PYTHON, HOME redirected to `isaac_home` or DEXAGENT_ISAAC_HOME), starts it headless, opens the stage through omni.usd, and reads the world transform of every /World/static/g<k> prim (and /World/soft/b<k>, /World/cords/<name>), comparing the statics with the scene again; optionally it resets the PhysX world and steps it `physics_steps` times and checks the dynamic prims stay finite. Non-robot geoms off by more than `pos_tol_m` or `rot_tol_deg` fail (robot geoms are reported, since the robot pose depends on the exported state); a stage that does not open, an Isaac run that exits non-zero or returns no result, a missing cord named in the export, or a missing static prim fail. Without Isaac the report says the load test was skipped.

inputs.name: usd
inputs.description: The exported stage (<tag>_scene.usda).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: The MuJoCo scene the stage must match.

inputs.name: export_json
inputs.description: export.json written with the stage; default the one next to the USD.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State the export was made at (npy or list); default the scene's keyframe 0.

inputs.name: isaac_python
inputs.description: Isaac Sim's Python; default DEXAGENT_ISAAC_PYTHON (skipped when unset).

inputs.name: isaac_home
inputs.description: HOME for Isaac's caches; default DEXAGENT_ISAAC_HOME, else a temporary folder.

inputs.name: physics_steps
inputs.description: PhysX steps after a world reset (0 = only open and read). Default 0.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed position difference per geom, metres. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed rotation difference per geom, degrees. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: Time limit of the Isaac run. Default 900.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies (their geoms are reported, not judged). Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; skipped_isaac (bool); export_vs_scene: {n, n_bad, worst}; usd_vs_scene: {n, n_bad, worst, n_prims, missing_statics, cords, soft}; bad: [{geom, body, source, pos_err_m, rot_err_deg}].

requirements: Isaac Sim 5.0 (pip isaacsim) in its own Python for the load test

tools.name: isaac_recording_check
tools.title: Isaac recording check
tools.summary: Re-checks an episode's Isaac Sim cord recording from its files: bound to the executed scene, trajectory, cord specifications and scripts by sha256; no PhysX errors; finite, untorn, above the table, under the speed limit; every grasp held; at rest at the end; its MuJoCo mirror reproduces it; optionally re-simulated in Isaac Sim.
tools.description: Deformables run in Isaac Sim while the robot and rigid objects run in MuJoCo (execute_isaac_deformables). The MuJoCo gates read the cord through its mirror (a construct_rope-named cable whose qpos is the recording); this check is what the MuJoCo physics checks are for a rigid object. It reads the workspace's trajectory_manifest.json `deformables` block (or the given report) and verifies: (1) BINDING: isaac_episode_report.json's sha256 of the executed scene and trajectory equal the manifest's files, the recording, mirror scene and mirror trajectory equal theirs, the cord specifications, grasps and events equal deformables.json's, and the Isaac scripts are the library's current ones; (2) PHYSX: the log shows no PhysX error and no invalid transform; (3) the RECORDING itself, re-measured: every link pose finite; neighbouring link centres no further apart than (1 + max_stretch) link lengths (a torn chain); no link more than table_pen_m below the table top; the peak link speed at most max_link_speed (a cord that flies or is snapped); every planned grasp held a link (none missed, none never closed); over the last rest_s seconds, after the last release, the cord moves at most rest_drift_m (it lies still where it was left); (4) MIRROR: the mirror trajectory's robot and rigid columns equal the executed trajectory's, and its cord rows put every link centre within mirror_tol_m of the recording (forward kinematics of scene_mirror.xml); (5) REPLAY (replay=True): the episode is simulated again in Isaac Sim from deformables.json on the same scene and trajectory, and the Stage 1 goal gate must pass on the replay's mirror as on the recording's (PhysX CPU contacts are not bit-reproducible, so the outcome is compared, not the bits; the final centreline deviation is reported). Returns ok, issues and the measurements.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Stage 3 workspace with trajectory_manifest.json (its deformables block).

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 scene_semantics.json (for the replay's goal gate).

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json (for the replay's goal gate).

inputs.name: max_link_speed
inputs.description: Default: deformables.json's max_link_speed (1.5 m/s).

inputs.name: max_stretch
inputs.description: Allowed neighbour gap beyond one link length, as a share of it. Default 0.25.

inputs.name: table_pen_m
inputs.description: Allowed link depth below the table top. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: rest_s
inputs.description: Seconds at the end over which the cord must lie still. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: rest_drift_m
inputs.description: Largest link displacement allowed over rest_s. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: mirror_tol_m
inputs.description: Mirror link centre error allowed. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: replay
inputs.description: Simulate the episode again in Isaac Sim and compare the goal outcome. Default False.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, binding {name: ok}, physx, cords {name: finite, max_stretch, lowest_m, peak_speed, end_drift_m}, grasps, mirror_error_m, replay {ok, goal_ok, final_deviation_mean_m}.

tools.name: joint_acceleration_audit
tools.title: Joint acceleration audit
tools.summary: Sustained (smoothed over about 0.3 s) arm joint accelerations against a per-joint limit, and the flange's linear acceleration against a payload limit.
tools.description: Covers what arm_jerk_check (raw single-frame second difference, 47 rad/s^2 spike budget) misses: acceleration that is kept, not spiked. Each arm joint trajectory is differentiated twice with a Savitzky-Golay filter (cubic, window window_s, default 0.3 s), which removes frame noise and keeps what a controller must actually deliver, and compared with limit_rad_s2 (default 15 rad/s^2 for every joint, or a per-joint list): a small arm's motors accelerate a joint at about that rate; the paper's executed episodes stay under 10. The flange (the arm tip the hand is bolted to) gets the same smoothing in Cartesian space against flange_limit_m_s2 (default 6 m/s^2): what a held object feels. Arms come from the bench stations (episode.robot_parts) or, for other robots, joints on bodies named '_arm'. Reports per arm and joint the peak smoothed acceleration with its frame and phase label.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: limit_rad_s2
inputs.description: Per-joint (or one) smoothed acceleration limit. Default 15.

inputs.name: flange_limit_m_s2
inputs.description: Smoothed flange linear acceleration limit; None skips. Default 6.

inputs.name: window_s
inputs.description: Savitzky-Golay window. Default 0.3 s.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, joint, frame, label, value, limit}; arms {side: {joint: peak rad/s^2, frame}, flange_peak_m_s2}.

tools.name: joint_armature_damping_check
tools.title: Joint armature and damping check
tools.summary: Every position-servoed joint is stable at the scene's timestep (servo frequency x timestep below a limit given its inertia including armature, no anti-damping), light free bodies carry no explicit damping that outruns their inertia, and joints shared with a reference scene (the setup) keep its armature, damping, friction loss and stiffness.
tools.description: A position servo of stiffness kp on a joint with inertia I oscillates at w = sqrt(kp / I), and MuJoCo integrates the position term explicitly (implicitfast and implicit treat only velocity terms implicitly), so w * timestep must stay well below 2. The Sharpa hand ships armature 1.0 on every joint for this reason: a finger link alone is ~1e-6 kg m^2, and without armature a kp 300 servo has w * dt ~ 30 at 2 ms and the fingers blow up. The check compiles the scene, reads each servo's effective inertia from the mass matrix diagonal at keyframe `key` (link inertia plus armature), and fails w * dt > `max_omega_dt`, a negative damping ratio (compiled bias velocity term positive, or negative joint damping), and with the explicit Euler integrator a velocity gain kv with kv * dt / I > 1. A free joint with damping d on a body whose smallest rotational inertia I gives d * dt / I > 1 is reported too (0.0002 N m s on a 1e-8 kg m^2 spin axis NaN'd a solver). With `reference` (the setup's scene.xml) or `expected` ({joint-name glob: {armature, damping, frictionloss, stiffness}}), each matching joint must carry those values within `rel_tol`.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Scene whose joints' armature/damping/frictionloss/stiffness shared joints must keep (e.g. setup/scene.xml).

inputs.name: expected
inputs.description: {joint name glob: {armature, damping, frictionloss, stiffness}} the matching joints must carry.

inputs.name: max_omega_dt
inputs.description: Largest servo frequency x timestep. Default 0.5 (explicit limit 2).

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe the inertia is read at. Default 0.

inputs.name: rel_tol
inputs.description: Relative tolerance of the reference comparison. Default 1e-6.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; timestep; integrator; servos: [{actuator, joint, kp, kv, armature, damping, inertia, omega_dt, zeta, problem}] (problems first); free_joint_damping: [...]; reference_mismatches: [{joint, field, scene, reference}]; worst.

tools.name: joint_limit_margin_audit
tools.title: Joint limit margin audit
tools.summary: Every robot joint of the episode stays inside the real limits of a reference robot (default: the repository's setup/scene.xml, matched by joint-name suffix and side), and the scene does not widen any range.
tools.description: Covers what wrist_stop_check (wrist roll joints only, scene limits unless real stops are passed) and arm_reach_check (margin to the SCENE's ranges, reported but not failed) miss. Every hinge and slide of the scene is matched to a joint of the reference robot: same name, else the same side word (left / right) and the longest common run of trailing name tokens (at least two, e.g. 'dof_joint2', 'index_MCP_FE'), so a twin whose arm is named 'arm_left_dof_joint2' still meets 'robot_left_arm_dof_joint2'. The hand's virtual wrist joints (pos_x..rot_z, the hand's world pose, no hardware) are skipped by default. Two failures: (1) the trajectory leaves the reference range by more than the tolerance on any frame (0.5 deg for arm joints, which are driven kinematically and should never pass a stop; 1.5 deg for finger joints, which MuJoCo's soft joint limits let a contact press about a degree past the stop; 0.5 mm for slides); (2) the scene's own range is wider than the reference's by more than the tolerance, or the scene joint is unlimited where the reference is limited: the scene was widened, and every limit-reading check is blind to it. The setup's arm joints 2 and 3 start at -0.15 rad on purpose (setup/README.md); they are judged against that. Reports per joint the reference and scene ranges, the extreme values and frames.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: MJCF of the real robot whose limits rule. Default the repository's setup/scene.xml.

inputs.name: tol_deg, tol_mm
inputs.description: Allowed excess over a reference limit for arm (and other) hinges and for slides. Defaults 0.5 deg, 0.5 mm.

inputs.name: finger_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed excess for hand joints: a contact-loaded finger sits up to about 1 deg past its stop under MuJoCo's soft joint limits. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: skip
inputs.description: fnmatch patterns of joints left out. Default the virtual wrist joints ['*_pos_x', '*_pos_y', '*_pos_z', '*_rot_x', '*_rot_y', '*_rot_z'].

inputs.name: check_scene_ranges
inputs.description: Also fail a scene range wider than the reference. Default True.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {joint, frame, label, value, limit, excess}; joints {scene joint: reference joint, reference range, scene range, min, max, excess}; widened [joints]; unmatched [robot joints with no reference]; notes (the unmatched joints were not audited).

tools.name: joint_range_check
tools.title: Joint range check
tools.summary: A named joint exists, is limited, and its built range equals the expected one within a tolerance.
tools.description: Checks the DEFINED limits of a joint, not its current position: a scene is one instant, and what can be asserted about a drawer slide or a lid hinge is the travel it was built with. Fails when the joint does not exist (and lists the ones that do), when it is unlimited, or when either limit differs from the expectation by more than `tol`.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: Joint name.

inputs.name: lo
inputs.description: Expected lower limit (m or rad).

inputs.name: hi
inputs.description: Expected upper limit (m or rad).

inputs.name: tol
inputs.description: Allowed difference per limit. Default 1e-6.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; range: the built limits; type; limited; current: the joint's value at the initial state.

tools.name: joint_release_hold_test
tools.title: Joint release hold test
tools.summary: Sets a hinge or slide joint to each of several positions, releases it under gravity with no actuation, and checks that it stays there (a lid that stays open, a drawer that stays half out).
tools.description: For every requested joint position the model is reset, the joint is set to that position with zero velocity, and the passive dynamics run for hold_s seconds with gravity. The joint must end within tol of where it was released, and a free root body must not slide more than root_slip_m. A model without a plane geom gets a floor at z=0 (add_floor) so a free base rests instead of falling, which would hide gravity torques on the joint. Positions are degrees for hinges and metres for slides. Positions outside the joint range are reported as issues, not clipped. Assumes the asset rests on the floor at its initial state (base at z=0).

inputs.name: xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the asset (or a scene) containing the joint.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: Name of the hinge or slide joint to test.

inputs.name: positions
inputs.description: Release positions: degrees (hinge) or metres (slide).

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Seconds of passive simulation per release. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: tol
inputs.description: Allowed drift: degrees (hinge) or metres (slide). Default 3.0 for hinges, 0.005 for slides when None.

inputs.name: root_slip_m
inputs.description: Allowed translation of a free root body. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: add_floor
inputs.description: Add a floor plane at z=0 when the model has no plane geom. Default True.

inputs.name: keyframe
inputs.description: Keyframe to start from (a scene's home pose). Default None = qpos0.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Every release position held within tol and the root did not slip.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and what parameter to change.

outputs.name: trials
outputs.description: Per position: released, final, drift, root_slip_m, held.

outputs.name: joint_type
outputs.description: hinge or slide.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: Joint range in the reported units.

tools.name: joint_speed_check
tools.title: Joint speed check
tools.summary: Largest per-frame step of every robot joint group against an absolute budget or a reference trajectory's own speed.
tools.description: Reads the qpos trajectory, groups the robot's scalar joints (arm, end effector, fingers per side, found from the end-effector bodies, or given explicitly) and computes the largest change between consecutive frames of each group. Without a reference the budgets are the replay limits the paper's episodes were held to: 3.5 deg/frame for arm joints, 15 mm/frame or 8 deg/frame for a floating wrist and 0.30 rad/frame for fingers at 30 fps; they scale with the frame rate. With a reference trajectory the limit is scale x the reference's fastest step plus a floor, so an adapted episode may not move faster than the one it came from. Reports the worst frame and phase label per group.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene the trajectory belongs to.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, labels, fps) or the qpos array.

inputs.name: end_effectors
inputs.description: Finds arm / end effector / finger joint groups per side.

inputs.name: chains
inputs.description: Explicit joint-name groups instead of discovery.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Reference trajectory; limits become scale x its fastest step + floor.

inputs.name: limits
inputs.description: Override the per-frame budgets: arm_deg, wrist_mm, wrist_deg, finger (rad).

inputs.name: scale, floor
inputs.description: Relative mode: 1.5 x reference + 0.5 rad/s (or m/s).

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per group: max step, limit, p99, frame and label of the worst step, frames over the limit.

tools.name: joint_target_gate
tools.title: Joint target gate
tools.summary: An articulation joint (drawer slide, lid hinge, latch) reaches a target value, a fraction of its range, or its open / closed state inside a window and stays there until the window ends.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the drawer is slid out far enough', 'the front panel is flush with the housing' and 'the flaps are hooked under the rim and stay there'. The joint's qpos column is read on every frame of the window. The target is a value (target, rad or m), a fraction of the joint's range from its lower limit, or a state: 'closed' is the joint's closed value -- 0 when the range contains it (the library's constructors close at 0), else the limit nearest 0 -- within tol (default 10 deg for a hinge, 10 mm for a slide); 'open' means at least open_fraction (0.5) of the way from closed to the far limit. The gate reports the first frame the target is met; with hold it also fails when the joint leaves the target before the window ends (a latch that springs back, a lid that reopens after the hand lets go), naming the frame. A joint without limits needs an explicit target.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: Hinge or slide joint name.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Target value, rad (hinge) or m (slide).

inputs.name: fraction
inputs.description: Target as a fraction of the range from the lower limit.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: 'open' or 'closed' instead of a value.

inputs.name: tol
inputs.description: Tolerance around a target, rad or m. Default 10 deg / 0.01 m.

inputs.name: open_fraction
inputs.description: How far from closed toward the far limit counts as open. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: hold
inputs.description: Require the target to hold to the window end. Default true.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.description: ok; issues; joint; unit; start; end; target; open_threshold; tol; range; reached_frame; lost_frame; closest.

tools.name: keyframe_dimension_check
tools.title: Keyframe dimension check
tools.summary: Every keyframe gives exactly nq/nv/na/nu/nmocap values (MuJoCo silently pads a short qpos from qpos0), its quaternions are unit, its joints lie inside their ranges, its ctrl inside ctrlrange and on the servoed joints' positions, and the robot pose matches the setup's home keyframe when a reference is given.
tools.description: Keyframes go wrong when a scene grows: attaching an object adds its free joint's 7 qpos in the middle of the robot's, and a keyframe extended at the wrong index puts robot joint values into the object's slots and the object's into the robot's. MuJoCo refuses a keyframe that is too long but pads one that is too short from qpos0 without a word. The check reads each keyframe's authored lengths through MjSpec (so the silent padding is seen) and compares them with nq, nv, na, nu and nmocap, and fails a robot scene keyframe that writes no qpos at all (a <size nkey> keyframe holds qpos0); then it fails non-finite entries, free and ball joint quaternions whose authored norm is off 1 by more than `quat_tol` (MuJoCo normalizes them when compiling, hiding the slip), limited joints outside their range by more than `range_tol`, ctrl outside a limited ctrlrange, and position servos whose ctrl differs from their joint's keyframe position by more than `ctrl_tol` (the servo yanks the joint at t = 0). With `reference` (the setup's scene.xml), every joint the two share is compared with the reference keyframe (`reference_key`, default 'home') within `ref_tol`: a split at the wrong index shows as a robot that is no longer at home. A bench scene (one with robot bodies) without any keyframe fails when `require_keyframe` is set: its initial state is qpos0, hands at the world origin and arms at zero.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model (a model cannot show authored lengths).

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Scene whose keyframe the shared joints must match (e.g. setup/scene.xml).

inputs.name: reference_key
inputs.description: Keyframe of the reference. Default 'home' (index 0 when absent).

inputs.name: require_keyframe
inputs.description: A scene with robot bodies must have a keyframe. Default True.

inputs.name: quat_tol
inputs.description: Allowed |norm - 1| of keyframe quaternions. Default 1e-3.

inputs.name: range_tol
inputs.description: Allowed excursion past a joint range (rad or m). Default 0.01.

inputs.name: ctrl_tol
inputs.description: Allowed |ctrl - joint position| of a position servo (rad or m). Default 0.02.

inputs.name: ref_tol
inputs.description: Allowed difference to the reference keyframe per shared joint. Default 1e-4.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; sizes {nq, nv, na, nu, nmocap}; keys: [{key, lengths, problems}]; reference: {key, n_shared, mismatches: [{joint, scene, reference}]}; worst.

tools.name: latch_snap_test
tools.title: Latch snap test
tools.summary: Pinches a latch box's straps shut, lifts the box by its lid, shakes it and prises the latches open; passes only if the nubs sit in the windows throughout.
tools.description: Loads a box built by construct_latch_box in its 'seated' layout with the lid 12 mm above the rim, lets it drop, then runs the five measured phases of the asset's own proof without rendering: seat (n_latched must read 0, nothing holds the lid), close (a `close_force_N` pinch at each strap tip along the strap's rotating normal, with the equal and opposite force on the body; the strap must bow out over the nub and spring back), lift by the lid (capped PD force; the body must rise more than 40 mm with at least n-1 latches still engaged), shake (+-0.45 g sideways while hanging), and open (the reversed pinch; every latch must release). Latched means the catch bar's top is under the nub's bottom and the bar still overlaps the nub radially by more than 0.2 mm, measured in the body's own frame.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_latch_box returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: close_force_N
inputs.description: The pinch at each strap tip. Default 10 N (a thumb). Compare with built['snap_force_N'].

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Durations of seat, close, lift, shake, open. Default (1.4, 3.0, 2.6, 2.0, 2.2).

inputs.name: out_mp4
inputs.description: Also render the trial to this video.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All four checks passed: latch, carry, hold through the shake, release.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence, or MECHANISM FAILED: <which phases>.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: after_seat, after_close (n_latched, peak strap bow per latch), after_lift (body_rose_mm), after_shake, after_prise_open (fold_deg per latch), snap_force_N.

outputs.name: video
outputs.description: The rendered mp4 when out_mp4 was given.

tools.name: lift_check
tools.title: Lift check
tools.summary: Object rise reaches a fraction of the demonstration's rise, and it stays in hand while up.
tools.description: Measures the body's height above its first frame along the trajectory and compares the peak with the demonstration's peak rise (or an explicit min_rise_m). The gate passes when peak rise >= lift_ratio x demonstration rise (default 0.5), and is skipped (ok with a note) when the demonstration never lifted the object more than lift_ref_floor (4 cm). When a holder body is given, the frames where the object is more than 1 cm up must have hand-object contact for at least carry_contact_frac (0.5) of them, measured with the scene's collision geometry; an object that rose because it was flung fails this part. Reports the frame and label of the peak.

inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: The rollout.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The lifted object.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Demonstration; defines the expected rise.

inputs.name: min_rise_m
inputs.description: Explicit required rise instead of a reference.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: Hand root body; enables the in-hand contact rule.

inputs.name: lift_ratio, carry_contact_frac

inputs.name: lift_ref_floor

tools.name: lift_clearance_gate
tools.title: Lift clearance gate
tools.summary: The object is lifted at least min_height_m clear of its support (the rise of its lowest point, or its distance to the support when the support is not below it) and no longer touches the support, at the end of the window or on some frame.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'held clear of the table'. The support is what the object touched when the window started (any non-robot body within 2 mm) -- or, when it was already off its support then, what it touched on the last frame it rested on something (a cap freed by the last turn of an unscrew) -- or the bodies given in `support`; with none found it is the table. On the decision frame (the window's last with at='end', any frame with at='any') the object passes when it does not touch the support and either its lowest point (exact support functions of its collision geoms) rose at least min_height_m above where it rested, or its distance to the support is at least min_height_m (a cap pulled off a bottle held on its side moves along the bottle, not up). The issue gives both numbers.

inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The lifted object.

inputs.name: frames

inputs.name: subgoal

tools.name: magnetic_coupling_test
tools.title: Magnetic ring coupling test
tools.summary: Hangs one magnetic ring from another, ramps a pull until it separates, then holds two rings like two hands and pulls them apart and back together: the third ring must stay attached to both throughout.
tools.description: Loads one to three ring asset MJCFs (one path is copied three times; every name is prefixed per copy), strips floors, and builds a gravity-only test world with the ring axes horizontal (along world y) so the rings move in the vertical x-z plane. A ring's magnet is found as the body targeted by a body-transmission (adhesion) actuator; its geom's radius sets the touching centre distance D = 2 r. Held rings are driven kinematically every step (pose and velocity set), the free ring is simulated. Trials: (1) hang: ring B hangs below held ring A for hold_s; it must stay attached and not sag; (2) pull-off: a downward force on B ramps to pull_max_N; the force at which B separates must lie in [min_pull_N, max_pull_N] (default min = 3 x B's weight); (3) chain: A and C held touching with B hanging (or sitting) against both, then A and C move apart to chain_frac x D centre separation over move_s: B must still touch both while A and C no longer touch; (4) rejoin: A and C move back together: B must still touch both. 'Touching' is a centre distance at most D + tol_m. Returns ok, issues (what to change), and every measurement.

inputs.name: rings
inputs.description: One to three ring asset MJCF paths (one path is used for all three rings).

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Hang duration in seconds. Default 2.0

inputs.name: pull_max_N
inputs.description: Peak of the pull-off force ramp in newtons. Default 20.0

inputs.name: pull_ramp_s
inputs.description: Duration of the pull-off ramp. Default 2.0

inputs.name: min_pull_N
inputs.description: Smallest acceptable separation force, or None for 3 x the hanging ring's weight. Default None

inputs.name: max_pull_N
inputs.description: Largest acceptable separation force (a hand must be able to pull rings apart). Default 15.0

inputs.name: chain_frac
inputs.description: Centre separation of the two held rings at the end of the pull, as a multiple of D (< 2). Default 1.95

inputs.name: move_s
inputs.description: Duration of each pull-apart / rejoin motion. Default 1.5

inputs.name: third_start
inputs.description: 'below' (B hangs under the held pair) or 'above' (B sits on top). Default below

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Contact tolerance on the centre distance. Default 0.0015

inputs.name: timestep
inputs.description: Simulation timestep; use the scene's own. Default 0.002

inputs.name: integrator
inputs.description: MuJoCo integrator of the test world; use the scene's own. Default implicitfast

inputs.name: impratio
inputs.description: Friction-to-normal impedance ratio of the test world; use the scene's own. Default 5.0

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
