tools.name: mesh_validity_check
tools.title: Mesh validity check
tools.summary: Every mesh geom is non-degenerate (enough vertices and thickness to collide), at a plausible metric scale (no millimetre-as-metre slips, no part a hundred times smaller than its object), and closed wherever MuJoCo computes mass and inertia from its volume.
tools.description: Meshes are where most reconstruction slips hide, and MuJoCo compiles many of them without complaint. The check compiles the scene through MjSpec (so each geom's mass, density, inertia mode and its body's inertial setting are known) and inspects every mesh geom on the compiled vertices (scale already applied): (1) a collidable mesh needs at least 4 vertices and 4 faces and a thickness above `min_thickness_m` in every axis, or MuJoCo collides a flat hull; (2) a mesh of a scene object larger than `max_extent_m` or smaller than `min_extent_m`, or more than `ratio_limit` times smaller than the largest geom of its own object, is reported as a unit slip (a cup authored in millimetres becomes 80 m; a part scaled twice becomes 0.08 mm); (3) a mesh that contributes mass from its volume (no explicit inertial on its body, mass not set to 0, volumetric inertia with MuJoCo's 'legacy' or 'exact' mode) must be closed: an open surface makes the legacy algorithm over-count volume, so the body's mass and inertia are an artifact. An open mass-carrying mesh fails only when its estimated mass is more than `open_mass_share` of its object's mass; smaller ones are listed as notes. Robot meshes are checked for degeneracy only (the setup ships them with explicit inertials). A scene that does not compile fails with MuJoCo's message.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model (a model skips the mass attribution).

inputs.name: min_extent_m
inputs.description: Smallest plausible size of an object mesh, metres. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: max_extent_m
inputs.description: Largest plausible size of an object mesh, metres. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: min_thickness_m
inputs.description: Thinnest axis a collidable mesh may have, metres. Default 1e-5.

inputs.name: ratio_limit
inputs.description: How many times smaller than its object's largest geom a mesh may be. Default 50.

inputs.name: open_mass_share
inputs.description: Share of its object's mass an open, volume-massed mesh may carry. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; n_mesh_geoms; meshes: [{geom, mesh, body, object, robot, collidable, nvert, nface, extent_m, thickness_m, open_edges, mass_from_volume, est_mass_kg, object_mass_kg, problem}] (problems first); worst.

tools.name: model_finite_check
tools.title: Model finite check
tools.summary: Every body has a finite, non-negative mass and inertia, and the forward kinematics of the initial state are finite.
tools.description: The first thing to ask of a reconstructed scene, before any physics is read: does MuJoCo compile it into numbers that mean anything? A mesh with a degenerate hull, a zero-density body or a geom placed at infinity produces a model whose masses or state are NaN or negative, and every later check would then fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the scene. This verifier compiles the MJCF, runs one forward pass, and reports the bodies whose mass or diagonal inertia is not finite or is negative, and whether the state itself is finite. Works on any scene.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; state_finite; bad_bodies: [{body, mass, inertia}] with the offending values; n_bodies.

tools.name: moving_joint_check
tools.title: Moving joint check
tools.summary: Opens each candidate joint in simulation, renders it from the video camera, and ranks the candidates by how well their edges match a video frame taken during the motion; optionally asserts that an expected joint ranks first.
tools.description: A four-drawer cabinet has four slide joints that are all equally drivable, and a trajectory optimized against the wrong one looks like success. Frame differencing cannot tell them apart because the arm sweeps across every drawer. This verifier tests hypotheses instead: for each candidate joint it sets the joint to its open limit, renders the scene from the camera registered to the video, and correlates the edge map of that render with the edge map of a real frame taken while the part was moving, inside the image footprint the candidates occupy. The joint whose rendering looks most like the video ranks first. With `expected` given, ok means that joint won; without it, ok means a clear winner exists (margin above `min_margin`; a single candidate needs a finite edge match).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model, with a camera registered to the video.

inputs.name: frame_during
inputs.description: Video frame (path or RGB array) taken while the part is moving.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Name of the video-registered camera in the scene.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.description: Candidate joint names, a name prefix, or None for every hinge and slide joint.

inputs.name: expected
inputs.description: The joint that should win, if known.

inputs.name: frame_before
inputs.description: Optional frame before the motion; if given, the still render is scored against it too and reported.

inputs.name: min_margin
inputs.description: Required gap between the best and second correlation when no expected joint is given. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: If given, writes the candidate renders and the scored crop there.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; best: joint name; ranking: [{joint, edge_match, bbox}]; margin; footprint: the scored image region; reason when a lone candidate has no score.

tools.name: mujoco_version_compat_check
tools.title: MuJoCo version compatibility check
tools.summary: Compiles the scene in each configured Python interpreter (e.g. the Stage 3 env with MuJoCo 3.10 and the Stage 4 env with 3.14) and fails when one cannot compile it or when the models disagree in sizes, options, masses, inertias, joint ranges, actuators, equalities or keyframes.
tools.description: Stage 3 executes a scene under one MuJoCo and Stage 4 replays and renders it under another, so a scene must mean the same thing in both. Newer MuJoCo versions accept attributes older ones reject (MuJoCo 3.14 knows geom 'adhesion', 3.10 refuses the file), and a changed default (mesh inertia, mesh frame alignment) changes masses and poses without an error. The check runs the same standalone compile-and-fingerprint script in every interpreter in `pythons` (or DEXAGENT_PYTHONS, separated by commas or the path separator; just this interpreter when neither is set) and compares each with the first: a compile failure, any size or option difference, body masses or inertias differing by more than `mass_rtol`, joint ranges, armature, damping, actuator gains/biases/ranges, equality data or keyframe qpos differing by more than 1e-6, and body positions, primitive geom sizes or any geom's world bounds at qpos0 (from the mesh vertices themselves, so a version's choice of mesh frame does not count) differing by more than `geom_atol_m` fail. Smaller differences (vertex digests, a mesh geom's equivalent-inertia size) are notes. With a single interpreter it reports that nothing was compared.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file path.

inputs.name: pythons
inputs.description: Python interpreters to compile in; default DEXAGENT_PYTHONS or this interpreter.

inputs.name: mass_rtol
inputs.description: Relative tolerance on body masses and inertias. Default 1e-3.

inputs.name: geom_atol_m
inputs.description: Absolute tolerance on body positions and geom sizes, metres. Default 1e-4.

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: Time limit per interpreter. Default 300.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; interpreters: [{python, version, ok, hash, error}]; differences: [{python, field, detail}]; compared (bool).

tools.name: multi_object_hold_test
tools.title: Multi-object hold test
tools.summary: Drives one hand through taking two (or more) objects one after another with disjoint fingers (the first cup between thumb and index, the second on the other three) and then shakes, lifts and turns them together; passes when every object rose with the hand and stayed in it through every phase.
tools.description: A second grasp can undo the first: the hand turns and travels with the first object hanging in it, the free fingers close next to the held ones, and the combined load changes how both grips hold. The test runs, through the actuators with the executor's clamps and timing (hand.multi_object_stress_rollout): the first grasp (open approach along its approach, close to its closed targets, the clamp), a lift of lift1_m; then for each next pose, holding what it has, the move to that pose's pre-grasp, the descent and the close of ONLY that pose's grip_fingers (the fingers already holding keep their press; overlapping allocations are refused); then every object together: lifts of lift_heights_m, shakes of shake_m in five directions, turns of turn_deg about the wrist's three axes and a hold. Every phase is judged on every object held by then: it rose with the hand (at least half of each lift), it drifted less than drift_max_m in the wrist frame on every integration step since that object's seating, turned no more than 15 degrees relative to the wrist for a rigid held part, and it still touches the hand; the seat of each grasp also needs one of its allocated fingers on its object. This is the stress test a candidate pair can use before execution (with the first grasp it was designed with: second_grasp_pose). For final grasp_more acceptance, run combined_hold_state_test on the actual executed segment-end state; a restart before the first grasp cannot certify the current retained-object state.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon) holding every object as it lies before the first grasp.

inputs.name: poses
inputs.description: Grasp poses in grasp order (dicts or JSON paths), each with its grip_fingers.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: The bodies the poses take, in the same order.

inputs.name: lift1_m
inputs.description: Lift after the first grasp. Default 0.04.

inputs.name: lift_heights_m
inputs.description: Lifts with every object held. Default [0.05, 0.10].

inputs.name: shake_m
inputs.description: Default 0.03.

inputs.name: turn_deg
inputs.description: Default 15.

inputs.name: drift_max_m
inputs.description: Largest drift of an object in the wrist frame. Default 0.03.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Every phase held every object.

outputs.name: first_fail
outputs.description: The first phase that failed.

outputs.name: phases
outputs.description: [{name, ok, objects: {object_i: {drift_mm, touching, rose_mm?}}, ...}].

outputs.name: allocation
outputs.description: The fingers each grasp uses.

tools.name: name_uniqueness_check
tools.title: Name uniqueness check
tools.summary: Names are unique, every object part is named and claimed by an object of the recon, no object's '<id>_' prefix captures another asset's bodies, collidable object geoms are named, and the robot namespace holds the robot and only it.
tools.description: The library finds an object's parts by name: the recon's root body and body list, '<id>_' prefixes, and the library's resolver (exact, slug, or the single body ending in '_<id>'). Parts that none of these reach are invisible: an obstacle set built from the root body never saw an open lid or loose tips that were separate bodies, and the executor gives hand contact pairs only to NAMED collidable object geoms, so an unnamed geom is one the fingers pass through. The check compiles the scene (a repeated name is MuJoCo's compile error, reported as such) and fails: an unnamed sub-body of an object; a collidable object geom without a name that stands out of its body's named collision geometry (one buried inside it, like support feet under a can, is a note); a recon body missing from the scene or a recon root that does not exist; a body with colliding or visible geometry that no recon object claims (root subtree or listed bodies); an object that follows the '<id>_' naming whose prefix also matches bodies of an object from another asset (ids 'battery' and 'battery_holder': a colour or silhouette check of the battery gathers the holder too; parts listed as their own object inside one asset, such as a cap of its bottle, share the prefix by design); an id the resolver maps to a body outside its object. For the robot it fails a non-robot part that uses the robot prefix and a body welded to the robot by an active equality without the prefix (an arm named 'arm_left_*' that every robot tool misses). Without a recon only unnamed parts and the robot namespace are judged. Names shared across element types are notes.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: scene_recon.json path or dict, or a list of object ids / {id, root_body, bodies}; default: the top-level non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of every robot body, joint and geom. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; objects: {id: {root, n_bodies, unnamed, missing_recon_bodies, resolves_to, unnamed_collision_geoms}}; unclaimed_bodies; prefix_collisions; robot: {foreign_prefixed, unprefixed_welded}; worst.

tools.name: no_contact_check
tools.title: No-contact check
tools.summary: Two bodies are not in contact, at the initial state or after the scene settles.
tools.description: The complement of contact_check, for relations such as 'the cup is not yet in the bowl': the scene is the task's starting state, and asserting the goal relation on it is a common mistake this pair of checks makes explicit. Contacts come from MuJoCo's collision detection on the settled scene by default.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: First body.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Second body.

inputs.name: settled
inputs.description: Judge after settling (default) or at the initial state.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time. Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; in_contact; contacts touching either body.

tools.name: no_float_check
tools.title: No-float check
tools.summary: A single free body touches something after settling; welded or jointed bodies pass trivially because they are held kinematically.
tools.description: The per-object form of the support check, for asserting one placement. Only a body with a free joint can float; a welded body or a part on a slide is reported as held. The scene is settled for `seconds` and the body must then have at least one contact.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The body to check.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time. Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; free (has a free joint); touching: bodies it is in contact with; fell_m: how far it dropped.

tools.name: object_count_vs_stage1_check
tools.title: Object count vs Stage 1 check
tools.summary: Reads the counts Stage 1 states for each object ('two slots', 'four flaps', 'a 3-slot holder', 'studs in a 2x2 grid', 'three drives', and parts lists such as near_slot/far_slot) and counts the same things in the scene (constructor parameters in scene_recon.json, Stage 1 objects of that kind present in the scene, or named parts inside the object), failing on a mismatch.
tools.description: A 3-slot battery holder once came out with 2 slots; a meal box lid needs its four latch flaps, a stacking task all of its bricks. For each Stage 1 object, counts are read from its name, appearance, size, properties and initial state: a number word or digit (one..twelve, single, pair of) followed within three words by a countable noun (slot, drawer, compartment, latch, flap, stud, hole, cell, tube, well, bay, drive, ring, cup, brick, block, door, shelf, hook, peg, pin, button, battery, lid, tray, ...), 'N-noun' compounds, 'AxB grid' next to a noun, and the parts list (parts whose name contains the noun). Several counts of one noun take the largest (the text also mentions subsets: 'fills one slot'). The scene count is, in order: an integer constructor parameter of the object (n_<noun>s, num_<noun>s, <noun>s, <noun>_count, or <noun>s_x * <noun>s_y), the number of Stage 1 objects named with that noun that exist in the scene, or the number of distinct named parts inside the object carrying the noun or a synonym (latch/flap/strap, drawer/tray, slot/bay, drive/hdd/disk). A count that cannot be found in the scene is reported as unverified, not failed. A group object (Stage 1 `pieces`: N separate pieces of one kind) is counted by the pieces its scene_recon.json entry declares under `parts` (at least N when Stage 1 says at_least); in the task-level counts a group counts its pieces toward its piece kind (Stage 1 `pieces.kind`, else the noun most of its part bodies are named with) and, since a task sentence then names some of a group's pieces, the scene must have at least as many as stated.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: semantic
inputs.description: scene_semantics.json (Stage 1).

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json (objects, bodies and constructor params).

inputs.name: nouns
inputs.description: Extra countable nouns (singular).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; counts [{object, noun, stage1, phrases, scene, source, verdict}]; unverified.

tools.name: object_disturbance_check
tools.title: Object disturbance check
tools.summary: Untouched free bodies stay within 10 mm and 5 degrees of their start; no body jumps between frames.
tools.description: Finds every free-jointed body outside the robot, removes the ones declared as manipulated, and measures each remaining body's largest displacement and rotation from its first frame over the trajectory. Fails above 10 mm or 5 degrees, the level at which a disturbed scene reads as a different task on video. Separately, every free body, manipulated or not, is checked for continuity: a per-frame translation step above 0.03 m at 30 fps (0.9 m/s, faster than any tabletop manipulation) is a teleport (a reset, a lost grasp re-seated by a constraint) and fails too. With a reference trajectory the continuity limit is the reference's own step plus 0.01 m, so an adapted episode may move an object as the original did and no faster.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: manipulated
inputs.description: Bodies the task is allowed to move (fnmatch patterns).

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Original trajectory for the relative continuity rule.

inputs.name: move_tol_m, rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed drift of an untouched object. Defaults 0.010 m, 5 deg.

inputs.name: step_tol_m
inputs.description: Per-frame translation step above which a body jumped. Default 0.03 at 30 fps; 0.01 above the reference's step in relative mode.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Bodies with this prefix are the robot. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; untouched: per body max drift (mm, deg) and the frame; steps: per body largest frame step (mm) and frame; lists of offenders.

tools.name: object_inertia_plausibility_check
tools.title: Object inertia plausibility check
tools.summary: For every object body with mass, compares the principal moments of inertia and the centre of mass with those of its geometry filled uniformly at the body's mass, flagging point masses, tiny inertia on big bodies, huge inertia on small ones and a centre of mass outside the body.
tools.description: A body's inertia decides how it turns in a grasp and how easily a push spins it. An explicit inertial with a point-mass diagonal (1e-9) lets a held object spin freely about any contact, a huge diagonal makes it a flywheel that no finger can turn, and a centre of mass placed outside the shape makes it tip from a light touch. For each object body (the Stage 2 manifest's bodies, else every non-robot body) heavier than min_mass_kg and carrying geometry, the expected inertia is computed from its collision geoms (all visible geoms when it has none: primitives exactly, meshes as their convex hull) at uniform density scaled to the body's mass, about the body's actual centre of mass. Each sorted principal moment of the body must be within [1/ratio_tol, ratio_tol] of the expected one, and the centre of mass must lie inside the geometry's bounding box grown by com_margin of its size. Jointed parts (a lid, a drawer) are judged as bodies of their own. Hollow shapes modelled with solid collision primitives get an inertia up to ~2x smaller than a thin shell, which the default tolerance of 4 accepts.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json naming the objects' bodies. Default: every non-robot body.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these objects (ids or body names).

inputs.name: ratio_tol
inputs.description: Allowed factor between actual and expected principal moments. Default 4.0.

inputs.name: com_margin
inputs.description: Allowed centre-of-mass excursion outside the geometry's box, as a fraction of its size. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: min_mass_kg
inputs.description: Bodies lighter than this (spring coils, carriers) are skipped. Default 0.001.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; bodies [{body, object, mass_kg, inertia (sorted principal), expected, ratios, com_outside_m, verdict}]; skipped; worst (largest factor off).

tools.name: object_mass_plausibility_check
tools.title: Object mass plausibility check
tools.summary: Divides each object's total mass by the volume of its collision geometry's convex hull and flags densities outside the band of its material (from a keyword such as plastic, glass, metal, foam, plush, cardboard, given or read from the Stage 1 appearance) or, without one, outside a broad band: weightless objects that a breath would move and lead-heavy ones no hand could lift.
tools.description: A rigid object's mass decides whether a grasp can lift it and whether a push moves it; a constructor called with mass=1e-5 or with a density of 50000 builds an object that makes Stage 3 trivially succeed or fail. For each object (the Stage 2 manifest's objects, else every top-level non-robot body with its subtree) the mass of all its bodies is summed and divided by the volume of the convex hull of its collision geoms (all visible geoms when it has none): the bulk density, which is below the material density for hollow things (a box, a cup) and equal to it for solid ones. The bulk density must lie inside the band of the object's material: `materials` maps an object id to a keyword, otherwise the Stage 1 appearance text (scene_semantic) is searched for material words, and several materials widen the band to their union. Without a material the broad band [5, 9000] kg/m^3 applies (air is 1.2, steel 7850, lead 11340). Objects that a hand manipulates (Stage 1 role manipulated or tool) must also weigh at most max_manipulated_kg. Massless objects fail.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json (Stage 2 manifest) naming the objects and their bodies. Default: top-level bodies.

inputs.name: semantic
inputs.description: scene_semantics.json (Stage 1) for materials (appearance) and roles.

inputs.name: materials
inputs.description: {object id: material keyword} overriding the Stage 1 text.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Only these objects (ids or body names).

inputs.name: bands
inputs.description: {keyword: [lo, hi] kg/m^3} added to / replacing the built-in material bands.

inputs.name: max_manipulated_kg
inputs.description: Heaviest object a hand may manipulate. Default 3.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; objects [{id, mass_kg, hull_volume_m3, bulk_density, material, band, role, verdict}]; worst (the density furthest outside its band, as a ratio).

tools.name: object_reach_check
tools.title: Object reach check
tools.summary: For every free object in a bench scene, solves whether at least one station's arm can put a palm-down hand over it (and a fingers-in hand beside it) at grasp height; pose probes and conservative contact-distance bounds are reported separately, so a known impossible placement can be caught before Stage 3.
tools.description: The bench arms reach a band in front of their stations; a video whose objects lie farther out (another table, a camera farther back than the calibration assumed, a mis-scaled reconstruction) gives a scene every grasp of which fails the final arm-reach audit. This verifier takes the scene and, per free object root (or the bodies in `objects`), the object's horizontal position and height; for each station it solves the arm for a palm-down hand `hover_m` above the object's top with the fingers forward, and a level hand beside it with the fingers pointing at it, reporting the smaller residual. An object is reachable when one station gets within `pos_tol_m` / `tilt_tol_deg`. A failed finite probe is inconclusive; only a violated conservative kinematic bound proves impossibility. A sampled pose witness may still need a turned pose; an unreachable one needs the scene (or the setup's stations) changed.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: objects
inputs.description: Body names to check; default every free object root outside the robot.

inputs.name: hover_m
inputs.description: Height of the palm-down wrist above the object's top. Default 0.06.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Default 0.02.

inputs.name: tilt_tol_deg
inputs.description: Default 20.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Report.

inputs.name: required_sides
inputs.description: Optional body -> acting arm names. Every listed arm must reach that body; otherwise any arm suffices.

inputs.name: requirement_mode
inputs.description: probe (default): require a sampled hand-pose IK witness; necessary: reject only objects outside a conservative kinematic contact bound, report unsuccessful pose probes as inconclusive. Neither mode certifies collision-free manipulation.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, verdict, objects {name: {pos, reachable, best_side, best_orientation, residual_mm, residual_deg, per_side {...}}}, unreachable [names].

tools.name: object_scale_vs_footprint_check
tools.title: Object scale vs footprint check
tools.summary: Renders every object at keyframe 0 through the registered video camera and compares the extent of its silhouette (width, height, square root of area) with the extent of its video mask (or of a measure_mask_footprint result): a uniform scale error such as the 0.78 a free-scale placement fit once returned shows as all three ratios off together. An object the recon declares hidden_at_frame0 is skipped.
tools.description: Silhouette IoU can stay above 0.8 while an object is 20% too small or too large, and a size error changes every grasp aperture and every fit. The scene is rendered by segmentation through camera.json (robot hidden, the other objects kept so occlusions match); pixels of the hand mask (ignore_mask, masks/hands.png by default when a masks folder is given) are removed from both silhouettes. For each object with a mask, the 2nd-98th percentile horizontal and vertical pixel spans and the square root of the pixel area of the rendered and the video silhouettes give three size ratios (model / video); a ratio is taken as an interval allowing slack_px of segmentation noise on each span, and spans of a mask cut by the image border are not used. The object's scale estimate is the median ratio; it fails when the whole interval lies outside ratio_band. A deformable simulated in Isaac Sim (scene_recon entry with simulator 'isaac' and isaac.cord_json) has no MuJoCo body: its silhouette is its settled cord drawn as a tube of its radius along the link centres (scene_assert.cord_tube_mask), judged the same way. With `footprints` (measure_mask_footprint outputs, {id: dict or json path}) the video spans are the footprint's bbox_px. An object mostly covered by the hand mask, out of view, or with fewer than two usable spans (from masks) is reported as not judged. A mask (or a mask file of a masks folder, hands.png and ignore_mask aside) that matches no object fails, and so does a call in which no mask or footprint matches an object at all. The metric width of the object across the view is reported too.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json path or dict (the video camera).

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: {object id: mask png} or a masks/ folder (files named by object id).

inputs.name: footprints
inputs.description: {object id: measure_mask_footprint output (dict or json path)} instead of masks.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json mapping object ids to bodies (and masks when masks is None).

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Hand mask whose pixels are ignored in both silhouettes. Default: hands.png in the masks folder.

inputs.name: ratio_band
inputs.description: Accepted model/video size ratio. Default [0.8, 1.3].

inputs.name: slack_px
inputs.description: Segmentation noise allowed on each span, pixels. Default 2.

inputs.name: max_side
inputs.description: Render at most this many pixels on the long side. Default 1280.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; objects [{id, ratios {width, height, sqrt_area}, scale, interval, model_width_m, verdict}]; worst (scale furthest from 1); unmatched_masks (mask files of a masks folder that name no object).

tools.name: object_spin_rate_audit
tools.title: Object spin rate audit
tools.summary: Sustained object angular speed (and linear speed) over several consecutive frames: flung, tumbling or numerically exploding objects.
tools.description: Distinct from object_teleport_audit (single-frame jumps) and episode_physics_check (a single-frame peak speed of 4 m/s). For every free object outside the robot it computes the angular speed between consecutive frames (deg/s, from the body's world orientation) and the linear speed of its origin, and takes the lowest value inside every run of min_frames consecutive frames (at 30 fps; scaled to the frame rate): that is the speed the object kept for the whole run. It fails when the sustained angular speed reaches max_deg_s (default 720 deg/s, two turns per second, far above any in-hand turn or a cap unscrewed by a robot hand) or the sustained linear speed reaches max_m_s (default 1.5 m/s). Mechanism joints outside the robot (lids, drawers, caps on threads) get the same rule on their own speed. Reports the worst run per object with its frames and phase labels.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: max_deg_s
inputs.description: Sustained angular speed that fails. Default 720.

inputs.name: max_m_s
inputs.description: Sustained linear speed that fails. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: min_frames
inputs.description: Run length (at 30 fps) over which the speed must be kept. Default 6 (0.2 s).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, kind, frames, labels, sustained}; objects {name: sustained deg/s and m/s, peak deg/s}; joints {name: sustained speed}.

tools.name: object_teleport_audit
tools.title: Object teleport audit
tools.summary: Per-frame object pose jumps the 3 cm step rule misses: one-frame glitches, orientation flips, snaps back to the start pose, jumping mechanism joints and non-unit quaternions.
tools.description: Covers what object_disturbance_check and episode_physics_check (translation step above 3 cm per frame) miss. For every free object outside the robot it measures, frame by frame: (1) the glitch offset, how far frame t sits off the midpoint of frames t-1 and t+1, in position and in orientation (slerp midpoint); a frame that sits farther off than glitch_m / glitch_deg AND more than glitch_ratio times the half-distance between its neighbours was displaced and put back, which neither a fall (the neighbours are far apart) nor an impact (the object does not come back) produces; (2) a single-frame rotation above rot_step_deg (at 30 fps) that is more than three times the rotation of both neighbouring frames, an orientation flip; (3) a snap back to the frame-0 pose (within reset_tol_m and 1 degree) from more than reset_from_m away in one frame, a reset; (4) a non-unit free-joint quaternion (an edited state); (5) non-finite values. Every hinge or slide joint outside the robot (drawers, lids, caps on threads) gets the glitch rule and a per-frame step limit (joint_step_deg / joint_step_m at 30 fps). Thresholds scale with the frame rate where they are speeds. Reports the worst event with its frame, phase label and body, and per-object maxima.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window to judge. Default all.

inputs.name: glitch_m, glitch_deg
inputs.description: Smallest glitch offset that counts. Defaults 0.005 m, 20 deg (a released cylinder rattling in its holder swings about 12 deg frame to frame).

inputs.name: glitch_ratio
inputs.description: Offset / neighbours' half-distance above which a frame is a glitch. Default 2.

inputs.name: rot_step_deg
inputs.description: Single-frame rotation (at 30 fps) above which an isolated turn is a flip. Default 60.

inputs.name: reset_tol_m, reset_from_m
inputs.description: A snap back to the start pose: within 1 mm of it, from 20 mm away. Defaults 0.001, 0.02.

inputs.name: joint_step_deg, joint_step_m
inputs.description: Per-frame step limit of mechanism hinges / slides at 30 fps. Defaults 45 deg, 0.03 m.

inputs.name: quat_norm_tol
inputs.description: Allowed |norm - 1| of a free-joint quaternion. Default 1e-3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {frame, label, body, kind, value}; objects {name: max glitch mm/deg, max rotation step deg}; joints {name: max step, max glitch}; events (up to 20).

tools.name: object_visual_penetration_audit
tools.title: Object visual penetration audit
tools.summary: Object-object and object-table interpenetration measured on the VISUAL meshes (what Stage 4 renders), which collision hulls and wedges can hide.
tools.description: episode_physics_check and penetration_check measure interpenetration on collision geometry; this audit measures it on the drawn geometry. Scene objects are the top-level non-robot bodies (free objects and fixtures) with their subtrees, leaving out a subtree bolted to the robot by an equality (an arm named without the robot prefix); each body's visual geoms (groups 0-2, drawn, not colliding; a body without them uses its collision geoms) become solids: a primitive is tested analytically, a closed (watertight) mesh by a filled voxel grid of pitch_m (default 1.5 mm) with the depth taken as the distance to dense surface samples, and an open mesh (which encloses nothing) provides probe points and causes an explicit incomplete-coverage failure. On every stride-th frame, for every pair of objects whose bounding boxes overlap, the surface samples of one (about one per spacing_m squared) are moved into the other's body frames and tested against its solids. The depth of a pair is the min_points-th deepest point (single points at a sharp edge do not count); it fails above tol_m (default 5 mm). Every object's lowest visual point may not sink more than table_tol_m (default 5 mm) into the tabletop over the table. Reports the worst frame per pair with its phase label and depth.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed object-object visual interpenetration. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: table_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed sinking of a visual mesh into the tabletop. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: spacing_m
inputs.description: Target surface sample spacing. Default 0.0025.

inputs.name: min_points
inputs.description: Points that must be that deep. Default 3.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Check every n-th frame. Default 2.

inputs.name: pitch_m
inputs.description: Voxel pitch of a closed mesh's inside test (also its depth resolution). Default 0.0015.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {objects, frame, label, depth_mm, bodies}; pairs {a|b: worst depth mm, frame}; table {object: deepest mm, frame}; open_meshes (geoms that could not be tested as containers).

tools.name: pad_press_slide_test
tools.title: Pad press-and-slide test
tools.summary: Lays a compliant pad (sponge, scrubber, eraser) on a floor, presses its top with a palm-like force, then drags it sideways below and above the friction limit: it must squash at its built stiffness, hold under the light drag, slide flat and in contact under the strong drag, and spring back on release.
tools.description: Loads the asset (built dict with `xml`, or an MJCF path), adds a floor plane with friction `floor_friction` and finds the free root body and the compliant slide joints in its subtree (the foam cells). Phases: settle; press (press_force_N spread evenly over the top bodies: the cells, or the root when there are none) and measure the mean squash and the whole-pad stiffness F / squash against built['stiffness_N_per_m'] or the sum of the cell stiffnesses; hold (keep the press, add a horizontal drag from a palm target moving at drag_speed_m_s (spring-damper coupling) capped at hold_frac x mu x normal load: the pad must move less than max_hold_slip_m); slide (the same servo capped at slide_frac x mu x load, i.e. a palm moving with the pad: the pad must travel at least min_slide_m while its slab stays within max_lift_m of the floor, tilts less than max_tilt_deg and keeps floor contact (or stays within 0.5 mm of its rest height) in min_contact_frac of the steps); release (all forces off: the squash must recover to within recover_frac of the cell travel). A rigid pad without compliant joints fails the squash check. Never raises on a bad pad; reports.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: Constructor output with 'xml', or an MJCF path.

inputs.name: press_force_N
inputs.description: Palm press. Default 5.0.

inputs.name: floor_friction
inputs.description: Floor sliding friction. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: hold_frac
inputs.description: Light drag as a fraction of the friction limit. Default 0.4.

inputs.name: slide_frac
inputs.description: Strong drag as a fraction of the friction limit. Default 1.6.

inputs.name: drag_speed_m_s
inputs.description: Speed the palm drags at; the drag force is servoed to it and capped. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: phase_s
inputs.description: Seconds per phase. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: stiffness_tol_pct
inputs.description: Allowed stiffness error. Default 40.

inputs.name: min_compression_m
inputs.description: Smallest squash that counts as compliant. Default 0.001.

inputs.name: max_hold_slip_m
inputs.description: Largest travel under the light drag. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: min_slide_m
inputs.description: Smallest travel under the strong drag. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_lift_m
inputs.description: Largest rise of the slab while sliding. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: max_tilt_deg
inputs.description: Largest tilt while sliding. Default 10.

inputs.name: min_contact_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of sliding steps with floor contact. Default 0.95.

inputs.name: recover_frac
inputs.description: Residual squash allowed after release, fraction of cell travel. Default 0.1.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report file.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; compression_m; measured_stiffness_N_per_m; expected_stiffness_N_per_m; hold_slip_m; slide_m; max_lift_m; max_tilt_deg; contact_frac; residual_compression_m; verdict.

tools.name: penetration_check
tools.title: Penetration check
tools.summary: Deepest interpenetration of every geom pair over a state or trajectory, on all visible geometry, optionally relative to a reference trajectory.
tools.description: Loads an MJCF scene and recompiles it with every visible geom collidable, so that parts a scene normally draws but does not collide, such as arm links, are checked as well. For each frame it runs MuJoCo's collision detection and keeps, per geom pair, the deepest penetration seen. A pair fails when its depth exceeds the tolerance; with a reference trajectory it fails only when it exceeds the depth the same pair reaches in the reference plus the tolerance, so contacts the verified episode already had (a grasp, a seated object) are not counted as new collisions. Bodies joined by an equality constraint and bodies of one limb are never checked against each other, and MuJoCo itself never collides two bodies that are both fixed to the world. Any robot and any environment work; nothing is task specific.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file of the scene. A compiled model also works, but then only geoms that already collide are checked, because mesh hulls are built at compile time.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: The state or trajectory to check; the model's initial state when omitted.

inputs.name: baseline_qpos
inputs.description: Reference trajectory. Each pair may penetrate as deep as it does here, plus the tolerance.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: Penetration allowed beyond the reference, or in absolute terms without one. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: limbs
inputs.description: Groups of body names whose members are not checked against each other, for example one arm with its hand. Child bodies are included.

inputs.name: ignore
inputs.description: Regular expressions; a geom pair is skipped when either geom's 'body/geom' name matches one of them.

inputs.name: visual_groups
inputs.description: MuJoCo geom groups that count as visible. Default [0, 1, 2].

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Check every n-th frame. Default 1.

inputs.name: max_violations
inputs.description: Default 20.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok (bool); violations: the failing pairs, worst first, each with the two 'body/geom' names, depth, excess over the reference and the frame; worst: the single worst pair; n_pairs_touching; n_frames; n_geoms_made_collidable; tolerance.

tools.name: phase_label_continuity_audit
tools.title: Phase label continuity audit
tools.summary: Labels are '<side>: <phase>' with a side the scene has, the '#k' tag agrees with the subgoal array, each hand's subgoal index never goes back, and the labelled hand is the one that moves.
tools.description: Empty labels, sub-three-frame phases and coverage of the video are uncovered_frames_check's; this audit covers what it misses. (1) Format: every label parses as '<side>: <phase text>' with an optional ' #k' / '#k.m' subgoal tag, or as several such parts joined by ' | ' when both hands act at once ('left: X | right: Y', each hand at most once); side is left, right or both, and a named side must be a hand the scene has. (2) Tag agreement: with a subgoal array in the trajectory, the integer part of a '#k' tag of the label equals subgoal[t]. (3) Order: per hand (its own part of each label, or a 'both' part), the subgoal index never decreases (two hands may interleave their branches, e.g. #14.1 left then #14.2 right). Repeated cycles (regrasp, turn back, regrasp) are legal. (4) Acting hand: over a phase run of at least 0.3 s labelled with one side only, that hand's wrist travels less than still_m (default 2 mm) and turns less than 2 degrees while the other hand travels more than moving_m (default 30 mm): the motion belongs to the other hand. Reports the offending frames and labels.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in (for the hands).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, fps, labels, optional subgoal).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: still_m, moving_m
inputs.description: Acting-hand rule (4): labelled hand under still_m while the other moves over moving_m. Defaults 0.002, 0.03.

inputs.name: check_acting_hand
inputs.description: Run rule (4). Default True.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst; malformed [labels]; unknown_sides; tag_mismatches [frames]; order_violations; mislabelled [runs]; phases n.

tools.name: physics_options_check
tools.title: Physics options check
tools.summary: Compares a scene's simulation options with the setup's: gravity, timestep (finer is allowed), integrator, friction cone, impratio, no-slip iterations, solver and iterations, the disable/enable flags (contact, gravity, constraint, override...) and medium density/viscosity/wind, and with require_execution_contact also the executor's contact model (elliptic cones, >= 5 no-slip iterations).
tools.description: A scene can make a task easy without touching any object: turning gravity down, contacts off, the friction cone pyramidal (pyramidal cones once made grasps seat with zero finger force), the solver to one iteration, or the air into syrup that holds a released object. The reference is the setup (default: the repository's setup/): setup.yaml's physics block (timestep, integrator, impratio) and the setup scene's compiled options for everything else. Rules: gravity equal; timestep not larger than the setup's (a finer step is allowed, e.g. 0.25 ms for screw threads) and not below min_timestep; integrator equal; impratio equal; cone not weaker (elliptic is stronger than pyramidal); noslip_iterations, iterations and ls_iterations not fewer; solver equal; no disable flag the setup does not set; no 'override' enable flag (it replaces every contact's solref/solimp/friction/margin); density, viscosity and wind zero when the setup's are. With require_execution_contact=True (a Stage 3 execution model written by build_execution_model) the cone must be elliptic and noslip_iterations >= 5, as the executor sets them.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: require_execution_contact
inputs.description: Also require the executor's contact model (elliptic cone, noslip >= 5). Default False.

inputs.name: min_timestep
inputs.description: Smallest timestep accepted, seconds (a step this fine stalls every rollout). Default 1e-5.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; scene {option: value}; reference {option: value}; violations [{option, scene, reference, rule}].

tools.name: physics_recording_check
tools.title: Physics recording check
tools.summary: Require named rigid robot states, velocities, controls and every integrator step; rendered frames must exactly match that recording.
tools.description: Rejects missing or nonfinite recording arrays, changed joint/actuator layouts, skipped integrator steps, out-of-range controls and frames edited after physics. Independently replays every recorded motor control from the complete initial simulator state and compares every integrator state; no object or arm coordinates are fitted during replay.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Actual execution MJCF.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Rigid runtime recording NPZ.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Trusted Stage 2 mechanism rules. Without it dynamic equalities cannot pass.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, frames, substeps, duration_s.

tools.name: pinch_support_clearance_check
tools.title: Pinch support clearance check
tools.summary: Pose a hand with its closed fingers in a floating-hand scene and measure how deep its collision geoms sink into the support (floor) and the other objects, then where the grip pads end once the support pushes the hand up by that depth: above the object, above a round object's centre line, or where they can hold it.
tools.description: Pose solvers that place pads on a part (handle_pinch_pose, pose_from_points) check the hand against the object but not against the support it lies on, so a pinch of a thin object lying on a table (a pen, a rod, a cable, a card) can put the fingertips centimetres below the table top with a zero overlap report. In physics the support stops the hand that much higher, the pads rise with it and close above the object's centre line (the squeeze presses the object into the table and the lift leaves it behind) or above the object altogether. This verifier applies the pose with its closed finger targets, measures the deepest penetration of every hand collision geom into the floor of the hand scene and into objects other than the grasped one (support_mm), and the deepest penetration of non-grip geoms into the grasped object (object_mm). It then shifts the grip pads up by support_mm (the vertical push of the support) and compares their heights with the grasped object's world box: a pad above the object's top cannot touch it; for a round cross-section (round_section=True: rods, pens, cables, cylinders lying on their side) a pad more than r*sin(atan(mu)) above the axis squeezes the object down instead of lifting it. Passes when support_mm and object_mm are within tol_mm and every grip pad can still hold. It does not replace the physics stress tests; it says before physics why one will fail and by how much.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Floating-hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output or its json); the last object (or grasp_body) is the grasped one.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Hand pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers} or a json path holding it.

inputs.name: grip_fingers
inputs.description: Fingers whose pads must hold (default the pose's grip_fingers, else thumb and index).

inputs.name: tol_mm
inputs.description: Allowed penetration into the support and of non-grip geoms into the object, mm. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: round_section
inputs.description: The grasped part is round in the pinch plane (a rod or pen on its side): apply the centre-line rule. Default False.

inputs.name: mu
inputs.description: Pad-object friction coefficient for the centre-line rule. Default 0.85.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; support_mm (deepest hand penetration into the floor or other objects) and support_pair; object_mm and object_pair; support_lift_m; pads {finger: {z_m, effective_z_m, above_top, above_hold_line}}; object {lo_z, hi_z, centre_z, radius_m}; hold_line_z_m (round sections).

tools.name: pinch_support_clearance_check_pad_margin
tools.title: Pinch support clearance check (pad margin)
tools.summary: (Pad-radius margin on the above-the-top rule.) Pose a hand with its closed fingers in a floating-hand scene and measure how deep its collision geoms sink into the support (floor) and the other objects, then where the grip pads end once the support pushes the hand up by that depth: above the object, above a round object's centre line, or where they can hold it.
tools.description: Pose solvers that place pads on a part (handle_pinch_pose, pose_from_points) check the hand against the object but not against the support it lies on, so a pinch of a thin object lying on a table (a pen, a rod, a cable, a card) can put the fingertips centimetres below the table top with a zero overlap report. In physics the support stops the hand that much higher, the pads rise with it and close above the object's centre line (the squeeze presses the object into the table and the lift leaves it behind) or above the object altogether. This verifier applies the pose with its closed finger targets, measures the deepest penetration of every hand collision geom into the floor of the hand scene and into objects other than the grasped one (support_mm), and the deepest penetration of non-grip geoms into the grasped object (object_mm). It then shifts the grip pads up by support_mm (the vertical push of the support) and compares their heights with the grasped object's world box: a pad above the object's top by more than its pad radius cannot touch it (a pad whose centre sits a few millimetres above a box's top edge still grips the edge, so the pad radius read from the hand is allowed); for a round cross-section (round_section=True: rods, pens, cables, cylinders lying on their side) a pad more than r*sin(atan(mu)) above the axis squeezes the object down instead of lifting it. Passes when support_mm and object_mm are within tol_mm and every grip pad can still hold. It does not replace the physics stress tests; it says before physics why one will fail and by how much.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Floating-hand scene (hand_scene_from_recon output or its json); the last object (or grasp_body) is the grasped one.

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: Hand pose {pos, euler, finger_targets, grip_fingers} or a json path holding it.

inputs.name: grip_fingers
inputs.description: Fingers whose pads must hold (default the pose's grip_fingers, else thumb and index).

inputs.name: tol_mm
inputs.description: Allowed penetration into the support and of non-grip geoms into the object, mm. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: round_section
inputs.description: The grasped part is round in the pinch plane (a rod or pen on its side): apply the centre-line rule. Default False.

tools.name: plug_port_retention_test
tools.title: Plug-port insertion and retention test
tools.summary: Pushes a standard plug into a built receptacle with a capped force, then loads it outward, ramps a pull-out force and tries a misaligned push, in the physics Stage 3 episodes run in and with the connector latch the executor applies: the plug must seat, stay seated, come out at about the latch's release force and be blocked when off the slot.
tools.description: Loads the asset XML of a device with a declared port (a build dict with xml, body and port: {width, height, depth, mouth_local, axis_local}), holds the device kinematically at the origin (as a hand would) and adds a free plug: a box tip sized to the port minus a clearance on a larger housing that stops at the edge face. By default the trials run in the episode's physics (common.episode.EXECUTION_PHYSICS: timestep 0.002, implicitfast, elliptic cones, noslip 5, impratio 5) and the test plug carries the latch Stage 3 gives a connector (add_connector_latch): an inactive weld between the device and the plug that the executor's own rule code (common.episode.latch_begin / latch_step, the code servo_rollout and Stage 4's physics replay run) switches on when the plug tip has bottomed out within seat_m of the port floor (and is no longer pressed on it) and off when the pull-out load exceeds release_N (a real USB-C plug is held by its latch springs, and a gram-scale friction fit holds or not depending on the contact model). latch=False tests a pure friction fit (with timestep 0.0002, noslip_iterations 0, Euler, pyramidal cones and impratio 1 it is the regime the port's grip was first tuned in), and the report says which retention and physics were tested. The device is held weightless and very heavy, re-posed every step (its gravcomp is set before compiling: set after, MuJoCo ignores it and the device fell at g inside every step, a load the plug felt; that is what made the friction fit look thrown out at the episode's timestep). Four force-only trials with gravity on: (1) insert: an axial push of insert_force_N for insert_s from 3 mm outside the mouth must reach seat_frac of the cavity depth (and engage the latch); (2) hold: with the push removed and an outward load of hold_load_N plus gravity along the pull direction (port facing down, the worst case), the tip must still be min_held_depth_m deep after hold_s (creep beyond max_slip_m is reported as a warning in hold_creep_warning and in the verdict, with the depths at the start and end of the hold, the creep speed and the time until the plug would leave the port); (3) extract: an outward force ramped to max_extract_N must pull the plug out (not a permanent weld) at no less than min_extract_N; with the latch it comes out where the latch lets go, about release_N; (4) blocked: a plug offset sideways by one port width must not enter deeper than 0.5 mm nor latch. Assumes the device is a rigid body with the port as a cavity in its collision geometry.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: Build dict (or its JSON path) with xml, body and port {width, height, depth, mouth_local, axis_local}.

inputs.name: latch
inputs.description: Give the test plug the connector latch (the executor rule: seat_m, release_N) as Stage 3 does; False tests a pure friction fit. Default True

inputs.name: seat_m
inputs.description: Latch: tip-to-floor distance that engages it, m. Default 0.0015

inputs.name: release_N
inputs.description: Latch: pull-out load at which it lets go, N. Default 15.0

inputs.name: tip_clearance_m
inputs.description: Gap between plug tip and cavity on each side. Default 0.0001

inputs.name: housing_scale
inputs.description: Housing cross-section relative to the port (must be > 1 so it stops at the edge). Default 1.5

inputs.name: housing_len
inputs.description: Housing length in metres. Default 0.013

inputs.name: plug_mass
inputs.description: Plug mass in kg. Default 0.006

inputs.name: insert_force_N
inputs.description: Axial push cap during insertion (a USB-C plug takes 5-20 N by hand). Default 8.0

inputs.name: insert_s
inputs.description: Insertion duration in seconds. Default 0.6

inputs.name: seat_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of the cavity depth the tip must reach. Default 0.85

inputs.name: min_extract_N
inputs.description: The static pull-out force must be at least this (the hold). Default 1.0

inputs.name: min_held_depth_m
inputs.description: After the hold the tip must still be at least this deep in the cavity. Default 0.001

inputs.name: hold_load_N
inputs.description: Outward load during the hold (cord weight). Default 0.3

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Hold duration in seconds. Default 1.0

inputs.name: max_slip_m
inputs.description: Slip during the hold above this is reported as soft-contact creep (a warning in the verdict, not a failure). Default 0.0015

inputs.name: max_extract_N
inputs.description: Peak of the pull-out ramp; the plug must come out below it. Default 25.0

inputs.name: push_speed
inputs.description: The push is a velocity servo along the axis toward this speed (m/s), capped at insert_force_N, like a hand that moves the plug at a steady pace. Default 0.4

inputs.name: contact_timeconst
inputs.description: Contact time constant of the plug geoms (they take priority over the device geoms). MuJoCo soft contacts scale with mass, so a gram-scale plug needs a short one or it sinks through the cavity floor; clamped to >= 2 timesteps. Default 0.0005

inputs.name: timestep
inputs.description: Simulation timestep. Default 0.002 (the episode's)

inputs.name: noslip_iterations
inputs.description: MuJoCo noslip iterations for the trials (without them soft friction lets a gram-scale plug creep out at a few mm/s under a steady load). Default 5 (the episode's)

inputs.name: integrator
inputs.description: MuJoCo integrator: 'implicitfast' (the bench's), 'Euler', 'implicit' or 'RK4'. Default implicitfast

inputs.name: cone
inputs.description: Friction cone: 'elliptic' (the episode's) or 'pyramidal'. Default elliptic

inputs.name: impratio
inputs.description: Friction-to-normal impedance ratio. Default 5 (the episode's)

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All four trials passed.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and which parameter to change.

outputs.name: retention
outputs.description: 'latch' (the executor's latch rule on the test plug) or 'friction' (a pure friction fit): what was tested.

outputs.name: physics
outputs.description: timestep, integrator, cone, noslip_iterations, impratio the trials ran with, and episode_physics (whether they are the episode's).

outputs.name: latch_report
outputs.description: With the latch: seat_m, release_N, engaged_in_insert, engage_time_s and engage_depth_m (trial 1), engaged_through_hold, release_force_N (the applied pull when it let go, trial 3), release_pull_N (the load the latch carried then), port_push_out_N (their difference: what the squeezed port pushes the plug out with), engaged_in_blocked.

outputs.name: insert_depth_m
outputs.description: Tip depth reached in trial 1.

outputs.name: hold_start_depth_m
outputs.description: Tip depth when the hold starts (seated by the push).

outputs.name: hold_end_depth_m
outputs.description: Tip depth when the hold ends (what min_held_depth_m is checked on).

outputs.name: hold_slip_m
outputs.description: Outward slip in trial 2 = hold_start_depth_m - hold_end_depth_m.

outputs.name: hold_creep_m_per_s
outputs.description: Outward creep speed over the second half of the hold.

outputs.name: hold_seconds_to_release
outputs.description: At that speed, seconds until the tip leaves the port (None without creep).

outputs.name: hold_creep_warning
outputs.description: Set when the plug crept more than max_slip_m during the hold without falling out; the verdict says so too.

outputs.name: extract_force_N
outputs.description: Force at release in trial 3 (None when it never came out).

outputs.name: blocked_depth_m
outputs.description: Depth reached by the misaligned plug in trial 4.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence naming the retention and physics tested.

tools.name: plunger_two_stage_test
tools.title: Plunger two-stage test
tools.summary: Thumb-force ramp on a micropipette plunger: first stop at the sprung stroke, blow-out past it under more force, spring return on release.
tools.description: Rebuilds the pipette upright on a floor, holds its body in place with a sized force grip, and applies a thumb force on the plunger body along the barrel axis in three phases: ramp to 4 N over 2.5 s and hold (the plunger must reach at least 70% of stroke1 and at most stroke1 + 1 mm: the sprung stage), ramp to 22 N and hold (the plunger must pass stroke1 + 2 mm: the blow-out stage behind the preloaded pin), then ease off over 0.8 s (the plunger must return to within 2 mm of the top). Reports the depth reached at each stage and the designed stroke numbers from the built dict.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_micropipette returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: first_stage_N
inputs.description: Thumb force for the first stage. Default 4.

inputs.name: second_stage_N

tools.name: pregrasp_clearance_test
tools.title: Pre-grasp clearance test
tools.summary: Find how far the open hand must back off along its approach before it clears every object by a margin, and fail when no retraction within reach is clear.
tools.description: Opening the fingers at the grasp position sweeps them through the very thing being grasped, so a grasp is only enterable if there is a nearby pose where the OPEN hand touches nothing. The fingers are opened open_frac of the way from the closed targets (idle fingers curled, an idle thumb extended), and the wrist is stepped back along the approach direction (the pose's own, else +z) in 12 mm steps until the smallest distance from any hand collision geom to any object or the floor is at least need_mm. Returns that retraction and the open targets so the caller can drive the entry from there. Failing means the grasp cannot be entered as posed, which is itself the answer.

tools.name: press_displacement_gate
tools.title: Press displacement gate
tools.summary: A pressed part was displaced by at least min_m inside a window -- a slide joint's travel (a pump head, a button, a latch) or a body's motion along a direction (a brick pressed onto studs) -- through at least min_strokes separate presses.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the pump head has been pressed through its stroke several times' and 'the brick is pressed onto the studs'. For a joint the displacement is |q - q(first frame)| on every frame of the window; for a body it is its motion along `direction` (world, default straight down), optionally measured in a reference body's frame so that a pressed part is judged against its base even when the whole assembly moves. peak judges the largest excursion (a button that springs back after the press); peak false judges the value at the window's end (a part that must stay seated). A stroke is an excursion that reaches min_m and returns below 30% of it (or the window ends); the gate fails when fewer than min_strokes strokes occurred, naming the count -- a single press where the goal says 'several times' is a miss.

tools.name: pump_stroke_test
tools.title: Pump stroke test
tools.summary: Pushes a sprung slide joint (a spray pump head, a push button, a plunger) along its axis with a capped force: it must rest on its stop, resist a sub-preload push, follow its spring rate, bottom out under a finger force and spring back, for several cycles.
tools.description: Loads the asset (a built dict with `xml` and `joint`, or an MJCF path), removes its free joints so the parent is held, and finds the slide joint (`joint`, else the built's `joint`, else the only slide joint). From the model it reads the stroke (the joint range), the stiffness and the preload (stiffness x (springref - top stop)). It then applies a force on the moving body along the joint axis, towards the bottom stop: 0 N (must rest within rest_tol_frac of the stroke from the top), half the preload (must not move: the preload is real), preload + half the spring travel force (displacement gives the measured stiffness, compared within stiffness_tol_pct), the full press force (must reach full_frac of the stroke) and release (must return to rest), repeated `cycles` times. The moving body's weight is included in the applied force. Reports every displacement and the verdict; never raises on a bad mechanism.

tools.name: redundant_motion_audit
tools.title: Redundant motion audit
tools.summary: Inside each phase, the hand's orientation (all three axes) turning away and back: the rotation path is longer than the net rotation the phase needs by an out-and-back excursion.
tools.description: Covers what wrist_spin_check misses: it reads one named roll joint; this audit reads the hand's world orientation (the body its wrist joints move), whatever joints produce it, about any axis. For every phase run of a hand (its own part of a '<side>: <phase>' label, a 'both' part, or its half of a two-hand label 'left: X | right: Y') it computes the angle from the phase's start orientation and the angle to its end orientation on every frame. The out-and-back excursion is the larger of (a) how far the hand came back toward its start after its farthest point and (b) how far it moved away from its end after its closest approach; a geodesic turn and a detour through a via orientation both score near zero, turning 40 degrees and back scores 40. It fails at excursion_deg (default 20). It also reports, per phase, the rotation path length against the net rotation. Phases whose label names a rotation task (turn, twist, unscrew, pour, flip, wipe...) are judged too: inside one such phase the turn should still be one way.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: excursion_deg
inputs.description: Out-and-back excursion that fails. Default 20.

inputs.name: min_frames
inputs.description: Shortest phase run judged. Default 5.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, frames, label, excursion_deg, path_deg, net_deg, turn_frame}; phases (top 10 by excursion).

tools.name: reference_video_similarity
tools.title: Reference video similarity
tools.summary: Compares a generated simulation video with a reference video of the same task frame by frame at matched normalized times (SSIM and absolute difference on downscaled grey frames, a motion-energy curve correlation), writes a side-by-side contact sheet, and passes when the similarity is above a threshold.
tools.description: A reproducibility check: the same video through the pipeline again, or a hand-built twin against the pipeline's output, should give the same simulation video up to rendering noise. The two videos may differ in length, so frames are compared at the same fraction of the duration (`n_samples` pairs), after resizing both to `width` x `height` grey. Per pair it measures SSIM and the mean absolute difference; over the whole video it correlates the two motion-energy curves (mean absolute frame-to-frame change) to see whether things move at the same times. The sheet puts the reference above the candidate for every sampled time, with the per-pair SSIM. Passes when the mean SSIM is at least `min_ssim` (0.9 is 'the same scene and motion', 0.75 'the same task from a similar layout', below 0.6 'something else is happening') and every sampled frame of both videos decodes (an undecodable frame would be compared as black). It judges pixels, not physics: use the subgoal and episode checks for what the robot did, and this one for whether the output looks like the reference.

inputs.description: The generated video (mp4).

inputs.name: reference

inputs.name: width

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Default 120.

inputs.name: min_ssim
inputs.description: Pass threshold on the mean SSIM. Default 0.75.

inputs.name: reference_window_s
inputs.description: [start, end] seconds of the reference that correspond to the whole generated video (a twin of a longer recording).

inputs.description: Side-by-side sheet.

inputs.description: Report.

tools.name: relative_pose_gate
tools.title: Relative pose gate
tools.summary: The final pose of body A expressed in body B's frame is within position and orientation tolerances of a target relative pose (an assembled part, a seated plug), with optional axis masks and rotational symmetry.
tools.description: Assembly goals are relations between two parts, wherever the pair ends on the table. On the decision frame A's root pose is expressed in B's root frame (p_rel = R_B^T (p_A - p_B), R_rel = R_B^T R_A) and compared with the target: rel_pos [m] on the axes listed in pos_axes, and rel_quat (w, x, y, z) or rel_euler_deg (xyz) as the geodesic rotation angle. A symmetric part (a cap, a square peg) gives sym_axis (in A's frame) and sym_deg: the smallest error over the symmetric copies of the target counts. reference_frame takes the target from the pair's relative pose on another frame (a part that must return to where it sat). The issue gives the correction as a world displacement.

tools.name: release_settle_gate
tools.title: Release and settle gate
tools.summary: After the release (the last frame a robot body touches the object in the window) the object seats itself by at most a small allowance and then stays still for a settle time: no fall, roll, slide or tip-over, supported at the end, optionally upright / upside down / on a named support.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'rests on the table without hand support' and 'stays in the slot when the hands let go'. The release is the last frame of the window on which any robot body touches the object (1 mm margin); with no touch in the window the object is judged from the window's start. In the first seat_s after the release it may seat itself (a brick let go at a slight tilt drops onto its studs, a battery pivots into its slot) by at most seat_tol_m of centre motion and seat_tol_deg of tipping; over the following settle_s its centre must stay within pos_tol_m and its up axis within rot_tol_deg, comparing the mean pose over the first third of that window with the last third, so an object rocking or spinning in place passes while one sliding, rolling or tipping away fails. When the window ends before the settle time, the following frames are watched until a robot body touches the object again; less than min_settle_s of observation fails (let it rest before the next move). At the end the object must touch something other than the robot (else it is falling), the `on` support when given, and with orientation 'upright' / 'upside_down' its frame-0 up axis (or up_local) must point up / down within orient_tol_deg ('horizontal': within orient_tol_deg + 15 deg of horizontal).

tools.name: released_contact_audit
tools.title: Released contact audit
tools.summary: After every phase whose label says the hand lets go, the hand stops touching the released object soon, does not drag it while withdrawing, and does not sink into any object while releasing.
tools.description: No other audit ties contact to the release phases. For every run of a let-go phase (labels with let go, release, open the hand, drop) of a side ('both' counts for each hand), the released objects are the free objects named in the label, else the objects that hand touches on the run's first frame. The frames checked run from grace_frames (default 3) before the end of the let-go run through the following away phases of the same hand (retreat, withdraw, back off, return home, hold clear...), at most after_s (default 1.5 s) past the let-go. On the scene as the bench executor runs it, the hand touches an object when their smallest distance is at most touch_m (default 0.5 mm). Three failures: (1) drag: while the hand touches a released object, the object moves more than drag_m (default 10 mm) or drag_deg (default 15 deg): the retreat pulls it off its placement (the spring-back of soft contacts as fingers separate nudges an object a few millimetres or degrees, which the defaults allow); (2) linger: the hand still touches a released object more than linger_s (default 1 s) after the let-go ends, or on the last frame checked (a fingertip sliding off a surface for a few frames as the hand lifts is normal); (3) sink: the hand's collision geometry is more than pen_m (default 5 mm) inside any object during the let-go and away phases (fingers buried in a container wall while opening). Reports per release the touching frames, the object's motion while touched and the deepest penetration.

tools.description: The scene has to contain exactly the objects the task analysis named; an object that was dropped during reconstruction makes every later stage silently work on a different task. Names are matched the way the rest of the library matches them: an exact body name, its slug ('yellow cup' is 'yellow_cup'), or a body whose name starts or ends with the slug as whole '_'-separated parts (a constructed object's 'cup_body', an assembly part 'cabinet_drawer'). A slug inside a longer word does not count ('cup' is not 'cupboard'), and a robot body (robot_ prefix) never stands in for a task object unless named exactly. Missing names are listed with the bodies that do exist, so the mismatch is easy to see.

tools.name: rest_inside_container_test
tools.title: Object set down inside a container comes to rest on its floor
tools.summary: Sets a free object in an open container, settles under gravity, and checks rest/contact/orientation. Always measures full 3D containment; require_full_containment makes protrusion fail rather than permitting a partially inserted object.
tools.description: Gravity-only trial for 'X fits inside Y and rests there' properties (a cup set into a bowl, a part dropped into a bin, an upside-down cup placed in a bowl). The object's free joint is moved so its lowest collision point is drop_gap above the container's floor level estimate (container root z + floor_z) at the container's xy plus an optional xy_offset, with its original orientation unless placed_quat_wxyz is supplied; every other free body starts in its original state. After settle_s seconds the verdict needs: the object's xy within the container-frame collision extents shrunk by wall_margin, the object's bottom below the container's top, tilt from the placed orientation <= max_tilt_deg, linear speed <= max_speed, and, when avoid_rim_contact, no contact between the object and container geoms whose contact point is higher than rim_band_frac of the container height (the walls and rim). The container is identified by its root body (all of its descendant geoms count). Full containment uses exact collision-geometry support extents in the container's axes and the final task gate's fixed 2 mm tolerance. Default require_full_containment=False preserves tasks that permit protrusion; an ordinary inside/rest pass does not establish full containment. placed_quat_wxyz can propose a placement orientation without editing the scene.

tools.name: robot_joint_jump_audit
tools.title: Robot joint jump audit
tools.summary: Single-frame discontinuities in arm, wrist and finger joints: isolated steps much larger than both neighbouring steps, and glitch frames displaced off their neighbours and put back.
tools.description: Covers what joint_speed_check (absolute per-frame budget) and arm_jerk_check (arm second difference only) miss: discontinuities measured against the joint's own neighbouring motion, on every robot joint including the fingers and a floating hand's virtual wrist. Two rules per joint: an isolated step, a frame-to-frame change at least `ratio` times larger than the larger of the two neighbouring steps and above the group's floor (the seam of two concatenated segments, a one-frame re-solve: a velocity that switches on and off within one frame, which no servo with finite acceleration follows); and a glitch, a frame that sits off the midpoint of its neighbours by more than the floor and more than glitch_ratio times the neighbours' half-distance (displaced for one frame, then back). Floors are per group at 30 fps (arm 1.5 deg, wrist rotation 1.5 deg, wrist translation 3 mm, fingers 6 deg), set well above what a physics-executed servo produces when a contact makes or breaks, and scale with the frame rate for steps. Groups come from the bench hands (episode.robot_parts) or, for other robots, from the side word and '_arm' in the body names. Reports the worst event per group with frame, phase label and joint.

inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: ratio
inputs.description: Step / larger neighbouring step above which a step is isolated. Default 10.

inputs.name: glitch_ratio
inputs.description: Offset / neighbours' half-distance above which a frame is a glitch. Default 3.

inputs.name: min_step
inputs.description: Floors at 30 fps: arm_deg, wrist_deg, wrist_mm, finger_deg. Defaults 1.5, 1.5, 3.0, 6.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {frame, label, joint, kind, value}; groups {group: max isolated ratio, max glitch, events}; events (up to 30).
