tools.name: robot_joint_range_check
tools.title: Robot joint range check
tools.summary: Every robot joint of a scene (arm, wrist and finger joints) is limited exactly as in the setup's reference robot; a widened, narrowed or unlimited range is reported with both values.
tools.description: A trajectory that only works because the scene's arm joints were given wider ranges than the real robot has (the hand-built giftbox twin widened its arm ranges to fit its trajectory) cannot be executed on the robot. The reference robot comes from a setup folder (default: the repository's setup/scene.xml, whose arm joints 2 and 3 have the documented lower limit -0.15 rad). Each reference robot joint is matched to the scene by name (exact, attach-prefix suffix or the same tokens without 'robot'); its 'limited' flag and both limits must equal the reference within `tol`. Missing robot joints are reported too. Only the robot is judged: object joints are checked by joint_range_check.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: tol
inputs.description: Allowed difference per limit (rad or m). Default 1e-6.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; n_joints compared; changed [{joint, reference [lo, hi], scene [lo, hi], limited_ref, limited_scene, widened_by}]; missing; worst (largest widening, rad or m).

tools.name: robot_model_integrity_check
tools.title: Robot model integrity check
tools.summary: Compares every robot body, geom (collision and visual), joint and the hand-flange welds of a scene with the setup's reference robot and reports anything deleted, added, moved, shrunk, made lighter or made non-colliding.
tools.description: Loads the reference robot from a setup folder (default: the repository's setup/scene.xml + setup.yaml) and matches its robot bodies, joints and welds to the scene by name (exact, attach-prefix suffix, or the same name tokens without 'robot'). Per body it compares mass, principal inertia, centre of mass, gravity compensation (a proposal-scene hand may carry 1.0; rigid execution permits only the canonical value) and the pose relative to its parent (the station root bodies are left to stage_station_integrity_check). Per body it compares the ordered list of geoms: type, size, pose, mesh (vertex count and extents), contype/conaffinity, condim, group, friction, solref/solimp, margin/gap and priority, so a deleted or shrunk collision primitive, a hidden visual or a collision switched off is named. The hand hull geoms (handgeom.add_hand_hulls) may be absent because the executor adds them, but if present must equal the reference. Joint type, axis, anchor, damping, armature, frictionloss and stiffness are compared (ranges are robot_joint_range_check's job), and robot bodies or geoms the reference does not have are reported when they carry mass or collide. Assumes the robot is named as in the setup. Judge the scene a trajectory was executed on. A rigid runtime is compared with an independently compiled rigid robot from the trusted setup, including physical arm inertias and fixed hand mounts; proposal scenes retain their original setup reference.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF (Stage 2 scene.xml or a Stage 3 executed scene).

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml) holding the reference robot. Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed difference of positions and sizes, metres. Default 1e-5.

inputs.name: rel_tol
inputs.description: Allowed relative difference of masses, inertias and other parameters. Default 1e-4.

inputs.name: angle_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed orientation difference, degrees. Default 0.01.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; n_bodies / n_geoms / n_joints compared; missing (robot entities absent from the scene); changed [{what, name, field, reference, scene}]; extra (robot bodies/geoms not in the reference); hulls_absent; worst (largest relative mass change).

tools.name: robot_self_collision_check
tools.title: Robot self-collision check
tools.summary: Replay the episode with every visible robot geom made collidable (its convex hull) and report frames where the two hands, a hand and an arm, two arm links that are not neighbours, an arm link and the table or an object, a hand and the table, or a hand's VISIBLE mesh and an object interpenetrate.
tools.description: The hands ship with contacts off and the arms carry no collision geoms at all, so physics never objects when the plan drives the left thumb through the right palm or an elbow through the table. This verifier compiles a copy of the scene in which every visual robot geom collides with everything (and the objects' collision geoms with the arms), replays the trajectory kinematically and runs collision detection on each frame. Contacts between a body and its parent or grandparent, and between the links of one finger, are ignored (they touch by construction). It fails on any interpenetration deeper than `tol_m` and lists the worst offending pair per category with its frame and label: hand-hand, hand-arm, arm-arm, arm-table, arm-object, hand-table, and hand-object (the hand's visual meshes against the objects' collision geoms, tolerance `hand_object_tol_m`: the physics touches objects with the hand's collision shapes, and what the camera shows must not sink into them).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz (qpos, labels) or a qpos array.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed interpenetration. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: hand_object_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed visible hand-object interpenetration (the pads' soft contact plus the finger meshes' 2 mm margin over their capsules). Default 0.004; None skips hand-object.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame stride. Default 1; raw integrator substeps are used when recorded.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.description: Deprecated: relative-to-baseline acceptance is rejected; absolute limits apply.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, failed [categories], worst {category: {frame, label, depth_mm, geoms}}, n_frames_checked.

tools.name: rod_seated_in_slot_check
tools.title: Rod seated in slot check
tools.summary: A cylindrical part (cell, dowel, pen, fuse) ends lying in its channel: its axis parallel to the slot axis, its centre line on the slot's, and both ends between the slot's end stops, measured in the holder's own frame on an executed trajectory.
tools.description: The outcome gate of an insertion into an open channel, where the part's root barely moves but its far end must come down (a battery whose + end is pressed past the end contact): a position check on the root cannot tell a seated cell from one still resting on the end wall. The check reads the frame (default the last; the median over the last `settle_frames` frames), expresses the rod's axis and centre in the frame of the holder body (so a holder that slid or turned during the task is followed), and measures: the angle between the rod axis and the slot axis (sign-free), the radial distance of the rod centre from the slot's axis line, the axial position of the centre, and, with `rod_half_length` and `stops`, where both ends lie along the slot. It passes when the angle is within axis_tol_deg, the radial offset within radial_tol_m and both ends inside the stops widened by stop_tol_m. It also reports the first frame from which the rod stays seated to the end. Kinematic only: it judges the recorded states, not forces.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene whose qpos layout the trajectory uses.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Executed episode (npz with qpos, or an array); None judges the scene's initial state.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The rod's body.

inputs.name: holder
inputs.description: The body that carries the slot (its frame defines slot_center and slot_axis).

inputs.name: slot_center
inputs.description: A point on the slot's axis line in the holder frame (the channel centre).

inputs.name: slot_axis
inputs.description: Slot axis direction in the holder frame. Default [1, 0, 0].

inputs.name: rod_axis
inputs.description: The rod's axis in its body frame. Default [0, 0, 1].

inputs.name: rod_center
inputs.description: The rod's mid-point on its axis in its body frame. Default [0, 0, 0].

inputs.name: rod_half_length
inputs.description: Half length of the rod along its axis; with stops, both ends are checked.

inputs.name: stops
inputs.description: Axial positions (holder frame, along slot_axis, relative to slot_center) of the two end stops the ends must lie between.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame judged. Default -1 (last).

inputs.name: settle_frames
inputs.description: Median of the measurements over this many frames ending at `frame`. Default 1.

inputs.name: axis_tol_deg, radial_tol_m, stop_tol_m
inputs.description: Defaults 3 deg, 1.5 mm, 1 mm.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; angle_deg, radial_m, axial_m, ends_m [2] (when half length given), stops, seated_from_frame, n_frames, frame.

tools.name: rope_knot_check
tools.title: Rope knot check
tools.summary: Is the rope knotted? Reads a cable's centreline on a frame of an executed trajectory (or a given polyline) and checks closure polynomials plus diagram certificates: unknot, trefoil (an overhand knot), figure-eight or other.
tools.description: A knot is a topological property, so crossings are not counted: a rope piled on itself, a rope through the table and a loose tangle all have crossings and none is a knot. The cable's segment bodies (construct_rope names them <prefix>B_first, <prefix>B_<i>, <prefix>B_last) give the centreline on the requested frame; the open curve is closed far away four ways (over / under the rope, radially / along the end tangents), each closure's planar diagram gives signed over/under crossings and an exact Alexander polynomial. A nontrivial polynomial proves nontriviality; polynomial matching alone cannot name a knot or prove the unknot. Independent 3-D segment checks reject self-intersections, overlapping backtracks and invalid artificial closures. A bounded deterministic search selects a regular projection before computing its invariant; no usable view means unverified. Named types require topology-preserving Reidemeister-I/II reduction to a certified small diagram for every closure. Inconclusive reduction fails a named-type request. The four normalized polynomials must agree exactly, including for knots named 'other'; zero polynomials and unresolved over/under crossings are rejected as ambiguous. ends_free is an informational projected-extension diagnostic, not a constraint on whether a hand or support holds an end. `expect` is 'trefoil' (an overhand knot, the default), 'knot' (any non-trivial agreement), 'figure-eight' or 'unknot'. `also_frames` checks the same verdict on further frames (a knot that survives the release and settling). A rope that dips more than 5 mm under the table top (table_z) is reported, because a strand through the table makes crossings no real rope has.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in (the scene that holds the cable).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq]). With scene and no trajectory the scene's home keyframe is read.

inputs.name: rope
inputs.description: Name prefix of the cable's bodies (e.g. 'red_rope'). Default: the only cable in the scene.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Frame to classify. Default -1 (the last).

inputs.name: also_frames
inputs.description: More frames that must give the same verdict.

inputs.name: expect
inputs.description: 'trefoil' | 'knot' | 'figure-eight' | 'unknot'. Default 'trefoil'.

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: A centreline polyline (k, 3) to classify instead of a scene.

inputs.name: table_z
inputs.description: Table top height for the through-the-table check. Default 0.0.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Every checked frame gives the expected verdict and the rope stays above the table.

outputs.name: type
outputs.description: unknot | trefoil | figure-eight | other | ambiguous, on `frame`.

outputs.name: frames
outputs.description: Per checked frame: frame, type, agree, polynomial_agreement, diagram_certificates, embedding_issues, topology_issues, ends_free, n_self_crossings, min_z_m.

outputs.name: closures
outputs.description: The four closures' polynomials on `frame`.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed.

tools.name: rope_severed_gate
tools.title: Rope severed gate
tools.summary: A cuttable rope's join equality was active when the window started and inactive at its end (the per-frame eq_active recorded in the trajectory), and the two sides of the join are at least min_gap_m apart.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the rope is separated into two pieces at the cut point'. A cut is run-time state that no qpos holds: the executor switches the rope's join (a CONNECT equality between two segment bodies, construct_cuttable_rope) off when the scissors' blades close on it and records eq_active [T, neq] and eq_names in the trajectory. The gate reads the join's state just before the window (or eq_active_start / the model's eq_active0 for a window starting at frame 0) and on the window's last frame, names the frame the join switched off, and measures the distance between the join's two anchors at the end (outcome.join_end_gap): a join switched off whose halves still sit together did not separate. joins names the equalities to judge; by default every rope join (a CONNECT/WELD between two non-robot bodies) that went from whole to cut in the window, and none doing so fails. A trajectory without eq_active fails with the instruction to record it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz with eq_active [T, neq] and eq_names.

inputs.name: joins
inputs.description: Join equality name(s); default every rope join cut in the window.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: min_gap_m
inputs.description: Separation of the cut ends at the window's end, m. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; recorded; joins {name: whole_at_start, whole_at_end, cut_frame, end_gap_m}.

tools.name: rotation_turns_gate
tools.title: Rotation turns gate
tools.summary: A part turned at least min_deg about its axis inside a window, counting full wraps (a screw cap, a knob, a box turned a quarter turn on the table), optionally in a given direction and until a thread runs out.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the thread is fully disengaged' and 'the box lies turned a quarter turn'. For a hinge joint the turn is its qpos travel over the window (hinge values are unbounded, so several turns count fully). For a body the rotation about `axis` (in the body frame; default its z) is integrated frame by frame from the incremental rotations, so wraps past 180 deg are counted and a back-and-forth twist cancels; relative_to measures it against another body (a cap against its bottle while the bottle itself turns). direction +1 / -1 requires the sign. With release_joint and release_travel_m (a construct_bottle cap: its lift joint and thread pitch x turns) the gate passes only when the lift joint reached the travel inside the window, i.e. the thread ran out and the cap is free, which is what 'fully unscrewed' means; the turned angle is reported.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: min_deg
inputs.description: Required turn, deg.

inputs.name: joint
inputs.description: The turning hinge joint.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The turning body, instead of a joint.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: Turning axis in the body frame. Default [0, 0, 1].

inputs.name: relative_to
inputs.description: Measure the body's turn relative to this body.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: +1 or -1 to require the sign of the turn.

inputs.name: release_joint
inputs.description: Lift joint that reaches release_travel_m when the thread runs out.

inputs.name: release_travel_m
inputs.description: Lift travel at which the part is free, m.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; source; total_deg (signed); peak_deg; required_deg; turns; release_travel_m, release_needed_m, released.

tools.name: scene_qc
tools.title: Scene QC
tools.summary: Runs the whole compile-time battery on a scene: finite model, units, initial penetration, settle stability, support, and optionally required objects, articulation and silhouette IoU, and returns one verdict with every measurement.
tools.description: The checks a reconstructed scene must pass before any task-specific assertion is worth running, in the order a failure explains the next: a model that does not compile into finite physics, geometry in the wrong units, objects that start inside each other, objects that fall or tip when physics runs, and objects left hanging in the air. With the optional inputs it also checks that the task's objects are all present, that the ones declared articulated have a mechanism, and that the render matches the video masks. Each sub-check is the standalone verifier of the same name, so a failing item can be rerun alone. The report keeps every number and lists the failures by check name.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Objects that must exist (required_bodies_check).

inputs.name: articulated
inputs.description: Objects that must have a joint (articulation_check).

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Object -> video mask for silhouette_iou_check; needs `camera`.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Pixels left out of every silhouette and mask (the demonstrator's hands): a PNG path sized like the masks.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Video-registered camera name for the silhouette check.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Mask key -> the piece root bodies of a group object (scene_recon `parts`): scored by the union silhouette of its pieces.

inputs.name: hidden
inputs.description: Mask keys of objects declared hidden at frame 0 (scene_recon `hidden_at_frame0`): they must render (near) invisible through the camera instead of matching an IoU.

inputs.name: penetration_tol
inputs.description: Initial interpenetration allowed. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: settle_seconds
inputs.description: Settle time for the stability and support checks. Default 2.0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; failed: names of the sub-checks that failed; checks: {name: that check's own report}.

tools.name: scene_recon_manifest_check
tools.title: Scene reconstruction manifest check
tools.summary: Checks a Stage 2 scene_recon.json against the Stage 1 scene_semantics.json: every object has an entry with the same type, a reconstruction skill that exists in the library, an asset file, a root body present in the compiled scene, a fitted pose, a mask with its silhouette IoU above a floor, a verification plan and passing verifier reports covering every Stage 1 property (a mechanism test for articulated objects), and for deformable objects their Isaac Sim cord (specification with settled poses, clean settling report, no MuJoCo copy) or, for one a subgoal cuts, a MuJoCo cable with cut joins; the scene, camera and comparison image exist.
tools.description: Form and bookkeeping of the Stage 2 deliverable so that Stage 3 can rely on it. Reads both JSON files and the library index. For each Stage 1 object (static ones may be omitted when `allow_missing_static`): an entry keyed by the same id; `type` equal to Stage 1's; `skill` naming a library skill of category Object Reconstruction (or `skill_origin: created` with a tool that now exists); `asset_xml` existing; `root_body` found in the compiled scene (deformables: the Isaac report instead); `pose` with x, y, yaw_deg; `mask` existing and `iou` >= min_iou; an object hidden at source frame 0 declares `hidden_at_frame0` {reason, reveal_frame, reveal_mask?} and needs no IoU (it must not be static in Stage 1; scene_qc tests that it renders invisible); a group object (Stage 1 `pieces`) lists its separate pieces' top-level root bodies under `parts` (root_body one of them, the count Stage 1 states; without Stage 1 `pieces` only similar pieces are accepted); `verifiers`: a dict of report dicts each with ok true, including at least one Reconstruction Mechanism Test for articulated objects and articulation_check or joint evidence; deformable objects simulated in Isaac Sim (entry `simulator: isaac`, or skill build_isaac_scene; the scene's simulator mujoco+isaac): no asset_xml or root_body, `isaac` with cord_json (an isaac_cord specification with its settled link poses), report_json (a passing settling report of that cord, no PhysX errors), sim_png, scene_usda (or .gz) and a drift below max_drift_m, and no MuJoCo body for it in scene.xml (isaac_deformable_rest_check re-measures the physics from these files); Isaac Sim cannot cut, so a deformable a `cut` subgoal names must instead be a MuJoCo cable: `simulation_model.kind=mujoco_cable`, its root_body (or one of its bodies) in scene.xml and `cut_joins` whose equalities and bodies are in scene.xml (construct_cuttable_rope), and any manipulated deformable not simulated in Isaac Sim must be such a MuJoCo cable (`require_mujoco_deformables=False` skips the subgoal-driven rules). Top level: scene_xml compiles, camera_json loads, frame0_compare_png exists, and the simulator field says mujoco or mujoco+isaac consistently with the verified backends; MuJoCo-only never claims Isaac rendering verification. Every finding names the object and the key to fix. Explicit full-containment final goals are independently replayed with rest_inside_container_test on the trusted scene and body identities; recorded reports may propose a placement orientation, but cannot certify success or relax the final gate's fixed 2 mm tolerance. Ordinary partial-inside goals do not require full containment. Articulated mechanism reports are proposals, never certificates: supported articulated_joint_travel_test claims are independently replayed on the current scene component with fixed verifier defaults after local asset/scene physics binding. This proves isolated fixed-base component mobility only. Specialized/coupled mechanism claims without an independent adapter fail closed.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: scene_recon.json.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 output; default: the manifest's scene_semantic field.

inputs.name: library_index
inputs.description: tool_library/index.json; default: the repository's.

inputs.name: min_iou
inputs.description: Per-object silhouette IoU floor. Default 0.4.

inputs.name: max_drift_m
inputs.description: Largest mean settling drift accepted for a deformable. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: allow_missing_static
inputs.description: Stage 1 objects with role static may be absent. Default True.

inputs.name: require_mujoco_deformables
inputs.description: A deformable that Stage 1 subgoals manipulate must be simulated somewhere (Isaac Sim with its cord, else a MuJoCo cable in scene.xml), and one that a cut subgoal names must be a MuJoCo cable with cut_joins (Isaac Sim has no cutting). Default True.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; per_object: {id: {found, iou, verifiers_ok, mechanism_evidence_ok, ...}}; counts; full_containment_trials and independent_mechanism_trials with scope, supported/unsupported claims, physical bindings and freshly replayed reports.

tools.name: scene_semantic_consistency_check
tools.title: Scene semantic consistency check
tools.summary: Cross-field checks on a Stage 1 scene_semantics.json: unique ids, subgoal references that resolve, consecutive ordered subgoals with time windows inside the clip, acting hands that match the hand roles and the hands list, type-specific blocks present, evidence that cites times, and the prompt's nouns covered by the objects.
tools.description: Reads the JSON and checks what a schema cannot: every object id is unique and every subgoal object_ref (id or id:part) resolves to an object (and a declared part when parts are listed); subgoal indices run 1..N in order; time windows are ordered, start no later than the next subgoal's start, and lie inside the clip when its duration is known; the acting hand of each subgoal is in hands.used and its hand_roles text is not a resting phrase; every hand in hands.used acts in at least one subgoal; articulated objects carry an articulation block whose moving and fixed parts are named parts, deformable objects a deformation block; a group object's `pieces` has an integer count of at least 2 and a piece kind, and is not typed articulated; every object is referenced by some subgoal unless its role is static; every evidence string cites a time or frame; and each content NOUN of the prompt (4+ letters) shares a stem with some word in the objects' names, parts, appearance or properties, the task summary, or the environment description. Only nouns are checked: function words, verbs, adverbs and common adjectives are on a stop list, and a word is taken for a verb or modifier by its form (-ly adverbs, -ing and -ed participles, unless a determiner precedes them or they are known nouns such as 'ring' or 'drawing') or its place (a clause-initial or post-'to' word followed by a determiner, as in 'build a tower'), so 'build freely' or 'keeping them connected' need no rewording while a missing object ('the pineapple') is still caught. Each finding names the JSON path and what to change.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The scene_semantics.json to check.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The task prompt; default: the file's task_prompt field.

inputs.name: video_duration_s
inputs.description: Clip length for the time-window check; default: the file's video.duration_s when present.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; uncovered_prompt_words; checked_prompt_words (the nouns the coverage check looked for); unreferenced_objects; hands_without_subgoals.

tools.name: scene_semantic_schema_check
tools.title: Scene semantic schema check
tools.summary: Validates a Stage 1 scene_semantics.json against the schema: required keys, enumerated object types, roles, hands and motions, id format, and the per-entry fields of objects and subgoals.
tools.description: Loads the JSON and checks it against stage1_semantic_understanding/schema.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12, via jsonschema when installed, otherwise an equivalent built-in walk). Reports every violation with its JSON path so the agent can fix the file. Form only: whether the content matches the video is the job of scene_semantic_consistency_check and of the agent.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The scene_semantics.json to check.

inputs.name: schema_path
inputs.description: Schema file. Default: the repository's stage1_semantic_understanding/schema.json.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues: list of '<json path>: <problem>'; counts of objects and subgoals.

tools.name: scene_size_budget_check
tools.title: Scene size budget check
tools.summary: Measures the peak arena memory (contacts, constraint rows, solver workspace) the scene uses at its keyframe, during a short passive simulation and on the frames of a trajectory, and fails when it exceeds `headroom` of the arena the model will run with, or when contacts or constraints overflow.
tools.description: MuJoCo allocates contacts, constraint rows and solver workspace from one arena whose size is fixed at compile time (<size memory=...>, about 18 MB by default for the bench). A contact-dense state (a seated lid with a strap over its catch and a hand pressing on it, a finger buried among many small geoms) overflows it: mj_stackAlloc fails and the simulation stops, which is why the hand scenes compile with 256 MB. The check compiles the scene as its consumer runs it (with `arena_mb` when given) and evaluates the keyframe, a passive simulation of `seconds` (robot joints held, servos holding the keyframe pose) and, with `trajectory`, every `stride`-th recorded frame, and records MuJoCo's peak arena use and the largest numbers of contacts and constraint rows (with `execution_model=True` it measures the paired model the Stage 3 executor builds, whose hand-object pairs make contact states much denser). An arena exhausted on the way (MuJoCo raises), a peak above `headroom` of the arena, a contact/constraint overflow warning, or nconmax/njmax caps that the measured counts exceed fail, naming the <size memory> to set.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF bench scene, or a hand-scene JSON path / dict.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz with qpos [T, nq] whose frames are evaluated.

inputs.name: arena_mb
inputs.description: Arena the consumer compiles the scene with; default the scene's own.

inputs.name: execution_model
inputs.description: Measure the executor's paired model (hand-object contact pairs). Default False.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Passive simulation from the keyframe (0 skips it). Default 0.5.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Evaluate every stride-th trajectory frame. Default 10.

inputs.name: headroom
inputs.description: Largest fraction of the arena the peak may use. Default 0.8.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; arena_mb (the budget); peak_mb; peak_frac; peak_at; max_contacts; max_efc; nconmax; njmax; warnings; suggested_memory_mb.

tools.name: scissors_cut_test
tools.title: Scissors cut test
tools.summary: Pushes the rings of a built pair of scissors with a capped force and checks that the blades open, shut, and really sever a cord laid in the wedge.
tools.description: Builds a trial scene from the scissors asset: the pair on the floor with its blades set open, and (with cord=True) a cuttable rope laid across the wedge perpendicular to its bisector at `cut_frac` of the blade length, the rope's cut join at the crossing. The scissors driver then holds the tool in place with a gentle in-plane grip and squeezes the upper ring with 0.7 N, retrying at 1.4 and 2.8 N while the cord has not parted (ring_force_N fixes one force); nothing writes the hinge. Every step try_sever measures the join against the blades and deactivates the join's equality only when the join is in the blades' span, in the wedge, in their plane, within cut_catch_m of the blade line, the hinge is closing, and both blades bite at least cut_pinch_mm with the edges closed to within the cord's diameter. Reports the opening reached, the smallest edge gap at the cord, and the cut record (blade gap and distance from the pivot at the moment it parted). With cord=False the pair starts shut, is opened by the ring force and must reach 60% of its range.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_scissors returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: cord
inputs.description: Lay a cuttable cord in the wedge and require the cut. Default True.

inputs.name: cord_params
inputs.description: construct_rope parameters for the cord (radius, rgba, stiffness...). Default: a 20 cm cord of radius 2.5 mm.

inputs.name: cut_frac
inputs.description: Where along the blade (0 pivot, 1 tip) the cord crosses. Default 0.55.

inputs.name: ring_force_N
inputs.description: Cap on the finger force at the ring. Default: escalate 0.7, 1.4, 2.8 N until the cord parts (longer blades put less force at the cord; a 7 mm cord jams plate blades at 0.7 N). The force it took is reported.

inputs.name: out_mp4
inputs.description: Also render the trial to this video.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: CUT with a cord, SCISSORS OK without one.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: CUT / NO CUT / SCISSORS OK / SCISSORS SUSPECT with numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: max_open_deg, min_gap_at_join_mm, ring_force_N (the force that cut), closed_deg, cut [records], attempts, and the per-gate sever_report at the end when nothing was cut.

outputs.name: scene_xml
outputs.description: The assembled trial scene, for inspection.

tools.name: settle_stability_check
tools.title: Settle stability check
tools.summary: Simulates the scene for a few seconds from its initial state; no free body may drift, fall or tip over.
tools.description: An object reconstructed at rest must stay at rest. The scene is stepped from its initial state for `seconds` (2 s by default) and every body with a free joint is measured against where it started: translation and rotation. A body that moves more than `drift_fail` (5 cm) or turns more than `rot_fail_deg` (30 degrees) fails; a body that moves more than `drift_warn` (1.5 cm) is reported as a warning. A translation with little rotation points at a placement error (the object hovers or sinks); a rotation beyond 90 degrees points at a wrong fitted orientation (it tips over). A diverging simulation is a failure of its own. The settled state is also returned so other checks can read it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: bodies
inputs.description: Free bodies to judge; all of them when omitted.

inputs.name: drift_fail
inputs.description: Translation that fails. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: rot_fail_deg
inputs.description: Rotation that fails. Default 30.

inputs.name: drift_warn
inputs.description: Translation that is reported as a warning. Default 0.015.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; drift: {body: {pos_m, rot_deg, verdict}}; failures and warnings as lists of body names; diverged (bool); settled_qpos: the state after settling.

tools.name: silhouette_iou_check
tools.title: Silhouette IoU check
tools.summary: Renders each object's silhouette from the video camera and compares it with the object's video mask; low IoU on one object means a wrong pose, on every object a wrong camera.
tools.description: The image-space proof that a reconstruction is registered to its footage. The scene is rendered with MuJoCo's segmentation renderer from the named camera at the resolution of the masks, each object's body (or the union of the bodies that make up a constructed object: the named body with its whole subtree, or every body matched by name prefix) becomes a silhouette, and its intersection over union with the given video mask is computed. An object below `min_iou` (0.25) fails; below `warn_iou` (0.45) is reported. When two or more objects are checked and all of them fail at once, the verifier reports `camera_suspect`: the camera they are all seen through is wrong, and re-fitting poses cannot help. The render and the masks must be the same aspect ratio, so the render is sized to the mask. Thin objects (a cord, a ribbon, a pen lying down: a mask whose skeleton is at least 8 times longer than the mask is wide, or the ids given in `thin`) are scored by their centrelines instead: a segmentation mask of a 3 mm cord is several times wider than the cord, which caps the plain IoU near 0.3 for a perfect placement. Both skeletons are widened to a common tolerance (half the wider of the two widths plus 2 px) and their IoU is the object's score; the plain IoU is reported too. A group object (several separate pieces under one mask: a tower of loose bars, a fan of cards) is given in `groups` as the list of its pieces' root bodies; its silhouette is the union of every piece with its subtree, and it is scored by plain IoU (its mask is several pieces, not one elongated object) unless it is listed in `thin`. An object declared hidden at frame 0 (given in `hidden`: a watch inside a closed box) is not scored by IoU: with the robot and ignore_mask pixels left out, its render must show at most 0.2% of the image and at most 10% (25 px floor) of its own silhouette drawn without the other objects, its frame-0 mask at most 0.2% of the image, and drawn alone it must be in the view (covered, not out of frame or under the table).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Object name -> binary mask (bool/uint8 array or PNG path), all the same size.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Named camera in the scene, or a free camera {lookat, distance, azimuth, elevation}.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State to render; the initial state when omitted.

inputs.name: min_iou
inputs.description: Failure threshold per object. Default 0.25.

inputs.name: warn_iou
inputs.description: Warning threshold. Default 0.45.

inputs.name: thin
inputs.description: 'auto' (default): elongated masks are scored by centreline; or the object ids to score so; [] for plain IoU everywhere.

inputs.name: ignore_mask
inputs.description: Pixels to leave out of every silhouette and mask (the demonstrator's hands over an object): a binary mask or PNG path, sized like the masks.

inputs.name: ignore_robot
inputs.description: Leave the pixels the robot covers at the rendered pose out of both silhouettes (a hand parked over an object in the ego view is not a placement error). Default true.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Mask key -> body names of a group object's pieces (scene_recon `parts`): its silhouette is their union. Default None.

inputs.name: hidden
inputs.description: Mask keys of objects declared hidden at frame 0 (scene_recon `hidden_at_frame0`): instead of an IoU, their render and their frame-0 mask must show (near) zero visible pixels while the object, drawn alone, lies in the view. Default None.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: If given, writes render.png and one overlay per object there.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; iou: {object: score} (the centreline IoU for thin objects); plain_iou; thin: {object: {width_px, render_width_px, elongation, tolerance_px}}; hidden: {object: {visible_px, bound_px, unoccluded_px, mask_px, ok, reason}}; failures; warnings; camera_suspect; bodies_used: which bodies formed each silhouette; render_size.

tools.name: simulation_stability_check
tools.title: Simulation stability check
tools.summary: A passive simulation of a few seconds from keyframe 0 (robot arms held, hand servos holding the keyframe pose) stays finite, raises no BADQACC/BADQVEL/BADQPOS warning, keeps every object below explosive speeds, and never gains mechanical energy beyond a small tolerance.
tools.description: MuJoCo answers an unstable scene by printing 'Nan, Inf or huge value in QACC ... The simulation is unstable' and silently resetting the state, after which every later measurement describes a different scene. The check steps the scene for `seconds` from keyframe `key` with the robot's kinematically driven joints (the arms) held at the keyframe and, by default, every position servo commanded to its joint's keyframe position (`ctrl='hold'`; `ctrl='key'` uses the keyframe's own ctrl). It records MuJoCo's warning counters, whether the state stays finite, the largest linear and angular speed of any non-robot body, and the mechanical energy of the passive non-robot bodies (kinetic + gravitational + joint springs; objects an actuator drives are left out, since actuators do work) relative to the start. A passive scene can only lose energy, so a gain above `energy_gain_j` means the solver pumped it in (a joint or weld violated at the start snapping into place, a contact too stiff for the timestep, an unstable servo). Distinct from settle_stability_check (where objects end up): this asks whether the physics itself holds together, everywhere and for the whole run.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Simulated time. Default 3.0.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe to start from. Default 0 (qpos0 without keyframes).

inputs.name: ctrl
inputs.description: 'hold' (servos hold the keyframe joint positions) or 'key' (the keyframe's ctrl). Default 'hold'.

inputs.name: hold_robot
inputs.description: Hold the robot joints that no actuator drives at the keyframe. Default True.

inputs.name: max_speed_mps
inputs.description: Largest linear speed of a non-robot body. Default 5.0.

inputs.name: max_ang_speed
inputs.description: Largest angular speed of a non-robot body, rad/s. Default 200.

inputs.name: energy_gain_j
inputs.description: Largest mechanical energy the non-robot bodies may gain, joules. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; finite; warnings {name: count}; first_warning_s; max_speed_mps {body, value, t}; max_ang_speed; energy {start_j, max_gain_j, t_max_gain, end_j, n_passive_bodies}; mj_messages (MuJoCo's own warning text); seconds.

tools.name: slot_insertion_test
tools.title: Slot insertion test
tools.summary: Pushes a free part (a drive tray, a card, a cartridge) into each named slot of a fixed receptacle with a capped force, releases it and shoves it sideways: it must slide in to the slot centre, stay there unheld and be penned in by the slot walls.
tools.description: Composes one throwaway model from the receptacle MJCF (its root held fixed: a free joint is removed) and the insert MJCF (its first body, kept free). Each slot is given by two sites in the receptacle: a floor site at the seated centre of the slot on its floor, and a mouth site in front of the opening; the insertion axis is the horizontal direction mouth -> floor site. The insert is turned so its nose axis (insert_nose_local, or the longest horizontal extent of its collision geometry when omitted) points along that axis, set on the slot floor with its leading face start_offset_m past the mouth site, and pushed by a plain body force along the axis while support_frac of its weight is carried (as a hand would), then released, then pushed sideways both ways. A slot passes when the insert's centre reaches the floor site within seat_tol_m along the axis, drifts less than max_drift_m after release, stays within max_rest_z_m of resting on the slot floor, and moves less than max_lateral_m under the side force. Assumes metres, z up, primitive or asset-free geometry in the insert.

inputs.name: receptacle_xml
inputs.description: MJCF of the receptacle (rack, cage, case) containing the slot sites.

inputs.name: insert_xml
inputs.description: MJCF whose first worldbody body is the part to insert.

inputs.name: slots
inputs.description: Per slot [floor_site, mouth_site] names in the receptacle.

inputs.name: insert_nose_local
inputs.description: Insert-body axis that goes in first. Default None = longest horizontal collision extent.

inputs.name: push_force_N
inputs.description: Push along the axis. Default 6.

inputs.name: push_s
inputs.description: Push duration. Default 1.5.

inputs.name: support_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of the weight carried during the push. Default 0.9.

inputs.name: release_s
inputs.description: Unheld rest after the push. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: lateral_force_N
inputs.description: Side shove after release, each way. Default None = 2.5 x the insert weight, enough to beat floor friction so only walls can hold it.

inputs.name: start_offset_m
inputs.description: Leading face past the mouth site at the start. Default 0.04.

inputs.name: seat_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed shortfall of the centre to the floor site. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_drift_m
inputs.description: Allowed motion while unheld. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: max_lateral_m
inputs.description: Allowed side motion under the shove. Default 0.012.

inputs.name: max_rest_z_m
inputs.description: Allowed gap between the insert's bottom and the slot floor at rest. Default 0.008.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Also write the report here.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; per slot: depth_error_m (centre vs floor site along the axis, negative = short), drift_m, lateral_m, rest_gap_m, seated, held, penned, ok; insert size and axis.

tools.name: soft_squeeze_test
tools.title: Soft squeeze test
tools.summary: Presses a soft free body onto a floor with a ramp of forces and checks that it compresses by a grasp-sized amount at a reference force, monotonically, and springs back when released.
tools.description: Loads the asset MJCF, adds a floor plane (MuJoCo's default contact parameters) when none is present, settles the object for settle_s, records its rest height, then applies each downward force of `forces_N` to the body's centre of mass for hold_s and records the sink (rest z minus loaded z of the body origin, in mm). Passes when the state stays finite, the sink grows with force (within 0.3 mm), the sink at ref_force_N is within [min_mm, max_mm], the object does not tunnel below the floor by more than max_mm at the largest force, and after release it returns to within recover_mm of the rest height. The measurement is the compliance a pinch would feel, combined with the floor's own contact parameters (MuJoCo mixes the two geoms' solref). It does not simulate fabric deformation; it judges contact compliance.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: Asset MJCF path, or a constructor result with 'xml'.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The free body to press; default the result's 'body' or the first free body.

inputs.name: forces_N
inputs.description: Downward forces, increasing. Default [0.5, 1, 2, 4].

inputs.name: ref_force_N
inputs.description: Grasp-sized reference force; must be one of forces_N. Default 2.

inputs.name: min_mm
inputs.description: Least sink at the reference force. Default 2.

inputs.name: max_mm
inputs.description: Largest acceptable sink at any force. Default 25.

inputs.name: recover_mm
inputs.description: Allowed residual sink after release. Default 1.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Settling time. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Time at each force. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All checks passed.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and which parameter to change.

outputs.name: compression_mm
outputs.description: Sink in mm per force.

outputs.name: rest_z_m
outputs.description: Settled body origin height.

outputs.name: recovered_mm
outputs.description: Residual sink after release.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence.

tools.name: solver_parameter_sanity_check
tools.title: Solver parameter sanity check
tools.summary: Contact, joint-limit and equality solref/solimp values are consistent with the timestep (time constant >= 2 x timestep, positive damping ratio, no mixed-sign 'negative' solref), solimp is valid, and light objects do not rest deeper in their supports than half their own size.
tools.description: A solref time constant below twice the timestep is silently raised to 2 x timestep by MuJoCo (refsafe), so the contact the author tuned is not the one simulated; a damping ratio <= 0 bounces; a solref with one negative and one positive entry is almost always a time constant negated by accident (MuJoCo reads negative entries as direct stiffness and damping, so the positive one becomes negative damping); a direct (negative) solref needs stiffness and damping both positive and a stiffness of at least `min_direct_stiffness`. solimp must keep d0 and dmax inside (0, 1), a positive width and a valid midpoint/power. The equilibrium depth of a resting contact does not depend on the mass: it grows with the square of the time constant and with a softer impedance (about g * tc^2 * (1 - d) / d), and on a gram-scale part it can exceed the part's own features; so for each free object lighter than `light_mass_kg` the scene is settled for `settle_s` from keyframe `key` (robot joints held) and each of the object's contacts is compared with the smallest half-size of the object's geom in that contact: a part resting more than `max_depth_frac` of its size deep needs a shorter time constant or a direct (negative) solref. Checked elements: collidable geoms, explicit pairs, limited joints (solreflimit), equalities and tendon limits.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: light_mass_kg
inputs.description: Free objects below this mass get the resting-depth test. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_depth_frac
inputs.description: Largest resting depth as a fraction of the part's smallest half-size. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Settling time for the resting-depth test (0 skips it). Default 0.4.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe the settle starts from. Default 0.

inputs.name: min_direct_stiffness
inputs.description: Smallest direct (negative solref) stiffness, 1/s^2 (rest depth g/k). Default 100.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Name prefix of robot bodies. Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; timestep; refsafe; bad: [{element, kind, solref, solimp, problem}]; light_objects: [{object, mass_kg, depth_m, min_half_size_m, frac}]; worst.

tools.name: spring_stiffness_test
tools.title: Spring stiffness test
tools.summary: Quasi-static force ramp on a built spring: measured N/m against the requested stiffness, plus a 10x overload check of the solid stop.
tools.description: Loads a spring built by construct_spring, presses its tip plate with each force in `forces` for 6 s of sim time, reads the compression, fits a line through the points still on the spring (under 85% of the travel) and reports the slope as the measured stiffness with its error against the requested value. It then presses with ten times the largest force and requires the compression to stay within 0.3 mm of the design travel, which is what a coil-bound stop does and a soft joint limit does not. Passes when the stiffness error is within `tolerance_pct` and the stop holds.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_spring returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: forces
inputs.description: The ramp. Default (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0); scale it to the spring.

inputs.name: tolerance_pct
inputs.description: Allowed |measured - requested| / requested in percent. Default 15.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Stiffness within tolerance and the solid stop holds.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence with the measured and requested N/m.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: requested_N_per_m, measured_N_per_m, error_pct, force_deflection [(N, mm)], travel_m, solid_stop_m, solid_stop_ok.

tools.name: stacked_on_gate
tools.title: Stacked-on gate
tools.summary: A rests on B at the end of a window: supported by B's top (an A-B contact whose normal points up out of B), level within a tolerance, optionally yaw-aligned modulo a symmetry, and not supported by the table; several supports mean A bridges all of them.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the pink brick rests on top of the sage green brick' and 'the cream brick bridges the two bricks'. On the decision frame (the window's last frame, or `frame`) the trajectory state is loaded in the execution model and collision detection runs with a 2 mm margin on A and each support. A is on a support when some contact between their subtrees has a normal pointing down from A into the support by at least normal_min (0.7, i.e. within 45 deg of vertical): A sits on the support's top, not against its side. Every support must carry A (bridging); A must not touch the table (unless allow_table); A's nearest body axis must be within level_tol_deg of vertical (a brick resting on a stud edge fails); with yaw_tol_deg, A's yaw relative to the first support, folded by yaw_sym_deg (90 for a square brick), must be within the tolerance. Two parts of one articulated object that the scene excludes from collision (a hinged lid on its box) are judged by the geometric gap of their primitive geoms and A's level. Fails with the gap to each support when A is elsewhere.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The stacked body A.

inputs.name: support
inputs.description: The supporting body B, or several bodies A must bridge.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last]; decided on the last frame.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Decide on this frame instead (negative counts from the end).

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Contact detection distance, m. Default 0.002.

inputs.name: level_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed tilt of A from level. Default 10.

inputs.name: normal_min
inputs.description: Minimum downward component of a supporting contact normal. Default 0.7.

inputs.name: yaw_tol_deg
inputs.description: Yaw alignment tolerance to the first support; None skips. Default None.

inputs.name: yaw_sym_deg
inputs.description: Rotational symmetry folded out of the yaw error. Default 90.

inputs.name: allow_table
inputs.description: Allow A to touch the table too. Default false.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; frame; supports {name: contacts, top_contacts, gap_m}; touches_table; level_err_deg; yaw_err_deg.

tools.name: stage1_goal_gate
tools.title: Stage 1 goal gate
tools.summary: Independently measure every Stage 1 subgoal and the task_success final scene; generated expectations cannot redefine success.
tools.description: Uses the trusted Stage 1 goal sentences, object identities and reviewed declarative predicates. Each subgoal is checked at its own execution boundary; its temporary grasp, lift or opening requirement is not automatically imposed on the final scene. The separate task_success sentence is checked at the actual end of the episode, with a final stability interval when release or holding is required. Clauses whose requirements are not covered by the supported language/predicate vocabulary fail closed. The trusted Stage 1 input can add task_success_predicates using {class, bodies: {A, B}, params, side}; they cannot waive unknown prose. Final predicates cannot provide earlier frame windows. A requirement that an object has not moved is checked throughout the episode against its initial pose. Object and hand roles for the final scene come from Stage 1/2, not the generated manifest. Generated goal_predicates only add checks; deviation predicates cannot replace independently inferred goals. Subgoal state sentences also require complete supported clause coverage; a recognised motion or a reviewed predicate cannot waive an unknown clause. Unsupported event language needs an implemented measurement. Unknown prose, unresolved objects, omitted final success, unsupported final-state classes and missing evidence block acceptance. This is a conservative supported-language verifier, not an unrestricted natural-language oracle.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 scene_semantics.json.

inputs.name: trajectory_manifest_json
inputs.description: Stage 3 trajectory_manifest.json (subgoals with stage1_indices, object, side, frames; optional goal_predicates, deviation).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: The delivered trajectory npz (qpos, fps, labels, subgoal).

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json; default the manifest's scene_recon.

inputs.name: subgoals
inputs.description: Stage 1 indices to diagnose; default all. A proper subset cannot return full-task ok.

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Frame step for per-frame predicates. Default 1.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; task_success {goal, predicates, coverage, issues, ok}; subgoals [{index, goal, motion, entries, frames, required_classes, predicates [{class, A, B, joint, frames, source, ok, measured, issues, note}], deviation {reason, classes, accepted}, notes, errors, ok}]; counts {subgoals, judged, passed}.

tools.name: stage2_gate_suite
tools.title: Stage 2 gate suite
tools.summary: Runs source-reference provenance, every scene assertion and compile check a Stage 2 scene must pass (robot and physics untouched, initial state settled, plausible objects, camera and Stage 1 consistency, stable compile) and returns one verdict.
tools.description: Reads `scene_recon.json` in the workspace for the scene, camera, masks and objects, and the Stage 1 file for the objects' roles and properties. Source masks (including the hands exclusion) require trusted harness receipts tied to the original video and matching reference frame; standalone/legacy masks and written provenance are unverified. Blocking checks (any failure fails the suite): source_reference_provenance_check, robot_model_integrity_check, robot_joint_range_check, actuator_limit_integrity_check, contact_exclusion_audit, physics_options_check, stage_station_integrity_check, initial_keyframe_state_check, hand_contact_pair_mask_check, object_mass_plausibility_check, object_inertia_plausibility_check, friction_parameter_check, free_body_policy_check, video_frustum_check, camera_registration_check, collision_visual_alignment_check, object_count_vs_stage1_check, articulation_axis_semantics_check, appearance_texture_check, asset_scene_consistency_check, deformable_topology_check and deformable_rest_check (when a deformable is a MuJoCo cable: one a subgoal cuts), isaac_deformable_rest_check (when a deformable is simulated in Isaac Sim: its cord specification, settled poses, settling report and placement re-measured from the files), hand_object_contact_consistency_check (when the workspace has metric hand joints: hands.npz in the workspace, egocam/ or episode/, or scene_recon's hands_npz), object_scale_vs_footprint_check (when masks exist; an Isaac Sim cord is drawn as a tube along its settled centreline; objects declared hidden_at_frame0 have no frame-0 footprint and are left out of it and of camera_registration_check), and the scene compile checks listed in COMPILE_CHECKS. camera_hand_overlay_check is reported as a warning only (demonstrators' hands rarely rest exactly at the robot's home pose). A check that crashes counts as failed. Each check's full report is returned under `reports`.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Stage 2 workspace holding scene_recon.json.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 deliverable.

inputs.name: setup_dir
inputs.description: Setup folder the robot and physics must match; default the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: skip
inputs.description: Check names to leave out (reported as skipped; for a custom setup without some data).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues (prefixed by check name), warnings, reports {check: report}, skipped, seconds {check: s}.

tools.name: stage3_gate_suite
tools.title: Stage 3 gate suite
tools.summary: Re-measures a delivered Stage 3 episode with every episode audit, goal gate, anti-tampering scene check and the Stage 4 hand-off (with randomization draws) and returns one verdict; incomplete diagnostic runs cannot pass.
tools.description: Reads trajectory_manifest.json in the workspace for the trajectory, the scene it was executed in (`scene_executed`, else the Stage 2 scene) and the subgoal entries. Groups: (1) episode physics: episode_physics_check, robot_self_collision_check, arm_reach_check and the AUDITS (teleports, joint jumps, silent resets, swept collisions, visual-mesh penetration, dynamics consistency, contactless motion, joint limits of the setup, start and end states, release and slip, labels, ...); (2) goals: subgoal_outcome_check on every executed entry, stage1_goal_gate (each subgoal against its Stage 1 goal sentence, so a weak `expect` cannot pass a missed goal) and bimanual_sync_gate; (3) the executed scene against the setup: robot_model_integrity_check, robot_joint_range_check, actuator_limit_integrity_check, contact_exclusion_audit, physics_options_check, stage_station_integrity_check (the supplied setup is fixed), initial_keyframe_state_check; (4) Stage 4: stage4_handoff_check and, with draws > 0, stage4_randomization_gate (two thirds of the randomized layouts, 2 of 3, must pass Stage 4's own checks). Deformables simulated in Isaac Sim (the manifest's deformables block from execute_isaac_deformables): the goal gates and the audits that read object states run on the episode's MuJoCo mirror (the executed scene plus each cord's recorded links), the checks that re-simulate MuJoCo physics on the executed recording, and isaac_recording_check (binding, PhysX, the cord's own physics, an Isaac re-simulation) is added. Quality audits block final acceptance. Disabling quality, omitting randomization, skipping a check, or a missing/crashing check cannot produce a final pass.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Stage 3 workspace with trajectory_manifest.json.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 deliverable.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json (the scene, camera.json next to it).

inputs.name: setup_dir
inputs.description: Setup folder the robot and physics must match; default the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: Stage 4 randomization draws to try. Default 3; zero is diagnostic only and cannot pass.

inputs.name: strict_quality
inputs.description: Default True. False is diagnostic only and cannot pass.

inputs.name: skip
inputs.description: Diagnostic check omissions; any requested omission prevents final acceptance.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues (prefixed by check name), warnings, reports {check: report}, skipped, seconds {check: s}, scene, trajectory.

tools.name: stage4_handoff_check
tools.title: Stage 4 handoff check
tools.summary: Validate a Stage 3 task folder the way Stage 4 will read it: files present, the scene compiles with the trajectory's qpos width, every segment phase matches frames, anchors change only through blends, carriers and releases resolve, cameras and table are set, and the video camera matches Stage 2's camera.json.
tools.description: Loads stage4.json with Stage 4's own config loader and builds its Episode object (the step that re-anchors frames), so the same assertions Stage 4 makes at the start of `randomize` run here with their messages. On top it checks that the trajectory's labels follow the 'side: phase' convention, that every segment's phase patterns match a frame, that every randomized object is a body of the scene, that the human video exists and decodes (its fps and duration go into the summary; they are not judged), that the cameras and the table are set, and that the ego camera in the config (pose, field of view, fx, fy, cx, cy) equals Stage 2's camera.json. Warnings of Stage 4's Episode (such as a hand never anchored to an object it holds) are passed on in summary.warnings without failing the check. With draws > 0 it also runs stage4_randomization_gate (that many randomize draws with Stage 4's own code) and fails when fewer than min_accepted layouts would be kept (default the gate's: two thirds of the draws), so a task Stage 4 cannot randomize is caught at the handoff. It also reports whether the folder hands off the executable Stage 3 plan (plan.json; the rigid runtime does not re-execute it) and checks that every entry of it names bodies of the scene. A task with deformable objects simulated in Isaac Sim (stage4.json `deformables`, written by execute_isaac_deformables) is checked too: deformables.json, the Isaac recording, its report (which must have passed) and the mirror exist; the report's sha256 binding matches the recording and the mirror files; the mirror's qpos width is scene_mirror.xml's nq and its frames the trajectory's; a randomized cord is named as a cord, not as a body of the scene; and Isaac Sim's Python is available to Stage 4 (DEXAGENT_ISAAC_PYTHON or stage4.json isaac.python). Returns ok with the list of issues.

inputs.name: task_dir
inputs.description: Folder with stage4.json (from write_stage4_config).

inputs.name: camera_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 camera.json to compare the ego camera with.

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: Randomize draws to try with stage4_randomization_gate (default 0: config checks only).

inputs.name: min_accepted
inputs.description: Kept layouts the draws must yield (default: the randomization gate's, two thirds of the draws).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues [...], summary {frames, fps, sides, objects, segments, labels, randomization, deformables}.

tools.name: stage4_physics_replay_gate
tools.title: Stage 4 physics replay gate
tools.summary: Replay the original layout and one randomized layout of a Stage 4 task folder in contact physics and re-measure every Stage 3 subgoal expectation on both; passes when the original holds them all and the randomized episode holds every one the original holds.
tools.description: Stage 4's kinematic checks prove the robot can follow an adapted trajectory without new collisions; they do not prove the objects still do what the task needs (a brick pushed into a neighbour that moved stops after 3 of its 15 mm; a cube left where it was when its support moved falls). This gate builds Stage 3's execution model of the task scene (hand collision hulls paired with every object and the table), replays the original servo commands (the `reference` stored in trajectory.npz; without it the executed joint values are replayed as commands, which presses no harder than the fingers touched) segment by segment as Stage 3 executed its subgoals, and judges the Stage 3 manifest's expectations (`manifest` in stage4.json: rise, in hand, no slip, at target, released, at rest, supported on, untouched, penetration, servo tracking ...) with the library's outcome evaluation, plus stability and every randomized object ending within physics_end_tol_m of where the plan puts it. Then it draws layouts exactly as Stage 4's randomize step does (its adaptive sampler, the reach pre-screen, the warp, retiming of a layout rejected only on joint speed) until one passes the kinematic checks (or uses the `layout` given), adapts the commands with the hands (retimed with the warp), moves world-frame targets with their objects, replays it and judges the same checks (with layouts > 1, that many accepted layouts, passing when one holds). A check that fails on the original is an issue on its own (the Stage 3 episode does not hold up in physics); failures cannot be removed from the new layout's requirements. Instability of the original blocks acceptance. Cost: two replays of the episode (4 to 150 ms per frame on the two-hand bench, depending on how many contacts the scene has). DEFORMABLES (stage4.json `deformables`): the robot and rigid objects replay in MuJoCo as above, then the cords run in Isaac Sim driven by the replayed robot, moved by the layout's draw for the cord (the original layout reuses the Stage 3 Isaac recording when its replay is the recorded trajectory bit for bit); the Isaac episode must pass (no PhysX error, no missed grasp, no link through the table or faster than the limit) and the Stage 1 goals and the expectations that name a cord are judged on the Isaac mirror with the same code; each Isaac episode adds its own run time (minutes for a long episode).

inputs.name: task_dir
inputs.description: Folder with stage4.json (from write_stage4_config).

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: Layouts to try until one passes the kinematic checks (default 10).

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Seed of the draws (default: the config's seed).

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: A layout to replay instead of drawing one: {objects: {name: [dx, dy, dyaw_deg]}, robot: {}}.

inputs.name: layouts
inputs.description: Kinematically accepted layouts to replay (default 1); the gate passes when at least one holds.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, warnings, original {checks, not_held, seconds}, layout, kinematic, physics {ok, failed, subgoals, end_error_m, seconds} of the layout shown, layouts_replayed, layouts_held, draws_tried.

requirements: Isaac Sim 5.0 for tasks with deformables

tools.name: stage4_randomization_gate
tools.title: Stage 4 randomization gate
tools.summary: Run N randomize draws of a Stage 4 task folder with Stage 4's own sampler, trajectory adaptation and feasibility checks, and pass when enough of them would be kept (by default two thirds: 2 of 3, so a Stage 3 episode leaves Stage 4 a margin, not one lucky layout); reports why the others were rejected.
tools.description: A Stage 3 episode can satisfy every Stage 3 check and still yield nothing in Stage 4: the randomize step discards every layout whose adapted trajectory fails reach, joint speed, object continuity or the no-new-penetration check (an EgoDex lego stack passed Stage 3 and Stage 4 kept 0 of 60 layouts, because stacked bricks were released relative to the wrong brick). This gate loads the task folder with Stage 4's config loader, builds its Episode (the anchor schedule, carriers, releases, rests_on / inside relations and their cycle check run here with Stage 4's messages) and draws `draws` layouts exactly as the randomize step does (the same seeds and adaptive sampler, the reach pre-screen of the anchored keyframes, the warp, retiming of a layout rejected only on joint speed, the same checks), optionally with the physics replay of every kinematically accepted layout (physics_replay=true; it costs one contact-physics replay of the episode per accepted layout plus one of the original); reexecute=true asks for the re-execution of the handed-off Stage 3 plan on layouts the warp rejects, which the rigid runtime does not offer (it stays off). Nothing is written. It passes when accepted >= min_accepted, by default ceil(min_fraction x draws) with min_fraction 2/3: one layout in three passing is luck, not an episode Stage 4 can randomize. The report counts the rejections per check, gives the first concrete example of each (the colliding pair and frame, the jumping object, the arm that cannot reach) and says what to change in the config (narrower ranges, attached_to for objects that touch, rests_on / inside for an object put on another one). Assumes the folder was written by write_stage4_config (or by hand in the same format). A cord simulated in Isaac Sim (stage4.json `deformables`) is drawn like an object by its name and the hands anchored to it move with it; with physics_replay the cords of every kinematically accepted layout also run in Isaac Sim and the goals are judged on its mirror (stage4_physics_replay_gate).

inputs.name: task_dir
inputs.description: Folder with stage4.json and the files it names.

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: Layouts to draw (default 10).

inputs.name: min_accepted
inputs.description: Kept layouts needed to pass (default: ceil(min_fraction x draws), 2 of 3).

inputs.name: min_fraction
inputs.description: Share of the draws that must be kept when min_accepted is not given (default 2/3).

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Seed of the draws (default: the config's seed, as the randomize step uses).

inputs.name: physics_replay
inputs.description: Also replay every kinematically accepted layout in contact physics (default false).

inputs.name: reexecute
inputs.description: Ask for the re-execution of the handed-off Stage 3 plan (plan.json) on layouts the warp rejects (default false; unavailable on the rigid runtime, where it stays off).

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, accepted, draws, min_accepted, rate, rejections {check: count}, examples {check: detail}, methods {warp | warp+retime | reexecuted: count}, rows [per draw: ok, failed, layout, method, detail], seconds_per_draw, relations, warnings, reexecution (whether a plan was handed off).

tools.name: stage_station_integrity_check
tools.title: Stage and station integrity check
tools.summary: The robot station roots, the table (body, geom pose and size) and the home keyframe of a scene equal the setup's, except for a station shift recorded by place_arm_stations, which must explain every moved station and the moved hand home exactly.
tools.description: Moving a station closer to an object, raising the table under a hand or lowering it under a forearm makes a trajectory feasible in simulation only. The reference is the setup (default: the repository's setup/): setup.yaml's stations.<side>.base_body / base_pos / base_quat_wxyz and table body / geom, the setup scene's table geom and its home keyframe. Each station root must sit at the reference position with the reference orientation, or be displaced by exactly the horizontal shift [dx, dy] of the place_arm_stations report (optional input; the skill moves both stations by default or only some), within tol_m. The table body and its collision geom must keep their pose and size. In keyframe 0 the arm joints, finger joints and wrist rotations must equal the setup's home, and each hand's wrist position must equal the setup's home plus its own station's displacement (place_arm_stations moves the hand home with its flange). A scene without a keyframe is reported (initial_keyframe_state_check says more).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF (Stage 2 scene.xml or the executed scene_stations.xml).

inputs.name: setup
inputs.description: Setup folder (or its setup.yaml / scene.xml). Default: the repository's setup/.

inputs.name: stations_report
inputs.description: place_arm_stations.json (or its dict) recording the shift [dx, dy]. Default None.

inputs.name: unrecorded_shift_ok
inputs.description: Without a report, accept a pure in-plane translation of a station within shift_bounds_m (the move place_arm_stations makes) as a warning. Default True.

inputs.name: shift_bounds_m
inputs.description: Allowed unrecorded translation. Default ((-0.5, 0.5), (-0.2, 0.5)).

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed position difference, metres. Default 1e-4.

inputs.name: tol_rad
inputs.description: Allowed joint difference in the home keyframe, rad (or m for slides). Default 1e-4.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; stations {side: {reference, scene, shift, explained}}; recorded_shift; table {body, geom, changed}; home {joints compared, changed [{joint, reference, scene}]}.

tools.name: start_state_audit
tools.title: Start state audit
tools.summary: Frame 0 equals the scene's keyframe (robot, objects and mechanisms), and simulating the scene from frame 0 with the robot held still leaves every object where it is.
tools.description: No other audit compares the trajectory with the scene's keyframe or simulates the start. (1) The scene must have a keyframe (index `key`, default 0). (2) Frame 0 must equal it: robot joints within robot_tol (default 0.01 rad or m), free objects within pos_tol_m (default 3 mm) and rot_tol_deg (default 2 deg), mechanism joints within robot_tol. (3) Settled: the scene as the bench executor runs it (hand-object pairs) is simulated for settle_s (default 1 s) from frame 0 with every robot joint held where it is (the hands' servos hold their start pose), and again from the keyframe when it differs from frame 0 (from qpos0 when the scene has no keyframe: that is where a replay would start); each free object's peak displacement and rotation must stay under settle_m (default 3 mm) and settle_deg (default 2 deg). An object that drops, slides or tips here starts the episode from a state the scene does not hold: re-place it (rest it on its support) and write the keyframe from the settled state. Reports the largest frame-0 differences and each object's settle motion.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Window whose first frame is judged as the start (the keyframe comparison applies when it is frame 0). Default all.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Keyframe index or name. Default 0.

inputs.name: robot_tol
inputs.description: Allowed robot / mechanism joint difference (rad or m; an arm re-fitted to the executed hand differs from the keyframe by a few thousandths). Default 0.01.

inputs.name: pos_tol_m, rot_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed object pose difference. Defaults 0.003, 2.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Simulated time. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: settle_m, settle_deg
inputs.description: Allowed peak object motion while settling. Defaults 0.003, 2.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst; keyframe {name, robot_max_diff, objects {name: diff mm, deg}, mechanisms}; settle {name: peak moved mm, rotated deg, final}.

tools.name: strand_crossing_check
tools.title: Strand crossing check
tools.summary: Counts the crossings between different strands of a multi-strand rope, cable or ribbon seen from above, records which strand lies on top at each, orders them along the braid by their mean arc length from the strands' first links (so a three-strand plait reads as alternating pairs), and optionally settles the scene and checks every crossing survives with the same strand on top.
tools.description: Each strand is an ordered list of link bodies (from a constructor's build dict, a scene_recon entry with 'strands', or a plain {label: [body, ...]}), listed from the joined end. At keyframe 0 (or a given qpos) every strand becomes the polyline of its link positions; segments of different strands are intersected in the horizontal plane and the height of both strands at the intersection decides which is on top. Each crossing gets the arc length from the first link along both strands (along_a, along_b) and is ordered by their mean (along_mean): strands that start together at a junction reach a given crossing at nearly the same arc length, so this is the order along the braid. Ordering along one strand alone would put every crossing that strand is not part of at the end, and a real three-strand plait (where each strand takes part in two crossings out of three) would read as repeating pairs. A three-strand plait shows crossings whose consecutive strand pairs differ; `expect_alternating` requires that.
