With settle_s > 0 the scene is simulated under gravity (robot actuators hold their keyframe controls) and the crossings are counted again: each initial crossing must be found again within match_m with the same strand on top, else the strands slid apart or passed through each other. Strands that share their first point (a fan of strands leaving one knot) touch there; an intersection lying within junction_m of both strands' first links is the joined end, not a crossing. Passes when the initial count is at least min_crossings (and at most max_crossings when given), the pairs alternate when asked, and, when settled, no crossing was lost or flipped. Assumes the strands lie roughly horizontal (crossings are judged in the x-y plane).

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene or asset.

inputs.name: strands
inputs.description: {label: [link body names in order from the joined end]} or a build dict / JSON with strands {label: {links: [...]}}.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State to judge; default keyframe 0 (or qpos0).

inputs.name: min_crossings
inputs.description: Least number of crossings required. Default 1.

inputs.name: max_crossings
inputs.description: Most crossings allowed (e.g. 0 for an unbraided goal). Default None.

inputs.name: expect_alternating
inputs.description: Consecutive crossings along the braid must be between different strand pairs (a plait). Default False.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Seconds of passive simulation before the persistence check; 0 skips it. Default 0.

inputs.name: match_m
inputs.description: How far a crossing may move during settling and still count as the same. Default 0.03.

inputs.name: junction_m
inputs.description: Intersections within this distance of both strands' first links are the shared joined end, not crossings. Default 0.005.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; n_crossings; crossings [{a, b, over, dz_m, xy, along_a, along_b, along_mean}] in braid order; pairs_sequence; alternating; order_rule; after_settle {n_crossings, lost, flipped} when settled.

tools.name: stud_stack_seat_test
tools.title: Stud stack seat test
tools.summary: Drops one brick asset onto another (aligned, misaligned by a few millimetres, and shifted by whole stud pitches) and checks that it seats over the studs, centres itself, stays level and resists a sideways shove, so stacked bricks interlock instead of resting block-on-block.
tools.description: Composes a test world from two brick MJCFs (the lower and the upper, the same file allowed) with a floor: names are prefixed, the lower brick stands on the floor at the origin, the upper brick is placed above it at each trial offset (dx, dy in the lower brick's frame, metres) with a small drop gap and released under gravity, then pressed down with press_N for press_s at the centre of the part of its top that lies over the lower brick (a hand pressing the supported half of an overhanging brick). A trial passes when, after settling, the upper brick's bottom is within seat_tol_m of the lower brick's top face (body_height_m, read from the built dict or measured from the lower brick's highest non-stud geom), its tilt is under max_tilt_deg, and its lateral position is within max_lateral_m of the nearest stud-grid position (offset rounded to whole pitches). A shove trial then pushes the seated aligned upper brick sideways with shove_N (default 0.75 x its weight) for shove_s; it passes when the upper brick moves less than max_shove_m relative to the lower one (the lower brick may slide along with it on the floor). Both bricks must be free bodies. The report gives every trial's measured seat height error, tilt, lateral error and the shove displacement.

inputs.name: lower
inputs.description: construct_stud_brick build dict (or its params json, or an MJCF path) of the bottom brick.

inputs.name: upper
inputs.description: The brick dropped on top; default the same as lower.

inputs.name: offsets_m
inputs.description: Release offsets of the upper brick in the lower brick's frame. Default: aligned, a lead-in offset of 0.3 x stud radius on both axes, and one pitch along x.

inputs.name: drop_gap_m
inputs.description: Release height of the upper brick's bottom above the lower brick's stud tops. Default 0.002

inputs.name: press_N
inputs.description: Downward press on the upper brick after release, applied over its supported part (a hand pressing it on). Default 3.0

inputs.name: press_s
inputs.description: Press duration. Default 0.3

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Settling time after the press. Default 1.0

inputs.name: seat_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed seat height error. Default 0.0015

inputs.name: max_tilt_deg
inputs.description: Allowed tilt of the seated brick. Default 3.0

inputs.name: max_lateral_m
inputs.description: Allowed distance from the nearest stud-grid position. Default 0.0015

inputs.name: shove_N
inputs.description: Sideways shove on the seated brick at its centre of mass, newtons (0 skips). Default None = 0.75 x the upper brick's weight, more than plain plastic-on-plastic friction holds

inputs.name: shove_s
inputs.description: Shove duration. Default 0.5

inputs.name: max_shove_m
inputs.description: Allowed displacement under the shove. Default 0.002

inputs.name: timestep
inputs.description: Simulation timestep. Default 0.001

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report file.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; trials: [{offset, seated, seat_err_m, tilt_deg, lateral_err_m, ok}]; shove: {force_N, displacement_m, ok}; body_height_m; pitch_m.

tools.name: subgoal_outcome_check
tools.title: Subgoal outcome check
tools.summary: Measure a subgoal's outcome on the executed (physics) trajectory against its expectations: rise, in hand, no slip, at target, released, at rest, supported, upright, joint reached, turned, tilted, displaced, a rope severed, a press-fit part seated, untouched bystanders, penetration and servo tracking; per hand for a two-hand entry.
tools.description: The simulation-verifiable subgoal of the paper. Expectations come from plan_subgoal_keyframes (`expect`) or are written by hand: object (body), hand (side), rise_m, in_hand (+min_links), no_slip (+slip_from frame), target_pos (+target_axes; the tolerance is half the subgoal's planned displacement, start to target over all three axes, at least 3 mm and at most pos_tol_m, default 30 mm, so a short move must arrive; target_frac and pos_tol_min_m override the half and the 3 mm; measured target_err_m, planned_move_m, target_tol_m), target_quat_wxyz (a finite unit object orientation, checked within 15 degrees), released, at_rest, supported (+on), upright, tilt_deg, stays_put, joint (+joint_target | turned_rad | joint_min_travel), displacement {dir, min_m}, yaw_turned_deg, knot (a cable's centreline is knotted at the end, true = trefoil or a knot name; see rope_knot_check), severed (a rope cut by scissors: a join equality name, a list of them or true for any rope join; it passes when the episode's recorded eq_active shows the join whole at the subgoal's start and cut by its end -- `severed` -- and the two cut ends are at least sever_gap_m (default 3 mm) apart at the end -- `cut_ends_apart`; measured.severed gives each join's cut_frame and end_gap_mm; an episode without eq_active fails it with a hint), seated (press_seat: {axis, target, depth_m, tol_m, phase}; the part's root must end within tol_m of the target along the press axis; measured seat_travel_mm, seat_remaining_mm, peak_press_force_n), untouched [bodies], and for a two-hand entry hands {side: expect} (each hand's checks named '<side>:<check>', slip and pad frames read from that hand's part of the 'left: ... | right: ...' labels) with hands_apart (no hand-hand contact on any frame). Every expectation is measured by forward kinematics and contacts on the frames of the subgoal (all frames, a frame range, or the frames whose `subgoal` index matches), and the rollout diagnostics stored in the episode (hand penetration, object penetration, wrist tracking) are judged when present. The report names each failed expectation with the number behind it.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Bench scene MJCF (the physics scene the episode was executed in, or the Stage 2 scene).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz from rollout_keyframes_physics / execute_subgoal_plan.

inputs.name: expect
inputs.description: Expectations (see description).

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Evaluate the frames whose subgoal index equals this (needs the npz `subgoal` array).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [start, end] frame range instead.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, failed [names], checks {name: bool}, measured {...}, frames.

tools.name: support_check
tools.title: Support check
tools.summary: After settling, every free body touches something, and every fixed object stands on a surface rather than hanging in mid-air or over an edge.
tools.description: Two ways an object can float. A free body that has no contact at all after the scene settles has fallen out of the world or hovers where no support was built. A fixed body, which the settle test cannot expose because it never falls, is probed with downward rays across its footprint: most of the footprint must have a surface directly below (`min_supported_frac`, 60 percent), and that surface must be close (`max_gap`, 15 mm). Static bodies whose name matches `support_names` (the table, the floor) are the supports themselves and are skipped. The report gives, per object, the supported fraction, the gap and the footprint, which is enough to decide whether to move the object or extend the surface.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time before judging free bodies. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: support_names
inputs.description: Regular expressions of bodies that are supports and are not checked. Default table|floor|ground|world.

inputs.name: min_supported_frac
inputs.description: Fraction of a fixed object's footprint that needs a surface below. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: max_gap
inputs.description: Largest hover of a fixed object over its surface. Default 0.015.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; floating: free bodies with no contact after settling; static: {body: {supported_frac, gap_m, base_z, footprint_x, footprint_y, verdict}}.

tools.name: swept_collision_audit
tools.title: Swept collision audit
tools.summary: Check every recorded physics state and interpolated configurations for robot-robot, robot-scene and object-scene penetration, including tunnelling between samples.
tools.description: Per-frame checks (robot_self_collision_check, episode_physics_check, penetration_check) cannot see a part that is outside an obstacle on frame t and on frame t+1 but passed through it in between. This audit compiles a copy of the scene in which every visible robot geom collides as its convex hull (as robot_self_collision_check does) and the objects and the table keep their collision geometry, then for each pair of consecutive frames bounds how far any colliding body moves (its origin's travel plus its radius times its rotation). When that exceeds sub_m (default 3 mm, thinner than a lid wall), it inserts evenly spaced sub-steps (joints interpolated linearly, free-body and ball rotations by slerp; at most max_sub) and runs collision detection on each. Absolute penetration deeper than tol_m (default 3 mm) fails, including on the recorded states themselves. Incomplete subdivision coverage fails. Only mechanically related robot bodies, redundant hand proxies, static-static pairs, and parts within one object are excluded. Reports each event's frames, sub-step fraction, geoms, bodies and depth.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in (a path: a collidable copy is compiled from it).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: sub_m
inputs.description: Largest motion between checked configurations. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: tol_m
inputs.description: Maximum absolute penetration. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: max_sub
inputs.description: Most sub-steps per frame pair. Default 12.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {frames, fraction, geoms, bodies, kind, depth_mm, frame_depth_mm}; events (up to 20); frame_pairs_subdivided, substeps.

tools.name: table_clearance_check
tools.title: Table clearance check
tools.summary: Lowest point of a carried body stays above the table top and above other bodies it passes over during the carry.
tools.description: Over the carry window (frames, phase patterns, or the object's own motion window), replays the trajectory, computes the world-space lowest point of the body's geoms (from the oriented bounds of each geom, meshes included) and reports the minimum clearance to the table top. It fails below min_clearance (default -12 mm: a sliver of soft-contact penetration is how a resting object is carried, more is a collision). With obstacles (body names, or every non-robot body by default) it also requires that whenever the carried body's footprint overlaps an obstacle's footprint in XY, its lowest point is above that obstacle's top. The table top height can be given or read from a body named table.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The carried object.

inputs.name: table_top_z
inputs.description: Table surface height; default from the body named 'table'.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Carry window; default the object's motion window.

inputs.name: obstacles
inputs.description: Bodies to clear when passing over; default all non-robot bodies.

inputs.name: min_clearance_m
inputs.description: Default -0.012.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; min clearance to the table (m) with frame and label; per obstacle the worst overlap; window used.

tools.name: table_workspace_bounds_audit
tools.title: Table workspace bounds audit
tools.summary: On every frame, hands and objects stay above the tabletop plane (vertex-exact), over the table's footprint, under a height ceiling, and optionally inside a given work area.
tools.description: Plane-and-footprint bounds, where robot_self_collision_check and episode_physics_check judge contacts with the table geometry on sampled frames. The table is the body named 'table' (top = the highest point of its geoms, footprint = their x-y extent) or a ground plane. On every frame: (1) the lowest point of each hand's visible geoms (mesh vertices, primitive surfaces) and of each object's colliding geoms may not lie more than below_tol_m (default 5 mm) under the tabletop while over the footprint; (2) an object's centre of mass may not leave the footprint (pushed or dropped off the table) nor drop more than fall_m (default 2 cm) under the tabletop anywhere (fell through or off); (3) no hand or object centre more than max_height_m (default 0.6 m) above the tabletop; (4) with work_area {x: [lo, hi], y: [lo, hi]} (setup.yaml's table.work_area, the cloth the camera covers), objects' centres stay inside it. Hands are the bench hands (or the robot bodies grouped by side); arms are left to robot_self_collision_check. Reports per body the worst frame and margin.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: below_tol_m
inputs.description: Allowed depth of a hand or object point under the tabletop over the table. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: fall_m
inputs.description: Object centre this far under the tabletop anywhere = fell. Default 0.02.

inputs.name: max_height_m
inputs.description: Ceiling above the tabletop for hand and object centres. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: work_area
inputs.description: {x: [lo, hi], y: [lo, hi]} objects must stay inside (metres). Default None.

inputs.name: table_top_z
inputs.description: Override the tabletop height.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {body, kind, frame, label, value}; table {top_z, xy}; bodies {name: lowest margin mm, frame, max height}.

tools.name: target_region_gate
tools.title: Target region gate
tools.summary: An object ends inside a region of the table (a box, a polygon or a disc in the table frame), optionally within a height band and a yaw or upright tolerance, and stays there for the last hold_s of the window.
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'the cap rests on the table to the right of the bottle' once the agent has written where 'right of the bottle' is. The table frame is the scene's world x, y with z measured from the tabletop (the top of the body named 'table', else 0). On the window's last frame the object's reference point (its body origin, or its mass-weighted centre with point='com') must lie inside the region polygon (even-odd test), its height above the table inside z_range when given, its yaw (body x axis about vertical) within yaw_tol_deg of yaw_target_deg folded by yaw_sym_deg, and its starting up axis within upright_tol_deg of vertical when given. With hold_s > 0 every frame of the last hold_s seconds must satisfy the same test. The issue names the distance to the region's centre.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The placed body.

inputs.name: region
inputs.description: {'box': [[xmin, ymin], [xmax, ymax]]} | {'polygon': [[x, y], ...]} | {'center': [x, y], 'radius': r}, metres in the table frame.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last]; decided at the last frame.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: z_range
inputs.description: [min, max] height of the reference point above the tabletop, m.

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: 'origin' (body frame origin) or 'com'. Default origin.

inputs.name: yaw_target_deg
inputs.description: Target yaw about vertical, deg.

inputs.name: yaw_tol_deg
inputs.description: Yaw tolerance, deg. Default 15 when a target is given.

inputs.name: yaw_sym_deg
inputs.description: Rotational symmetry folded out of the yaw error, deg.

inputs.name: upright_tol_deg
inputs.description: Allowed tilt of the starting up axis, deg.

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: The object must stay in the region for the last hold_s seconds. Default 0.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; end {frame, xy, z_above_table, in_region, in_height, yaw_err_deg, tilt_deg, ok}; frames_evaluated.

tools.name: task_final_state_vs_video_gate
tools.title: Final state vs video gate
tools.summary: Render each object's silhouette at the trajectory's final state through the video camera (a per-frame camera for a moving head camera) and compare it with the video's last-frame object mask (IoU per object); objects below min_iou ended somewhere else than in the demonstration.
tools.description: A whole-task check that needs no goal sentence: where the human left each object is where the robot should leave it, unless a declared deviation says otherwise. The scene is compiled with the video camera -- a camera named in the scene, a pinhole camera dict / JSON (width, height, fx, fy or fovy_deg, pos, quat_wxyz or R_cv, as Stage 2's camera.json), or a per-frame camera (a list indexed by video frame or {'frames': [{frame, pos, quat_wxyz, ...}]}) from which the camera of video_frame (default the last) is taken -- and rendered with MuJoCo's segmentation renderer at the masks' resolution on trajectory frame `frame` (default the last). Each object's silhouette is the union of the bodies in its subtree (scene_recon_json maps Stage 1 ids to root bodies; otherwise names resolve as exact, slug or a unique '_<name>' suffix). Pixels covered by the robot at that state (ignore_robot) and by occluder_mask (the human hands in the video frame) are removed from both silhouettes, since neither image shows the object there. IoU below min_iou fails the object and names it; between min_iou and warn_iou is a warning. Objects listed in `exclude` (an accepted deviation) are skipped; when no other mask names a body, nothing is judged and the gate fails (unless every mask was excluded, which is only noted). With out_dir it writes the render and one overlay per object. The camera's aspect ratio must match the masks'.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Object -> binary mask of the video's last frame (PNG or array), or a folder of <object>.png.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Scene camera name, camera dict / JSON, or per-frame camera list / JSON.

inputs.name: video_frame
inputs.description: Video frame of a per-frame camera; default its last.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Trajectory frame to render. Default -1.

inputs.name: min_iou
inputs.description: Failure threshold per object. Default 0.4.

inputs.name: warn_iou
inputs.description: Warning threshold. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: ignore_robot
inputs.description: Drop the pixels the robot covers. Default true.

inputs.name: occluder_mask
inputs.description: Mask of video pixels that hide objects (hands); dropped from both.

inputs.name: scene_recon_json
inputs.description: Stage 2 scene_recon.json for Stage 1 id -> bodies.

inputs.name: exclude
inputs.description: Objects not judged (accepted deviations).

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: Write render.png and overlay_<object>.png here.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; iou {object: value}; failures; warnings; bodies_used; unmatched_masks (folder masks that name no body, skipped); render_size; camera_frame; frame.

tools.name: texture_material_resolution_check
tools.title: Texture and material resolution check
tools.summary: Every texture file exists and decodes to the size MuJoCo compiled, texture sizes and total texture memory stay within budget, every material's texture resolves, and a 2D-textured material is not put on a mesh without texture coordinates (MuJoCo maps it automatically, but the Stage 4 exporter and any UV-based renderer drop it).
tools.description: Textures fail quietly: a renderer that cannot find a texture draws the base colour (a missing texture has killed a Cycles render without an error), a 2D texture on a mesh that has no UV coordinates is drawn by MuJoCo with automatic coordinates but dropped by the Stage 4 exporter (it writes UVs only when the mesh has them), so the photoreal render shows the base colour while the MuJoCo render shows the texture; and an 8k texture costs 256 MB of model memory per copy. The check reads every texture file reference of the MJCF (following includes, resolved as MuJoCo resolves them) and fails a missing file or one that does not decode (PNG/JPG via OpenCV, KTX skipped); it compiles the scene (a missing file or unknown material is MuJoCo's compile error, reported as such) and compares each file texture's decoded size with the compiled one; it fails a texture whose face exceeds `max_texture_px` per side or is under 2 px, total texture data above `max_total_mb`, a material whose texture index does not exist, and a mesh geom whose material carries a 2D texture while the mesh has no texture coordinates. 2D textures no material uses and repeated skyboxes (only the first is drawn) are notes.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model (a model skips the file tests).

inputs.name: max_texture_px
inputs.description: Largest texture face side, pixels. Default 4096.

inputs.name: max_total_mb
inputs.description: Largest total texture data, MB. Default 256.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; notes; textures: [{index, name, type, width, height, face_px, file, decoded_size, problem}]; untextured_meshes: [{geom, mesh, material}]; total_texture_mb; worst.

tools.name: thread_self_locking_test
tools.title: Thread self-locking test
tools.summary: Force-only trial of a screw cap: straight push/pull must not move it, a twist must unscrew it along the full thread, then it must come free.
tools.description: Loads a bottle built by construct_bottle, seats the cap at the top of the thread (or leaves it as compiled with start='seated'), and runs the bottle driver: settle, push 20 N straight down, twist 0.1 N*m closed, pull 20 N straight up, twist open until the thread runs out, lift the free cap away, drop it. Only xfrc_applied is written. It measures the cap travel without turning, the pitch coupling error between lift and yaw, the turns applied, and how far the twist actually got before the thread released. THREAD OK requires under 2 mm of travel under the straight forces, under 2 mm of coupling error and the twist reaching at least 90% of the thread. TWIST STALLED means the cap jammed (contact interference or friction); NOT A THREAD means straight force alone moved the cap. The same trial runs on any asset that exposes the bottle contract: bodies cap/bottle/carrier, joints yaw/lift, equalities thread/engaged and total_lift_m.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_bottle returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json (the asset is rebuilt beside it).

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: 'top' seats the cap at the top of the thread so the closing twist is exercised too; 'seated' tests the compiled state (open only). Default 'top'.

inputs.name: out_mp4
inputs.description: Also render the trial to this video with captions (slower).

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

inputs.name: hold_body
inputs.description: Default True.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: True when the verdict is THREAD OK.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: THREAD OK / NOT A THREAD / TWIST STALLED with the numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: push_N, twist_Nm, travel_without_turning_mm, thread_travel_mm, turns_applied, coupling_error_mm, lift_at_release_mm, turns_at_release.

outputs.name: video
outputs.description: The rendered mp4 when out_mp4 was given.

tools.name: tilt_pour_gate
tools.title: Tilt and pour gate
tools.summary: A container is tilted past min_tilt_deg with its mouth over a target body's footprint (or a table region) for a contiguous min_time_s inside a window -- a pour; without a target, a tilt (optionally one kept to the window's end).
tools.description: The goal predicate behind 'water transfers from the bottle into the mug' (whose liquid the simulation does not carry: the gate checks the motion that would pour it) and 'the bottle's long axis is roughly horizontal'. The tilt is the angle between the container's up axis (up_local, default the body axis that pointed up on frame 0) and the vertical. The mouth is mouth_local in the body frame, by default the point of the container's collision geoms farthest along its up axis on frame 0 (the top centre). A frame pours when the tilt reaches min_tilt_deg and the mouth's x, y lie over the target's collision footprint expanded by target_margin_m (or inside `region`, table frame); the longest contiguous pouring run must last min_time_s. With neither target nor region only the tilt counts; at_end requires the qualifying run to reach the window's last frame (a tilt that must be kept). The issue says whether the tilt was too small, the mouth never over the target, or the pour too short.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the trajectory was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: Episode npz.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The tilted container.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Body the mouth must be over (the mug).

inputs.name: region
inputs.description: Table-frame region instead of a target body (see target_region_gate).

inputs.name: min_tilt_deg
inputs.description: Tilt to reach, deg. Default 45.

inputs.name: min_time_s
inputs.description: Contiguous pouring time, s. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: mouth_local
inputs.description: Mouth point in the body frame, m.

inputs.name: up_local
inputs.description: Container up axis in the body frame.

inputs.name: target_margin_m
inputs.description: Footprint margin around the target, m. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: at_end
inputs.description: The tilted run must reach the window's end. Default false.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: [first, last] window.

inputs.name: subgoal
inputs.description: Use the frames of this npz subgoal index.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; peak_tilt_deg; end_tilt_deg; required_tilt_deg; longest_pour_s; pour_from_frame; required_s; at_end.

tools.name: timing_realism_audit
tools.title: Timing realism audit
tools.summary: Episode and per-subgoal durations against the human video's duration and the Stage 1 time windows: missing subgoals, rushed subgoals, subgoals out of proportion with the rest, and an absurd overall ratio.
tools.description: uncovered_frames_check holds a video-locked trajectory to the video's length (0.98-1.10); a Stage 3 episode is paced by its executor and is legitimately several times longer, so that rule does not apply to it. This audit uses broad bands. Per Stage 1 subgoal it sums the robot time of the Stage 3 subgoals that implement it (the manifest's stage1_indices; a Stage 3 subgoal shared by several Stage 1 subgoals is split evenly; without a manifest the indices are taken to be equal) and divides by the human time window: a Stage 1 subgoal with no robot frames fails (not executed), a ratio below ratio_band[0] (default 0.2: the robot five times faster than the person) or above ratio_band[1] (default 120) fails, and a ratio more than share_factor (default 10) times above or below the episode's median ratio fails (one subgoal out of proportion with the rest: a stalled retry loop or a skipped motion). Any executed Stage 3 subgoal shorter than min_subgoal_s (default 0.3 s) fails. The whole episode against the video duration (scene_semantic's video.duration_s, or video_duration_s, or the end of the last time window) must lie in episode_band (default 0.5-60). Inputs it lacks are skipped and named in the report.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in (used only to validate the trajectory width; may be None).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, fps, labels, subgoal).

inputs.name: scene_semantic
inputs.description: Stage 1 scene_semantics.json (video duration, subgoals with time_window_s).

inputs.name: manifest
inputs.description: trajectory_manifest.json (subgoals with index and stage1_indices).

inputs.name: video_duration_s
inputs.description: Human video length when scene_semantic lacks it.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window counted. Default all.

inputs.name: ratio_band
inputs.description: Robot / human time per Stage 1 subgoal. Default [0.2, 120].

inputs.name: share_factor
inputs.description: Allowed factor between a subgoal's ratio and the episode median ratio. Default 10.

inputs.name: episode_band
inputs.description: Episode / video duration. Default [0.5, 60].

inputs.name: min_subgoal_s
inputs.description: Shortest executed Stage 3 subgoal. Default 0.3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst; episode {robot_s, video_s, ratio}; stage1 {index: robot_s, human_s, ratio, stage3}; stage3 {index: robot_s}; median_ratio; skipped [what was not checked].

tools.name: trajectory_audit
tools.title: Trajectory audit
tools.summary: Runs the smoothness, weld, wrist, disturbance, penetration and coverage checks on an episode and returns one pass/fail table.
tools.description: Bundles joint_speed_check, arm_jerk_check, weld_gap_check, wrist_stop_check, wrist_spin_check, object_disturbance_check, penetration_check and uncovered_frames_check. Robot structure is discovered from the end-effector bodies (the arm bolted to each is found through its equality constraint); checks whose preconditions the scene does not meet (no arm, no wrist hinge by name, no welds) are reported as skipped, not failed; a trajectory whose qpos width is not the scene's nq fails (a 'qpos_width' row) instead of letting every check skip. With a reference trajectory the speed, disturbance and penetration checks become relative to it, which is how an adapted or re-fitted episode is held to the verified one. The report keeps every sub-report, a list of the failing checks and a plain-text table.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene (.xml, needed for the all-geometry penetration check).

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos, labels, fps).

inputs.name: end_effectors
inputs.description: Hand root per side. Default: the setup's stations (setup.yaml hand_root_body).

inputs.description: Objects the task may move (fnmatch).

inputs.name: reference

inputs.name: wrist_joints
inputs.description: Wrist joints with their real stops; default found by name.

inputs.name: real_stops
inputs.description: Real wrist range per side, applied to the default joints by name.

inputs.name: video_frames, video_fps
inputs.description: For the coverage check.

inputs.name: skip
inputs.description: Check names to leave out.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; failed: names; skipped: names with reasons; checks: every sub-report; table: text.

tools.cli: python -m tool_library.verifiers.trajectory_audit scene.xml trajectory.npz --ee right=<hand body> left=<hand body>

tools.name: trajectory_manifest_check
tools.title: Trajectory manifest check
tools.summary: Check a Stage 3 trajectory_manifest.json: every Stage 1 subgoal is executed (or merged/skipped with a reason), each subgoal names its hand pose source and the stress tests that passed on it, every executed subgoal's outcome passed, the episode files exist and agree, and the Stage 4 task folder is referenced.
tools.description: The floor for finishing Stage 3. Reads the manifest and the Stage 1 scene_semantics.json it points to, and verifies: `subgoals` covers every Stage 1 index (an entry may list several Stage 1 indices it merges, or carry `skipped` with a reason and `skip_kind` 'no_robot_action' (the human only looks or waits) or 'merged' (done inside another entry); a manipulation step skipped for any other reason fails: the task is not complete); each entry has motion, side, object (body in the scene), and for grasping motions a `pose` with `source` (the skill that produced it) and, for grasping motions (grasp_lift, hold, unscrew, screw, open_joint, close_joint, pull, regrasp), `stress_tests` naming at least one library verifier with ok true; grasp_more requires combined_hold_state_test bound to its actual segment-end frame and every retained object in the trusted execution history (a push or press is proved by its outcome alone; a `cut` is proved by its outcome's `severed` check -- the rope's join switched off by the blades during the subgoal, read from the recorded equality state -- and, when present, `cut_ends_apart`, and then the trajectory must carry eq_active / eq_names with that join off at its last frame); each has `outcome.ok` true; `episode.trajectory` exists, has the scene's nq columns and 'side: phase' labels; `episode.sim_video` exists; `stage4.task_dir` holds stage4.json; the checks block carries the episode verifiers (episode_physics_check, robot_self_collision_check, arm_reach_check, stage4_handoff_check); when Stage 2 simulates a deformable in Isaac Sim, the deformables block names the Isaac report, deformables.json, the recording and the MuJoCo mirror scene and trajectory (of matching width) with ok true. Returns ok and the list of issues.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: trajectory_manifest.json.

inputs.name: scene_semantic_json
inputs.description: Stage 1 manifest (default from the manifest).

inputs.name: library_index
inputs.description: index.json to validate verifier names against.

inputs.name: trusted_verifiers
inputs.description: Run-start snapshot mapping independently reviewed grasp verifier names to source SHA-256; new tools cannot certify their own result.

inputs.name: trusted_execution_reports
inputs.description: Harness-captured SHA-256 digests of successful direct executor report files. An empty list rejects all executions; None permits standalone diagnostics.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok, issues, counts {subgoals, executed, skipped, stress_tests}.

tools.name: tube_seat_test
tools.title: Tube seat test
tools.summary: Shakes and tilts a loaded tube rack by force and drops a spare tube into an empty well; every tube must end seated in its own well.
tools.description: Rebuilds the rack with a floor, adds one spare tube 30 mm above an empty socket well, and holds the rack body with a spring-damper force grip: settle 1 s, shake laterally at 1.5 Hz up to 9 mm for 4 s, tilt 15 degrees and back over 2 s, then hold still. Afterwards every seated tube and the dropped tube are checked with tube_seated(): lateral offset from their well centre under 4 mm and upright (cosine over 0.9), measured in the rack frame. Requires at least one seated tube in the built dict.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: Every tube, including the dropped one, is seated at the end.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: PASS/FAIL sentence.

tools.name: uncovered_frames_check
tools.title: Uncovered frames check
tools.summary: Trajectory length matches the video, every frame has a phase label, no phase is shorter than a few frames.
tools.description: Compares the trajectory's frame count and frame rate with the demonstration video's (given directly or read from the video file; a video_path that cannot be opened or reports no frames fails), fails when the trajectory covers less than cover_frac (default 0.98) of the video's duration or runs more than 10% longer, lists frames with empty labels, and lists phases shorter than min_phase_frames (default 3). Optionally also requires a list of expected phase patterns to each match at least one frame, which is how a subgoal plan is checked against the trajectory that claims to implement it.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz with qpos, labels and fps.

inputs.name: video_frames, video_fps
inputs.description: The demonstration's length; or give video_path.

inputs.name: video_path
inputs.description: Read frame count and fps from this file (needs opencv).

inputs.name: expected_phases
inputs.description: fnmatch patterns that must each match a frame.

inputs.name: cover_frac
inputs.description: Minimum covered fraction of the video duration. Default 0.98.

inputs.name: min_phase_frames
inputs.description: Shortest legal phase run. Default 3.

inputs.name: label_sep
inputs.description: Labels may carry telemetry after this separator; only the part before it is the phase. Default three or more spaces (' | ' separates the two hands of a two-hand step and is kept).

tools.name: units_check
tools.title: Units check
tools.summary: No geom is positioned or sized at a scale that only pixel coordinates could produce; the scene fits inside a table-sized world.
tools.description: A reconstruction that copies image coordinates into the scene puts a 500 m table a kilometre from the origin; every object then free-falls and the physics checks report instability, which sends the author chasing the wrong fault. This verifier looks at the geometry alone: the position of every collidable geom and its largest extent must stay under a limit (50 m by default, generous for any tabletop or room scene). It names the geoms that break it, so the units mistake is reported as a units mistake.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: max_extent_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed geom half-size or distance from the origin. Default 50.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; offenders: [{geom, body, position, size}]; scene_radius_m: how far the farthest geom sits from the origin.

tools.name: urdf_articulation_check
tools.title: URDF articulation check
tools.summary: A URDF describes a real mechanism: valid joint types with limits, geometry in its links, and mesh-based geometry rather than a few primitive boxes typed by hand.
tools.description: When a construction tool keeps rejecting its inputs, the easy escape is to type a URDF by hand: three boxes and an invalid joint type that count as 'articulated' while looking nothing like the object. This verifier parses the URDF and decides from its structure: every joint type must be one URDF defines; at least `min_moving_joints` joints must be prismatic, revolute or continuous, with finite limits where the type needs them; the links must carry some geometry (a link without any, such as a root frame, is allowed); and, unless `allow_primitives` is set, the visual and collision geometry must include meshes, because a measured reconstruction is never only primitives. Mesh files referenced by the URDF must exist next to it. The report lists joints with their types and limits and the reasons for any failure.

inputs.name: urdf_path
inputs.description: The URDF file.

inputs.name: min_moving_joints
inputs.description: Prismatic/revolute/continuous joints required. Default 1.

inputs.name: allow_primitives
inputs.description: Accept a URDF whose visuals are only boxes, cylinders and spheres. Default False.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; joints: [{name, type, parent, child, limits}]; links: count; mesh_files: found and missing; reasons: why it failed.

tools.name: vessel_containment_test
tools.title: Vessel containment test
tools.summary: Drops the vessel (lands upright), drops a ball into it (stays inside, below the rim) and optionally a second vessel (nests inside); gravity only.
tools.description: Loads the vessel asset and attaches a ball (radius 0.4 x the inner rim radius by default, capped at 2 cm) and, with inner_built, the second vessel's XML under a prefix. Trial 1 lifts the vessel 2 cm and lets it fall for 1.5 s: its z axis must stay within 15 degrees of vertical and its base within 5 mm of the floor. Trial 2 releases the ball 3 cm above the rim centre and after 2 s requires it inside: horizontal distance from the vessel axis under the inner rim radius minus the ball radius, centre below the rim and above the inner floor. Trial 3 lowers the inner vessel in (its body origin 1 cm above the outer vessel's floor, on the axis, as a hand sets a cup into a bowl; dropped from the rim it would tunnel through the base) and after 2 s requires its body origin more than 5 mm below the outer rim and both vessels within 15 degrees of upright. Reports every number; passes when all requested trials pass.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_cup/construct_bowl returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: inner_built
inputs.description: A second vessel to nest inside (its rim must fit through this one's mouth).

inputs.name: ball_radius
inputs.description: Test ball radius; default 0.4 x inner rim radius, max 2 cm.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All trials passed.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence with the measured numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: drop {tilt_deg, base_height_mm, ok}, fill {ball_off_axis_mm, ball_z_mm, below_rim, above_floor, ok}, nest {inner_base_below_rim_mm, tilt_deg, ok} when requested.

tools.name: video_frustum_check
tools.title: Video frustum check
tools.summary: Projects every Stage 1 object's geometry at keyframe 0 through the video camera (camera.json or a scene camera) and requires it in front of the camera with its centre and most of its surface inside the image, so an object placed off-screen, behind the camera or under the table is caught.
tools.description: Every object Stage 1 found was seen in the video's first frame or later, so its reconstruction must stand where the video camera sees it; an object placed outside the frustum (a sign flip in a placement, a pose fitted against the wrong camera, an object dropped below the table) silently breaks Stage 3's targets and Stage 4's composite. Objects come from scene_semantics.json (mapped to bodies through scene_recon.json, else by id), or every object when no Stage 1 file is given. Each object's visible geoms (collision geoms when it has none) are sampled at keyframe 0 and projected through the camera: the fraction of points in front of the camera and inside the image shrunk by margin_px must be at least min_inside_frac, and the centroid must project inside the image. Objects of type deformable that Stage 1 lists are checked the same way on all their bodies. A Stage 1 object with no body in the scene is reported.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: Scene MJCF.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: camera.json path / dict, or the name of the scene's video camera (then give width and height). Default 'video_cam'.

inputs.name: semantic
inputs.description: scene_semantics.json (Stage 1); default: every object of the scene.

inputs.name: recon
inputs.description: scene_recon.json mapping Stage 1 ids to bodies.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Image width when camera is a scene camera name. Default 640.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Image height when camera is a scene camera name. Default 480.

inputs.name: min_inside_frac
inputs.description: Smallest fraction of an object's surface points inside the image. Default 0.5.

inputs.name: margin_px
inputs.description: Border of the image not counted as inside, pixels. Default 0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; objects [{id, inside_frac, behind_frac, centroid_px, verdict}]; camera {width, height, fovy_deg}.

tools.name: weld_gap_check
tools.title: Weld gap check
tools.summary: Position and angle residual of every active weld or connect constraint on every frame.
tools.description: For each active weld (or connect) equality constraint in the scene, replays the trajectory kinematically and measures how far the two anchor points are apart and, for a weld with a rotational part, the angle between the two frames. Fails when the gap exceeds 5 mm or the angle 3 degrees anywhere, the tolerance below which a physics replay starts without a visible snap. Constraints can be selected by body name pattern; by default all are checked. Works on any scene that uses equality constraints to assemble a robot or an object.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: gap_tol_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed anchor separation. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: angle_tol_deg
inputs.description: Largest allowed frame misalignment for torque-carrying welds. Default 3.

inputs.name: only
inputs.description: fnmatch patterns on either body name; others are skipped.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per constraint: bodies, max gap (mm), max angle (deg), worst frame and label, position-only flag.

tools.name: wrist_servo_offset_check
tools.title: Wrist servo offset check
tools.summary: Measure the steady-state error of the hand's wrist position servos at a pose with the fingers closed, and return the command offset that cancels it.
tools.description: The wrist actuators are position servos with steady-state error under load: a solved grasp pose can sit 7 mm low once the hand hangs on it dynamically, which lifts the pads clear of a cord while every static measurement still says the pose is seated. The hand is driven to the pose for `steps` steps, the error between commanded and reached wrist position is read, the command is corrected by it, and this repeats for a few rounds. The offset is kept only while it helps: if the error does not shrink (the hand is blocked by the table, not lagging) the search stops and the best offset so far is returned. Passes when the residual error is below tol_mm. Measure it with the hand CLOSED: the same grasp reads -1.7 mm open and +7.3 mm closed. It calibrates the wrist servo at the pose; it does not judge whether the grasp holds, so it is not evidence for a grasp stress test.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor}

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: {pos, euler, finger_targets}

inputs.name: tol_mm
inputs.description: acceptable residual (default 1.5)

inputs.name: steps / rounds
inputs.description: settle steps per round (250) and rounds (3)

inputs.name: give_up_mm
inputs.description: offset beyond which the hand is considered blocked (default 15)

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: residual error below tol_mm

outputs.name: offset_m
outputs.description: subtract from the commanded wrist position

outputs.name: residual_mm
outputs.description: error after correction

outputs.name: raw_error_mm
outputs.description: error with no correction

tools.name: wrist_singularity_audit
tools.title: Wrist singularity audit
tools.summary: Frames where an arm's flange Jacobian is near singular (smallest singular value) while its joints move fast or amplify the flange motion many times.
tools.description: Per-frame Jacobian measure, distinct from arm_branch_flip_audit (windows of large joint motion with a still flange) and from the speed checks (which do not know why a joint is fast). For each arm it computes the 6 x n Jacobian of the flange body over the arm joints, rotation rows scaled by rot_scale_m (default 0.3 m, so a radian of flange rotation weighs like 30 cm of travel), and its smallest singular value sigma_min (metres per radian). A frame is near-singular when sigma_min < smin_m (default 0.01 m). It fails when, on a near-singular frame, the fastest arm joint exceeds rate_deg_s (default 90 deg/s, about the rate the arm fill caps at) or the joint speed per unit of flange twist exceeds amp_rad_per_m (default 60 rad per metre: the joints race while the flange crawls; the paper's executed episodes stay under 25). Reports the worst frame per arm with sigma_min, joint rate, flange speed, phase label, and how many frames run near singular in total.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF the episode was executed in.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz (qpos [T, nq], fps, labels).

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Inclusive frame window. Default all.

inputs.name: smin_m
inputs.description: sigma_min below which a frame is near-singular. Default 0.01.

inputs.name: rate_deg_s
inputs.description: Arm joint speed that fails on a near-singular frame. Default 90.

inputs.name: amp_rad_per_m
inputs.description: Joint speed / flange twist speed that fails on a near-singular frame. Default 60.

inputs.name: rot_scale_m
inputs.description: Weight of flange rotation against translation. Default 0.3.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; issues; worst {side, frame, label, sigma_min_m, joint_rate_deg_s, amplification, flange_speed}; arms {side: min sigma, frames near singular, worst frame}.

tools.name: wrist_spin_check
tools.title: Wrist spin check
tools.summary: Largest monotone turn of each wrist joint stays under 180 degrees and the joint does not wander back and forth.
tools.description: Splits each named hinge trajectory into monotone runs (ignoring reversals smaller than the noise floor) and reports the largest run in degrees, failing when it reaches the spin limit (180 degrees by default). It also counts reversals larger than redundant_deg (15 degrees by default) that happen inside one phase label; a wrist that turns 30 degrees one way and back within the same phase did not need to turn. Joints default to every hinge whose name contains 'roll' or ends in the last arm joint index; pass them explicitly for other robots.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array; phase labels enable the redundancy rule.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.description: Hinge joints to check. Default: hinges with 'roll', 'j6' or 'wrist' in their name.

inputs.name: spin_limit_deg
inputs.description: Largest monotone turn allowed. Default 180.

inputs.name: redundant_deg
inputs.description: A reversal this large inside one phase counts as redundant turning. Default 15.

inputs.name: noise_deg
inputs.description: Reversals below this are jitter. Default 1.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per joint: largest turn, its frames and labels, net turn, redundant reversals (frame, size, label).

tools.name: wrist_stop_check
tools.title: Wrist stop check
tools.summary: Named joints stay inside the real hardware's ranges, with a margin, on every frame.
tools.description: Compares each named joint's trajectory against the range the real hardware can reach (degrees for hinges, metres for slides), minus a safety margin, and fails on any frame outside it. By default it finds the wrist hinges by name (roll, wrist, j6) and uses the scene's own joint limits (a joint the scene leaves unlimited, with no real range given, is skipped and listed); pass joints={name: (lo, hi)} with the real stops, or real_stops={side: (lo, hi)} to apply one range per side by name. The report gives each joint's minimum and maximum, the remaining margin to each stop and the frame and phase label of the closest approach. The module carries the real wrist-roll stops the paper's arms were deployed with, right (-20, 180) and left (-180, 20) degrees, as REAL_WRIST_STOPS_DEG.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.type: dict joint name -> (lo, hi) | list[str] | None
inputs.description: Joints to check with their real ranges (degrees for hinges). A list uses the model's limits; None finds wrist hinges by name.

inputs.name: real_stops
inputs.description: Real range applied to each default joint whose name contains the side.

inputs.name: margin_deg
inputs.description: Reserve kept from each explicit real range. Default 2; the model's own limits get 0.

inputs.name: robot_prefix
inputs.description: Default 'robot_'.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per joint: min, max, range, margin to each stop, worst frame and label; unlimited_skipped: joints with no range to check.
